However, Los Angeles ambushed the visitors on both ends of the floor over the final 12 minutes, going on a decisive 37 - 15 run in the fourth quarter. As is often the case, shooting was the difference in the game, as the Thunder managed to drain just 36 percent of their attempts, including 21 percent from three - point range. In turn, the Clippers shot a solid 44 percent, a tally that featured a 42 percent success rate from distance. Paul George paced the Thunder with 20 points, although he went 7 - for - 27 from the field. He added eight rebounds, four assists and two steals. Steven Adams generated a 17 - point, 18 - rebound double - double that also included one steal. Raymond Felton followed with a bench - leading 12 points and also supplied four rebounds, three assists and one block. Alex Abrines poured in 10 points and supplemented them with two rebounds, one assist and one steal. Dennis Schroder scuffled while filling in for Westbrook, totaling eight points on 2 - for - 15 shooting while dishing out eight assists and hauling in a pair of rebounds. Danilo Gallinari and Tobias Harris led the Clippers with matching 26 - point efforts. Gallinari added five boards and one assist, while Harris registered 10 rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block. Lou Williams lead the second unit with 17 points. Boban Marjanovic had his second strong performance off the bench to open the season, posting 13 points and five rebounds. Starting center Marcin Gortat mustered four points but also brought down 12 rebounds and handed out one assist. The Thunder next take the court Sunday evening versus the Sacramento Kings, while the Clippers do battle with the Houston Rockets at home that same night.

The Los Angeles Clippers defeated the Houston Rockets 115 - 112 at Staples Center on Sunday. An eventful weekend for the Rockets as back - to - back games against both Los Angeles teams resulted in a split, but the some hungover damage came on Chris Paul's end after being suspended for two games following a fight with Rajon Rondo of the Lakers on Saturday. The suspension was handed down Sunday afternoon leaving Paul out of the Rockets (1 - 2) lineup. The matchup on Sunday resulted in the Clippers getting off to a strong start by taking a 29 - 24 lead into the second quarter. Tobias Harris and Danilo Gallianari continued their productive scoring effort amongst the starters, where they combined for 43 points on 16 - of - 34 shooting. The Rockets would not go away in the second quarter, where James Harden found his stroke from behind the arc and orchestrated Clint Capela into some easy layups. The momentum shifted back in Los Angeles favor for the majority of the second half, specifically the waning minutes of the third quarter where they built a nine point lead. Los Angeles had little issue in the final period until the final two minutes. After a Montrezl Harrell layup with 1:43 remaining, James Harden single handedly brought the Rockets back within one possession after a quick two point jumper, followed up by an and - 1 from behind the arc. Harden missed the 22 - footer at the buzzer a possession later and the Clippers escaped with their second win of the season. Harden led all scorers with 31 points on 11 - of - 26 shooting, while Eric Gordon and Clint Capela pitched in 21 points and 23 points, respectively. Carmelo Anthony still looks to adjust to his bench role and finished with nine points and six rebounds across27 minutes. Harrell was the bench leader for the Clippers and posted a double - double with 17 points and 10 rebounds in the win. Next up, the Clippers will play their first road game of the season when they visit the New Orleans Pelicans on Tuesday, while the Rockets return home to face the Utah Jazz on Wednesday.

The Los Angeles Clippers blew out the Washington Wizards 136 - 104 at Staples Center on Sunday. The Clippers had nine players finish in double figures and had no trouble looking back after posting 41 points in the second quarter to improve to 4 - 2 on the season. The rebound battle and ball movement on the Clippers end resulted in the blowout as unselfish basketball and the strength of their bench all factored into stifling the Wizards, who fell to 1 - 4 on the season. Tobias Harris led all scorers with 22 points to go with 11 rebounds, while Patrick Beverley and Avery Bradley combined for 26 points on 19 shots. One of the most productive bench players early in this season has been Montrezl Harrell, who pitched in 13 points and six rebounds on 6 - of - 7 shooting in just 16 minutes of action. Harrell also blocked two shots and entered the game averaging just over two swats per game. Rookie Shae Gilgeous-Alexander added 10 points on 4 - of - 8 shooting, alongside eight rebounds and seven assists in 28 minutes. The Wizards starters could not muster enough offense to pace with Los Angeles, as Bradley Beal and John Wall combined for 38 points on 36 shots. Ian Mahinmi was getting bullied around the glass and grabbed just seven rebounds in his 29 minutes. Kelly Oubre Jr also struggled to find a rhythm off the bench as he scored nine points on 2 - of - 12 shooting. Both teams are on the road Tuesday, as the Clippers take on the Oklahoma City Thunder, while the Wizards will face the Memphis Grizzlies.

The Los Angeles Clippers defeated the visiting Minnesota Timberwolves, 120 - 109, at Staples Center on Monday evening. Minnesota (4 - 7) has been in a rough patch recently, and the Clippers (6 - 4) made sure to capitalize. Los Angeles held its opponent to just 5 - of - 22 shooting from three - point range, allowing it to take a lead thanks to its own stellar 14 - of - 31 night from deep. The Clippers also outperformed Minnesota on the boards, grabbing 12 offensive rebounds while holding the Wolves to only eight. The loss for Minnesota was the team's third straight, and it comes at an inopportune time for the team, as rumors continue to swirl around All-Star Jimmy Butler's trade demand. Three Clippers scored at least 20 points in the team's win. Forwards Tobias Harris and Danilo Gallinari scored 22 apiece to lead the team, while star guard Lou Williams delivered 20 points and six assists. Big man Boban Marjanovic scored 10 points and had eight rebounds in only 17 minutes on the floor. Minnesota, meanwhile, saw 20 points from Butler in the loss. All-Star big man Karl-Anthony Towns scored another 20 and also blocked four shots. Veteran point guard Derrick Rose led the Wolves with 21 points, coming a week after he delivered a career - high 50 point performance. Rose shot 8 - of - 20 from the field and dished out four assists in Monday's loss. The Timberwolves will attempt to snap their losing streak with a visit to the Los Angeles Lakers on Wednesday. The Clippers, meanwhile, travel to Portland to face the Trail Blazers on Thurdsay.

The Los Angeles Clippers defeated the visiting Milwaukee Bucks in overtime, 128 - 126, at Staples Center on Saturday. While there were only nine ties and six lead changes in this game, it took an overtime session to determine a winner. Lou Williams was the hero, as he hit a game - winning floater with just 1 seconds remaining to win the game for the Clippers. Free-throw shooting was critical, with Los Angeles connecting on 22 - of - 27 while Milwaukee hit just 16 - of - 23. The Clippers also outshot the Bucks from the field and from three - point range. The Clippers bench played a huge factor too, outscoring the Bucks bench, 52 - 27. Los Angeles also did a good job of cleaning up the glass, winning the defensive rebounding differential, 44 - 37. The Bucks (9 - 3) were led by Giannis Antetokounmpo, as he tallied 27 points, 18 rebounds, four assists, five steals and two blocks on 11 - of - 19 from the field. Malcolm Brogdon totaled 23 points, four rebounds and three assists. Brook Lopez accrued 20 points, four rebounds, two steals and three blocks. Eric Bledsoe finished with 15 points, five rebounds and five assists while Khris Middleton generated 14 points, three rebounds and five assists. The Clippers (7 - 5) leading scorer came off the bench, as Montrezl Harrell provided 26 points and nine boards on 9 - of - 12 shooting. Lou Williams finished with 12 points, five rebounds and 10 assists. Patrick Beverley led the starters with 21 points, five rebounds and three assists on 7 - of - 11 from the field. Tobias Harris collected 20 points, 11 rebounds and two steals. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander amassed 16 points, six rebounds, four assists and three blocks. Milwaukee plays again on Sunday, as they travel to face the Denver Nuggets. As for Los Angeles, they play host to the Golden State Warriors on Monday for their next outing.

The Los Angeles Clippers took down the Golden State Warriors, 121 - 116, in overtime at Staples Center on Monday. The Warriors (11 - 3) were without league - leading scorer Steph Curry (groin), but still managed to hang with the Clippers until the very end. It was shaping up to be an easy win for the Clippers (8 - 5) in the fourth quarter, as the team held a 12 - point lead with just five minutes remaining. The Warriors, though, clawed back in signature fashion, tying the game on a Klay Thompson three - pointer with 86 seconds remaining. Golden State's momentum did not carry over to OT, though, as the Clippers were able to earn the win behind the strong play of big man Montrezl Harrell. Warriors superstar Kevin Durant fouled out with two minutes remaining in overtime, leaving the Warriors without both Curry and Durant to try to close the game on LA's home court. Harrell led the Clippers with 23 points and four blocks in the win. He was nearly matched by Lou Williams, who scored 22 points. Williams, though, shot just 5 - of - 18 from the field, struggling to find the basket for much of the fourth quarter. Rookie point guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored another 18 points on 8 - of - 11 shooting. For Golden State, Durant led the way with a triple - double. The former MVP scored 33 points, grabbed 11 rebounds, and dished out 10 assists in the loss. Thompson also had a big night, scoring 31 points despite his team being unable to secure the win. Both teams will return to action on Thursday, with the Warriors visiting the struggling Houston Rockets and the Clippers hosting the San Antonio Spurs.

The Los Angeles Clippers defeated the San Antonio Spurs, 116 - 11, at Staples Center on Thursday. The Clippers (9 - 5) have made a statement over the last week, with Thursday's win serving as their third straight win after the team knocked off both the Bucks and Warriors within the last seven days. Thursday night, Los Angeles let the Spurs (7 - 7) remain within striking distance, but it never allowed the visiting team to breakthrough. This was thanks in large part to Lou Williams in the closing moments, as his game - winning three - pointer with 40 seconds left put the Clippers up for good. Williams finished with 23 points on 9 - of - 20 shooting in 28 minutes off the bench to lead the way for the Clippers. Danilo Gallinari was close behind with 19 points, while Tobias Harris put together a great all - around performance with 18 points, eight rebounds and assists in 28 minutes. For the Spurs, it was all about DeMar Derozan, who scored a game - high 34 points on 14 - of - 30 shooting to go along with six rebounds, five assists and three steals in 41 minutes. Unfortunately for DeRozan, when the Spurs had a chance to tie the game down three points in the closing moments, their star turned the ball over, and the game was officially out of reach. DeRozan still didn't get much help Thursday night, however, as LaMarcus Aldridge shot a miserable 3 - of - 15 from the field en route to scoring just 10 points in 38 minutes, but he did have a game - high 16 rebounds. Rudy Gay posted 19 points off the bench in what was the team's third straight loss.

The Los Angeles Clippers defeated the visiting Memphis Grizzlies in overtime, 112 - 107, at Staples Center on Friday. There were 15 ties and 13 lead changes in this competitive game, as neither club ever led by more than eight points. In fact, the Grizzlies trailed by five points heading into the fourth quarter, as they started that quarter on a 14 - 3 run to take their largest lead. The Clippers did bounce back though, as they hit three free - throws with one second left in regulation to send the game into overtime. Los Angeles made the final run that mattered most, as they finished the game on a 14 - 6 run in the extra session. The biggest factor for the Clippers was the turnover differential, as they committed just 10 turnovers while forcing 16 from the Grizzlies. Free-throw shooting was also critical, with Los Angeles hitting 24 - of - 27 and Memphis connecting on 14 - of - 18. The Clippers bench was huge as well, outscoring the Grizzlies, 53 - 24. The Grizzlies (12 - 6) got a sparkling performance out of Marc Gasol, as he collected 27 points, 13 rebounds and seven assists. Mike Conley fouled out in regulation but still finished with 19 points, three rebounds and 11 assists. Jaren Jackson Jr. amassed 20 points, seven rebounds, three assists and three blocks. Kyle Anderson accrued 11 points, five rebounds and four assists. The Clippers (12 - 6) were led by Montrezl Harrell, as he provided 22 points, 11 rebounds and two blocks off the bench. Danilo Gallinari led the starters with 20 points, nine rebounds and two assists. Tobias Harris totaled 12 points, seven rebounds and four assists while Lou Williams generated 16 points and six assists off the bench. Both teams return to action on Sunday, with Memphis playing host to the New York Knicks and Los Angeles traveling to face the Portland Trail Blazers.

The Los Angeles Clippers took down the visiting Phoenix Suns, 115 - 99, on Wednesday evening. It was a battle of first meets last on Wednesday, as the top - ranked Clippers (14 - 6) hosted the 15th - place Suns (4 - 17). The game went accordingly, as LA earned a blowout win to maintain its first - place standing. With 11 made three - pointers and 18 offensive rebounds, the Clippers were able to overcome some struggles with ball management. It was an easy win for the team despite committing 21 turnovers on the night. LA has now won eight of its last nine games and is showing no signs of slowing down. Danilo Gallinari led the Clippers with 28 points and grabbed 10 rebounds in the win. His fellow forward, Tobias Harris, added another 10 rebounds to go with 18 points on the night. Big man Boban Marjanovic, in just 19 minutes on the court, secured 12 rebounds, including eight on the offensive end. All three stellar frontcourt performances contributed to LA's comfortable victory. Phoenix, on the other hand, struggled mightily on the offensive end. The team shot just 31 percent from three - point range and 43 percent overall. Devin Booker led the team with 23 points. It was an off night for rookie big man DeAndre Ayton, who committed five fouls and finished with just four points in 30 minutes of play. The Clippers visit the Kings on Thursday, while Phoenix will host the Orlando Magic on Friday.

The Miami Heat defeated the host Los Angeles Clippers, 121 - 98, at Staples Center on Saturday. While this was a one - point game heading into the fourth quarter, Miami really took control late. In fact, they started the fourth quarter on a 19 - 2 run, as Los Angeles went just 1 - of - 13 from the field in the first nine minutes of the quarter. The Heat ended up outscoring the Clippers, 30 - 9, in that quarter. The game was tightly contested before that lopsided fourth quarter, as there were seven ties and 11 lead changes in the first three quarters. The Heat's defense was key, as they held the Clippers to 37 percent from the field and 24 percent from three - point range. Ball movement played a huge factor in that, with Miami out - assisting Los Angeles, 27 - 16. The Heat also outrebounded the Clippers, 58 - 48. The Heat (11 - 14) got a vintage performance from Dwyane Wade, as he provided 25 points, six rebounds and six assists off the bench. Justise Winslow led the starters with 21 points, six rebounds, nine assists and two steals. James Johnson totaled 18 points, eight rebounds and three assists. Kelly Olynyk was also a huge spark off the bench, amassing 15 points, 10 rebounds and four assists. The Clippers (16 - 9) were led by Tobias Harris, as he collected 20 points, six rebounds and two steals. Danilo Gallinari accrued 12 points, 10 rebounds and three assists. Lou Williams led the bench with 18 points, three rebounds and five assists. Montrezl Harrell generated 10 points, nine boards and three blocks off the bench as well. Both teams play road games on Monday for their next outing, with Miami playing the Los Angeles Lakers and the Clippers facing the Phoenix Suns.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the host Los Angeles Clippers, 123 - 99, at Staples Center on Tuesday. Toronto played this game without Kawhi Leonard (hip) but Los Angeles is the team who came out flat. In fact, the Raptors started the game with a 36 - 23 first quarter, as they held a double - digit lead for the entirety of the second half. The third quarter solidified their domination, with Toronto outscoring Los Angeles, 33 - 17. The Raptors offense was unstoppable, as they connected on 52 percent from the field and 48 percent from three - point range, despite missing seven of their final nine shots with the reserves in. They did that while dominating the assist - to - turnover ratio, with Toronto out - assisting Los Angeles, 34 - 25, while winning the turnover differential, 16 - 7. That allowed Toronto to outscore Los Angeles in points off turnovers, 24 - 5. The Raptors also won the fastbreak scoring differential, 28 - 4, while outscoring the Clippers in the paint, 54 - 44. The Raptors (22 - 7) were led by Serge Ibaka, as he tallied 25 points, nine rebounds, two assists and three blocks. Kyle Lowry accrued 21 points, five rebounds and seven assists on 8 - of - 13 from the field. Pascal Siakam amassed 13 points, three rebounds and five assists. Fred VanVleet got a rare start and finished with five points, six rebounds and 14 assists. Jonas Valanciunas was a huge spark off the bench, generating 16 points, five rebounds and two steals in 18 minutes. The Clippers (17 - 10) highest - scoring starter was Danilo Gallinari, as he finished with 11 points, five rebounds and two assists. Tobias Harris totaled just 10 points and three rebounds. Both those players went 4 - of - 10 from the field. Marcin Gortat accumulated seven points, four rebounds and four assists. Tyrone Wallace was their best player, as he provided 15 points, four rebounds and six assists off the bench. Boban Marjanvoic also played plenty of garbage time, collecting 18 points and seven rebounds off the pine. On deck for Toronto is another road matchup versus the Golden State Warriors on Wednesday. As for Los Angeles, they return to action on Thursday when they travel to face the San Antonio Spurs.

The Portland Trail Blazers defeated the Los Angeles Clippers, 131 - 127, at Staples Center on Monday evening. Monday's contest saw two of the premier teams in the Western Conference go head - to - head, and the game did not disappoint. Portland (17 - 13) squeaked by LA (17 - 13) in the game's final minute thanks to clutch play from its stars. While the Trail Blazers had led by double - digits in the fourth quarter, the Clippers quickly caught up in the final five minutes of action. LA took a bit of a blow after big man Montrezl Harrell was assessed a flagrant foul and ejected for elbowing Portland's Jusuf Nurkic with just over seven minutes left in the fourth quarter. Still, the Clippers fought back, carried by a career night from star forward Tobias Harris. Harris led his team with 39 points, a new career high. Portland, however, answered back, as Damian Lillard hit a handful of clutch shots down the stretch and scored 39 points of his own. It was C.J. McCollum, though, that hit the dagger for the Blazers, knocking down a step - back jumper to make it a two - possession game with 27 seconds remaining. Lillard shot 11 - of - 20 from the field, including 6 - of - 7 from three - point range, en route to his big night. 21 of Lillard's points came in the third quarter, as he simply could not miss in the second half. McCollum, meanwhile, added another 27 points in the win. Nurkic scored 20 as well, adding seven rebounds and two blocks. Harris's 39 points led all Clippers scorers and set a new career - high for the budding star. He added 11 rebounds on the night. The Clippers, who remain without star guard Lou Williams (hamstring), saw 24 points from rookie point guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander. Harrell had 15 points as well prior to his ejection. Portland will host the Memphis Grizzlies on Wednesday, while LA will see the Dallas Mavericks on Thursday evening.

The Los Angeles Clippers defeated the visiting Dallas Mavericks, 125 - 121, at Staples Center on Thursday evening. The Clippers got out to a good start at home, as they emerged from a hard - fought first quarter with a 30 - 27 lead. They built with momentum in the second, where they outscored the visitors by eight in the quarter, to take a 65 - 54 lead into halftime. The Mavericks came out strong in the second half and chipped away at the deficit through the third, but still trailed by eight heading into the final frame. The Mavs kept pressing and tied it up at 90 early in the fourth, and led 105 - 102 at the halfway point in the quarter. However, the Clippers pulled ahead with a four - point lead with 2:37 left in the contest and were able to hold the edge from there, to end a four - game losing streak. Danilo Gallinari led the Clippers with 32 points, six rebounds, four assists and two blocks, in 33 minutes. Lou Williams returned to action after missing sometime with a hamstring injury, to finish with 26 points, eight assists, two steals and one rebound, in 23 minutes off the bench. Montrezl Harrell added 18 points, six rebounds, four assists and two blocks, in 28 minutes off the bench. Meanwhile, Luka Doncic led the Mavs with 32 points, five assists, four rebounds and four steals, in 31 minutes. J.J. Barea added 19 points, eight assists and three rebounds, in 27 minutes off the bench, while DeAndre Jordan tallied 11 points, 22 rebounds, four assists and one steal, in 32 minutes. The Mavs (15 - 15) take on the Warriors in Golden State on Saturday. The Clippers (18 - 13) play host to the Nuggets on Saturday.

The Los Angeles Clippers defeated the visiting Denver Nuggets, 132 - 111. at Staples Center on Saturday. This marks the Nuggets worst loss of the season, as the Clippers dominated throughout. In fact, they won all four individual quarters, as a 34 - 26 first quarter really set the tone. Rebounding was huge for Los Angeles, as they won that battle, 56 - 37. Much of that came on the defensive end, winning that differential, 43 - 24. The Clippers ended up shooting 58 percent from the field and 50 percent from three - point range while holding the Nuggets to 42 percent from the field and 29 percent from long range. The Nuggets (21 - 10) leading scorer was actually ejected in the third quarter, as Nikola Jokic tallied 19 points, six rebounds and three assists before being handed two technicals for arguing. Jamal Murray totaled 18 points, three rebounds and two assists. Monte Morris led the bench with 15 points and five assists while Malik Beasley amassed 11 points, four rebounds and five steals. The Clippers (19 - 13) were led by Danilo Gallinari, as he accrued 21 points, four rebounds and two assists against his former team. Tobias Harris matched those 21 points, adding seven rebounds and three assists to his tally. Shai Gilegous-Alexander collected 14 points, two rebounds, six assists and two steals. Montrezl Harrell was huge off the bench, providing 20 points and 10 boards on 9 - of - 11 shooting. Both these teams have time off before their next game, as they both don't play again until Wednesday. Denver will travel to face the San Antonio Spurs while Los Angeles will play host to the Sacramento Kings.

The Los Angeles Clippers defeated the Sacramento Kings, 127 - 118, at Staples Center on Wednesday evening. It was shaping up to be an easy wire - to - wire win for the Clippers (20 - 14), who never trailed over the course of the game. Strong bench play helped the Clippers maintain their early lead, as the second unit scored 57 points in total. Things became complicated in the fourth quarter, though, as Sacramento (18 - 16) launched a last - minute comeback effort to trim the lead to as little as three points. Once again, LA's bench players came up big, as Lou Williams knocked down a clutch shot with a minute remaining to extend his team's lead back to five points. Montrezl Harrell, meanwhile, sealed the win with a game - clinching block on the other end of the floor. The block was Harrell's fifth of the night in only 27 minutes of action. Williams was LA's leading scorer with 24 points, including 4 - of - 5 shooting from three - point range. Harrell added 22 more points and nine rebounds to go along with his strong rim protection. All five Clippers starters scored in double digits, and the team as a whole shot 50 percent and knocked down 12 three - pointers. Sacramento, meanwhile, saw a team - best 19 points from De'Aaron Fox. Fox also tallied nine assists and six rebounds. It was an off night for his back court partner, Buddy Hield, though. Hield shot just 4 - of - 18 from the floor en route to only 11 points, well below his season average of 20. Sacramento will host the Los Angeles Lakers on Thursday, while the Clippers will see the Lakers in LA on Friday.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the host Los Angeles Clippers, 122 - 111, at Staples Center on Saturday evening. The Spurs got out to a good start on the road as they led by two after one quarter. The Clippers evened things up through the second and the teams ended up tied at 56 by halftime. The Spurs came out on another level in the third, as they outscored the Clippers by 20 in the quarter, to bring a 20 - point lead into the final frame. The Clippers made a solid push in the fourth, outscoring the visitors by nine, however it was not enough to complete the comeback. LaMarcus Aldridge led the Spurs with 38 points, seven rebounds, two assists and two blocks, in 36 minutes. DeMar DeRozan followed up with 25 points, 13 rebounds, six assists, four steals and one block, in 37 minutes. Derrick White and Rudy Gay added 12 points each, while Marco Belinelli added 11 points off the bench. Meanwhile, Danilo Gallinari led the Clippers with 21 points, nine rebounds and two assists, in 28 minutes. Montrezl Harrell finished with 21 points, five rebounds, four steals and one assist, while Tobias Harris and Lou Williams finished with 16 points each. The Clippers (21 - 15) will look to bounce back as they play host to the 76ers on Tuesday. The Spurs (20 - 17) play host to the Celtics on Monday.

The visiting Philadelphia 76ers defeated the Los Angeles Clippers, 119 - 113, at Staples Center on Tuesday. The 76ers (24 - 14) staved off a fourth - quarter comeback by the Clippers (21 - 16), who cut a 15 - point deficit to as little as four points. However, the lead proved insurmountable for LA, as the team was unable to close the gap by the end of regulation. Things got testy between the two teams in the fourth quarter, as Jimmy Butler and Avery Bradley were each ejected following a spat midway through the period. The Sixers managed to close out the game without their All-Star wing, who had 16 points prior to his ejection. Philly was led by a monumental 28 - point, 19 - rebound performance from Joel Embiid. Embiid added three assists and three blocks. Ben Simmons scored 14 points and flirted with a triple - double, grabbing nine rebounds and dishing eight assists. The win brings Philadelphia to 2 - 2 over the course of its current road trip. LA, meanwhile, saw four different players score at least 20 points. Lou Williams led the team with 22 points off the bench, while the duo of Tobias Harris and Danilo Gallinari scored 21 points each. Ultimately, though, sub - par shooting sank the Clippers' chances. LA went just 5 - of - 25 from beyond the arc in the loss. Both the Sixers and Clippers will be playing their next game in Phoenix. Philly continues its road trip with a visit to Talking Stick Resort Arena on Tuesday, while the Clippers will visit the Suns for a divisional matchup on Thursday.

The Los Angeles Clippers defeated the visiting Orlando Magic, 106 - 96, at Staples Center on Sunday. While Orlando led 28 - 18 after the first quarter, Los Angeles dominated from there. In fact, they won each of the final three quarters by at least five points apiece, as a 17 - 2 run in the middle of the fourth quarter really put the game away for the Clippers. Los Angeles defense was stifling in this victory, as they held Orlando to 37 percent from the field and 29 percent from three - point range. That was also evident in the turnover differential, with the Clippers winning that battle, 12 - 7. Los Angeles also did a ton of work down low, outscoring Orlando in the paint, 52 - 38. The Magic (17 - 22) got a spectacular performance from Nikola Vucevic, as he collected 16 points, 24 rebounds, eight assists and two blocks. Aaron Gordon amassed 17 points and five boards. Evan Fournier finished with 12 points, three rebounds and two assists. Mo Bamba played well off the bench, totaling eight points, 10 rebounds and two blocks. The Clippers (23 - 16) were led by Tobias Harris, as he tallied 28 points, nine rebounds and two assists against his former team. Danilo Gallinari accrued 13 points, five rebounds and two assists. Marcin Gortat generated eight points, 10 rebounds and six assists. Lou Williams led the bench with 17 points, four rebounds and four assists. Orlando will continue their west coast trip on Monday, as they play the Sacramento Kings. As for Los Angeles, they play host to the Charlotte Hornets on Tuesday for their next fixture.

The Los Angeles Clippers defeated the Charlotte Hornets, 128 - 109, at Staples Center on Tuesday evening. Los Angeles (24 - 16) hopped out to an early lead, going up by as much as nine in the first half. While Charlotte (19 - 21) kept the game close for much of regulation, the Clippers' offense exploded for 42 fourth - quarter points and a double - digit win. LA's dominant bench unit helped lead the charge, as Lou Williams and Montrezl Harrell combined to score 50 points in the win. The Clippers finished the night shooting over 51 percent from the field and 46 percent from three - point range. In addition to a team - high 27 points, Williams contributed 10 assists in the win. Harrell, the Clippers' breakout big man, added 11 rebounds and five assists. The team also saw an impressive defensive effort from rookie point guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, who grabbed three steals and blocked four shots in just 21 minutes of play. Charlotte, meanwhile, relied heavily on its own bench for production. Shots weren't falling for All-Star guard Kemba Walker, who went just 6 - of - 18 for 13 points. Sophomore Malik Monk picked up some of the slack, though, delivering a team - high 24 points off the bench. Ultimately, however, Charlotte's offense could not match LA's top - notch production, shooting just 40 percent from the field. The Hornets will visit Portland on Friday, while the Clippers have a trip to Denver on Thursday.

The Detroit Pistons defeated the host Los Angeles Clippers, 109 - 104, at Staples Center on Saturday. While this wasn't a wire - to - wire win for Detroit, they held the lead for the final 45 - plus minutes. A 37 - 24 first quarter in advantage of the Pistons really set the tone, as the Clippers couldn't recover from that. Rebounding was key for Detroit, as they outrebounded Los Angeles, 48 - 38. The Pistons also recorded 12 steals while the Clippers recorded just seven thefts. Detroit's starters really dominated the game as well, outscoring Los Angeles' starters, 93 - 48. The Pistons (18 - 23) got a spectacular performance from Blake Griffin, as he abused his former team with 44 points, eight rebounds, five assists and three steals on 13 - of - 23 from the field. Andre Drummond finished with 20 points, 21 rebounds and three steals. Reggie Bullock amassed 17 points, seven rebounds and four assists. The Clippers (24 - 18) two - best players came off the bench, as Lou Williams led the team with 22 points, two rebounds and three assists. Montrezl Harrell was just as good, providing 21 points, nine rebounds, six assists and four steals. Danilo Gallinari led the starters with 23 points, six rebounds and two assists. Tobias Harris totaled 11 points, 10 rebounds, two assists and two steals. Both teams return to action on Monday, with Los Angeles playing host to the New Orleans Pelicans and Detroit traveling to face the shorthanded Utah Jazz.

The New Orleans Pelicans took down the Los Angeles Clippers, 121 - 117, at Staples Center on Monday evening. It was shaping up to be an easy win for New Orleans (21 - 23), as the team led by as much as 20 points midway through the third quarter. The Clippers (24 - 19), however, had other plans, and mounted a furious comeback late in the fourth. LA cut the lead to as little as two points by the end of the fourth quarter, thanks in large part to a 13 - 2 run in the third quarter. Lou Williams, Montrezl Harrell, and Tobias Harris all scored for LA during the run. Unfortunately for the Clippers, though, Anthony Davis and the Pelicans were able to hold off the comeback. Davis delivered a monster performance to help protect his team's lead. The superstar big man scored 46 points to go with a game - high 16 rebounds and three steals. It was Davis's seventh 40 - point outing of the season. The Pelicans also saw impressive outings from Julius Randle and Jrue Holiday. Holiday scored 19 points and dished out eight assists. Randle, meanwhile, had 27 points and grabbed six rebounds. LA saw its own fair share of strong performances despite coming up short. Danilo Gallinari delivered 25 points on 8 - of - 13 shooting, adding five rebounds and six assists. Bench big man Montrezl Harrell led the second unit with 26 points and also had 10 rebounds. On Wednesday, the Pelicans will visit Golden State while the Clippers will host the Utah Jazz.

The Utah Jazz took down the Los Angeles Clippers, 129 - 109, at Staples Center on Wednesday. It was a comfortable win for the Jazz (25 - 21), who held a double - digit lead for the majority of regulation. Utah played a remarkably efficient game, shooting 52 percent from the field and reaching the free - throw line 37 times. Los Angeles (24 - 20), on the other hand, was unable to make a dent in Utah's impressive defense. Despite boasting one of the league's highest - scoring offenses, the Clippers shot only 45 percent from the field and tallied just 49 first - half points. Utah saw an incredible 23 - points, 22 - rebound performance from star center Rudy Gobert. The reigning Defensive Player of the Year set a new season high on the boards and also blocked four shots. The Jazz also enjoyed a team - high 28 points from sophomore guard Donovan Mitchell. The Clippers, meanwhile, were not themselves in Wednesday's loss. LA's combo of star forwards, Tobias Harris and Danilo Gallinari, shot just 9 - of - 28 from the field for 26 points. Big man Montrezl Harrell, fresh off consecutive 20 - point performances, scored only 11 points off the bench on the night. On Friday, Utah will host the Cleveland Cavaliers, while Los Angeles will square off with the Golden State Warriors.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the host Los Angeles Clippers, 112 - 94, at Staples Center on Friday evening. The Warriors took the early advantage on the road, with a 28 - 25 lead after one quarter. However, the Clippers stayed with it and cut the deficit to just one, as they trailed 52 - 51 at the half. The Warriors regained control through the third, where they outscored the Clippers by eight, to take a nine - point lead into the fourth. They maintained the upper hand through the final quarter, outscoring the Clippers by nine, to walk away with their seventh straight win. Stephen Curry led the Warriors with 28 points on 10 - of - 19 shooting, five rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block, in 33 minutes. Kevin Durant followed up with 24 points, seven rebounds, five assists, two steals and two blocks, while DeMarcus Cousins tallied 14 points, six rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block, in 15 minutes of action. Meanwhile, Tobias Harris led the Clippers with 28 points, nine rebounds and two assists, in 35 minutes. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander followed up with 24 points, five assists, three rebounds and three steals, while Marcin Gortat chipped in six points and four rebounds. Lou Williams (hamstring) did not play. The Clippers (24 - 21) will look to bounce back as they take on the Spurs in San Antonio on Sunday. The Warriors (32 - 14) take on the Lakers in Los Angeles on Monday.

The Los Angeles Clippers defeated the Sacramento Kings, 122 - 108, at Staples Center on Sunday afternoon. The Clippers (28 - 22) have now won four out of their last five games and seem to be leaving behind an ugly five - game losing run that complicated their position in the standings, and they looked like the better side against the Kings (25 - 25) right from the beginning of the contest. The Clippers quickly jumped to a huge 34 - 21 lead following the first 12 minutes of action, and they never looked back from there. Los Angeles also won the second quarter (33 - 30) and while Sacramento showed some signs of life in the third quarter, period they won 25 - 20, it wasn't enough to put the Clippers' win in any sort of danger. Los Angeles won the final quarter as well, 35 - 32, and closed things out rather comfortably. Six Clippers scored in double digits in this one and surprisingly, the top scorer came off the bench since Montrezl Harrell had 25 points and seven rebounds while going 11 - 13 from the field. Tobias Harris had 18 points, and Patrick Beverley delivered a strong double - double since he finished the contest with 16 points, 10 rebounds and eight assists. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander had 17 points, five assists and four rebounds. De'Aaron Fox led the way for the Kings since he finished with 21 points, four rebounds and three assists. Iman Shumpert and Buddy Hield each contributed 16 points, although the latter also chipped in with five assists, four rebounds and two steals. Marvin Bagley III had 14 points off the bench, while Bogdan Bogdanovic also impressed off the bench with 19 points in 31 minutes.

The Atlanta Hawks took down the Los Angeles Clippers, 123 - 118, at Staples Center on Monday evening. Hawks point guard Trae Young set the bar high the last time these two teams met, delivering a season - high 17 assists against the Clippers in November. On Monday, he once again left an impression on LA, scoring a team - high 26 points to help his team earn a much - needed win. The Hawks (16 - 33) went up early thanks to strong play from Young and John Collins, who scored seven points each in the first quarter. While LA (27 - 23) fought its way back and evened the game at 71 - 71, a late third - quarter run helped Atlanta maintain control of the game. Big man Alex Len helped spark the run by scoring eight points in under three minutes of action. The win brought Atlanta to 3 - 3 in its last six games, as the team continues to distance itself from its slow start to the season. Young has been a big part of that, averaging 18 points per game since the start of January. In addition to his strong scoring on Monday, he dished out eight assists and committed only one turnover. Collins finished the game with 22 points, while Len contributed another 19 off the bench. As a team, Atlanta shot over 50 percent from the field. Los Angeles, meanwhile, was led by 30 points from star forward Tobias Harris. Harris also flirted with a triple - double, grabbing eight boards and dishing out seven assists. Off the bench, Lou Williams and Montrezl Harrell combined for 39 points and five steals, with Williams also recording nine assists. However, the team could not quite match Atlanta's efficient production, shooting 48 percent from the field. The loss snapped a three - game winning streak for the Clippers. Next on the agenda for Atlanta is a trip to Sacramento on Wednesday. The Clippers, meanwhile, will shift their focus to their tilt with their crosstown rival, the Lakers, on Thursday.

The Los Angeles Lakers took down the Los Angeles Clippers, 123 - 120, in overtime at Staples Center on Thursday. After missing the Lakers' (27 - 25) last 17 games with a groin injury, superstar forward LeBron James made his return to the court on Thursday. Things started quietly for the four - time MVP, as he notched only two points in the first quarter and finished the first half with just five points under his belt. James delivered when it counted, though, scoring nine points in the fourth quarter and scoring or assisting on nine of the team's points in overtime. The Clippers (28 - 24), meanwhile, fought hard to force the game into overtime. They ended regulation on a 70 run, tying the game on a three - pointer from Tobias Harris. Victory, however, eluded the team's grasp in overtime, as the Lakers went up by five points quickly and never looked back. James finished the game with a team - high 24 points for the Lakers. He flirted with a triple - double, tallying 14 rebounds and nine assists. His play was complemented by fellow veteran Rajon Rondo, who finished with 14 points, 13 rebounds, and seven assists. The Clippers, meanwhile, saw 15 points, eight rebounds, and eight assists from Harris. The team also got a gem from Lou Williams, who scored 24 points and dished out six assists while committing only one turnover. Next on the agenda for the Clippers is a trip to Detroit on Saturday. The Lakers will also hit the road on Saturday, as they pay a visit to the Warriors at Oracle Arena.

The Los Angeles Clippers rolled past the Phoenix Suns, 134 - 107, at Staples Center on Wednesday. The Suns (11 - 48) entered Wednesday's contest having lost 14 in a row, and it became apparent early in the game that their streak was going to continue. The Clippers (32 - 27) grabbed a quicklead and never looked back. LAC shot a blistering 60 percent in the win, taking advantage of Phoenix's 29th - ranked defense. As always, the Clippers relied heavily on their strong second unit in the win. LA's bench scored 70 points, with the tandem of Lou Williams and Montrezl Harrell doing much of the heavy lifting. Williams and Harrell contributed 49 points and 13 assists in the blowout win. LA also saw a 20 - point night from Danilo Gallinari, who was wildly efficient in just 19 minutes on the court. New Clipper Ivica Zubac also impressed, scoring 16 points to go with seven rebounds. Phoenix, meanwhile, saw a promising night from forward Kelly Oubre, who scored 28 points to lead the team. Star guard Devin Booker went cold in the loss, though, shooting just 2 - of - 10 en route to 10 points. Both teams will head into the All-Star break after Wednesday's lopsided contest.

The Los Angeles Clippers took down the Dallas Mavericks, 121 - 112, at Staples Center on Monday. Things started to look dicey for the Clippers (34 - 28) in the fourth quarter, as a pair of free - throws from Mavericks rookie Jalen Brunson brought Dallas to within two. Veteran guard Lou Williams, though, helped give LA some breathing room, knocking down a deep three to answer and following it with a quick assist to Montrezl Harrell. That put the Clippers up by seven, and LA was able to hang on comfortably until the final buzzer. Dallas (26 - 34) had some costly turnovers late in the game, including a pair from Luka Doncic, who lost possession nine times in total. It was another big night for Clippers big man Montrezl Harrell. Harrell, who set a career - high with 30 points last Friday, bested himself once again with 32 on Monday. The big man shot a staggering 14 - of - 17 from the field and finished with five assists. Williams, meanwhile, notched a double - double with 21 points, 10 assists, and no turnovers. For the Mavericks, Doncic tallied his fourth career triple - double despite committing nine turnovers. The rookie sensation led the team with 28 points. Dwight Powell added another 24, which he complemented with two blocks and two steals on the defensive end. On Wednesday, Dallas will host the Indiana Pacers while the Clippers will make a visit to Utah.

The Los Angeles Clippers defeated the New York Knicks, 128 - 107, at Staples Center on Sunday afternoon. Perhaps it was sluggishness brought about by the cross - country travel, but the Knicks (13 - 50) came out of the gates looking nothing like the team that had been much more competitive in recent games. The Clippers (36 - 29) were able to build an 18 - point first quarter lead that they had doubled up by halftime. With coach Doc Rivers letting his bench getting plenty of run in the second half, New York was much more competitive, but the outcome was naturally never in doubt. One of the visitors' biggest struggles came on the shooting front, as they drained just 40 percent of their attempts, including 38 percent from three - point range. Noah Vonleh and Damyean Dotson paced the Knicks with matching 17 - point tallies, with Vonleh notably adding 12 rebounds. New York's second unit managed a trio of 16 - point performances, with Emmanuel Mudiay, Allonzo Trier and MItchell Robinson all reaching the mark. Robinson also pulled down 13 rebounds and recorded another four blocks. Dennis Smith, Jr. turned in eight points, six assists, one rebound, two steals and one block. Landry Shamet paced the Clippers with 21 points, adding three rebounds. Danilo Gallinari supplied 20 points, seven rebounds and four assists. Montrezl Harrell and Lou Williams furnished 18 points apiece while posting five rebounds and six assists, respectively. JaMychal Green finished with 16 points, four rebounds and one block. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander tallied 15 points, four assists, three rebounds and one steal. The Knicks remain on their Western Conference swing and face the Sacramento Kings on Monday night, while the Clippers remain home but will serve as the visitors against the Los Angeles Lakers on Monday evening.

The Los Angeles Clippers defeated the visiting Oklahoma City Thunder, 118 - 110, at Staples Center on Friday evening. The Clippers got out to a good start at home, as they led for almost the entire first quarter, and took a 36 - 32 lead into the second. The score stayed close to start the second, with the Clippers leading by four at the halfway point. However, they rallied from there to build a 12 - point lead by halftime. The Thunder came out strong in the third and chipped away at the deficit, until they made it just a four - point game entering the final frame. The Thunder kept fighting and managed to tie it up at 101, with three minutes to go. However, Lou Williams came up clutch down the stretch, as he closed out a 40 - point performance to lead the Clippers to their fourth straight win. Williams led the Clippers with 40 points, seven rebounds, five assists and four steals, in 34 minutes. Danilo Gallinari followed up with 34 points, six rebounds and two assists, while Ivica Zubac chipped in 14 points, seven rebounds, two blocks, one steal and one assist. The Clippers shot 45 percent from the field, including 9 - of - 25 from deep. Meanwhile, Russell Westbrook led the Thunder with 32 points, eight rebounds, seven assists and one block, in 31 minutes. Paul George tallied 15 points, six rebounds and one assist, while Dennis Schroder added 15 points, four rebounds and four assists. The Thunder shot 40 percent from the field, including 11 - of - 44 from long range. The Thunder (40 - 26) will look to bounce back as they take on the Jazz in Utah on Monday. The Clippers (38 - 29) play host to the Celtics on Monday.

The Los Angeles Clippers blew out the Boston Celtics, 140 - 115, at Staples Center on Monday evening. Boston (41 - 27) entered Monday's tilt on the heels of three straight wins, but quickly fell behind against the Clippers (39 - 29). Los Angeles had one of its best offensive nights of the season, knocking down seemingly everything from every spot on the floor. The Clippers shot over 60 percent from the floor and saw seven double - digit scoring performances en route to the win. LA's big night was headlined by 34 points off the bench for sixth man Lou Williams. With his 29th point, Williams passed Dell Curry as the all - time leader in bench points in NBA history. Williams finished the historic night shooting 14 - of - 21 and added five assists. The Clippers saw another 25 points from Danilo Gallinari, who shot 9 - of - 12 from the floor and 4 - of - 5 from three - point range. As a team, LA went an impressive 13 - of - 28 from beyond the arc. Boston, meanwhile, had a relatively strong offensive performance itself. Terry Rozier led the team with 23 points off the bench, while Jaylen Brown pitched in 22. Nine of Brown's points came in the third quarter, where he knocked down three consecutive three - pointers. Overall, though, Boston could not keep up with LA's up - tempo offense, as the Celtics shot just 48 percent from the floor. Los Angeles will host the Portland Trail Blazers on Tuesday, while Boston will return home to face off with the Sacramento Kings on Thursday.

The Portland Trail Blazers defeated the Los Angeles Clippers, 125 - 104, at Staples Center on Tuesday. The hosting Clippers (39 - 30), who entered Tuesday's contest as winners of five in a row, maintained control of the game for all of the first half and majority of the third quarter before the Trail Blazers (41 - 26) managed to head into the final period with a one - point edge. Then, a Los Angeles team that was playing the second game of a back - to - back set appear to run out of gas, as Portland dominated the final period, 40 - 20, and walked away with a key victory with the playoffs not - so - far away. The Blazers pulled away on the back of C.J. McCollum, who after starting the game 0 - of - 7 from the field and scoring just five points in the first half, went on to score 30 points over the final 24 minutes for a game - high of 35 points in 35 minutes. He shot an impressive 6 - of - 11 from behind the arc and 12 - of - 21 from the field overall. With McCollum's shouldering much of the team's offensive workload, fellow backcourt star Damian Lillard took a backseat, but he still finished with 20 points and 12 assists across 34 minutes. Jusuf Nurkic added 20 points of his own to go along with 12 rebounds in just 25 minutes. As for the Clippers, Tuesday's defeat ended up being their first home loss since they dropped a game to the Lakers back on Jan. 31, so it was the end of an impressive run. After scoring a total of 74 points over his last two games, Lou Williams failed to bring the same offensive firepower Tuesday night, going just 5 - of - 16 from the field and scoring 18 points thanks to multiple trips to the free throw line. Montrezl Harrell wound up leading the team in scoring, posting a double - double of 22 points and 11 rebounds off the bench. As a team, Los Angeles shot an efficient 9 - of - 15 from behind the arc, but they only made to threes in the second half as they watched Portland pull away.

The Los Angeles Clippers defeated the visiting Chicago Bulls, 128 - 121, at Staples Center on Friday evening. The Bulls got out to a good start at home, with a 34 - 29 lead after one quarter. The Clippers applied some pressure in the second but could not make a dent in the deficit, as the Bulls took a six - point lead into halftime. However, the Clippers came out with a purpose in the third, where they outscored the visitors by 24, to take an 18 - point lead into the final frame. The Bulls were not done, as they rallied through the fourth, outscoring the Clippers 37 - 26, however, it was not enough to pull ahead, as the Clippers held on four their fourth win in their last five home games. Danilo Gallinari led the Clippers with 27 points, seven rebounds, two assists, a steal and a block, in 34 minutes. Montrezl Harrell followed up with 26 points, five rebounds, three blocks, two assists and one steal, while Shai Gilgeous-Alexander added 17 points seven rebounds, seven assists, three steals and one block. Meanwhile, Zach LaVine led the Bulls with 31 points, seven rebounds and seven assists, in 38 minutes. Robin Lopez followed up with 22 points, eight rebounds, three assists, three blocks and a steal, while Kris Dunn added 14 points, five rebounds, three assists and one block. The Bulls shot 52 percent from the field, including 11 - of - 21 from long range. The Bulls (19 - 51) will look to bounce back as they take on the Kings in Sacramento on Sunday. The Clippers (40 - 30) play host to the Nets on Sunday.

The Los Angeles Clippers edge out the Brooklyn Nets, 119 - 116, at Staples Center on Sunday evening. After picking up steam with a 37 - point second quarter, it seemed that the Clippers (41 - 30) had all but wrapped up the win after going up by 10 late in the fourth. The Nets (36 - 36), though, did not go down without a fight, going on a quick 100 run to tie the game with just 5 seconds remaining. Brooklyn was able to force the tie on an uncontested dunk from center Jarrett Allen, who broke free after the Clippers attempted to trap Brooklyn point guard D'Angelo Russell. Clippers' sixth man Lou Williams, though, quickly erased his team's mistake with a game - winning three - pointer on the other end. The buzzer - beater came from well beyond the arc and capped off a 25 - point night for Williams. In what has become a trend for the Clippers, their bench contributed to the win in a big way. LA saw 58 combined points from its second unit in the win, including another 20 - point performance from big man Montrezl Harrell. Veteran forward Danilo Gallinari led the starters with 21 points and a game - high 11 rebounds. Brooklyn, meanwhile, was led by an impressive performance from Russell. The All-Star contributed 32 points and 10 assists in the narrow loss. His play was complemented by strong play from DeMarre Carroll, who finished with 19 points and seven rebounds off the bench. The Nets will continue their road trip with a visit to Sacramento on Tuesday. Los Angeles, meanwhile, will play host to the Indiana Pacers.

The Los Angeles Clippers defeated the visiting Indiana Pacers, 115 - 109, at Staples Center on Tuesday. While this wasn't a wire - to - wire win for the Clippers, they held the lead for the final 46 minutes. It was a 25 - 16 first quarter that really set the tone, as a 34 - 26 third quarter was simply too much for Indiana to overcome. Turnovers were the difference in the game, with Los Angeles winning that battle, 20 - 13. That allowed the Clippers to win the points off turnover differential, 22 - 9. Los Angeles also did a ton of damage through transition, outscoring Indiana in fastbreak scoring, 19 - 6. The Pacers (44 - 28) were led by Bojan Bogdanovic, as he tallied 19 points, five rebounds and two assists. Myles Turner finished with 11 points, five rebounds, two assists and five blocks. Tyreke Evans was huge off the bench, providing 19 points, eight rebounds and seven assists. Domantas Sabonis also played well off the bench, amassing 13 points, 16 rebounds and six assists. The Clippers (42 - 30) were led by Danilo Gallinari, as he collected 24 points, two rebounds, three assists and two steals. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander totaled 17 points, three rebounds, three assists and two steals. Montrezl Harrell led the bench with 20 points, 12 rebounds, two assists and two steals. Lou Williams amassed 11 points and nine assists off the bench as well. The Pacers will continue their West Coast road trip on Thursday, as they travel to face the Golden State Warriors. As for the Clippers, they return to action on Friday in a road matchup versus the Cleveland Cavaliers.

The Los Angles Clippers defeated the visiting Cleveland Cavaliers, 132 - 108, at Staples Center on Saturday. Los Angeles came into this matchup as a monster favorite and they showed why in this dominating victory. They did most of their damage in the second and fourth quarters, outscoring the Cavaliers, 75 - 48. The shooting disparity was incredible, with Los Angeles shooting 62 percent from the field and 46 percent from three - point range while holding Cleveland to 45 percent from the field and 13 percent from long range. Rim protection was critical as well, with the Clippers winning the defensive rebounding battle, 35 - 22, while out - blocking them, 50. Los Angeles also out - assisted Cleveland, 33 - 18. The Cavaliers (19 - 58) were led by Collin Sexton, as he tallied 21 points, three rebounds and three assists. Cedi Osman accrued 19 points, five rebounds, three assists and four steals. Tristan Thompson amassed 10 points, 10 rebounds and three assists. Jordan Clarkson led the bench with 26 points on 11 - of - 16 from the field. The Clippers (46 - 31) were led by Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, as he tallied 22 points, two rebounds and eight assists. JaMychal Green totaled 18 points and 10 boards as a starter. Montrezl Harrell led the bench with 23 points, six rebounds and two assists. Lou Williams also played well off the bench, providing 18 points and six assists. Los Angeles has to play again on Sunday, as they play host to the Memphis Grizzlies. As for Cleveland, they return to action on Monday against the Phoenix Suns.

The Los Angeles Clippers beat the Memphis Grizzlies, 113 - 96, at Staples Center on Monday evening. The Clippers (47 - 31) jumped out to a quick 13 - 3 lead to start the game. That run set the tone, as LA led for 47 of the 48 minutes of gameplay. Memphis (31 - 46) struggled to find offense after missing all of its three - point attempts in the first quarter. LA was able to keep the foot on the gas pedal throughout due to strong play from its second unit. The Clippers' bench combined for 64 points in the win. Danilo Gallinari scored a game - high 27 to lead the Clippers. Gallinari also grabbed a season - high 15 rebounds. Off the bench, Montrezl Harrell contributed 20 points, while Lou Williams poured in another 17. After Sunday's blowout, the Clippers have picked up nine wins in their last 11 games. They currently share fifth place in the Western Conference with the Utah Jazz. Memphis, meanwhile, shot only 38 percent from the floor in the loss. Although the team struggled, Delon Wright turned in a nice performance. Wright finished with 20 points, eight rebounds, four assists, and three steals in 35 minutes of action. Memphis remains out of the Western Conference playoff picture and is currently sitting in 11th place in the West. Los Angeles will host the Houston Rockets on Wednesday, while Memphis will travel to Portland to take on the Trail Blazers

The Houston Rockets cruised past the Los Angeles Clippers, 135 - 103, at Staples Center on Wednesday evening. Just one night after blowing out Sacramento by 25 points, the Rockets (51 - 28) won by an even wider margin against Los Angeles (47 - 32). While the Rockets did not match their record - setting three - point barrage from Tuesday night, Houston did knock down a whopping 18 three - pointers en route to the win. It was a wildly efficient night for the Rockets, who shot over 53 percent from the field and 47 percent from three - point range. Houston jumped out to a double - digit lead in the first quarter and only cemented it with a commanding second half. James Harden was the team's leading scorer with 31 points. The Rockets' "big three "of Harden, Chris Paul, and Clint Capela combined to score 84 points, as Paul put up 29 points and seven assists while Capela finished with 24 points and 15 boards. Six Houston players scored in double figures in total. Rookie guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander led the Clippers with 20 points. LA was clearly outmatched from three - point range, making only eight shots from beyond the arc. The normally lights - out bench duo of Lou Williams and Montrezl Harrell had a relatively slow night, combining for just 27 points on 9 - of - 19 shooting. On Friday, Houston will host the New York Knicks while the Clippers will play the Lakers.

The Los Angeles Lakers defeated the host Los Angeles Clippers, 122 - 117, at Staples Center on Friday. In a battle of Los Angeles, it took 14 ties and 14 lead changes to determine a winner. In addition, neither team ever led by more than 12 points, as it came down to the final seconds. The Lakers rode a monster second half to victory, outscoring the Clippers, 61 - 50. Offensive rebounding was key for the Lakers, as they outrebounded the Clippers, 14 - 7. Three-point shooting was also critical, with the Lakers hitting 14 - of - 32 and the Clippers connecting on just 10 - of - 29 from long range. The Lakers (36 - 44) got a career performance from Alex Caruso, as he tallied 32 points, 10 rebounds, five assists and two steals. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope totaled 25 points, six rebounds, four assists and two steals. JaVale McGee amassed 18 points, 10 rebounds and three blocks while Rajon Rondo collected 15 points, six rebounds and 12 assists. The Clippers (47 - 33) were led by Danilo Gallinari, as he finished with 27 points, six rebounds, eight assists, three steals and two blocks. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander generated 20 points, eight rebounds and six assists. Lou Williams led the bench with 18 points, four rebounds and eight assists while Montrezl Harrell totaled 14 points, eight rebounds and four assists. Both teams return to action on Sunday, with the Lakers playing host to the Utah Jazz and the Clippers traveling as big underdogs to face the Golden State Warriors.

The Los Angeles Clippers took down the Utah Jazz, 143 - 137, at Staples Center in the final game of the 2018 - 19 NBA regular season on Wednesday. The two teams kept the season going a little longer, as Wednesday's tightly - contested game ended in overtime. Both teams exercised caution with their key players in anticipation of the playoffs. For Utah (50 - 32), regular starters Donovan Mitchell, Rudy Gobert, and Derrick Favors sat out the game for rest. Los Angeles (48 - 34), on the other hand, simply held all of its players to under 30 minutes on the court. The Clippers secured the win thanks to a strong OT period which featured six points from rookie guard Jerome Robinson. The Clippers saw 24 points from Montrezl Harrell to lead the team. Ivica Zubac recorded the team's only double - double, notching 11 rebounds to go with 22 points. The Clips also saw 15 points from veteran Lou Williams. For Utah, rookie Grayson Allen scored a whopping 40 points. Allen clearly had the green light on Wednesday, as he attempted a game - high 30 field goals in the loss. Utah also saw 24 points from Georges Niang. Both teams will be heading to the playoffs. Los Angeles will face the Golden State Warriors in the first round, while Utah will match up against the fourth - seeded Houston Rockets.

The Memphis Grizzlies defeated the Atlanta Hawks, 131 - 117, at FedEx Forum on Friday evening. The Grizzlies (1 - 1) shed their defensive - minded reputation in decisive fashion for their first win of the season, shooting 54 percent from the field, including 50 percent from three - point range. Memphis saw six players hit double digits in the scoring column, including 2018 first - round pick Jaren Jackson, Jr., who produced a bench - leading 24 points. The home squad set the tone with a 77 - point first half, allowing them to still notch a comfortable win despite the Hawks (0 - 2) outscoring them by a 56 - 54 margin in the second half. Taurean Prince paced the Hawks with 28 points, a total he supplemented with four rebounds, three assists and three steals. Rookie Trae Young followed with 20 points and added nine assists, two rebounds, one steal and one block. DeAndre' Bembry and Miles Plumlee co - led the bench with matching 12 - point tallies. Alex Len drew another start at center and finished with nine points, four rebounds and two assists. Garrett Temple led the Grizzlies with a game - high 30 points and also posted four rebounds, two assists, one steal and one block. Jackson added seven boards, two assists, two blocks and one steal to his aforementioned scoring total. Mike Conley provided a 16 - point, 11 - assist double - double that also included four rebounds. Marc Gasol shook off the back injury he entered the game with to muster 13 points, seven rebounds and five assists. The Hawks now head to Cleveland, where they'll take on the Cavaliers in a Sunday evening showdown. The Grizzlies are back in action Monday, when they'll take on the Utah Jazz in a road matchup.

The Memphis Grizzlies defeated the Phoenix Suns, 117 - 96, at FedEx Forum on Saturday night. The Grizzlies (3 - 2) had some solid momentum coming into Saturday's game, and they finished the contest even hotter than when they started. Memphis jumped on the Suns (1 - 4) early by building a 26 - 18 first - quarter lead, and they extended their advantage to 25 points by halftime. That essentially decided the contest, and the home squad closed things out in decisive fashion with a 30 - point fourth quarter. Both teams shot well overall, but the Grizzlies managed to coax 19 turnovers from the visitors while only committing 12 themselves. Deandre Ayton paced the Suns with 24 points, a total he supplemented with eight rebounds, five assists and one steal. Elie Okobo followed with 12 points and two assists. Isaiah Canaan and Jamal Crawford generated matching 11 - point tallies from the first unit and bench, respectively. Josh Jackson drew the start for Devin Booker (hamstring) and turned in eight points, three rebounds, three assists and three steals. Marc Gasol led the Grizzlies with 19 points and added eight rebounds, three assists and three steals. Mike Conley registered 18 points, seven assists and two steals. Garrett Temple managed 15 points, three rebounds, one assist and one steal. MarShon Brooks led the bench with 18 points, while Wayne Selden contributed 14. The Suns remain on the road and battle the Oklahoma City Thunder on Sunday evening, while the Grizzlies are home again versus the Washington Wizards on Tuesday evening.

The Memphis Grizzlies defeated the visiting Washington Wizards, 107 - 95, at FedEx Forum on Tuesday. There was only one tie and one lead change in this matchup, as Memphis controlled the game throughout the second half. In fact, the Grizzlies led by 19 points at times in the second half, as the Grizzlies started the third quarter on an 18 - 1 run while finishing the game on a 21 - 13 spurt. Defense was key for Memphis, as they forced 20 turnovers from Washington, thanks to 16 recorded steals. Bench production was also huge for the Grizzlies, as they outscored the Wizards bench, 40 - 30. Much of Memphis' offense came down low, as they outscored Washington in the paint, 44 - 30. The Wizards (1 - 6) were led by John Wall, as he collected 22 points, five rebounds, seven assists and three steals. Bradley Beal finished with 17 points, three rebounds, seven assists, two steals and three blocks. Those two did combine for 13 turnovers though. Otto Porter Jr. amassed 15 points, six rebounds and three assists. Kelly Oubre Jr. led the bench with 16 points, two boards and two steals. The Grizzlies (4 - 2) got an all - around gem out of Marc Gasol, as he accumulated 19 points, five rebounds, six assists and five steals. Garrett Temple led the team in scoring, generating 20 points and seven boards. Mike Conley accrued 19 points, three rebounds and seven assists. Kyle Anderson scored just five points but provided 11 rebounds, three assists and four steals. Shelvin Mack scored 14 points and handed out eight dimes, with almost all of that production coming in the second half. Both teams return to action on Friday, with Memphis traveling to play the Utah Jazz and Washington playing host to the Oklahoma City Thunder.

The Memphis Grizzlies defeated the Denver Nuggets, 89 - 87, at FedExForum on Wednesday. The Grizzlies managed to win Wednesday's game by making sure the game was played at their style, which is in a slow, grind - it - out fashion. Despite falling behind early, Memphis managed to chip away and take a lead at halftime thanks to a 28 - 18 second quarter. From there, the score went back and forth, but some timely shots from Mike Conley and Marc Gasol helped ice the game for the home team. Conley struggled for the most part, scoring just four points on 2 - of - 9 shooting, but one of those shots was a timely floater that put the team up four late. Gasol, on the other hand posted a double - double of 20 points, including the game - winning free throws, and 12 rebounds in 36 minutes. The most impressive performance, however, may have come from rookie Jaren Jackson Jr., who has had a stellar start to his first NBA season. Jackson terrific on offense with 20 points and seven rebounds in 33 minutes, but he was even better on the defensive end, where he recorded three steals and three blocked shots. As for the Nuggets, the loss put an end to their five - game winning streak, and it came on the back of a very poor defensive effort. As a team, the Nuggets shot just 25 percent from behind the arc and 39 percent from the field overall. Star big man Nikola Jokic hardly made a contribution to those percentages, as he attempted just one shot in 26 minutes, and it was the final shot of the game, which was a potential game - winning three. Jokic finished with just four points thanks to a pair of trips to the free throw line. Gary Harris led the team in scoring with 20 points, while Jamal Murray shot a poor 6 - of - 21 from the field en route to scoring 15 points in 37 minutes.

The Memphis Grizzlies defeated the Philadelphia 76ers, 112 - 106, in overtime at FedEx Forum on Saturday evening. The 76ers (8 - 6) had played far from their best on the road in the early going of the season, but they came out of the gates seemingly determined to change that Saturday. Philadelphia forged a 63 - 50 halftime advantage over the Grizzlies (7 - 4), who hadn't lost in their first four games on their home floor. However, Memphis bounced back with its trademark defense in the second half, limiting the Sixers to 17 points in the third quarter and 22 in the fourth. That gave them enough to chip away at their double - digit deficit, and a Garrett Temple 24 - foot three - pointer with 40 seconds remaining knotted the game at 102 - 102. With both Joel Embiid and Marc Gasol missing potential game - winning shots, the contest went into overtime. In the extra period, Conley scored the final four points with a floating jumper and a pair of free throws to clinch the hard - fought win. J.J. Redick led the way for the Sixers with 20 points, and he added one assist. Ben Simmons followed with an 18 - point, 14 - rebound double - double that also included five assists and one block. T.J. McConnell filled out the stat sheet off the bench with 16 points, seven assists, three rebounds, one steal and one block. Embiid generated a 14 - point, 16 - rebound double - double that also included five assists, one steal and one block. Markelle Fultz matched Embiid's scoring total. Conley paced the Grizzlies with 32 points, a total he supplemented with six assists, four rebounds, two steals and one block. Gasol followed with an 18 - point, 12 - rebound double - double that also included six assists and two steals. Temple poured in 17 points, while Shelvin Mack and MarShon Brooks tallied 12 and 11 points, respectively. The Sixers next pay a visit to the Miami Heat on Monday, while the Grizzlies remain home and take on the Utah Jazz on Monday evening as well.

The Utah Jazz defeated the host Memphis Grizzlies, 96 - 88, at FedEx Forum on Monday evening. The Jazz got out to a great start on the road, as they led, 13 - 2, halfway through the first quarter. However, the Grizzlies did eventually wake up and managed to trail just, 20 - 16, heading into the second. The Grizzlies stayed with it in the second, outscoring the Jazz, 27 - 20, to take a, 43 - 40, lead into halftime. The Grizz were able to hang on to the edge to start the third, but the Jazz made a push, as they closed the quarter on an, 18 - 7 run, to claim a 74 - 69 advantage, entering the final frame. The Jazz stayed in control from there, as they did not let the Grizzlies get closer than a two - point deficit, before they pushed the lead back up to 10 in the final minutes. This marks the third straight win for the Jazz, as well as their fifth road win of the season. Joe Ingles led Utah with 19 points, six rebounds, five assists and one steal, in 36 minutes. Rudy Gobert followed up with 15 points, 16 rebounds, three blocks and two assists, while Derrick Favors and Donovan Mitchell chipped in 12 points each. The Jazz shot 39 percent from the field, including 9 - of - 32 from long range. Meanwhile, Mike Conley led the Grizzlies with 24 points, four rebounds and three assists, in 35 minutes. Marc Gasol tallied 16 points, five rebounds, three assists, two blocks and a steal, while Jaren Jackson Jr. tallied 10 points, 11 rebounds, five blocks, three assists and one steal. The Grizzlies shot 42 percent from the field, including just 4 - of - 24 from long range. The Grizzlies (7 - 5) will look to bounce back as they take on the Bucks in Milwaukee on Wednesday. The Jazz (7 - 6) take on the Mavericks in Dallas on Wednesday.

The Memphis Grizzlies defeated the visiting Sacramento Kings, 112 - 104, at FedEx Forum on Friday. While the final scoreline shows a close game, Memphis held the lead for all but a few minutes. The second quarter played a big part of that, with the Grizzlies outscoring the Kings, 33 - 23. Memphis actually held the lead for the entirety of the second half, as Sacramento never got the game within a four - point margin from there. The Grizzlies ended up shooting 51 percent from the field and 44 percent from three - point range while holding the Kings to 46 percent from the field and 36 percent from long range. Memphis also dominated the turnover differential, forcing 21 turnovers from Sacramento while committing just 13 on their end. The Grizzlies also dominated down low, outscoring the Kings in the paint, 54 - 42. The Kings (8 - 7) got another gem out of De'Aaron Fox, as he tallied 23 points, four rebounds, 10 assists and two steals. Buddy Hield finished with 16 points, four rebounds, three assists and two steals. Willie Cauley-Stein accrued 11 points, eight rebounds, two assists and three steals. Bogdan Bogdanovic led the bench with 12 points, two rebounds and two assists. The Grizzlies (9 - 5) leading scorer was Jaren Jackson Jr., as he collected 27 points, six rebounds, four steals and two blocks on 11 - of - 16 from the field. Mike Conley accumulated 19 points, three rebounds and six assists. Marc Gasol generated 19 points, 15 rebounds and two assists. Garret Temple totaled 14 points, five rebounds, two assists and three steals. On deck for Sacramento is a road matchup versus the Houston Rockets on Saturday. As for Memphis, they return to action on Sunday when they face the Minnesota Timberwolves on the road as well.

The Memphis Grizzlies defeated the Dallas Mavericks, 98 - 88, at FedEx Forum on Monday evening. The Grizzlies (11 - 5) have gotten off to a strong start this season thanks in large part to the return to health of star point guard Mike Conley, and they've been especially dominant at home. That much was evident again Monday, as Memphis utilized a final - quarter defensive push to limit the Mavericks (7 - 9) to just 14 points over the final 12 minutes. As has often been the case this season, Conley's efforts were key to the victory, as he led all scorers with 28 points. The Grizzlies also limited Dallas to just 34 percent shooting. Dennis Smith, Jr. led the Mavericks with 19 points, which he supplemented with five assists, three rebounds and two steals. DeAndre Jordan generated a 17 - point, 20 - rebound double - double. Luka Doncic tallied 15 points, 10 rebounds, three assists and one block. Dorian Finney-Smith managed 13 points, three rebounds, two steals and one block. Harrison Barnes poured in 10 points. Conley also dished out seven assists, hauled in five rebounds and recorded two steals. Marc Gasol contributed a 17 - point, 15 - rebound double - double that also included four assists, four blocks and one steal. Jaren Jackson, Jr. filled out the stat sheet with 13 points, three rebounds, two assists, four blocks and two steals.
