The New York Knicks defeated the host Memphis Grizzlies, 103 - 98, at FedEx Forum on Sunday evening. The Grizzlies got out to a good start at home, as they took a, 26 - 21, lead after one quarter. They kept the pressure on in the second, and outscored the Knicks, 26 - 22, in the quarter, to take a, 52 - 43, lead into halftime. The Knicks turned the tide in the third quarter, as they poured in 35 points in the quarter, to form a seven - point, 78 - 71, lead heading into the final frame. The Grizzlies came out with a purpose in the fourth and managed to tie it up at 89 with about four minutes left. They then grabbed a one - point lead, but the Knicks would not back down, as they rallied again, starting with an and - one dunk from Emmanuel Mudiay, followed by 6 - of - 6 free - throw shooting, which clinched the impressive road win. This marks the third straight win of the Knicks, and the second straight loss for the Grizzlies. Enes Kanter came up huge for the Knicks, with 21 points, 26 rebounds and three assists, in 40 minutes. Tim Hardaway Jr. finished with 22 points on 6 - of - 16 shooting, in 38 minutes, while Emmanuel Mudiay tallied 17 points, four assists, two rebounds, one steal and a block. The Knicks shot 37 percent from the field, including 8 - of - 22 from long range. Meanwhile, Marc Gasol led the Grizzlies with 27 points, eight rebounds, five blocks, four assists and two steals, in 39 minutes. Mike Conley tallied 23 points, 11 assists, four rebounds and one steal, while Jaren Jackson Jr. chipped in 16 points, six rebounds, seven blocks and three assists. The Grizzlies (12 - 7) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Raptors on Tuesday. The Knicks (7 - 14) take on the Pistons in Detroit on Tuesday.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the Memphis Grizzlies, 122 - 114, at FedEx Forum on Tuesday night. The Grizzlies (12 - 8) have been especially impressive at home this season and appear to have their defense back to elite status, so the Raptors (18 - 4) undoubtedly faced an uphill climb for a road victory. Things looked somewhat bleak in the first half as well, as Memphis built a 12 - point halftime lead. However, the light went on for Toronto at intermission, as they racked up 63 points over the final 24 minutes while limiting their hosts to just 43. The Raptors got it done with red - hot shooting, as they drained 61 percent of their attempts, including 54 percent from three - point range. Kyle Lowry paced Toronto with 24 points and added six assists and two rebounds. Fred VanVleet followed with a bench - leading 18 points. Kawhi Leonard produced a 17 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included five assists, two steals and one block. Serge Ibaka supplied 16 points, three boards, two assists and one block. Danny Green poured in 14 points, while Pascal Siakam turned in 10 points, six boards, four assists and one block. Marc Gasol led the Grizzlies with 27 points, a total he supplemented with four rebounds, four assists, two steals and two blocks. Mike Conley provided 20 points, six assists, five rebounds, three steals and two blocks. Kyle Anderson and JaMychal Green each turned in 13 - point efforts, along with five and seven rebounds, respectively. Garrett Temple managed 12 points, four rebounds, four assists and one steal. Omri Casspi and Shelvin Mack had matching 10 - point tallies off the bench. The Raptors return home for a Thursday night showdown with the Golden State Warriors, while the Grizzlies head to the Big Apple for a Friday night battle with the Brooklyn Nets.

The Memphis Grizzlies defeated the visiting Los Angeles Clippers, at FedEx Forum on Wednesday evening. The Grizzlies got out to a great start at home, as they outscored the visitors, 27 - 15, through the first quarter. The Grizz kept the heat on in the second, where they pushed their lead to 16 at the halfway point, however, the Clippers did not back down, and managed to cut the deficit to nine points by halftime. The Clippers carried the energy into the third and used an 110 run to take a one - point lead with 7:50 left in the quarter. The Grizzlies held their ground from there, as the teams went into the fourth tied at 69. The Grizzlies took an edge early in the fourth and slowly built a nine - point lead, with seven minutes left in the contest. They held strong from there, to earn their eighth home win. Mike Conley led the Grizzlies with 22 points, seven rebounds, four assists, two steals and two blocks, in 34 minutes. JaMychal Green followed up with 19 points, 11 rebounds, two steals and one assist, in 28 minutes off the bench. Jaren Jackson Jr. added 13 points, six rebounds and one block. The Grizzlies shot 44 percent from the field, including 7 - of - 28 from long range. Meanwhile, Boban Marjanovic led the Clippers with 19 points, eight rebounds, one assist and one steal, in 13 minutes off the bench. Danilo Gallinari followed up with 17 points, five rebounds, two assists and one steal, in 33 minutes. Lou Williams added 12 point and seven assists, in 25 minutes off the bench. The Clippers (16 - 8) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Heat on Saturday. The Grizzlies (14 - 9) take on the Pelicans in New Orleans on Friday.

The Los Angeles Lakers defeated the Memphis Grizzlies, 111 - 88, at FedEx Forum on Saturday evening. The Lakers (16 - 10) were presumably a bit on the spent side after a hard - fought loss to the Spurs on Friday, which was followed by a late - night trip into Memphis. Rookie Sviatoslav Mykhailiuk offered 11 points off the bench. JaVale McGee posted a 10 - point, 10 - rebound double - double. Wayne Selden, Jr. paced the Grizzlies with 17 points off the bench. He supplemented them with five rebounds, four assists, two steals and one block. Mike Conley totaled 12 points, three assists, one rebound and four steals. Marc Gasol managed 11 points, six rebounds, three assists, two blocks and one steal. Jaren Jackson, Jr. matched Gasol's scoring total and added eight boards. Garrett Temple poured in nine points. The Lakers head back home to face the Miami Heat on Monday night, while the Grizzlies pay a visit to the Denver Nuggets on Monday evening as well.

The Memphis Grizzlies defeated the visiting Portland Trail Blazers, 92 - 83, at FedEx Forum on Wednesday. While there were only three ties and three lead changes in this game, it was tight until a late run by the Grizzlies. In fact, Memphis scored 13 unanswered points in the final five minutes, as that turned a one - point lead into a 14 - point margin with 80 seconds remaining. Portland did score the final five points to cut it to a single - digit margin but that 130 run was simply too much to overcome. The Grizzlies defense was critical, as they held the Blazers to 37 percent from the field and 27 percent from three - point range. Memphis also dominated down low, winning the rebounding differential. 51 - 44, while outscoring Portland in the paint, 40 - 28. Bench production was also huge for the Grizzlies, as they outscored the Trail Blazers bench, 38 - 15. The Trail Blazers (15 - 13) got a season - high 40 points from C.J. McCollum, as he also provided five rebounds and two assists on 16 - of - 27 from the field. Damian Lillard went just 4 - of - 18 from the field to amass 14 points, seven rebounds, three assists and two steals. Jusuf Nurkic scored just two points on 1 - of - 15 shooting but accrued 10 rebounds, two steals and three blocks. The Grizzlies (16 - 11) were led by Mike Conley, as he tallied 23 points, six rebounds and six assists. Jaren Jackson Jr. finished with 14 points, six rebounds, two assists and two blocks. MarShon Brooks and JaMychal Green both reached double figures in scoring off the bench, combining for 25 points. Both teams play home games on Friday for their next outing, with Memphis welcoming the Miami Heat and Portland playing host to the Toronto Raptors.

The Miami Heat defeated the host Memphis Grizzlies, 100 - 97, at FedEx Forum on Friday. This game was competitive throughout, as it took six ties and 11 lead changes to determine a winner. In fact, neither team led by more than 11 points, as it was within a seven - point margin for the entirety of the second half. Jaren Jackson Jr. tallied 15 points, four rebounds and two steals while Marc Gasol finished with 14 points, seven rebounds and five assists. The Houston Rockets defeated the Memphis Grizzlies, 105 - 97, at FedEx Forum on Saturday night. The Rockets (14 - 14) came into the contest looking to continue building on their recent momentum, one that had seen them notch three straight victories. James Harden led the way for the Rockets with a 32 - point, 12 - rebound, 10 - assist triple - double that also included two steals. Clint Capela posted a 26 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also featured a pair of blocks. Gerald Green poured in 17 points to lead the bench. P.J. Tucker posted 14 points and seven rebounds. Chris Paul put up 10 points and dished out 10 assists. Mike Conley paced the Grizzlies with 22 points, a total he supplemented with six assists and two rebounds. Marc Gasol posted a near double - double with 17 points, nine rebounds, four assists and three steals. JaMychal Green totaled 13 points, six boards and three assists. The Memphis Grizzlies defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 95 - 87, at FedEx Forum on Wednesday evening. The Grizzlies (18 - 16) set a dominant tone early, outscoring the Cavaliers (8 - 27) by a 21 - 9 margin through the first 12 minutes. The next three periods were much more competitive, but Memphis was able to withstand a late Cleveland run that saw them get as close as 86 - 82 with 1:19 remaining. The Grizzlies got it done with their trademark suffocating defense, limiting the Cavs to 36 percent shooting and forcing 16 turnovers from them. Jordan Clarkson led the Cavaliers with 24 points in 31 minutes off the bench. He added five rebounds, two assists and three steals. Collin Sexton managed 16 points, six assists, five rebounds and one steal. Osman supplied 10 points and seven boards. Ante Zizic drew the start at center and contributed six points, 11 rebounds and two assists. Larry Nance, Jr. matched Zizic's scoring and also hauled in nine rebounds, dished out three assists and recorded two steals. Marc Gasol paced the Grizzlies with 20 points and also posted nine rebounds, six assists, four blocks and one steal. Mike Conley registered 15 points, eight assists, two rebounds and two steals. Kyle Anderson matched Conley's scoring total and also totaled three rebounds, three assists, three steals and two blocks. Garrett Temple and Jaren Jackson, Jr. pitched in matching 11 - point tallies. The Cavaliers remain on the road and take on the Miami Heat on Friday night, while the Grizzlies remain home and tangle with the Boston Celtics on Saturday night.

The Boston Celtics defeated the Memphis Grizzlies, 112 - 103, at FedEx Forum on Saturday evening. The game was ultimately a tale of two halves, with the Celtics (21 - 14) ultimately prevailing in the one that mattered most. After a tightly contested first quarter that ended with the Grizzlies (18 - 17) trailing by a 29 - 26 score, Memphis roared back to take a 64 - 47 halftime lead. However, the second half was all Boston, as they outscored their hosts by a 65 - 39 margin. The offense was heavily concentrated for the visitors among the trio of Kyrie Irving, Marcus Morris and Al Horford. The Celtics enjoyed a strong shooting night overall, draining 50 percent of their attempts, including 44 percent from three - point range. Irving paced the Celtics with a 26 - point, 13 - assist double - double that also included four rebounds and one steal. Morris followed with 22 points and four rebounds. The Atlanta Hawks defeated the visiting Miami Heat, 106 - 82, at State Farm Arena on Sunday evening. The Hawks got out to a good start at home, as they took a 23 - 16 lead after one quarter. The Heat shot 36 percent from the field, including 5 - of - 34 from long range. The Heat (19 - 19) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Nuggets on Tuesday. The Hawks (12 - 27) take on the Raptors in Toronto on Tuesday.

The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the host Atlanta Hawks, 133 - 114, at State Farm Arena on Sunday. John Collins finished with 13 points, 11 rebounds and four assists while Alex Len led the bench with 12 points and eight rebounds. Both teams return to action on Tuesday, with Milwaukee playing host to the surging Miami Heat and Atlanta welcoming the Oklahoma City Thunder to State Farm Arena.

The Atlanta Hawks defeated the visiting Oklahoma City Thunder, 142 - 126, at State Farm Arena on Tuesday. On deck for Oklahoma City is a home matchup versus the lackadaisical Los Angeles Lakers on Thursday. As for Atlanta, they return to action on Saturday against the Boston Celtics.

The Boston Celtics defeated the Atlanta Hawks, 113 - 105, at State Farm Arena on Saturday night. The Toronto Raptors defeated the Atlanta Hawks, 119 - 101, at Phillips Arena on Thursday. Dewayne Dedmon was the only other Hawks player to score in double figures with 10 points in 24 minutes.

The Orlando Magic defeated the host Atlanta Hawks, 124 - 108, at State Farm Arena on Sunday evening. The contest got out to a competitive start, as the Magic led 26 - 25 after one quarter. The Atlanta Hawks defeated the visiting Los Angeles Lakers, 117 - 113, at State Farm Arena on Tuesday. In a battle between two of the fastest paced teams in the league, this ended up being a barnburner. Atlanta did almost all their damage in the first and third quarters, outscoring Los Angeles, 73 - 58. While the Hawks didn't dominate any statistic, they won the field goal percentage, three - point percentage, free - throw shooting, rebounds and assists differentials all by slim margins. As for Atlanta, they play host to the New York Knicks on Thursday for their final game before the break.

The New York Knicks defeated the host Atlanta Hawks, 106 - 91, at State Farm Arena on Thursday evening. The Knicks got out to a great start on the road, with a 28 - 13 lead after one quarter. The Hawks responded in the second, as they outscored the visitors by 12 in the quarter, to cut the deficit to three points by halftime. The Knicks pushed their lead to double digits in the final frame and went on to earn their first win after an 18 - game losing streak. The Knicks (11 - 47) play host to the Timberwolves on February 22nd.

The Detroit Pistons defeated the Atlanta Hawks, 125 - 122, at State Farm Arena on Friday evening. The Pistons (27 - 30) enjoyed plenty of offensive success in the first half, but it still wasn't enough to keep up with the hot - shooting Hawks (19 - 40). Atlanta impressively racked up 70 points over the first 24 minutes, good for a two - point halftime lead. However, when Detroit built a seven - point third - quarter lead, it appeared that they might be on their way to a comfortable victory, even after losing All-Star forward Blake Griffin to ejection during the period. The hosts would persevere, though, and even held a five - point lead with just 1:53 remaining. The Pistons would finish on a 10 - 2 run from that point forward, with Thon Maker's 23 - foot three - point jumper at the 17 - second mark the difference in the contest. Trae Young led the Hawks with a 30 - point, 10 - assist double - double that also included two rebounds. John Collins tallied 19 points, six rebounds and one block. Vince Carter delivered 16 points. Dewayne Dedmon generated a 14 - point, 12 - rebound double - double that also included two assists, three blocks and one steal. Kent Bazemore poured in 12 points and also posted seven boards and two steals. DeAndre' Bembry produced an efficient 10 points, four rebounds, two assists and two steals. The Pistons remain on the road and face off with the Miami Heat on Saturday night, while the Hawks remain home to tangle with the Phoenix Suns on Saturday evening as well.

The Atlanta Hawks defeated the visiting Phoenix Suns, 120 - 112, at State Farm Arena on Saturday night. The contest got out to a tight start, as the Suns and Hawks played each other to a standstill in the first quarter, pouring in 33 points each. The score stayed tight through the second, while the Hawks and Suns exchanged leads. until the Hawks stood on top with a four - point lead at halftime. Deandre Ayton tallied 14 points, 12 rebounds, one steal and one block, while Devin Booker finished with 26 points, eight assists, seven rebounds and one block. The Suns shot 44 percent from the field, including 13 - of - 37 from long range The Suns (11 - 50) will look to bounce back as they take on the Heat in Miami on Monday. The Hawks (20 - 40) take on the Rockets in Houston on Monday.

The Atlanta Hawks defeated the Minnesota Timberwolves, 131 - 123, in overtime at State Farm Arena on Wednesday evening. The Hawks (21 - 41) didn't exactly have the look of a sharp team through the first three quarters, as they entered the final 12 minutes trailing the Timberwolves (29 - 32) by a 95 - 86 margin. Dewayne Dedmon contributed seven points, 10 rebounds, three assists and one block. The Timberwolves next pay a visit to the Indiana Pacers on Thursday night, while the Hawks remain home to tangle with the Chicago Bulls on Friday evening.

The Chicago Bulls defeated the host Atlanta Hawks in quadruple - overtime, 168 - 161, at State Farm Arena on Friday. The end of regulation was most exciting, as Trae Young hit a three - pointer with two seconds left to take break a tied game. Free-throw shooting was the critical difference, with the Bulls connecting on 35 - of - 48 and the Hawks hitting 17 - of - 25. Lauri Markkanen totaled 31 points, 17 rebounds, two assists and two blocks while Robin Lopez amassed 11 points, 11 rebounds and three blocks. Taurean Prince finished with 17 points, three rebounds, four assists and two steals. Dewayne Dedmon accrued 14 points, 12 rebounds and four blocks. Alex Len led the bench with 24 points and 10 rebounds. Both these teams will be off until Sunday, as they ironically have a rematch in Chicago.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the host Atlanta Hawks, 111 - 104, at State Farm Arena on Wednesday. As for Atlanta, they return to action on Saturday when they play host to the Brooklyn Nets,

The Brooklyn Nets defeated the Atlanta Hawks, 114 - 112, at State Farm Arena on Saturday night. The Atlanta Hawks defeated the New Orleans Pelicans, 128 - 116, at State Farm Arena on Sunday evening. The Atlanta Hawks defeated the visiting Memphis Grizzlies, 132 - 111, at State Farm Arena on Wednesday evening.
