The Houston Rockets defeated the Atlanta Hawks, 121 - 105, at State Farm Arena on Tuesday evening. While Atlanta (24 - 48) hung tight for much of the game, Houston (45 - 26) ultimately gained an edge thanks to its superior offensive play. After knocking down 21 three - pointers in their last outing, the Rockets impressed with another 19 makes from deep in Tuesday's win. For the second straight game, too, both James Harden and Chris Paul tallied double digits in the assist column. Everything seemed to be going right for the Rockets, making it difficult for the Hawks to keep up despite their 15 made three - pointers. On top of his 10 assists, Harden scored a game - high 31 points. With that, Harden is the first player since Michael Jordan in 1987 to score 30 points against every team in a single season. It was just another notch in the belt of an already historic season for Harden, who is leading the league in scoring at 36 points per game. The Rockets also saw 26 points and 11 rebounds from Clint Capela. Danuel House pitched in another 19 points in a true top - to - bottom effort for the surging team. Budding star Trae Young led the way for Atlanta, scoring 21 points while dishing out 12 assists. It was Young's fourth straight game scoring 20 or more. John Collins added another 20 points and 10 rebounds for the Hawks. Houston faces the second half of a back - to - back as it visits Memphis on Wednesday. The Hawks, meanwhile, will host the Utah Jazz on Thursday.

The Atlanta Hawks defeated the visiting Utah Jazz, 117 - 114, at State Farm Arena on Thursday evening. The contest got out to a competitive start, as the teams traded the lead through the first quarter, before the Hawks took a 29 - 28 lead into the second. The Hawks turned it up in the second, as they started the quarter on a 13 - 5 run. The Hawks led for the entire quarter and took an 11 - point lead into halftime. The Jazz turned the tables in the third quarter, as they rallied to tie it up at 71, halfway through the quarter. The Jazz went on to outscore the Hawks by 16 points in the quarter, to take a five - point lead into the fourth. The Hawks started chipping away to start the fourth and made it a one - point game with just over seven minutes to go. The Jazz responded and pulled ahead by a couple of possessions, however, the Hawks outscored the visitors 19 - 8 through the final five minutes, to snap a three - game losing streak. For the Jazz, it marks the end of a five - game winning streak. Trae Young led the Hawks with 23 points, 11 assists and two rebounds, in 34 minutes. Dewayne Dedmon followed up with 18 points, nine rebounds, three blocks and two assists, while Kevin Heurter added 14 points, two assists and a rebound. The Hawks shot 47 percent from the field, including 19 - of - 40 from long range. Meanwhile, Donovan Mitchell led the Jazz with 34 points, four rebounds, two assists, two blocks and a steal, in 35 minutes. Derrick Favors added 15 points, 15 rebounds, two steals, a block and an assist, while Ricky Rubio tallied 17 points, seven assists, five rebounds and two steals. The Jazz shot 43 - of - 94 from the field, including 10 - of - 32 from deep. The Jazz (42 - 30) will look to bounce back as they take on the Bulls in Chicago on Saturday. The Hawks (25 - 48) play host to the 76ers on Saturday.

The Atlanta Hawks defeated the Philadelphia 76ers, 129 - 127, at State Farm Arena on Saturday night. A game with all the potential to turn into a scoreboard - busting affair started to live up to the hype from the opening tip. The 76ers (47 - 26) and Hawks (26 - 48) combined for 75 points in the first quarter alone, and it was Atlanta that owned a 74 - 68 halftime lead. Philadelphia erased that deficit in the third quarter, fittingly sending what would be a wire - to - wire battle tied into the final period. The game continued as a see - saw affair until Trae Young clinched the win by draining a running floater with 0 seconds remaining for the victory. Joel Embiid led the way for the 76ers with a 25 - point, 12 - rebound double - double that also included two assists. Ben Simmons and Jimmy Butler contributed matching 17 - point efforts. Simmons added nine assists, six rebounds, four steals and two blocks, while Butler provided six boards, four assists, one steal and one block. Tobias Harris turned in 13 points, nine rebounds, two assists and one block. J.J. Redick poured in 12 points and added two assists and one rebound. Michael Scott furnished nine points and eight rebounds. Young paced the Hawks with a 26 - point, 11 - assist double - double that included six rebounds and one block. Taurean Prince tallied 21 points, five rebounds, three assists and one steal. Dewayne Dedmon delivered 17 points, eight rebounds, one assist and one steal. Alex Len managed 14 points, four rebounds, one assist and one block. John Collins contributed 11 points, eight boards, two assists, two blocks and one steal. The 76ers next pay a visit to the Orlando Magic on Monday night, while the Hawks head to the Big Easy to face the New Orleans Pelicans on Tuesday evening.

The Portland Trail Blazers defeated the Atlanta Hawks, 118 - 98, at State Farm Arena on Friday evening. The Trail Blazers (48 - 27) haven't been anywhere near the same team on the road this season, but early indications Friday were that things would be different versus the Hawks (27 - 49). Portland amassed 60 first - half points and held a nine - point advantage at halftime. Their steady play throughout the second half ensured Atlanta would be kept at bay, as the visitors tacked 11 more points onto their lead over the final two periods. The Blazers' most impressive edge may have been on the boards, as they out - rebounded the home squad by a 55 - 41 margin. Damian Lillard led the way for the Trail Blazers with 36 points, adding seven assists and three rebounds. Al-Farouq Aminu generated a 17 - point, 11 - rebound double - double that also included two assists and a block. Enes Kanter furnished 14 points, eight rebounds and one block. Seth Curry poured in 12 points to lead the bench. Jake Layman and Zach Collins posted matching nine - point tallies, with Collins also hauling in nine boards. Trae Young paced the Hawks with 26 points, supplmenting them with nine rebounds, seven assists and one steal. John Collins collected 20 points, three assists, two rebounds and two blocks. Kyle Huerter totaled 11 points, four rebounds and four assists. Vince Carter led the second unit with nine points and also brought down three rebounds and recorded one steal. The Trail Blazers next pay a visit to the Detroit Pistons on Saturday night, while the Hawks remain home and tangle with the Milwaukee Bucks on Sunday afternoon.

The Atlanta Hawks defeated the Milwaukee Bucks, 136 - 135, in overtime at State Farm Arena on Sunday afternoon. The record doesn't show it, but the Hawks (28 - 49) are one of the NBA's most improved teams during the latter portion of the season and have given plenty of postseason contenders fits along the way. Therefore, it wasn't exactly surprising to see Atlanta answer a 43 - 26 thrashing by the Bucks (57 - 20) after one quarter by erasing 14 points off their deficit in the second. The home squad then entered the final period with a slim one - point advantage, but were down by a 114 - 104 margin with 6:53 remaining. The Hawks then finished on a 18 - 8 run capped off by an Alex Len three - pointer with 20 seconds left in regulation to force overtime. In the extra period, Trae Young came through in the clutch once again, draining a jumper at the buzzer for the one - point win. Sterling Brown led the way for the Bucks with 27 points, adding nine rebounds, three assists, three steals and one block. Tim Frazier stepped up with a 20 - point, 15 - assist double - double that also included seven rebounds and one steal. Brook Lopez provided 19 points, six rebounds, three assists and one steal. George Hill led the bench with 18 points and added six rebounds, one assist and one block. Patrick Connaughton posted a 15 - point, 12 - rebound double - double, while Bonzie Colson contributed 15 points, 16 rebounds, two assists, one steal and one block. D.J. Wilson turned in 12 points, seven rebounds and five assists. Justin Anderson paced the Hawks with 24 points, adding 12 rebounds, three assists and two steals. John Collins and Len had matching 23 - point tallies, with Collins notably hauling in 12 boards. DeAndre' Bembry managed 16 points, six rebounds, three assists, three steals and one block. Young managed just 12 points but dished out 16 assists, brought down five rebounds and recorded two steals. The Bucks remain on the road and visit the Brooklyn Nets on Monday night, while the Hawks pay a visit to the San Antonio Spurs on Tuesday evening.

The Atlanta Hawks defeated the visiting Philadelphia 76ers, 130 - 122. at State Farm Arena on Wednesday. While Atlanta held the lead for the final 18 minutes of action, this game was close throughout. In fact, there were 13 ties and 27 lead changes in total. With that said, the Hawks won the first and fourth quarters by equal four - point margins while these clubs tied both the second and third quarters. The Hawks ended up shooting 52 percent from the field and 79 percent from the free - throw line while the Sixers shot just 46 percent from the field and 58 percent from the charity stripe. In addition, Atlanta won the fastbreak scoring differential, 24 - 7, and the points off turnovers battle, 22 - 10. The Sixers (49 - 29) were led by J.J. Redick, as he tallied 30 points, two rebounds and three assists. Tobias Harris accrued 21 points, seven rebounds and two assists. Jimmy Butler collected 16 points, seven rebounds and two assists while Ben Simmons accumulated 15 points, 15 rebounds, eight assists and four steals. Jonah Bolden amassed 13 points, 10 rebounds and three assists. The Hawks (29 - 50) were led by Trae Young, as he totaled 33 points, seven rebounds and 12 assists. John Collins started and finished with 25 points, eight rebounds and two blocks. Kevin Huerter generated 16 points, four rebounds and five assists while DeAndre Bembry led the bench with 17 points, six rebounds and four assists. The Sixers have to play again on Thursday, as they travel home to face the Milwaukee Bucks. As for the Hawks, they hit the road to face the Orlando Magic on Friday for their next outing.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the host Atlanta Hawks, 135 - 134, at State Farm Arena on Wednesday. While there wasn't anything on the line for this game, it was incredibly tight throughout. In fact, there were 19 lead changes in total, as neither club led by more than three points for the final five minutes. Those final minutes were extremely hectic, with six lead changes alone in the final 70 seconds. While Taurean Prince appeared to hit a game - winning three with 2 seconds left, Edmond Sumner nailed three free - throws with 0 seconds left to recapture the lead and win the game. Defense was key for Indiana, as they recorded 12 steals and seven blocks while winning the turnover differential. 17 - 8. The Pacers (48 - 34) were led by T.J. Leaf, as he tallied 28 points, 10 rebounds, two assists, two steals and two blocks. Tyreke Evans accrued 27 points, two rebounds and five assists. Edmond Sumner not only hit the game - winning free - throws, he led the bench with 22 points, four rebounds and two steals. The Hawks (29 - 53) were led by Taurean Prince, as he totaled 23 points, five rebounds and two assists. Trae Young generated 23 points, five rebounds and 11 assists. Alex Len finished with 20 points, 10 rebounds, three assists and three blocks while John Collins collected 20 points, 25 rebounds and six assists. This ends the season for Atlanta, as they finished with the fifth - worst record in the NBA. As for Indiana, they will play the Boston Celtics in the opening round of the playoffs.

The Charlotte Hornets defeated the Miami Heat, 113 - 112, at American Airlines Arena on Saturday night. It would have been difficult to envision the final score at the half, when the Hornets (2 - 1) held a commanding 72 - 52 lead. However, the Heat (1 - 2) refused to be embarrassed in their home opener, shaving 10 points off their deficit with a 30 - point third quarter and matching that total in the fourth while holding the visitors to 21. That left them just a point short at the final buzzer, but Miami's bench generated 43 points to help spearhead the rally. Ultimately, the Heat won both the rebounding battle by a 49 - 40 margin and slightly out - shot Charlotte, 46 percent to 44 percent. Kemba Walker led the way with a game - high 39 points, a total he supplemented with seven assists and five rebounds. Malik Monk was a distant second with 15 points, one rebound, one assist and one steal. Marvin Williams generated 13 points, six boards, one assist and three blocks. Jeremy Lamb supplied 12 points, five rebounds, four assists, three steals and two blocks. Cody Zeller managed 11 points and eight rebounds. Dwyane Wade paced the Heat with 21 points off the bench, adding three rebounds, three assists and two blocks. Goran Dragic provided 20 points, seven assists and four rebounds. Rodney McGruder continued his productive start to the season with a 19 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included two assists, two steals and one block. Derrick Jones, Jr. and Bam Adebayo - - the latter another key bench performer - - mustered matching 12 - point tallies. Hassan Whiteside contributed an 11 - point, 15 - rebound double - double that also included two blocks. The Hornets remain on the road and head north of the border to tangle with the Toronto Raptors on Monday night, while the Heat remain home and next take the court against the New York Knicks on Wednesday evening.

The Miami Heat defeated the New York Knicks, 110 - 87, at American Airlines Arena on Wednesday evening. Despite the lopsided final score in favor of the home squad, it was the Knicks (1 - 4) that looked like the early favorite for a blowout win. New York held a 27 - 16 lead after one quarter, but the Heat (2 - 2) quickly erased their deficit with a 31 - 18 advantage in the second period. Their dominance only expanded coming out of intermission, as they compiled 45 points while limiting their visitors to 20 in a decisive third period that essentially put the game away. As the final score implies, Miami won the battle on the stat sheet in the majority of categories, and they out - shot the Knicks by a 48 percent - 36 percent margin. Dewayne Dotson paced the Knicks with 20 points from the bench, a total he supplemented with 10 rebounds, two assists, one steal and one block. Tim Hardaway, Jr. poured in 14 points and added three rebounds and two assists. Mario Hezonja was the only other double - digit scorer with 13 points. Enes Kanter logged only 19 minutes on his way to an eight - point, five - rebound night. Hassan Whiteside led the Heat with a 22 - point, 14 - rebound double - double that also included three blocks. Josh Richardson supplied 21 points, eight rebounds, one assist and one steal. Rodney McGruder drew another start and posted 19 points, six rebounds, five assists and one steal. Goran Dragic pitched in 13 points, five rebounds and three assists. Kelly Olynyk poured in 11 points, dished out six assists, hauled in three rebounds and recorded one steal. The Knicks head back home and await a visit from the Golden State Warriors on Friday night, while the Heat are also home for their next game, a Saturday night matchup versus the Portland Trail Blazers.

The Miami Heat defeated the visiting Portland Trail Blazers, 120 - 111, at American Airlines Arena on Saturday. A 33 - 22 first quarter in advantage of Miami really set the tone in this game, as they held the lead for nearly 40 minutes of action. A late run did decide the game for the Heat though, as they finished their victory on a 19 - 7 run. Rebounding was the difference for the Heat, as they outrebounded the Trail Blazers, 56 - 42. In addition, Miami won the points in the paint battle, 48 - 32, while outscoring Portland in fastbreak points, 15 - 4. The Trail Blazers (3 - 2) got a spectacular performance out of Damian Lillard, as he tallied 42 points, seven rebounds and six assists. C.J. McCollum finished with 19 points, seven rebounds and two assists. Zach Collins was the only other Blazer in double figures, as he provided 13 points, four rebounds and two blocks off the bench. The Heat (3 - 2) were led by Goran Dragic, as he collected 28 points, three rebounds and five assists. Kelly Olynyk finished with 19 points, five rebounds and five assists. Rodney McGruder amassed 14 points, 10 rebounds and two assists. Hassan Whiteside scored just five points but still provided 16 rebounds and six blocks. Both teams return to action on Monday, with Portland playing the Indiana Pacers on the road while Miami plays host to the Sacramento Kings.

The Sacramento Kings defeated the host Miami Heat, 123 - 113, at American Airlines Arena on Monday. While Miami came into this game as a sizable favorite, Sacramento rode some elite offense to a road win. In fact, the Kings connected on 50 percent from the field and 46 percent from three - point range while recording 28 assists. Despite the fact the Heat led by 11 points after the first quarter, the Kings ended up outscoring them, 77 - 55, in the second and third quarters. Sacramento absolutely dominated down low, outscoring the Heat in the paint, 68 - 38. Turnovers were also key for the Kings, as they forced 19 turnovers from the Heat while committing just 12 on their end. The Kings (4 - 3) were led by Willie Cauley-Stein, as he tallied 26 points and 13 rebounds. Buddy Hield finished with 23 points, eight rebounds, five assists and two steals. De'Aaron Fox accrued 20 points, four rebounds, eight assists and two steals. Nemanja Bjelica generated 19 points, five rebounds and five assists. The Heat (3 - 3) were led by Josh Richardson, as he collected 31 points, three rebounds, two steals and three blocks. Goran Dragic accumulated 20 points, five assists and two steals. Hassan Whiteside finished with 16 points, 24 rebounds, two steals and five blocks. Tyler Johnson led the bench with 11 points, four rebounds and four assists. Both teams play road games on Tuesday for their next outing, with Sacramento playing the Orlando Magic and Miami facing the Charlotte Hornets.

The Miami Heat defeated the San Antonio Spurs, 95 - 88, at American Airlines Arena on Wednesday evening. The Heat (5 - 5) came into the contest undermanned, as Goran Dragic was announced as unavailable shortly before tip - off due to an ankle injury. However, the Spurs (6 - 4) were missing a key starting piece in their own right, as veteran wing Rudy Gay was sidelined yet again with a heel injury. The home squad looked more engaged in the first half, jumping out to a 50 - 42 lead at intermission. They would create even more of a cushion in the third, expanding their advantage by another three points entering the final 12 minutes. San Antonio trailed by as much as 89 - 71 with 5:56 remaining before finishing the game on a 17 - 6 run. However, all it did was serve to make the final score appear more respectable in a contest in which they shot just 33 percent from the field. Patty Mills paced the Spurs with 20 points and four rebounds. Davis Bertans came off the bench to supply 19 points, four rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block. DeMar DeRozan led the starting five with an 18 - point, 14 - rebound double - double that also included eight assists, two steals and one block. Bryn Forbes provided 12 points. LaMarcus Aldridge mustered just six points on 2 - for - 14 shooting but did haul in 16 rebounds and record two blocks. Hassan Whiteside, who'd been a game - time decision due to a knee issue, with led the Heat with a 29 - point, 20 - rebound double - double that also included nine blocks. Wayne Ellington drew the start and delivered 20 points, four rebounds, one assist and two steals. Justise Winslow managed 16 points, five boards and three assists. Josh Richardson turned in 14 points, five rebounds, five assists and two steals. The Spurs head back home to take on the Houston Rockets on Saturday evening, while the Heat remain home and await a Friday night visit from the Indiana Pacers.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the Miami Heat, 110 - 102, at American Airlines Arena on Friday evening. The game was a tale of two halves, with the short - handed Heat (5 - 6) forging a 59 - 51 first - half lead despite playing without Goran Dragic (knee). However, the Pacers (8 - 5) turned it on coming out of intermission despite seeing Thaddeus Young get ejected for elbowing Kelly Olynyk after playing just 17 minutes. Indiana outscored Miami by a 59 - 43 margin over the final 24 minutes and excelled on both ends of the floor. The Pacers shot a stellar 54 percent from the floor while also eliciting 23 turnovers from their hosts. Both benches thrived in the contest, with the Indiana second unit generating 44 points and the Miami reserves posting 48. Victor Oladipo led the Pacers with 22 points, a total he supplemented with 10 assists, five rebounds and four steals. Darren Collison and Domantas Sabonis turned in 17 points each, with the latter also supplying 11 rebounds. Bojan Bogdanovic poured in 16 points, while Cory Joseph turned in 14 points, five rebounds and two assists in 32 minutes. Olynyk paced the Heat with 20 points and added four boards and two assists. Josh Richardson shifted to point guard with Dragic out and produced 18 points, six assists and two steals. Tyler Johnson supplied 15 points, five assists, two rebounds and one block. Hassan Whiteside posted an 11 - point, 20 - rebound double - double. Justise Winslow and Rodney McGruder managed 11 points and five assists apiece. The Pacers remain on the road and head to the Lone Star State, where they'll tangle with the Houston Rockets on Sunday night. The Heat remains home and faces the Washington Wizards on Saturday evening.

The Washington Wizards defeated the host Miami Heat, 116 - 110, at American Airlines Arena on Saturday evening. The first quarter started out close, but the Heat closed the quarter on a 12 - 3 run, to take a 35 - 25 lead into the second. The Heat held their lead through most of the second, leading by nine, with just over four minutes left, but the Wizards closed the quarter well, to cut the deficit to just three, as they trailed, 61 - 58, at halftime. Neither team could break away in the third, while the Heat maintained a small advantage, the Wizards stayed close behind, trailing by two entering the final frame. Finally, the Wizards broke out in the fourth quarter, as they started off with a quick 9 - 1 run, to take a six - point lead just two minutes into the quarter. The Wiz did not look back from there, as they pushed their lead to 10, halfway through the quarter, and held on to earn the much - needed win. John Wall led the way for Washington with 28 points, nine assists, two rebounds, one steal and one block, in 40 minutes. Jeff Green followed up with 19 points, 10 rebounds and one steal, while Bradley Beal and Austin Rivers tallied 18 points each. Dwight Howard contributed 11 points, 16 rebounds and one steal. The Wizards shot 48 percent from the field, including 8 - of - 22 from deep. Meanwhile, Josh Richardson led the Heat with 24 points, five assists, three rebounds and one steal, in 36 minutes. Rodney McGruder followed up with 22 points, two rebounds, two assists and one steal, while Hassan Whiteside tallied 15 points, 14 rebounds, three assists, four blocks and one steal. The Heat (5 - 7) will look to bounce back as they play host to the 76ers on Monday. The Wizards (3 - 9) play host to the Magic on Monday.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the host Miami Heat, 124 - 114, at American Airlines Arena on Monday. This final scoreline is a bit unfair to Miami, as neither club attained a double - digit lead until the final five minutes. With that said, Philly held the lead for the entirety of the second half, as they finished the game on a 13 - 7 run. The assist - to - turnover ratio was the difference in the game, with Philly recording 24 assists to nine turnovers while Miami committed 15 turnovers to just 19 assists. These benches did a whole lot of damage, as they combined for 92 points between the two teams. The Sixers (9 - 6) got a gem out of Joel Embiid, as he tallied 25 points, 18 rebounds and three assists. Ben Simmons collected 13 points, seven rebounds and seven assists. J.J. Redick amassed 25 points and three assists. Furknan Korkmaz, Mike Muscala and Landry Shamet all reached double figures in scoring off of the bench. The Heat (5 - 8) were led by Goran Dragic, as he accumulated 22 points, three rebounds, five assists and two steals. Josh Richardson dropped 17 points in an otherwise empty stat line. Hassan Whiteside played 21 minutes as he battled foul trouble, finishing with 13 points and 11 boards. Tyler Johnson, Wayne Ellington and Kelly Olynyk all scored between 12 and 14 points to lead the bench. Both teams return to action on Wednesday, with Miami traveling to face the Brooklyn Nets and Philly playing the Orlando Magic on the road as well. Jimmy Butler is expected to make his Sixers debut in that game on Wednesday.

The Los Angeles Lakers defeated the host Miami Heat, 113 - 97, at American Airlines Arena on Sunday evening. The Lakers got out to a great start on the road, as they jumped out to a 34 - 21 lead after one quarter. They kept their cushion for most of the second quarter, until the Heat cut the deficit to seven with 3:30 to go. However, the Lakers closed the half on an 11 - 3 run, to take a 15 - point lead into halftime. Both teams came out strong in the third, but the Heat could not cut into the lead, as the Lakers held a double - digit advantage for almost the entire quarter. The fourth featured no surprises, as the Lakers were able to hold their ground and cruise to a much - needed win. LeBron James went off against his former squad, as he finished with 51 points on 19 - of - 31 shooting, eight rebounds, three assists, two steals and one block, in 38 minutes. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope followed up with 19 points, four rebounds, one steal and one block, in 28 minutes off the bench, while Kyle Kuzma chipped in 15 points on 7 - of - 12 shooting. The Lakers shot 45 percent from the field, including 11 - of - 27 from long range. Meanwhile, the Heat were without Goran Dragic (toe). Wayne Ellington led Miami with 19 points on 7 - of - 14 shooting, in 37 minutes. Josh Richardson and Tyler Johnson added 17 points each, while Rodney McGruder tallied 14 points, seven rebounds and four assists. The Heat shot 40 percent from the field, including 13 - of - 32 from deep. The Heat (6 - 10) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Nets on Tuesday. The Lakers (9 - 7) head to Cleveland to take on the Cavaliers on Wednesday.

The Brooklyn Nets took down the Miami Heat, 104 - 92, at American Airlines Arena on Tuesday evening. Last week, Brooklyn (8 - 10) took a loss to Miami (6 - 11) on its home court. On Tuesday, the Nets evened the score, stealing one from the Heat in Miami. While the Heat entered the fourth quarter with the lead, Brooklyn was able to quickly jump ahead, going on a 90 run to take the lead in the first three minutes of the fourth quarter. After returning from a timeout, point guard D'Angelo Russell returned to the floor, delivering an electric performance to close out the game. Eight of Russell's 20 points came in the fourth quarter, including two jumpers in under 20 seconds, which helped push the Brooklyn lead to six. The win snapped Brooklyn out of a bit of a cold streak, as the team had dropped four of its previous five contests. Russell led the Nets with 20 points; he also added nine rebounds, six assists, and four steals. Big man Jarrett Allen, meanwhile, scored 13 points to go with 14 rebounds and two blocks. Both Russell and Allen have stepped up in recent games, as the team continues to cope with the absence of breakout star Caris LeVert (ankle). Miami's offense simply could not get things going, as the team shot just 36 percent from the field. Star center Hassan Whiteside did everything he could to make up for his team's poor shooting, grabbing 11 offensive rebounds to finish with a whopping 23 total boards. Even a 20 - 20 night from Whiteside could not win it for the Heat, though, as the team went just 7 - of - 32 from three - point range in a night they will hope to soon forget. Veteran star Dwyane Wade made his return to action after missing nearly two weeks due to the birth of his child. He scored five points in 13 minutes off the bench. The Nets face the second half of a back - to - back on Wednesday, as they will visit the Mavericks in Dallas. Miami, meanwhile, will regroup on Friday to face off against the Bulls.

The Atlanta Hawks defeated the Miami Heat, 115 - 113, at American Airlines Arena on Tuesday night. The Hawks (5 - 16) entered this game as the team with fewer wins in the entire Association, while the Heat (7 - 13) ranked dead last in home wins, with only three over the course of the season thus far. But in this matchup of struggling teams, Atlanta came through and managed to survive Miami's furious comeback attempt in the fourth quarter. Miami jumped to a 38 - 35 lead after the first quarter, but Atlanta responded with a 33 - 14 second quarter that proved to be decisive. Miami won the third quarter by a two - point margin (34 - 32) and the final one by a 12 - point differential (27 - 15), but it wasn't enough and a late free throw sealed the deal for Atlanta. Josh Richardson had the chance to win it for the Heat, but missed his three - point attempt with 1 seconds left on the clock. Taurean Prince converted the decisive free throw late in the fourth quarter, but also led Atlanta offensively with an 18 - point, five - rebound performance. Rookie sensation Trae Young continues to lit it up for the Hawks and finished with 17 points, 10 assists and five rebounds. John Collins contributed 16 points, and Omari Spellman added 14 points in 20 minutes off the bench. Kent Bazemore chipped in with 12 points. As it has been the trend for the Heat this season, Richardson once again led the team in scoring with 22 points, but also added eight rebounds, four assists and five steals. Hassan Whiteside had 11 points with 10 rebounds, and Wayne Ellington added 15 points, five rebounds, and five steals. Dwyane Wade (18 points), Bam Adebayo (12 points) and Justise Winslow (11 points) thrived off the bench.

The Miami Heat defeated the New Orleans Pelicans, 106 - 101, at American Airlines Arena on Friday evening. The Heat (8 - 13) arguably played their best quarter of basketball of the season over the first 12 minutes of the contest, exiting the period with a 37 - 17 lead. They still held a 20 - point lead at halftime, but the Pelicans (11 - 12) refused to go quietly. New Orleans cut their deficit down to six entering the final quarter, and they'd continue to threaten throughout. The Pels were as close as 103 - 100 with 1:12 remaining, but Miami managed to hold on for only their fourth home win of the campaign. Anthony Davis led the Pelicans with 41 points and added nine rebounds, two assists, one steal and four blocks. Jrue Holiday supplied 21 points, eight assists, four rebounds and one block. Nikola Mirotic registered 15 points and four boards. Julius Randle managed eight points, 10 rebounds, two assists and one block. E'Twaun Moore posted six points, four rebounds, one assist and one steal across 26 minutes before exiting late in the game with a foot injury. Josh Richardson paced the Heat with 20 points, a total he supplemented with two rebounds, one assist, three steals and one block. Dwyane Wade totaled 18 points, six assists and five rebounds. Kelly Olynyk contributed 13 points, seven boards, two assists and two steals. Hassan Whiteside delivered 12 points, eight rebounds, three assists, two blocks and one steal. Rodney McGruder collected 11 points, five boards, one assist and two steals. The Pelicans next head to Charlotte to tangle with the Hornets on Sunday afternoon, while the Heat remain home and take on the Utah Jazz on Sunday evening.

The Miami Heat defeated the Utah Jazz, 102 - 100, at American Airlines Arena on Sunday evening. The Heat (9 - 13) came into the contest looking to build a little momentum, as they'd struggled to string wins together in the early portion of the season. Things looked to be headed in the wrong direction early against the Jazz (11 - 13), as Utah jumped out to a 35 - 27 first - quarter lead. Miami was able to claw back and reduce their deficit to 55 - 53 by intermission. The game ultimately came down to the final seconds, with Donovan Mitchell's misfire on a 24 - foot three - point jumper with 1 seconds remaining sealing the win for the home squad. The Heat was able to escape with a victory despite shooting just 40 percent overall. Ricky Rubio paced the Jazz with 23 points, a total he supplemented with six assists, five rebounds and one steal. Jae Crowder drew the start and produced 19 points, six rebounds, two assists and one steal. Donovan Mitchell managed 18 points despite shooting just 8 - for - 24, and he added five rebounds, three assists and one steal. Rudy Gobert generated a 12 - point, 18 - rebound double - double that also included four assists, three blocks and one steal. Joe Ingles supplied 11 points, four rebounds, four assists and two steals. Hassan Whiteside led the Heat with a 23 - point, 20 - rebound double - double that also included two assists, three blocks and one steal. Kelly Olynyk contributed 16 points and eight rebounds, while Josh Richardson matched his scoring total and added four assists and three rebounds. Dwyane Wade poured in 15 points and also registered eight assists, three rebounds, one steal and one block. Wayne Ellington turned in 12 points, seven rebounds, one assist and one steal. The Jazz head back home to take on the San Antonio Spurs on Tuesday evening, while the Heat remains home and tangles with the Orlando Magic on Tuesday night as well.

The Orlando Magic defeated the host Miami Heat, 105 - 90, at American Airlines Arena on Tuesday. While Miami led for the majority of the first half, Orlando dominated in the second half. The third quarter was the difference, as the Magic outscored the Heat, 30 - 12. That allowed Orlando to lead by at least five points for the entirety of the fourth quarter. The Magic's defense was key, as they held the Heat to 42 percent from the field and 34 percent from three - point range. Orlando was lights out from long distance, hitting 14 - of - 28 of their three's. Getting to the free - throw line was also critical, with the Magic hitting 15 - of - 20 and Miami connecting on just 2 - of - 5. The Magic (12 - 12) were led by Aaron Gordon, as he collected 20 points, 13 rebounds and five assists. Nikola Vucevic finished with 19 points, 10 rebounds and three assists. Terrence Ross was a huge spark off the bench, as he provided 19 points, three rebounds and three assists. Evan Fournier, Jonathan Isaac and D.J. Augustin all scored between 11 and 13 points as well. The Heat (9 - 14) had no player score more than 14 points, as Justise Winslow led the team with 14 points, five rebounds, two assists and two blocks off the bench. Hassan Whiteside led the starters with 12 points, nine rebounds and three blocks on 6 - of - 7 shooting. Kelly Olynyk also played well off the bench, totaling 13 points, six rebounds and two assists. Josh Richardson had a nightmare game, as he accrued six points, four rebounds and five assists on 2 - of - 14 from the field. On deck for Orlando is a home matchup versus the Denver Nuggets on Wednesday. As for Miami, they'll travel to play the Phoenix Suns on Saturday for their next outing.

The Miami Heat defeated the visiting Houston Rockets, 101 - 99, at American Airlines Arena on Thursday. While there were only two ties and five lead changes in this game, it was full of swings. In fact, Houston led for the entirety of the first half thanks to a 33 - 21 first quarter but Miami led for the majority of the second half. That can be attributed to the Heat outscoring the Rockets, 61 - 43, in the second and third quarters. Houston then went on a 12 - 2 run at the beginning of the fourth to make it close, as it stayed within a five - point margin for the final eight minutes. Miami was able to prevail though, as Eric Gordon missed a three - pointer at the buzzer that would have won the game. The Heat's defense was the difference, as they held the Rockets to 35 percent from the field and 33 percent from three - point range. They also controlled the boards, outrebounding Houston, 62 - 41. Much of that came on the offensive end, with Miami winning that battle, 20 - 9. That allowed the Heat to win the points in the paint differential, 52 - 20. The Rockets (16 - 15) were led by James Harden, as he collected 35 points, six rebounds, 12 assists and two steals. Eric Gordon totaled 20 points, three rebounds and three assists. P.J. Tucker totaled 14 points and seven boards while Clint Capela led the team with 14 rebounds. Chris Paul played just 12 minutes, as he departed in the second quarter due to a hamstring injury. The Heat (14 - 16) were led by Josh Richardson, as he accumulated 22 points, six rebounds and seven assists. Tyler Johnson tallied 19 points, four rebounds and two blocks. James Johnson accrued 11 points, five rebounds and three assists while Hassan Whiteside generated nine points, 17 rebounds, two assists and two steals. Derrick Jones Jr. led the bench with 15 points, eight rebounds, two steals and two blocks. Both teams return to action on Saturday, with Houston welcoming the San Antonio Spurs to Toyota Center and Miami remaining home to face the Milwaukee Bucks.

The Miami Heat defeated the Milwaukee Bucks, 94 - 87, at American Airlines Arena on Saturday night. The Heat (15 - 16) came into the contest on a bit of a surge, having won seven of their prior 10 games after a rough start to the season. They seemed to set a dominant tone early against the Bucks (22 - 10), jumping out to a 21 - 8 lead during the first 12 minutes. However, Milwaukee turned the tables on their hosts in the second with a 30 - 16 advantage, allowing them a slim 38 - 37 halftime edge. Miami came out of intermission a focused bunch, and their 35 - point third quarter proved to be pivotal to their win. The Heat did allow a 16 - point fourth - quarter lead to be whittled down to just one point with 2:42 remaining, but they finished the game on a 12 - 6 run to secure victory. Khris Middleton led the way for the Bucks with 18 points and added seven rebounds, four assists and two steals. Eric Bledsoe produced 17 points, six assists, three rebounds and one steal. George Hill turned in 10 points, three rebounds and three assists. Giannis Antetokounmpo mustered nine points, 13 rebounds, three assists and two blocks. Brook Lopez and Tony Snell posted nine points apiece as well. Josh Richardson paced the Heat with 16 points and supplemented them with five rebounds, three assists and two steals. Dwyane Wade managed 13 points, eight rebounds, three assists and one steal. Hassan Whiteside generated an 11 - point, 13 - rebound double - double that also included one assist. James Johnson and Kelly Olynyk had matching 11 - point tallies and hauled in six and five rebounds, respectively. The Bucks next take the court against the New York Knicks in the Big Apple on Christmas Day, while the Heat make the short trip to Central Florida to tangle with the Orlando Magic on Sunday evening.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the host Miami Heat, 106 - 104, at American Airlines Arena on Wednesday evening. The Heat got out to a good start at home as they outscored the East's top team 31 - 23 through the first quarter. The Heat kept their foot on the gas in the second, where they outscored the visitors by six, to push their lead to 58 - 44 by halftime. The Heat led by as many as 17 points early in the third, but the Raptors kept fighting and put together a great quarter, where they outscored the Heat by 16, to take a two - point lead into the final frame. The score stayed tight through the fourth, with Miami holding a two - possession lead with 2:27 to go, but the Raptors came up clutch with a couple of threes and some solid defense to earn an impressive road win, and end the Heat's five - game winning streak. Kawhi Leonard led Toronto with 30 points, eight rebounds, two assists and two steals, in 35 minutes. Danny Green followed up with 18 points, six rebounds, two assists and one steal, while Fred VanVleet added 16 points, two assists and one rebound. The Raptors shot 47 percent from the field, including 13 - of - 30 from long range. Meanwhile, Justise Winslow led the Heat with 21 points, four assists, two rebounds and one steal, in 32 minutes. Hassan Whiteside finished with 16 points, 12 rebounds, three blocks and one assist, while Josh Richardson tallied 17 points, seven assists, two rebounds, one steal and a block. The Heat shot 52 percent from the field, including 12 - of - 29 from distance. The Heat (16 - 17) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Cavs on Friday. The Raptors (26 - 10) head to Orlando to take on the Magic on Friday.

The Miami Heat defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 118 - 94, at American Airlines Arena on Friday night. The Heat (17 - 17) came into the contest a much improved team of late, winning five of their prior six games. However, the Cavaliers (8 - 28) arrived in South Florida ready to play, as they jumped out to a surprising 30 - 29 first - quarter lead. That seemed to wake up the home squad, as they owned a 56 - 52 lead by halftime and an 82 - 69 advantage at the end of three. They then finished off the game with their best offensive quarter, compiling 36 points overall in the final 12 minutes. Miami was impressive on both ends of the floor, shooting 53 percent while limiting Cleveland to a 38 percent success rate from the floor. Jordan Clarkson paced the Cavaliers with 18 points off the bench, adding five boards and four assists. Alec Burks mustered 17 points, six rebounds and five assists. Cedi Osman supplied 12 points, five boards, one assist and one steal. Larry Nance, Jr. pitched in 11 points, seven rebounds, four assists, two steals and one block, Matthew Dellavedova poured in nine points, while Channing Frye and Jaron Blossomgame had matching eight - point tallies. The Heat had seven players hit double digits in the scoring column led by Justise Winslow, who totaled 24 points. He added 11 rebounds, seven assists and two steals. Bam Adebayo followed with 18 points, nine rebounds and five assists. Rodney McGruder and Josh Richardson generated 16 points apiece. Hassan Whiteside turned in 12 points, four rebounds, one assist and two blocks. Tyler Johnson and Dwyane Wade posted 11 and 10 points while hauling in four and six rebounds, respectively. The Cavaliers remain on the road and jump right back into action against the Hawks on Saturday night, while the Heat remain home to take on the Minnesota Timberwolves on Sunday evening.

The Minnesota Timberwolves defeated the Miami Heat, 113 - 104, at American Airlines Arena on Sunday evening. The Timberwolves (17 - 19) came into the contest with an unsightly 4 - 13 road record, while the Heat (17 - 18) had been trending in the right direction with a 6 - 1 record over their last seven games. All of that went out the window after the opening tip, as Minnesota jumped out to a 30 - 19 first - quarter lead. While Miami put a 10 - point dent into that deficit with a 35 - point second period, the visitors would ensure victory with a 58 - point second half. The T-Wolves benefited from balanced contributions, as all five members of their starting five hit double digits in the scoring column. Karl-Anthony Towns paced the Timberwolves with 34 points, a total he supplemented with 18 rebounds, seven assists, six blocks and three steals. Robert Covington followed with 16 points, four rebounds and one steal. Taj Gibson supplied 14 points, seven rebounds and one assist. Andrew Wiggins pitched in 13 points. Tyus Jones filled in again for both Jeff Teague and Derrick Rose, who both sat due to ankle issues, and registered 12 points, five assists, four rebounds and five steals. Dario Saric mustered a bench - leading 13 points. Dwyane Wade paced the Heat with 21 points and added five assists, four rebounds and one block. Josh Richardson was next with 17 points and also mustered four rebounds and two assists. Derrick Jones, Jr. compiled 16 points, nine boards, one steal and one block. Kelly Olynyk tallied 13 points, six rebounds, three assists, two steals and one block. Justise Winslow shot just 4 - for - 15 but still produced 10 points, seven rebounds, three assists and four steals. Hassan Whiteside delivered eight points and 13 rebounds. The Timberwolves remain on the road and tangle with the New Orleans Pelicans on Monday night, while the Heat pay a visit to the Cleveland Cavaliers on Wednesday evening.

The Miami Heat defeated the visiting Washington Wizards, 115 - 109, at American Airlines Arena on Friday evening. The Heat got out to a strong start at home, as they took a 31 - 24 lead after one quarter. The Wizards gained some ground in the second, outscoring the Heat by four in the quarter, to cut the deficit to just three by halftime. However, the Heat stayed strong through a hotly contested third quarter and pushed their lead to nine by the start of the final frame. The Wizards made a valiant push in the fourth but ultimately came up short, as the Heat held on for their second straight win. Hassan Whiteside led Miami with 21 points, 18 rebounds, two blocks and one steal, in 29 minutes. Justise Winslow tallied 13 points, 10 assists and three rebounds, while Josh Richardson finished with 18 points, five rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block. The Heat shot 49 percent from the field, including 9 - of - 29 from long range. Meanwhile, Bradley Beal led the Wizards with 33 points, nine rebounds and seven assists, in 40 minutes. Trevor Ariza followed up with 21 points, six assists, three rebounds and one steal, while Otto Porter Jr. added 14 points, six rebounds, three steals and one assist. The Wizards shot 43 percent from the field, including 10 - of - 36 from deep. The Wizards (15 - 24) will look to bounce back as they take on the Thunder in OKC on Sunday. The Heat (19 - 18) take on the Hawks in Atlanta on Sunday.

The Denver Nuggets defeated the Miami Heat, 103 - 99, at American Airlines Arena on Tuesday. The Nuggets (27 - 12) and the Heat (20 - 19) have been two of the hottest teams in the league of late and as expected, this was a thrilling contest that was only decided during the final minutes of the contest. Denver went ahead in the first quarter (24 - 18), but Miami responded brilliantly during the second quarter and entered halftime leading by three points (52 - 49) following a 34 - 25 second - quarter score. But the Nuggets turned things around in the final two quarters and after winning both in the second half (27 - 24 and 27 - 23, respectively) they ended clinching a huge win against a tough opponent. Nikola Jokic started 2019 playing at a very high level and finished this game with a triple - double thanks to 29 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists, as well as a key bucket with less than three seconds left on the clock. Jamal Murray delivered 18 points with six assists, while Paul Millsap contributed 12 points, nine boards and four assists. Trey Lyles chipped in with 15 points coming off the bench. Miami had a balanced scoring output with seven players scoring over 10 points, but none going past the 15 - point mark. Dion Waiters led the way with 15 points off the bench, while both Kelly Olynyk and Bam Adebayo added 13. A trio of starters (Justise Winslow, Hassan Whiteside and Jason Richardson) had 12 points, but Whiteside also added 11 rebounds. Dwyane Wade had 10 points with six assists.

The Miami Heat defeated the Boston Celtics, 115 - 99, at American Airlines Arena on Thursday evening. The Celtics (25 - 16) came in the much hotter team, but it was the hometown Heat (20 - 20) that looked like the more prepared squad from the opening tip. After forging a 28 - 24 first - quarter lead, Miami outscored Boston by a 33 - 19 margin in the second to build a commanding 61 - 43 halftime advantage. Although the visitors made a game of it for a time in the third quarter, the hosts took control and never looked back down the stretch. The Heat enjoyed sizable shooting and rebounding advantages, draining 48 percent of their attempts, including 46 percent from three - point range, while limiting the Celtics to a 40 percent success rate. They also won the battle of the boards, 51 - 37. Kyrie Irving paced the Celtics with 22 points, a total he supplemented with five rebounds, five assists, one steal and one block. Marcus Smart followed with 18 points, two assists, one rebound and one block. Jayson Tatum and Marcus Morris had matching 17 - point tallies and brought down four and six rebounds, respectively. Al Horford had just two points over 28 minutes on 1 - for - 8 shooting. Dwyane Wade led the Heat with 19 points, adding an assist and a steal. Josh Richardson supplied 18 points, six assists and three rebounds. Derrick Jones, Jr. turned in 14 points, seven boards, two steals and one block. Justise Winslow supplied 13 points, 11 assists and seven rebounds. James Johnson registered 12 points, five rebounds, three assists and one block. Tyler Johnson checked in with 11 points, three rebounds and one assist. The Celtics next head to Central Florida and take on the Orlando Magic on Saturday night, while the Heat remains home to take on the Memphis Grizzlies on Saturday afternoon.

The Miami Heat defeated the visiting Memphis Grizzlies, 112 - 108, at American Airlines Arena on Saturday. While there were only seven ties and five lead changes in this game, it came down to the wire. In fact, this game was within a four - point margin for the final eight minutes of play. With that said, Miami either held the lead or were tied for the entirety of the second half. The Heat's offense was on point, as they shot 50 percent from the field and 48 percent from three - point range while holding the Grizzlies to 48 percent from the field and 31 percent from long range. Ball movement played a huge factor in that, with Miami out - assisting Memphis, 25 - 18. Bench production was also big, with Miami having four bench players reach double figures in scoring while Memphis had just two. The Grizzlies (19 - 23) were led by Mike Conley, as he tallied 22 points, three rebounds, seven assists and three steals. JaMychal Green was huge off their bench, providing 24 points and 11 rebounds. Marc Gasol finished with 15 points, five rebounds, five assists and two blocks while Jaren Jackson accrued 13 points, five rebounds, two assists, three steals and two blocks. The Heat (21 - 20) were led by Justise Winslow, as he collected 26 points, seven rebounds and four assists on 10 - of - 16 from the field. Josh Richardson accumulated 14 points, six rebounds, nine assists and two steals. Bam Adebayo started and totaled 11 points, 10 rebounds, two assists and two steals. Tyler Johnson, Kelly Olynyk, Derrick Jones Jr. and Dwyane Wade all reached double figures in scoring off the bench. On deck for Memphis is a road matchup versus the scorching - hot Houston Rockets on Monday. As for Miami, they're off until Tuesday when they travel to face the equally hot Milwaukee Bucks.

The Los Angeles Clippers defeated the host Miami Heat, 111 - 99, at American Airlines Arena on Wednesday evening. The Heat got out to a good start at home, as they emerged with a 31 - 27 lead after one quarter. The Clippers battled through the second and brought the game to a tie at 54 by halftime. They carried the momentum into the second half, and held a slight edge through the third quarter, before taking a 77 - 72 lead into the final frame. The Clippers sealed the deal through the fourth, where they outscored the Heat by seven, to earn their 12th road win of the season. This marks the second straight loss for Miami. Tobias Harris led the Clippers with 31 points, seven rebounds, six assists and one steal, in 39 minutes. Montrezl Harrell followed up with 16 points, five rebounds, one assist and one block, while Lou Williams chipped in 13 points, six assists, five rebounds, one steal and one block, in 21 minutes off the bench. The Clippers shot 53 percent from the field, including 7 - of - 22 from long range. Meanwhile, Hassan Whiteside led the Heat with 22 points, 16 rebounds, two assists, one steal and one block, in 32 minutes. Josh Richardson followed up with 17 points, five rebounds, five assists and one steal, while Tyler Johnson added 15 points, five assists, two rebounds and one block. The Heat shot 47 percent from the field, including 8 - of - 28 from long range. The Heat (22 - 24) will look to bounce back as they take on the Cavaliers in Cleveland on Friday. The Clippers (26 - 22) take on the Bulls in Chicago on Friday.

The Chicago Bulls defeated the host Miami Heat, 105 - 89, at American Airlines Arena on Wednesday. While Miami came into this game as a sizable favorite, Chicago dominated them in this surprising upset. What's even more shocking is the fashion of the win, with the Bulls leading for nearly 40 minutes of this game. They did most of their damage in the first, third and fourth quarters, outscoring Miami, 86 - 62. The shooting disparity was key, with Chicago shooting 51 percent from the field while holding Miami to just 38 percent shooting. Much of that can be attributed to scoring down low, with the Bulls outscoring the Heat in the paint, 48 - 36. The Bulls (12 - 40) were without Zach LaVine (ankle) for this game but picked up just their second win in their last 16 games. Bobby Portis was their best player, as he provided 26 points and four rebounds on 10 - of - 17 shooting off the bench, Wayne Selden Jr. led the starters with 20 points, two rebounds and eight assists. Kris Dunn accrued 14 points, five rebounds, eight assists and two steals while Lauri Markkanen finished with 14 points, 13 rebounds and four assists. The Heat (24 - 25) were led by Tyler Johnson, as he provided 15 points, three rebounds and two assists off the bench. Justise Winslow led the starters with 14 points, six rebounds, five assists and two steals. On deck for Miami is a home matchup versus the Oklahoma City Thunder on Friday. As for Chicago, they return to action on Saturday when they play the Charlotte Hornets on the road.

The Oklahoma City Thunder defeated the host Miami Heat, 118 - 102, at American Airlines Arena on Friday. While this wasn't a wire - to - wire win for Oklahoma City, they won this game in dominating fashion. In fact, a 31 - 24 first quarter really set the tone, with a 41 - 29 second quarter sealing the victory. The Thunder actually led by at least 15 points for the entirety of the second half. Three-point shooting was the key difference, with Oklahoma City hitting 16 - of - 30 and Miami connecting on 11 - of - 36. The Thunder also dominated in transition, winning the fastbreak differential, 23 - 8. The Thunder (33 - 18) were led by Paul George, as he tallied 43 points, seven rebounds, five assists and two steals. Russell Westbrook collected 14 points, 12 rebounds and 14 assists. Steven Adams accrued 13 points, seven rebounds, two assists and three steals. Dennis Schroder was huge off the bench, as he provided 28 points on 11 - of - 13 from the field. The Heat (24 - 26) were led by Kelly Olynyk, as he provided 21 points, seven rebounds and two assists off the bench. Josh Richardson led the starters with 18 points, four rebounds, three assists and two steals. Hassan Whiteside amassed 12 points and 16 rebounds. Justise Winslow finished with 10 points, two rebounds and five assists. Oklahoma City returns to action on Sunday, as they travel to face the Boston Celtics. As for Miami, they play host to the struggling Indiana Pacers on Saturday for their next outing.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the Miami Heat, 95 - 88, at American Airlines Arena on Saturday evening. The Pacers (32 - 19) came into the contest with a stellar record, but it likely felt like anything but after looking nothing like themselves over the prior four games. Their uncharacteristic slide was prompted by Victor Oladipo's season - ending knee injury, and it certainly hasn't helped that backup Tyreke Evans succumbed to a back injury recently as well due to a traffic accident. When the Heat (24 - 27) jumped out to a 27 - 21 first - quarter lead, it must have therefore felt like more of the same for Indiana, but they bounced back to outscore their hosts by a 63 - 50 margin during the middle periods. Both teams then impressively shut the other down during the final 12 minutes, with only 22 combined points being scored. That was enough for the visitors to escape with the narrow win, one that came about in large part to the 23 turnovers they forced. Bojan Bogdanovic paced Indiana with 31 points, adding seven rebounds, one assist and one steal. Darren Collison followed with 20 points, supplementing them with six assists, two rebounds and one steal. Myles Turner produced 14 points, five rebounds, two assists, two blocks and two steals. Thaddeus Young filled out the stat sheet with 11 points, nine boards, four assists and three steals. Dwyane Wade led the Heat with 21 points and also offered six rebounds, four assists and one block. Hassan Whiteside generated a 19 - point, 14 - rebound double - double that also included one steal and one block. Josh Richardson and Kelly Olynyk turned in matching 14 - point tallies, with Olynyk also hauled in seven rebounds. The Pacers next visit the New Orleans Pelicans on Monday night, while the Heat hit the road and take on the Portland Trail Blazers on Wednesday evening.

The Detroit Pistons defeated the Miami Heat, 119 - 96, at American Airlines Arena on Saturday night. The Pistons (28 - 30) did not exactly have the look of a team that would finish the night as double - digit victors early on, as they were down by nine points after one quarter. However, Detroit doubled up the Heat (26 - 32) in the second quarter by a 34 - 17 margin, giving them an eight - point halftime advantage. After matching Miami basket for basket in the third to maintain their lead, the visitors put the finishing touches on the big win with a 35 - point fourth quarter. As the final score implied, the Pistons shot particularly well, draining 52 percent of their attempts, including 42 percent of their tries from behind the arc. Ish Smith paced the Pistons from bench, supplying 22 points, nine assists, two rebounds and one steal. Blake Griffin followed with 20 points, six assists and four rebounds. Langston Galloway poured in 17 points. Luke Kennard matched Galloway's scoring tally and added five rebounds, one assist and three steals. Reggie Jackson registered 13 points, two assists and one rebound. Andre Drummond generated a 12 - point, 14 - rebound double - double that also included four blocks. Josh Richardson led the Heat with 22 points, adding three boards and two assists. Dion Waiters netted 17 points and five assists. Dwyane Wade provided a bench - leading 15 points and complemented them with four assists, three rebounds, one steal and one block. Hassan Whiteside mustered a 13 - point, 15 - rebound double - double that also included three blocks and two steals. The Pistons head back home to take on the Indiana Pacers on Monday night, while the Heat remain home to face the Phoenix Suns on Monday evening as well.

The Phoenix Suns defeated the Miami Heat, 124 - 121, at AmericanAirlines Arena on Monday. The Heat (26 - 32) headed into halftime with a fairly comfortable 11 - point lead after scoring 63 points over the first 24 minutes, but the visiting Suns (11 - 50) wasted no time making their comeback in the second half. And after scoring 40 points in the final quarter and some timely free throws in the closing minutes, Phoenix was able to walk away with the upset victory. Seven different Suns players would score in double figures Monday, and the team managed to torch Miami's defense, shooting 41 percent from behind the arc and 51 percent from the field overall. Devin Booker, who hit what ended up being the game - winning free throws with 17 seconds remaining, led the way with a team - high 20 points and nine assists in 33 minutes, while former Heat player Tyler Johnson, who was traded to Phoenix at the trade deadline, was close behind with 18 points of his own. In the end, it was just a complete team effort from the Suns, who recorded 30 assists on their 45 made field goals to just 14 turnovers. As for the Heat, their shocking home struggles continue, as they dropped to 11 - 17 on their home floor this season and have now lost five of their last six games. Miami did, however, get stellar play out of their starting frontcourt, with Hassan Whiteside scoring a game - high 29 points to go along with 11 rebounds in 27 minutes and Kelly Olynyk posting 28 points and 10 rebounds of his won in 41 minutes. However, for the Heat, offensive production was not the problem, as they simply could not string together stops in the second half against this lowly Suns team. It was the second game in a row that Miami gave up more than 115 points in a game.

The Miami Heat defeated the visiting Golden State Warriors, 126 - 125, at American Airlines Arena on Wednesday evening. The Heat got out to a great start at home, with a 32 - 22 lead after one quarter. They kept the pressure on in the second, where they held the upper hand, as they pushed their lead to 20, before setting on a 15 - point advantage by halftime. The Warriors came out energized in the third and chipped away at the deficit, but the Heat maintained the advantage, as they carried an eight - point lead into the final frame. The Warriors kept battling and made it a one - point game with three minutes left. They then took a slight advantage, holding a three - point lead with 56 seconds left. However, thanks to last minute heroics by Dwyane Wade, with two three - pointers, including the buzzer beating game - winner, the Heat earned an impressive home win and ended a three - game slide. Wade finished with 25 points, seven rebounds, three assists, two blocks and a steal, in 25 minutes off the bench. Goran Dragic led the Heat with 27 points on 7 - of - 11 shooting, in 20 minutes off the bench, while Josh Richardson tallied 21 points, five rebounds and five assists. The Heat shot 51 percent from the field, including 18 - of - 40 from deep. Meanwhile, Klay Thompson led the Warriors with 36 points, three steals, two rebounds and one assist, in 37 minutes. Kevin Durant tallied 29 points, five rebounds, five assists and two blocks, while Stephen Curry added 24 points, six rebounds and four assists. The Warriors shot 49 percent from the field, including 17 - of - 48 from long range. The Warriors (43 - 18) will look to bounce back as they take on the Magic in Orlando on Thursday. The Heat (27 - 33) head to Houston to take on the Rockets on Thursday.

The Miami Heat defeated the visiting Brooklyn Nets, 117 - 88, at American Airlines Arena on Saturday. This was a dominating victory for Miami, as they won all four individual quarters by at least five points apiece. That gave them a wire - to - wire victory, as the Heat led by at least 20 points for the entirety of the fourth quarter. Miami's defense was critical, as they held Brooklyn to 35 percent from the field and 21 percent from three - point range while winning the rebounding battle, 56 - 36. Ball movement was also key, with the Heat out - assisting the Nets, 36 - 20. The Nets (32 - 33) were led by Joe Harris, as he tallied 15 points, three rebounds and two blocks. D'Angelo Russell amassed 10 points and eight assists. Caris LeVert finished with eight points, two rebounds and six assists. Rodions Kurucs led the bench with 11 points and seven rebounds. The Heat (28 - 34) were led by Kelly Olynyk, as he provided 25 points, six rebounds, four assists and two blocks. Justise Winslow accumulated 13 points, four rebounds and six assists. Josh Richardson collected 12 points, five rebounds and seven assists while Bam Adebayo generated nine points, 16 rebounds and six assists in a start for Hassan Whiteside. Derrick Jones Jr. led the bench with 18 points while Rodney McGruder finished with 17 points, six rebounds, two steals and two blocks. Both teams return to action on Monday, with Brooklyn playing host to the Dallas Mavericks and Miami welcoming the Atlanta Hawks to American Airlines Arena.

The Miami Heat defeated the visiting Atlanta Hawks, 114 - 113, at American Airlines Arena on Monday. Neither team won any individual quarter by more than a single point, as this game wasn't decided until the final seconds. In fact, there were 12 lead changes in total, with neither team leading by more than 10 points. Atlanta actually nearly came back, as they finished the game on an 11 - 3 run but Miami ran out the clock in the final seconds thanks to some smart passing. The shooting disparity was key, with Miami shooting 56 percent from the field while holding Atlanta to just 42 percent shooting. Rim protection was key for the Heat, as they out - blocked the Hawks, 7 - 2. Miami ended up outscoring Atlanta in the paint, 56 - 38 while outscoring them in fastbreak scoring, 16 - 4. The Hawks (22 - 43) were led by Kent Bazemore, as he tallied 18 points, seven rebounds and three assists. Dewayne Dedmon accrued 14 points, six rebounds, two assists and three steals. Trae Young tallied 14 points, three rebounds and eight assists. Vince Carter led the bench with 21 points and four rebounds. The Heat (29 - 34) were led by Josh Richardson, as he accumulated 19 points, five rebounds and five assists. Justise Winslow collected 18 points, five rebounds, three assists and three steals. Dwyane Wade had another big game off the bench, as he provided 23 points, two rebounds, five assists and two blocks.' On deck for Miami is a road matchup versus the Charlotte Hornets on Wednesday. As for Atlanta, they also return to action on Wednesday when they play host to the San Antonio Spurs.

The Miami Heat defeated the visiting Cleveland Cavaliers, 126 - 110, at American Airlines Arena on Friday evening. The contest got out to a competitive start, with multiple lead changes through the first, before the Cavs emerged with a 29 - 28 lead heading into the second. The trend continued in the second, as the teams exchanged the lead, with the Heat this time outscoring the Cavs 29 - 28, to tie the game at 57 at halftime. The Heat picked it up in the third, as they outscored the Cavs by 11, to take a 94 - 83 lead heading into the final frame. The Heat stayed in control through the fourth, as they cruised to their fourth straight win. Josh Richardson led the Heat with 20 points, five assists, two rebounds and one steal, in 35 minutes. Bam Adebayo followed up with 17 points, seven rebounds, two assists and one block, while Justise Winslow added 16 points, nine rebounds, nine assists and one steal. The Heat shot 58 percent from the field, including 12 - of - 24 from long range. Meanwhile, Collin Sexton led the Cavs with 27 points and six assists, in 34 minutes. Jordan Clarkson followed up with 21 points, two rebounds and one assist, while Kevin Love added 19 points, four rebounds, three assists and one steal. The Cavs shot 48 percent from the field, including 19 - of - 43 from deep. The Cavs (16 - 50) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Raptors no Monday. The Heat (31 - 34) play host to the Raptors on Sunday.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the host Miami Heat, 125 - 104, at American Airlines Arena on Sunday. Miami had a great chance to win here against a shorthanded Toronto club but the Raptors won in dominating fashion. In fact, they held the lead for the final 44 minutes, as a 68 - 54 first half really set the tone. In fact, the Raptors held a double - digit lead for the entirety of the second half, as a 34 - 25 fourth quarter was the dagger. Defensive rebounding was big, with the Raptors winning that battle, 38 - 27. Rim protection was also huge, with Toronto recording eight blocks and Miami failing to record a block. The Raptors ended up shooting 57 percent from the field and 53 percent from three - point range. The Raptors (48 - 17) were led by Kyle Lowry, as he tallied 24 points, seven rebounds and 10 assists. Pascal Siakam accrued 20 points, five rebounds and five assists. Danny Green totaled 15 points, six rebounds and four assists. Norman Powell, Jeremy Lin and OG Anunoby all reached double figures in scoring off the bench. The Heat (31 - 35) were led by Bam Adebayo, as he finished with 19 points, six rebounds, five assists and two steals. Dion Waiters totaled 15 points, three rebounds and three assists. Dwyane Wade led the bench with 15 points, two rebounds, four assists and three steals. Josh Richardson, Kelly Olynyk and Justise Winslow combined to go 7 - of - 31 in the starting unit. Toronto will have to play again on Monday, as they travel to face the Cleveland Cavaliers. As for Miami, they play host to the Detroit Pistons on Wednesday for their next outing.

The Miami Heat defeated the Detroit Pistons, 108 - 74, on Wednesday at AmericanAirlines Arena. From start to finish Wdnesday night, it was a dominate defensive effort from the Heat (32 - 35), as they didn't give an already - struggling Detroit team an inch on that end of the floor and held them to a season - low 75 points.
