Jeremy Lamb played the hero, as he hit a game - winning jumper with 0 seconds left to break a tied game. Charlotte actually won this game in comeback fashion, as a 26 - 14 fourth quarter allowed them to overcome a double - digit deficit. Free-throw shooting was the only noticeable difference for the Hornets, as they connected on 29 - of - 37 while the Pistons hit just 14 - of - 21. Detroit dominated many of the statistics, winning the field goal percentage, rebounds, assists and block differentials. Turnovers really killed the Pistons though, as they committed 14 of them while forcing just seven from the Hornets. The Pistons (13 - 13) were led by Blake Griffin, as he tallied 26 points, 10 rebounds and seven assists. Reggie Jackson finished with 18 points and two assists. Andre Drummond accumulated 14 points, 13 rebounds and six blocks. Langston Galloway led their bench with 17 points, three rebounds, two assists and two steals. The Hornets (14 - 13) got a near triple - double out of Kemba Walker, as he collected 31 points, eight rebounds and nine assists. Jeremy Lamb totaled 13 points, four rebounds and two assists. Marvin Williams amassed nine points and 10 boards while Cody Zeller generated 12 points and nine rebounds. Tony Parker led their bench with 16 points, three assists and three steals. On deck for Charlotte is a home matchup versus the New York Knicks on Friday. As for Detroit, they return to action on Saturday when they welcome the Boston Celtics to Motown.

The New York Knicks defeated the Charlotte Hornets, 126 - 124, in overtime at Spectrum Center on Friday evening. Knowing the track record of the two teams, the Hornets' (14 - 14) body of work on their home court and the fact Charlotte jumped out to a 33 - 16 first - quarter lead, the final outcome would have been extremely difficult to envision after the first 12 minutes. However, the Knicks (9 - 21) refused to lay down, beginning their comeback with a 37 - point haul in the second quarter and continuing with a 48 - 31 second - half advantage that sent the game into overtime. In the extra period, New York managed to pull ahead by a 126 - 121 margin with 17 seconds remaining, and a Kemba Walker misfire on a jumper at the buzzer sealed the win for the Knicks. Emmanuel Mudiay paced the Knicks with 34 points, a total he supplemented with eight assists, three rebounds and two steals. Kevin Knox provided 20 points, three rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block. Noah Vonleh generated a 15 - point, 11 - rebound double - double that included seven assists and one block. Enes Kanter matched Vonleh's scoring total and hauled in eight boards. Luke Kornet led the bench with 13 points and added six rebounds. Tim Hardaway, Jr. turned in 12 points. Nicolas Batum and Cody Zeller co - led the Hornets with 21 - point efforts. Batum also dished out seven assists and hauled in six rebounds, while Zeller hauled in 13 rebounds. Marvin Williams posted 20 points and five boards. Walker delivered 16 points, 10 assists, seven rebounds and one steal. Jeremy Lamb matched his scoring total and also managed nine rebounds and five assists. The Knicks next pay a visit to the Indiana Pacers on Sunday afternoon, while the Hornets remain home to face the Los Angeles Lakers on Saturday evening.

The Los Angeles Lakers defeated the Charlotte Hornets, 128 - 100, at Spectrum Center on Saturday night. The Lakers (18 - 11) have made tremendous strides since the beginning of the season, but they've remained a somewhat inconsistent road squad. That much had been evident in a Thursday night loss to the Rockets, one in which Los Angeles appeared to lose composure after a fourth - quarter technical. They were out for redemption Saturday against a tired Hornets (14 - 15) squad, one that had just dropped a 126 - 124 overtime decision to the Knicks on Friday night. The first half remained tightly contested, with the visitors forging a modest 57 - 50 lead. However, they completely pulled away in the third quarter, racking up 40 points while limiting their hosts to 17. As the final score implied, the Lakers held sizable advantages in most categories, including shooting (53 percent to 42 percent) and rebounding (52 - 38). LeBron James led the Lakers with a 24 - point, 12 - rebound, 11 - assist triple - double that also included one steal. JaVale McGee overcame an illness to suit up and offer 19 points, six rebounds, three blocks and one steal. Lonzo Ball also posted a triple - double, supplying 16 points, 10 rebounds, 10 assists, five steals and one block. Kyle Kuzma produced 14 points, while Sviatoslav Mykhailiuk (12 points), Lance Stephenson (11 points) and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope (11 points) were all contributors off the bench. Malik Monk paced the Hornets off the bench with 19 points, a total he supplemented with five rebounds and one assist. Miles Bridges posted 17 points, three rebounds and two blocks. Jeremy Lamb poured in 12 points and added five boards. Willy Hernangomez collected 11 points, six rebounds and one assist. Kemba Walker mustered just four points on 2 - for - 13 shooting. The Lakers remain on the road and face the Washington Wizards on Sunday evening, while the Hornets remain home and face the Cleveland Cavaliers on Wednesday night.

The Charlotte Hornets defeated the visiting Cleveland Cavaliers, 110 - 99, at Spectrum Center on Wednesday. This was a tale of two halves, as Cleveland held the lead for the entirety of the first half while Charlotte held the lead for the majority of the second half. In fact, the Cavaliers rode a 25 - 16 first quarter to that lead but the Hornets responded with a 41 - 29 third quarter to take control. Rebounding was the difference in the game, with Charlotte outrebounding Cleveland, 51 - 35. The Hornets ended up shooting 51 percent from the field while holding Cleveland to 48 percent shooting. The Hornets did a ton of damage down low, outscoring the Cavaliers in the paint, 60 - 42. The Cavaliers (8 - 24) leading scorer came off the bench, as Jordan Clarkson led the team with 20 points, three rebounds and two assists. Cedi Osman led the starters with 13 points, two rebounds and two assists. Larry Nance Jr. was their best player, collecting 10 points, 15 rebounds, seven assists and two steals. The Hornets (15 - 15) were led by Kemba Walker, as he tallied 30 points, three rebounds, six assists and two steals. Marvin Williams amassed 18 points, 10 rebounds and two assists. Jeremy Lamb accrued 18 points, 12 rebounds and five assists. Michael Kidd-Gilchrist was a nice spark off the bench, providing 12 points, eight rebounds, two assists, two steals and two blocks. On deck for Charlotte is a home matchup versus the Detroit Pistons on Friday. Cleveland also returns to action on Friday, as they travel to play the Toronto Raptors.

The Charlotte Hornets defeated the visiting Detroit Pistons, 98 - 86, at Spectrum Center on Friday. While this game remained close throughout, Charlotte led for over 40 minutes. In fact, they won each individual quarter, as they held the lead for the entirety of the second half. The Hornets defense was critical, as they held the Pistons to 39 percent from the field and 23 percent from three - point range while forcing 14 turnovers. Three-point shooting was also huge for Charlotte, as they connected on 12 - of - 24 from long range. The Hornets bench was also big, as they outscored the Pistons bench, 36 - 23. The Pistons (15 - 15) were led by Blake Griffin, as he tallied 23 points, seven rebounds and five assists. Andre Drummond tallied 17 points, 16 rebounds and three steals. Reggie Jackson finished with 12 points, six rebounds and four assists. Reggie Bullock was the only other player in double figures, as he amassed 11 points, two rebounds and three assists. The Hornets (16 - 15) were led by Marvin Williams, as he amassed 24 points, six rebounds, two assists and two steals on 7 - of - 11 from three - point range. Kemba Walker collected 22 points, two rebounds, five assists, two steals and two blocks. Michael Kidd-Gilchrist led the bench with 12 points, five rebounds and two steals. Both teams return to action on Sunday, with Detroit playing host to the Atlanta Hawks and Charlotte traveling to Beantown play the Boston Celtics.

The Charlotte Hornets defeated the Brooklyn Nets, 100 - 87, at Spectrum Center on Friday evening. The Hornets (17 - 17) have been a much better team at home all season, and the Friday's first quarter served as a good example as to why. Charlotte jumped out to a 33 - 17 first - quarter lead that gave them the cushion they'd eventually need for a double - digit home victory. The Nets (17 - 20) did manage to shave eight points off their deficit over the middle periods, but the home squad put any thoughts of a comeback by repeatedly pulling away in the fourth quarter when Brooklyn got to within five points on multiple occasions, the last coming with 4:15 remaining. As the final score implied, it was a strong defensive effort for the Hornets, which limited the visitors to 40 percent shooting, including a meager 15 percent from three - point range. D'Angelo Russell paced the Nets with 33 points and added four rebounds, two assists and one block. DeMarre Carroll followed with a bench - leading 15 points and also supplied eight rebounds, two assists, one steal and one block. Shabazz Napier collected 11 points and one assist. Jarrett Allen tabulated eight points, 10 rebounds, two blocks and one steal. Rodions Kurucs, Joe Harris and Rondae Hollis-Jefferson all underwhelmed with contributions of five, four and two points, respectively. Kemba Walker led the Hornets with 29 points, a total he supplemented with four rebounds, three assists, two blocks and one steal. Jeremy Lamb and Tony Parker turned in 19 points apiece, with Lamb notably adding five boards and three assists. Cody Zeller managed a 14 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also featured four assists, four blocks and one steal. Nicolas Batum (five points) and Marvin Williams (six points) didn't do much on the scoreboard, but they pulled down nine and eight rebounds, respectively. The Nets remain on the road and are right back in action Saturday afternoon versus the Milwaukee Bucks, while the Hornets also travel and take on the Washington Wizards on Saturday night.

The Charlotte Hornets defeated the Orlando Magic, 125 - 100, at Spectrum Center on Monday evening. The Hornets (18 - 18) have been an appreciably better home team all season, and Monday's comfortable double - digit victory was just the latest example. The Magic (16 - 20) actually jumped out to a 70 lead to start the game, but that would essentially turn out to be the highlight of their night. Charlotte roared back to take a 36 - 23 lead by the end of the first quarter, and they held a 63 - 53 edge at intermission. However, the home squad would put any doubts to rest in the third, adding eight more points to their advantage and scoring 62 points overall in the second half. Aaron Gordon led the way for the Magic with 14 points and added eight rebounds and five assists. Nikola Vucevic turned in 12 points, five rebounds, two assists, two blocks and one steal. Jonathan Isaac produced 11 points. Terrence Ross supplied 10 points, five boards, one assist and one steal. Jerian Grant and Evan Fournier generated matching nine - point tallies. Kemba Walker led the way for the Hornets with 24 points, adding seven assists and three rebounds. Malik Monk registered 21 points, four assists, three rebounds, one steal and one block. Cody Zeller pitched in 14 points, six rebounds and two assists. Marvin Williams, Willy Hernangomez and Devonte' Graham all poured in 10 points apiece. The Magic continue on the road and take on the Chicago Bulls on Wednesday evening, while the Hornets remain home and take on the Dallas Mavericks on Wednesday night.

The Dallas Mavericks defeated the Charlotte Hornets, 122 - 84, at Spectrum Center on Wednesday. The Mavericks (18 - 19) looked as if they were the only team on the court tonight, as the Hornets (18 - 19) looked brutally overmatched from start to finish, and didn't find answers for their Western Conference opponent. Things got so bad that Dallas already jumped to a 16 - point lead in the first quarter (42 - 26) and they never looked back from there. The Mavs won each quarter individually (23 - 15, 29 - 24 and 28 - 19, respectively) and cruised their way towards one of the biggest wins of the 2018/19 NBA season thus far. Five Dallas players scored in double - digits, but things were balanced since no player reached the 20 - point mark, and every single player that stepped on the court registered at least two points. Luka Doncic led the way with 18 points, 10 rebounds and four assists, while Dennis Smith Jr. chipped in with 18 points and seven assists. Harrison Barnes had 17 points, Wesley Matthews added 11, and Dwight Powell contributed 15 points and eight rebounds off the bench. The Hornets only had four players scoring over 10 points and their top scorer, as it has been the case during the entire year, was Kemba Walker, who only had 11 points on 4 - 14 from the field. Devonte' Graham and Marvin Williams each delivered 10 points, while Bismack Biyombo had 10 points and seven boards coming off the bench.

The Charlotte Hornets defeated the visiting Sacramento Kings, 114 - 95, at Spectrum Center on Thursday. A 43 - 25 second quarter really decided this game, as that allowed Charlotte to hold the lead for the entirety of the second half. In fact, the Hornets led by at least seven points for the final two quarters, as a 39 - 13 run at the end of the second quarter really decided this game. Getting to the free - throw line was the difference in the game, with Charlotte connecting on 25 - of - 29 and Sacramento hitting just 6 - of - 13. The Hornets also did a ton of damage down low, outscoring the Kings in the paint, 52 - 38. In addition, Charlotte's bench outscored Sacramento's bench, 60 - 42. The Kings (23 - 22) were led by Buddy Hield as he amassed 24 points and two steals. De'Aaron Fox accrued 10 points, five rebounds and eight assists. Bogdan Bogdanovic led the bench with 17 points and two assists. Marvin Bagley also played well off the bench, collecting 15 points and eight boards. The Hornets (21 - 23) were led by Kemba Walker, as he tallied 23 points, five rebounds and five assists. Marvin Williams totaled 10 points, five rebounds, two assists and three steals. Wily Hernangomez was huge off the bench, providing 11 points and 16 rebounds. Tony Parker, Miles Bridges and Michel Kidd-Gilchrist all reached double figures in scoring off the bench as well. Both teams return to action on Saturday, with Sacramento traveling to face the struggling Detroit Pistons and Charlotte playing host to the Phoenix Suns.

The Charlotte Hornets defeated the visiting Phoenix Suns, 135 - 115, at Spectrum Center on Saturday. This was a dominating effort from the Hornets, as they won this game in wire - to - wire fashion. They did most of their damage in the first and third quarters, outscoring the Suns, 77 - 52. Charlotte actually led by at least eight points for the final 42 minutes, as they held a double - digit lead for the final 20 minutes of action. Charlotte's offense was unstoppable, as they connected on 55 percent from the field and 47 percent from three - point range while recording 31 assists. The rebounding differential was decisive too, with the Hornets winning that battle, 53 - 26. The Suns (11 - 36) were led by Devin Booker, as he tallied 32 points, two rebounds and 11 assists. T.J. Warren amassed 16 points, three rebounds and two blocks. Kelly Oubre Jr. was a nice spark off the bench, as he provided 24 points, three rebounds and two blocks. DeAndre Ayton finished with just 10 points and two rebounds. The Hornets (22 - 23) were led by Kemba Walker, as he accumulated 21 points, eight rebounds, three assists and two steals. Jeremy Lamb amassed 18 points, five rebounds and six assists. Nicolas Batum totaled 15 points, three rebounds and six assists while Bismack Biyombo provided 11 points, 13 rebounds, three assists and five blocks. Both teams have to play again on Sunday, with Charlotte traveling to face the Indiana Pacers and Phoenix remaining on the road to face the Minnesota Timberwolves.

The Charlotte Hornets defeated the visiting New York Knicks, 101 - 92, at Spectrum Center on Monday. While Charlotte came into this game as a sizable favorite, it took five ties and 10 lead changes to determine a winner. The Hornets took control in the fourth quarter though, outscoring the Knicks, 30 - 21. Offensive rebounding was huge for Charlotte, as they outrebounded New York, 14 - 7. Ball movement was also decisive, with the Hornets out - assisting the Knicks, 25 - 19. Charlotte's bench was probably the difference though, as they outscored New York's bench, 53 - 37. The Knicks (10 - 39) were led by Kevin Knox, as he amassed 19 points and three rebounds. Tim Hardaway Jr. finished with 17 points, 10 rebounds and four assists. Noah Vonleh accrued five points, 12 rebounds and two assists. No other player on the roster reached double figures in scoring, rebounding or assists. The Hornets (24 - 25) were led by Jeremy Lamb, as he collected 15 points, nine rebounds and three assists. Kemba Walker amassed 14 points, five rebounds, five assists and two blocks. Four players reached double figures in scoring off the bench, with Tony Parker leading the way with 15 points and four assists. Wily Hernangomez tallied 11 points and 11 rebounds off the bench as well. Both teams return to action on Wednesday, with Charlotte traveling to face the surging Boston Celtics and New York playing host to the Dallas Mavericks.

The Charlotte Hornets defeated the Memphis Grizzlies, 100 - 92, at Spectrum Center on Friday evening. The Grizzlies (20 - 33) came into the contest with a significant personnel shortage, as Mike Conley (knee), Garrett Temple (shoulder), Kyle Anderson (shoulder), Jaren Jackson, Jr. (quadriceps) and Omri Casspi (knee) were all out of action. However, that didn't stop Memphis from surprisingly ambushing the home - court Hornets (25 - 26) by a 29 - 17 margin over the first 12 minutes. Charlotte did bounce back in strong form in the second, leading to a 45 - 45 halftime deadlock. After both teams virtually matched each other bucket for bucket in the third, the hosts went on a 30 - 19 run over the final 12 minutes to clinch victory. Shelvin Mack paced the Grizzlies with 19 points, adding nine assists, one rebound and two steals. Ivan Rabb and Justin Holiday contributed matching 15 - point efforts while hauling in five and four rebounds, respectively. Joakim Noah contributed a 10 - point, 11 - rebound double - double off the bench that also featured two assists and one block. JaMychal Green matched Noah's scoring tally and also posted three rebounds. Kemba Walker led the Hornets with 23 points while also supplying four assists and three rebounds. Malik Monk poured in 20 points and added three boards and one block. Marvin Williams registered 16 points, four rebounds and one steal. Tony Parker turned in 15 points and dished out seven assists. Michael Kidd-Gilchrist delivered 10 points, four rebounds, one steal and one block. The Grizzlies remain on the road and pay a visit to the New York Knicks on Sunday afternoon, while the Hornets remain home and face the Chicago Bulls on Saturday night.

The Charlotte Hornets defeated the visiting Chicago Bulls, 125 - 118, at Spectrum Center on Saturday. This game was full of swings, as it took 11 ties and 10 lead changes to determine a winner. Charlotte took control in the second half, outscoring Chicago, 74 - 58. Both offenses were on point, as they each connected on 52 percent of their shots. The key for the Hornets was three - point shooting, as they connected on 14 - of - 32 while the Bulls hit 9 - of - 24. Charlotte's starters really dominated this game, as they had four starters score at least 13 points while Chicago had only two starters score more than seven points. The Bulls (12 - 41) got a majestic performance from Bobby Portis off their bench, as he scored 26 of his 33 points in the first half, adding nine rebounds to his tally. Lauri Markkanen led the starters with 30 points and nine rebounds. Zach LaVine amassed 18 points, five rebounds and three assists. The Hornets (26 - 26) were led by Kemba Walker, as he tallied 37 points, six rebounds and 10 assists. Nicolas Batum amassed 16 points and five rebounds. Jeremy Lamb accumulated 13 points, nine rebounds and two assists while Malik Monk led the bench with 18 points, three rebounds and five assists. On deck for Charlotte is a home matchup versus the Los Angeles Clippers on Tuesday. As for Chicago, they're off until Wednesday when they play host to the dysfunctional New Orleans Pelicans.

The Los Angeles Clippers defeated the Charlotte Hornets, 117 - 115, at Spectrum Center on Tuesday. The Clippers (30 - 25) and the Hornets (26 - 27) played a back - and - forth game that was decided with less than five seconds left in the final quarter. The Clippers jumped to a 26 - 25 lead in the first quarter, but Charlotte stormed back in both the second and third quarters; they won 33 - 27 in the second and 34 - 31 in the third, so they were up by eight points entering the final 12 minutes of action. However, Los Angeles didn't give up and they flipped the script during the final 12 minutes of action. A 33 - 23 win gave them the win, headlined by a game - winning, mid - range jumped from Tobias Harris with only 4 seconds left on the clock. Harris was the best player in this game and aside from hitting the game - winning shot, he finished the contest with 34 points, seven rebounds and five assists. Patrick Beverley had a solid performance as well and ended with 15 points, six rebounds and three assists. Montrezl Harrell delivered 16 points and 10 rebounds, while Lou Williams shone off the bench with a stellar 31 - point, six - assist performance. Kemba Walker was the best player for the Hornets in this game as he finished with 32 points, nine assists and five boards. Jeremy Lamb had a strong performance as well since he contributed 22 points, four boards and three steals. Marvin Williams chipped in with 13 points with seven boards, while Malik Monk looked solid off the bench as he ended with 12 points in 14 minutes of action.

The Charlotte Hornets defeated the visiting Washington Wizards, 123 - 110, at Spectrum Center on Friday. This was a tale of two halves, as Charlotte took control in the second half. In fact, the Wizards got out to a big lead thanks to a 38 - 27 first quarter but the Hornets took control because of a 38 - 22 second quarter. That allowed them to hold the lead for the entirety of the second half, despite the fact that Washington led for the majority of the first half. Rebounding was key for the Hornets, as they outrebounded the Wizards, 53 - 43. Charlotte ended up shooting 48 percent from the field and 39 percent from three - point range while holding Washington to 43 percent from the field and 26 percent from long range. The Wizards (24 - 35) were led by Bradley Beal, as he tallied 46 points, six rebounds and seven assists. Jeff Green amassed 16 points, two rebounds and three assists. Tomas Satoransky collected 15 points, three rebounds and four assists while Bobby Portis led the bench with 12 points, 12 rebounds and four steals. The Hornets (28 - 30) were led by Kemba Walker, as he accrued 27 points, five rebounds and 11 assists. Nicolas Batum totaled 20 points, eight rebounds and five assists. Miles Bridges finished with 14 points, six rebounds and three steals while Jeremy Lamb led the bench with 16 points, six rebounds and four steals. Both teams return to action on Saturday in the second half of a back - to - back set, with Washington playing host to the Indiana Pacers and Charlotte welcoming the Brooklyn Nets.

The Brooklyn Nets defeated the host Charlotte Hornets, 117 - 115, at Spectrum Center on Saturday evening. The Nets got out to a great start on the road, as the took a 34 - 20 lead after one quarter. The Hornets tightened it up in the second, and managed to outscore the visitors by one in the quarter, to make it a 13 - point deficit at halftime. The Hornets stayed determined in the third quarter, as they chipped away, until they trailed by just six points entering the fourth quarter. The Hornets kept up the momentum to start the fourth and managed to take a four - point lead by the mid - way point in the quarter. They held on to the lead until the Nets made a huge run in the final minutes, fueled by 12 straight points from D'Angelo Russell, which ultimately sealed the win for the visitors. Russell led the Nets with 40 points, seven assists, two steals, a block and a rebound, in 35 minutes. Joe Harris followed up with 19 points, four assists, two rebounds, one steal and one block, while Jarrett Allen added 11 points, 11 rebounds, three blocks and two assists. The Nets shot 46 percent from the field, including 17 - of - 43 from long range. Meanwhile, Kemba Walker led the Hornets with 32 points, three assists, two steals and one rebound, in 40 minutes. Tony Parker followed up with 21 points, five rebounds, five assists and one block, while Nicolas Batum added 14 points, four rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block. The Hornets shot 45 percent from the field, including 12 - of - 35 from long range. The Hornets (28 - 31) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Warriors on Monday. The Nets (31 - 30) play host to the Spurs on Monday.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the Charlotte Hornets, 121 - 110, at Spectrum Center on Monday evening. The Warriors (43 - 17) came into the contest looking to bounce back from a rather surprising home loss to a James Harden-less Rockets squad on Saturday night. They got off to a solid start in that regard, racking up 68 first - half points on their way to an eight - point halftime advantage. Golden State then turned on their defense in the second half, holding the Hornets (28 - 32) to 22 points in the final 12 minutes to ensure the victory. The visitors outpaced their hosts in both shooting (50 percent to 44 percent) and rebounds (49 to 38). Klay Thompson led the way for the Warriors with 26 points, supplementing them with five assists and two rebounds. DeMarcus Cousins generated a 24 - point, 11 - rebound double - double that also included three assists, three blocks and one steal. Kevin Durant contributed 20 points, seven rebounds, four assists and one steal. Stephen Curry endured a rough shooting night, draining just five of 18 attempts on his way to 16 points. He added six assists, five rebounds and four steals. Draymond Green overcame a mild ankle sprain that he'd suffered Saturday to post a 14 - point, 10 - assist double - double that also included eight rebounds, three blocks and one steal. Cody Zeller paced the Hornets with 28 points, adding nine rebounds, two assists, three steals and three blocks. Kemba Walker supplied 23 points, six assists and three rebounds. Jeremy Lamb paced the second unit with 16 points and also pitched in seven assists, five rebounds, four steals and one block. Nicolas Batum turned in 14 points, six assists, five rebounds, three steals and one block. Marvin Williams tallied 11 points, four boards and one block. The Warriors remain on the road and tangle with the Miami Heat on Wednesday night, while the Hornets remain home to tangle with the Houston Rockets on Wednesday evening as well.

The Houston Rockets defeated the Charlotte Hornets, 118 - 113, at Toyota Center on Wednesday evening. The Rockets (36 - 25) got off to an impressive start in the interconference battle, racking up 41 first - quarter points on their way to an eight - point lead through the first 12 minutes. However, the hometown Hornets (28 - 33) made a statement in the second by eradicating their deficit and building a seven - point halftime lead. Houston would get the best of their hosts on both ends of the floor during the second half, however, outscoring Charlotte by a 56 - 44 margin over the final two quarters. After falling behind by a 98 - 95 margin early in the final period, the Rockets finished on a 23 - 15 run over the final 9:20. James Harden paced the Rockets with 30 points, adding seven assists, three rebounds, two steals and one block. Clint Capela generated a 23 - point, 17 - rebound double - double that also included two assists, one steal and one block. Chris Paul managed 17 points, 10 assists, four rebounds and two steals. Gerald Green and P.J. Tucker contributed matching 15 - point tallies while hauling in five and two rebounds, respectively. Kemba Walker led the Hornets with 35 points, supplementing them with four rebounds, four assists and five steals. Jeremy Lamb furnished 18 points, 14 rebounds, six assists, one steal and one block. Nicolas Batum delivered 17 points, six rebounds, six assists, two steals and two blocks. Cody Zeller turned in 13 points, seven rebounds, two assists and one steal. Marvin Williams pitched in 12 points, six boards and three assists. The Rockets head back home to face the Miami Heat on Thursday night, while the Hornets pay a visit to the Brooklyn Nets on Friday evening.

The Portland Trail Blazers defeated the Charlotte Hornets, 118 - 108, at Spectrum Center on Sunday. The Trail Blazers (39 - 24) and the Hornets (29 - 34) played a surprisingly tight encounter although judging how the game happened, the Blazers always looked on top of the game. Portland jumped to a 32 - 25 lead in the first quarter and they were set to cruise their way, but Charlotte responded and won both the second and third quarters, 25 - 24 and 30 - 25, so the fourth quarter began with a one - point differential. But the Blazers stepped it up and closed things out with a strong 37 - 28 period that gave the Western Conference franchise their sixth win in their last seven games. Damian Lillard had a strong game for the Blazers and filled the stat sheet admirably, since he ended with 23 points, three rebounds, two assists and two steals. However, the best player was Jusuf Nurkic since he ended with 26 points, 15 rebounds, six assists and two steals. Al-Farouq Aminu had 14 points with six rebounds and four dimes. Rodney Hood impressed and was the top scorer despite coming off the bench thanks to his 27 points. Kemba Walker delivered a double - double thanks to 18 points and 12 rebounds in this game, but it wasn't enough for the Hornets. Miles Bridges was the only other starter who scored in double digits since he had 10 points, but most of the offense came through the bench. Jeremy Lamb led the way with 23 points, while Frank Kaminsky had 18 points with seven boards. Tony Parker added 14 points with five assists.

The Miami Heat defeated the Charlotte Hornets, 91 - 84, at Spectrum Center on Wednesday evening. The Heat (30 - 34) entered this game on quite a run since they were coming off three wins in their previous four games, and they did nothing to stop their impressive streak of results since they had little problems to defeat the Hornets (29 - 35) on their own court. Miami quickly jumped to a 29 - 18 lead in the first quarter and while Charlotte would get closer, they would never complete a potential comeback. The first half ended with a 43 - 43 score thanks to a 25 - 14 run for the Hornets, but Miami would run away with the game after winning both the third (18 - 15) and the fourth (30 - 26) quarters. Kelly Olynyk was the top scorer for the Heat since he finished with 22 points and 11 rebounds. Josh Richardson had 13 points, and Bam Adebayo contributed on both ends of the court since he finished with 10 points, five rebounds, two steals and two blocks. But if it's about filling the stat sheet, then Dwyane Wade deserves credit after posting a stat line of eight points, six assists, four rebounds and two steals. Only three Charlotte players topped the 10 - point mark and as it has been a trend during the entire season, Kemba Walker led the way for the Hornets since he finished with 20 points and seven assists in 37 minutes. Cody Zeller contributed on both ends of the floor, and produced a double - double of 10 points with 10 rebounds. Frank Kaminsky thrived off the bench with 20 points in only 23 minutes.

The Charlotte Hornets defeated the visiting Washington Wizards, 112 - 111, at Spectrum Center on Friday This game was close throughout, as neither club ever led by more than 11 points. In fact, there were 11 ties and 14 lead changes in total, as Charlotte scored the final four points in the final 2:19 to win the game. The key for the Hornets was their rebounding, as they outrebounded the Wizards, 52 - 45. Three-point shooting was also huge, with Charlotte connecting on 14 - of - 41 and Washington hitting just 9 - of - 27. They also won the turnover differential, 14 - 12. The Wizards (27 - 38) were led by Bobby Portis, as he collected 23 points, nine rebounds and three assists. Bradley Beal went just 4 - of - 21 from the field to amass 15 points, four rebounds, seven assists and five steals. Tomas Satoransky generated 11 points, nine rebounds and six assists while Jabari Parker led the bench with 15 points, five rebounds and two assists. The Hornets (30 - 35) were led by Marvin Williams, as he tallied 30 points, seven rebounds and two blocks on 10 - of - 16 from the field. Kemba Walker finished with 18 points, four rebounds, six assists and two steals. Nicolas Batum amassed 10 points, eight rebounds and five assists while Jeremy Lamb led the bench with 19 points, 10 rebounds, four assists and three blocks. This is the front end of a back - to - back for both these teams, with Washington traveling to face the Minnesota Timberwolves on Saturday and Charlotte playing the Milwaukee Bucks on the road as well.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the Charlotte Hornets, 118 - 114, at Spectrum Center on Tuesday evening. The 76ers (46 - 25) likely figured they'd be in for a wire - to - wire battle against the increasingly desperate Hornets (31 - 39), which were in desperate need of a win to stay alive for the eighth seed in the Eastern Conference. Philadelphia was also resting Joel Embiid for the contest, which made their challenge that much greater, and Charlotte had lost the prior three meetings between the teams by a combined total of just six points. True to form, the contest was a back - and - forth - affair until the closing seconds, when Nicolas Batum missed a tip - in that would have tied it at 116 with approximately one second remaining and Tobias Harris drained a pair of subsequent free throws for the win. Ben Simmons led the way in Embiid's absence with 28 points, adding eight rebounds, five assists, two blocks and one steal. J.J. Redick followed with a 27 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included eight assists. Jimmy Butler provided 23 points, nine assists, four rebounds, two steals and one block. Tobias Harris generated a 22 - point, 11 - rebound double - double that also included three assists and one steal. James Ennis III led the second unit with 14 points. Jeremy Lamb paced the Hornets with 26 points and also contributed 11 rebounds and three assists. Kemba Walker turned in 21 points, four rebounds, four assists and one steal. Frank Kaminsky pitched in 14 points, three rebounds, two assists and one block. Dwayne Bacon managed 13 points and three boards. Nicolas Batum supplied nine points, four rebounds, one assist and one block. Miles Bridges furnished eight points, 10 rebounds, two assists and two steals. The 76ers return home to face the Boston Celtics on Wednesday evening, while the Hornets remain home to tangle with the Minnesota Timberwolves on Thursday night.

The Charlotte Hornets defeated the Minnesota Timberwolves, 113 - 106, at Spectrum Center on Thursday evening. The Timberwolves (32 - 40) came into Thursday's contest looking to essentially play spoiler to a Hornets (32 - 39) squad still hanging on to hopes of an eighth seed in the Eastern Conference. Minnesota was effective in its mission, matching Charlotte bucket for bucket in the first and trailing by only three at the half. After another deadlock in the third, the Hornets finally opened up a 10 - point lead with 1:42 remaining. Despite a modest late surge by the visitors, the hosts were able to hold off them off for the win. Karl-Anthony Towns paced the Timberwolves with a 21 - point, 16 - rebound double - double that also included six assists, two blocks and one steal. Andrew Wiggins delivered 20 points, five rebounds, two assists and one steal. Dario Saric posted 15 points, seven rebounds and one assist. Tyus Jones furnished 14 points, seven assists, two rebounds and two steals. Gorgui Dieng and Josh Okogie contributed matching 10 - point tallies while hauling in five and three rebounds, respectively. Kemba Walker led the Hornets with 31 points, adding six assists and five rebounds. Malik Monk followed with a bench - leading 14 points and also provided four rebounds. Jeremy Lamb and Marvin Williams offered matching 13 - point totals, with Lamb also hauling in 10 rebounds. Miles Bridges finished with 11 points, 12 rebounds, four assists and two steals. Willy Hernangomez registered 10 points, seven rebounds and two assists. The Timberwolves next pay a visit to the Memphis Grizzlies on Saturday night, while the Hornets remain home to face the Boston Celtics on Saturday evening as well.

The Charlotte Hornets defeated the Boston Celtics, 124 - 117, at Spectrum Center on Saturday evening. The Hornets (33 - 39) are in must - win mode each time they take the court for the balance of the season, but they appeared to be outmatched early in Saturday's game. Charlotte fell behind by a 35 - 29 margin at the end of one quarter, but they bounced back to erase all but one point of their deficit by halftime. The Celtics (43 - 30) appeared to regain control in the third by extending their advantage out to nine points. However, Charlotte fired on all cylinders from the 7:43 mark of the fourth onward, as they finished the contest on an eye - popping 30 - 5 run from that point. Kyrie Irving led the way for the Celtics with 31 points, adding seven rebounds, six assists and two steals. Jaylen Brown poured in 29 points and added four rebounds, four assists, two blocks and one steal. Marcus Morris produced 15 points, nine rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block. Jayson Tatum and Terry Rozier generated matching 12 - point tallies, with Tatum also hauling in six boards and dishing out four assists. Kemba Walker paced the Hornets with 36 points, supplementing them with 11 rebounds, nine assists and two steals. Miles Bridges furnished 20 points, seven rebounds, three assists and three steals. Marvin Williams and Malik Monk tallied 13 points each. Dwayne Bacon delivered 11 points, five rebounds, three assists and one block. The Celtics head back home to face the San Antonio Spurs on Sunday night, while the Hornets pay a visit to the Toronto Raptors on Sunday evening as well.

The Charlotte Hornets defeated the San Antonio Spurs at Spectrum Center on Tuesday evening. In a game that required overtime to find a winner, the Hornets (35 - 39) and the Spurs (43 - 32) played a back - and - forth encounter that did show an interesting pattern: the Spurs were always coming from behind on the score. Charlotte won the first quarter 29 - 23, but the Spurs turned things around and secured a 36 - 26 win in the second, going up by four at the break. The Hornets would get the lead back after the third (27 - 21) but the differential was only two points, and the Spurs erased in the fourth (26 - 24) so both teams needed to play five extra minutes to decide which team will take home the win. The Hornets looked impressive in OT and a 19 - 10 lead was enough to secure the victory. Undoubtedly, Kemba Walker was the biggest star of the game since he came just one rebound short of a triple - double thanks to a 38 - points, 11 - assist, nine - rebound performance. Dwayne Bacon contributed 24 points in 36 minutes, and Miles Bridges filled the stat sheet thanks to 10 points, five rebounds and three assists. Frank Kaminsky chipped in with a double - double off the bench (15 points, 10 rebounds). LaMarcus Aldridge was the best player for the Spurs since he finished with 20 points and 15 rebounds, but the top scorer was DeMar DeRozan, who had 30 points, eight boards and four assists. Bryn Forbes chipped in with 16 points, while two bench players eclipsed the 15 - point mark: Rudy Gay had 16 points with nine rebounds, and Marco Belinelli had 17 points and 10 boards.

The Charlotte Hornets defeated the visiting Toronto Raptors, 113 - 111, at Spectrum Center on Friday. There were three lead changes in the final minute of this game, as it came down to the wire. In fact, there were 17 lead changes in total, with Jeremy Lamb playing the hero. Lamb actually hit a game - winning three - pointer with four seconds left to snatch the win for Charlotte. The Hornets defense was critical, as they tripled up the Raptors in steals, 6 - 2 while winning the turnover differential, 14 - 6. Charlotte's bench was also decisive, as they outscored Toronto bench, 59 - 38 The Raptors (56 - 24) were led by Kawhi Leonard, as he tallied 29 points, six rebounds and four assists. Kyle Lowry accrued 16 points, five rebounds and 11 assists. Pascal Siakam amassed 14 points, five rebounds and three assists. Serge Ibaka was huge off the bench, providing 20 points and 12 rebounds. The Hornets (37 - 42) were led by Kemba Walker, as he collected 29 points, six rebounds and eight assists on 11 - of - 18 shooting. Jeremy Lamb led the bench with 22 points, five rebounds, four assists and three steals. Frank Kaminsky also played well off the bench, amassing 22 points, 13 rebounds and two assists. Both teams return to action on Sunday against playoff hopefuls, with Toronto playing host to the hungry Miami Heat and Charlotte traveling to face the Detroit Pistons.

The Orlando Magic defeated the host Charlotte Hornets, 122 - 114, at Spectrum Center on Wednesday. This game had a lot on the line in terms of the Eastern Conference playoffs, as this Orlando victory knocked Charlotte out of the playoffs. The Magic dominated throughout, as they held the lead for the final three quarters. Orlando's offense was on point, as they shot 55 percent from the field and 37 percent from three - point range. Rebounding was also big for the Magic, as they outrebounded the Hornets, 39 - 32. The Magic (42 - 40) were led by Aaron Gordon, as he collected 27 points, seven rebounds and three assists. D.J. Augustin totaled 18 points and four boards. Evan Fournier accumulated 14 points, two rebounds and three assists. Terrence Ross was probably their best player, as he provided 35 points and six rebounds off the bench. The Hornets (39 - 43) were led by Kemba Walker, as he tallied 43 points, two rebounds, five assists and two blocks. Miles Bridges accrued 18 points, five rebounds, three assists, two steals and two blocks. Jeremy Lamb led the bench with 22 points, eight rebounds and two assists while Dwayne Bacon generated 12 points, two rebounds and two assists. This loss knocked the Hornets out of playoff contention. As for Orlando, they landed the seven - seed in the east and will travel to face the Toronto Raptors in the opening round.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the host Utah Jazz, 124 - 123, at Vivint Smart Home Arena on Saturday evening. The first quarter was tight the whole way, but the Jazz emerged with a 34 - 32 lead heading into the second. The second stayed close until Jazz turned up the heat with an 18 - 8 run, to take an 81 - 69 lead into halftime. Utah was able to maintain a good cushion through most of the third, but the Warriors closed the quarter strong and cut the deficit to just six, heading into the fourth. The Jazz pushing their lead back to double digits early in the fourth, however the Warriors used an 110 run midway through the quarter to take a 112 - 111 lead. The game went back and forth down the stretch, until the Jazz led 123 - 122 with 6 seconds left and Warriors ball. The Warriors went to Kevin Durant who missed a foul - line jumper, but Jonas Jerebko was right there for a put - back layup to help the Warriors steal one in Utah. Kevin Durant led the way for Golden State, with 38 points, nine rebounds, seven assists, one steal and a block, in 39 minutes. Stephen Curry followed up with 31 points, eight assists, four rebounds and two steals, while Draymond Green tallied 14 points nine rebounds, six assists, two blocks and one steal, in 33 minutes. The Warriors shot 57 percent from the field, including 10 - of - 19 from deep. Meanwhile, Joe Ingles was the high - point man for the Jazz, with 27 points on 10 - of - 15 shooting, in 35 minutes of action. Donovan Mitchell followed up with 19 points, while Jae Crowder chipped in 17 points, seven rebounds. four assists and two steals, in 28 minutes off the bench. The Jazz shot 46 percent from the field, including 19 - of - 46 from long range. The Jazz (1 - 1) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Grizzlies on Monday. The Warriors (20) head to Denver to take on the Nuggets on Sunday.

The Memphis Grizzlies defeated the host Utah Jazz, 92 - 84, at Vivint Smart Home Arena on Monday evening. The first quarter started out with some back and forth action but slowed down to set the pace for the rest of the low - scoring game. The Jazz led, 22 - 19, after one quarter and looked solid on their home court. However, the Grizzlies started the second quarter on a 60 run to take the lead. They controlled the game for most of the quarter and closed strong to take a, 47 - 46, lead into halftime. The Grizzlies kept up their momentum in the third, as they started the quarter on with an 11 - 4 run, and held on to take a, 70 - 63, lead heading into the final frame. The Jazz were not able to get it together and trailed by ten or more for much of the fourth quarter. On the other hand, the Grizzlies earned their second straight win in impressive fashion. Mike Conley led the Grizzlies with 23 points, seven rebounds, four assists and three steals, in 35 minutes of action. Marc Gasol also had a big night with 18 points, 13 rebounds, four assists and one steal, in 34 minutes. Shelvin Mack added 12 points, while Jaren Jackson Jr. tallied 11 points, seven rebounds, one assist and one steal. The Grizzlies shot 37 percent from the field, including 9 - of - 28 from deep. Jae Crowder was the high - point man for the Jazz with 15 points on 4 - of - 7 shooting, in 29 minutes off the bench. Donovan Mitchell tallied 14 points, four assists, three rebounds and two steals, while Rudy Gobert finished with 11 points, 12 rebounds, two blocks, one assist and one steal. The Jazz shot 35 percent from the field, including 8 - of - 32 from long range. The Jazz (1 - 2) will look to bounce back as they take on the Rockets in Houston on Wednesday. The Grizzlies (2 - 1) head to Sacramento to face the Kings on Wednesday.

The Memphis Grizzlies defeated the Utah Jazz, 110 - 100, at Vivint Smart Home Arena on Friday evening. The contest set up as a grind - it - out battle between two defensive - minded teams, especially with Donovan Mitchell (hamstring) out for the Jazz (4 - 4). It ultimately played out according to script, with Utah jumping out to an early 31 - 29 first - quarter lead, an advantage they extended to 60 - 53 by halftime. However, the third quarter was pivotal, as Memphis outscored their hosts by a 30 - 18 margin. They then held on in the final 12 minutes, adding five more points to their edge and holding the Jazz to just five points over the final 3; 38. Mike Conley led the way for the Grizzlies with a game - high 28 points, a total he supplemented with five rebounds, five assists and one steal. Shelvin Mack led the bench with 19 points and added six rebounds and three assists. Marc Gasol generated a 17 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included seven assists, four steals and one block. Jaren Jackson, Jr. supplied 13 points. Garrett Temple registered 12 points, four rebounds and two steals. Ricky Rubio paced the Jazz with 22 points and he added 11 assists, two rebounds and one steal. Joe Ingles managed 19 points, three rebounds, two assists, one block and one steal. Jae Crowder totaled 18 points and six rebounds. Derrick Favors posted 12 points, six rebounds, one assist and two blocks. Rudy Gobert mustered nine points but also hauled in 16 rebounds. The Grizzlies next pay a visit to the Phoenix Suns on Sunday evening, while the Jazz visit the Denver Nuggets on Saturday night.

The visiting Toronto Raptors took down the Utah Jazz, 124 - 111, at Vivint Smart Home Arena on Monday evening. Toronto (10 - 1) was facing an uphill battle, playing in the second half of a back - to - back and missing superstar forward Kawhi Leonard (ankle). None of that seemed to matter, though, as the Raptors jumped out to a convincing lead from the get - go. Spurred by 57 percent team shooting, the Raptors delivered one of their best offensive nights of the season. Five different Toronto players scored 16 or more points, including four of the team's starting five. All in all, it was a tough night for the Jazz (4 - 6), whose normally strong defense seemed powerless to stop the red - hot Raptors. Utah did not help its case by failing to capitalize on its opportunities at the free - throw line, where the team shot an unfortunate 27 - of - 41 clip. All-Star Kyle Lowry continued his early - season tear, scoring 17 points to go with 11 assists in the win. Lowry is averaging a league - best 11 assists per game this season, well above his career high of 7. Big man Serge Ibaka added another 17 points in a strong follow - up to his career - high 34 points on Sunday evening. Ibaka was a perfect 8 - of - 8 from the field after starting Sunday's game shooting 14 - of - 14. The Jazz, meanwhile, were nowhere near as fortunate offensively. Sharpshooting wing Joe Ingles had an off night, going just 3 - of - 13 from the field. The team shot just 44 percent from the field as a whole. Sixth man Alec Burks led the team with 22 points off the bench. On Wednesday, Utah will host the Dallas Mavericks, while the Raptors will travel to Sacramento to take on the Kings.

The Utah Jazz defeated the visiting Dallas Mavericks, 117 - 102, at Vivint Smart Home Arena on Wednesday evening. The Jazz got out to a blistering start, as they poured in 30 points in the first quarter, while holding the Mavs to just 18. They kept the pressure on in the second and pushed the lead to 21, just five minutes into the quarter. The Mavs had no answer, as they went on to trail, 68 - 45, at halftime. Mavericks managed to make a push in the third, including a 12 - 6 run, that cut the gap to 16, halfway through the quarter. However, they would not get any closer than that in the quarter, as the Jazz led 99 - 83 entering the fourth. The Jazz did not give up though, as they picked it up again to start the fourth, cutting the gap to nine, just three minutes in. Despite the Mavericks' effort, the Jazz would not give it up that easily, as they held on to earn their first home win of the season. Donovan Mitchell led the Jazz with 23 points, seven assists, five rebounds and two steals, in 32 minutes. Rudy Gobert followed up with 17 points, 10 rebounds, four blocks, two assists and one steal, while Ricky Rubio tallied 10 points, 12 assists, five rebounds and three steals. The Jazz shot 49 percent from the field, including 13 - of - 36 from long range. Meanwhile, Luka Doncic led the Mavs with 24 points on 7 - of - 14 shooting, six rebounds and two assists, in 35 minutes. Harrison Barnes followed up with 14 points and five rebounds, in 35 minutes, while Wesley Matthews chipped in 13 points, six rebounds, four assists and one steal. The Mavericks shot 40 percent from the field, including 8 - of - 24 from long range. The Mavs (3 - 8) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Thunder on Saturday. The Jazz (5 - 6) play host to the Celtics on Friday.

The Utah Jazz defeated the visiting Boston Celtics, 123 - 115, at Vivint Smart Home Arena on Friday evening. The first quarter started out close with the Jazz taking the early two - point advantage heading into the second. The Jazz stayed strong in the second and managed to take 58 - 51 lead into halftime. The Celtics could not find the answer in the third, as the Jazz quickly pushed their lead to 12. The Jazz held on to their lead through the quarter, as they outscored the Celtics 35 - 29 in the quarter to take a 93 - 80 lead into the final frame. The Celtics made a push in the fourth, as they made it a five - point game with three minutes to go. However, Jae Crowder, the former Celtics player, came up huge down the stretch with a dunk and a three - pointer, to help the Jazz hold on for their second straight win. Joe Ingles led the Jazz with 27 points on 10 - of - 14 shooting, seven assists, five rebounds, one steal and one block, in 35 minutes. Donovan Mitchell followed up with 21 points on 5 - of - 14 shooting, five assists, two rebounds and two steals, in 33 minutes, while Jae Crowder added 20 points, in 30 minutes off the bench. The Jazz shot 56 percent from the field, including 13 - of - 34 from long range. Meanwhile, Terry Rozier led the way for the Celtics with 22 points, six rebounds and three assists, in 36 minutes. Jayson Tatum tallied 21 points, four assists, three rebounds and five steals, in 36 minutes, while Marcus Smart finished with 13 points, 10 assists, three rebounds and two steals, in 33 minutes off the bench. The Celtics shot 44 percent from the field, including 17 - of - 43 from long range. The Celtics (7 - 5) will look to bounce back as they take on the Trail Blazers in Portland on Sunday. The Jazz (6 - 6) head to Memphis to take on the Grizzlies on Monday.

The Sacramento Kings defeated the Utah Jazz, 119 - 110, at Vivint Smart Home Arena on Wednesday evening. Two of the league's more notable second - year players squared off in Wednesday's contest, as both Donovan Mitchell and De'Aaron Fox delivered impressive performances to lead their respective teams. For Sacramento (10 - 8), Fox was at the center of the win, dishing out 13 assists and scoring 17 points. His strong facilitation helped contribute to an excellent offensive night for the Kings. They finished the game shooting 53 percent from the field. Utah (8 - 10), on the other hand, shot only 43 percent in the loss, but kept the game close by making it to the free - throw line 31 times on the night. While Fox's double - double helped propel the Kings to victory, a number of other players also had big performances. Willie Cauley-Stein shot 11 - of - 15 on his way to a team - high 23 points. Nmanja Bjelica finished with 18 points and seven rebounds, while rookie big man Marvin Bagley III impressed on the defensive end, blocking two shots and grabbing two steals. Utah, meanwhile, saw 35 points from Donovan Mitchell. Mitchell shot 13 - of - 22, but his big night was not enough to earn his team a win. Rudy Gobert added 13 points and 15 rebounds, while Joe Ingles had 12 points and seven assists. The Jazz will visit the Los Angeles Lakers on Friday, while the Kings will take a short trip to face the Golden State Warriors at Oracle Arena on Saturday.

The visiting Indiana Pacers blew out the Utah Jazz, 121 - 88, at Vivint Smart Home Arena on Monday evening. It was a wire - to - wire win for the Pacers (12 - 8), who succeeded despite the absence of star guard Victor Oladipo (knee). With Oladipo sidelined, the Pacers scored by committee, as seven players scored in double figures in the win. It was an altogether brilliant offensive night for Indiana, as the team shot 58 percent from the field and 9 - of - 18 from three - point range. The Jazz (9 - 12), meanwhile, were missing their own star guard, as Donovan Mitchell sat out due to a rib contusion. Making up for Mitchell's missing offense, however, did not prove easy for Utah. The team shot just 42 percent from the field in the loss. Doug McDermott scored a team - high 21 points off the bench for Indiana. Big man Domantas Sabonis had a double - double, finishing with 13 points and 10 rebounds. Point guard Darren Collison was just two points shy of another double - double, scoring eight points to go with 10 assists. The win snapped a quick two - game losing streak for the Pacers, who now sit at fourth place in the Eastern Conference. The Jazz, meanwhile, saw only three double - digit scoring performances. Derrick Favors was the team's leading scorer, despite putting up only 13 points. Joe Ingles scored another 10 points and also had a season - high five steals. The Pacers will travel to Phoenix to take on the Suns on Tuesday, while the Jazz will kick off a road trip with a visit to Brooklyn on Wednesday.

The Utah Jazz defeated the San Antonio Spurs 139 - 105 at Vivint Smart Home Arena on Tuesday. The Jazz knocked down 20 three pointers as part of a 61 percent night as a unit from behind the arc and handed the Spurs a crushing defeat that was over late in the first quarter. The Spurs were unable to mount any comeback attempt as six Jazz players knocked down two - plus three pointers. All five Jazz (12 - 13) starters finished in double figures, and the bench went eight players deep. Quinn Snyder rotated the minutes across the 13 players with 10 of them getting at least 15 minutes of action. Kyle Korver has been a welcome edition after the trade that sent Alec Burks and a pair of picks to the Cavs, and was ever efficient in his 15 minutes where he scored 15 points on 3 - of - 4 shooting from deep. Donovan Mitchell went on to lead all scorers with 20 points. The Spurs (11 - 13) were unable to stop the barrage of three pointers, although they shot a respectable 49 percent from the floor. Jacob Poetl had the standout performance for San Antonio and finished with 20 points and seven rebounds on 9 - of - 11 shooting in just 19 minutes of action. DeMar DeRozan only logged 24 minutes, while LaMarcus Aldridge registered just 22 minutes. Both players combined for 32 points. Next up, the Spurs play the second game of a back - to - back when they visit the Los Angeles Lakers on Wednesday, while the Jazz host the Houston Rockets on Thursday.

The Utah Jazz blew out the Houston Rockets, 118 - 91, at Vivint Smart Home Arena on Thursday Evening. Utah (13 - 13) seemed unhindered by the ejection of its star player in the first quarter. Reigning Defensive Player of the Year Rudy Gobert was ejected less than three minutes into the game after he slapped a water cup off the scorer's table in frustration following a foul call. Despite Gobert's absence, Utah earned its most commanding win of the season. In addition to a strong offensive night, the Jazz held Houston (11 - 13) to just 56 points through three quarters. The Rockets looked like a different team than the one that boasted the number one offense in basketball last season. Houston shot just 40 percent from the field on the night. The Jazz were led by a stellar performance from Derrick Favors, who scored 24 points and pulled down 10 rebounds. Six players scored in double figures in the win, and the team as a whole shot 51 percent from the floor. Joe Ingles dropped 18 points and grabbed two steals to help in what was an overall dominant night for the Jazz. Houston, meanwhile, saw an uncharacteristically poor night from reigning MVP James Harden. Harden shot 4 - of - 15 from the field, tallying just 13 points and committing seven turnovers. Chris Paul, too, struggled to make anything work, committing five turnovers while notching only four assists. All in all, it was a night that the Rockets will surely hope to soon forget. Next up for the Jazz is a trip to San Antonio on Sunday evening. Houston, meanwhile, will return to Texas to square off with the Mavericks in Dallas on Saturday.

The Utah Jazz defeated the Miami Heat, 111 - 84, at Vivint Smart Home Arena on Wednesday. It was a much - needed win for the Jazz (14 - 15), who put together a dominant effort after losing back - to - back games to the Spurs and Thunder. Utah jumped out to an early lead and won the first quarter by a ridiculous 25 - point margin. From there, they never looked back and continued to take advantage of a struggling Miami team. Donovan Mitchell led the way with a game - high 21 points on 9 - of - 17 shooting, while Derrick Favors came off the bench to drop 17 points and eight rebounds in just 19 minutes. Rudy Gobert added another double - double to his season total, putting up 10 points and 11 rebounds. Wednesday night, however, was not about Utah's offensive output. Rather, it was about the team's defensive effort, which has been missing all season. The Jazz forced the Heat (11 - 16) into shooting just 38 percent from the field and the 84 points Miami scored was the lowest amount a team has scored on Utah this season. It's worth noting, however, that offensive struggles are nothing new for this Heat team, as they are the 22nd best scoring team in the NBA, and Wednesday night was no different. Not only did Miami shoot under 40 percent from the field, but visiting team was 14 - of - 24 (58 percent) from the free throw line. Rodney McGruder led the way scoring for Miami with 16 points on 4 - of - 5 shooting from downtown, while Kelly Olynyk posted 14 points and eight rebounds in 28 minutes off the bench. Josh Richard was the only other Heat player to reach double figures with his 11 points.

The Utah Jazz defeated the visiting Golden State Warriors, 108 - 103, at Vivint Smart Home Arena on Wednesday evening. The Jazz were solid from the start, as they took a 24 - 21 lead after one. They held tight as the Warriors pushed through the second quarter, and managed to retain a one - point lead at halftime. The score stayed close during the third, while the Jazz came up with the edge once again, to push their lead to four at the start of the fourth quarter. The home team stayed focused down the stretch, as they pushed their lead to 10 early in the fourth, and despite the Warriors cutting the deficit to two, the Jazz would not relinquish the lead, and held on two end a two - game slide. Joe Ingles led the Jazz with 20 points on 7 - of - 13 shooting, three rebounds, three assists and two steals, in 34 minutes. Rudy Gobert tallied 17 points, 15 rebounds, four blocks and one assist, while Jae Crowder tallied 18 points, 11 rebounds, two assists and one steal, off the bench. Donovan Mitchell finished with 17 points, six assists, five rebounds, two steals and a block. Meanwhile, Stephen Curry led the Warriors with 32 points, three rebounds, three assists, three steals and a block, in 37 minutes. Kevin Durant tallied 30 points, seven rebounds, two assists and one block, in 36 minutes. Draymond Green finished with eight points, 12 rebounds, two steals and one assist. The Warriors shot 40 percent from the field, including 10 - of - 31 from deep. The Warriors (21 - 11) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Mavericks on Saturday. The Jazz (15 - 17) take on the Trail Blazers in Portland on Friday.

The Oklahoma City Thunder defeated the host Utah Jazz, 107 - 106, at Vivint Smart Home Arena on Saturday evening. The Jazz got out to a strong start at home with a six - point lead after one quarter. They pushed their lead to double digits early in the second, but the Thunder were able to rally back and cut the deficit to just three, as they trailed 61 - 58 at halftime. The Thunder carried the momentum into the third, where they outscored the home team by 15, to take a 93 - 81 lead into the final frame. The Jazz kept fighting and managed to make it at four - point game with two minutes remaining. The Thunder did not score in the final two minutes of the game but were able to slip away with the one - point win. This marks the fourth straight win for the Thunder and the end of a two - game winning streak for Utah. Paul George led the Thunder with 43 points, 14 rebounds, six assists, five steals and one block, in 40 minutes. Steven Adams followed up with 15 points, 10 rebounds, one steal and one block, while Jerami Grant added 15 points, seven rebounds, two blocks and a steal. Russell Westbrook finished with eight points, 12 rebounds, nine assists and three steals. Meanwhile, Rudy Gobert tallied 20 points, 10 rebounds and one block, in 34 minutes for the Jazz. Donovan Mitchell added 20 points, nine rebounds, six assists and one steal, while Ricky Rubio finished with 12 points, 14 assists, seven rebounds and three steals. The Jazz shot 45 percent from the field, including 11 - of - 34 from long range. The Jazz (16 - 18) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Trail Blazers on Tuesday. The Thunder (21 - 10) play host to the Timberwolves on Sunday.

The Utah Jazz took down the visiting Portland Trail Blazers, 117 - 96, at Vivint Smart Home Arena on Tuesday evening. Tuesday's clash was the final of five Christmas-Day games around the league, and the Jazz (17 - 18) made quick work of it, jumping out to a double - digit lead in the first half. After leading by just two points with four minutes remaining in the second quarter, Utah went on a quick run to build a 12 - point run by halftime. Utah thrived thanks to its strong defensive effort, headlined by seven blocks from star center Rudy Gobert. Damian Lillard managed to score 16 first - half points to lead the Trail Blazers (19 - 15), but the rest of the team shot just 26 - of - 68 in the blowout loss. Gobert's dominance extended beyond simply protecting the rim, as the 7 - foot center scored 18 points and grabbed a team - high 14 rebounds in the win. Utah saw seven double - digit scoring performances on Tuesday, including 15 points off the bench for Dante Exum and a team - high 19 points for sophomore guard Donovan Mitchell. Portland, meanwhile, shot just 39 percent from the field despite Lillard's best efforts. The superstar point guard shot 9 - of - 21 en route to a team - high 20 points. His teammates, though, could not match his scoring output, as no other Portland player scored more than 12 points in Tuesday's loss. The Trail Blazers will take to the road for a visit to Golden State on Thursday. Utah, meanwhile, will see a visit from the Philadelphia 76ers.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the host Utah Jazz, 114 - 97, at Vivint Smart Home Arena on Thursday evening. The Jazz got out to a strong start at home, with a 29 - 22 lead after one quarter. However, the visitors picked it up in the second, as they rallied to outscore the Jazz 35 - 23 in the quarter and take a 57 - 52 lead at halftime. The Sixers carried the momentum into the third, where they outscored the Jazz by 11 to expand their lead to 16 at the start of the fourth quarter. The Jazz put up a fight in the fourth but it was not enough to make a dent in the deficit, as the 76ers held on for their seventh road win of the season. Ben Simmons tallied a triple - double with 13 points, 14 rebounds and 12 assists, along with three steals and one block, in 31 minutes. The visiting Utah Jazz defeated the Sacramento Kings at Golden 1 Center, 123 - 117, on Wednesday evening. The Sacramento Kings defeated the visiting Washington Wizards, 116 - 112, at Golden 1 Center on Friday evening. The Portland Trail Blazers defeated the host Sacramento Kings in overtime, 113 - 108, at Golden One Center on Tuesday. The Sacramento Kings blew out the Orlando Magic, 111 - 95, at Golden Once Center on Monday evening. The Sacramento Kings defeated the visiting Charlotte Hornets, 104 - 97, at Golden 1 Center on Saturday evening. The Kings got out to a solid start at home wit a 35 - 29 lead after one quarter. The Sacramento Kings defeated the Portland Trail Blazers, 115 - 107, at Golden 1 Center on Monday. McCollum didn't have the same the same level of success, as he shot a miserable 2 - of - 14 from the field and scored only six points in 30 minutes. The Sacramento Kings defeated the Atlanta Hawks, 135 - 113, at Golden 1 Center on Wednesday. The Kings (26 - 25) let their visitors stick around for one quarter Wednesday before deciding to start pouring it on in the second quarter and never look back. The team did shoot a respectable 35 percent from behind the arc, but Atlanta hit just 44 percent of its shots from the field overall. Trae Young was responsible for five of those turnovers, but he did have yet another impressive offensive performance, finishing with a game - high 23 points and eight assists in 29 minutes. Six other Hawks players managed to score in double figures, but none scored higher than John Collins' 14 points in 25 minutes.

The Sacramento Kings defeated the visiting Philadelphia 76ers, 115 - 108, at Golden 1 Center on Saturday evening. The Sacramento Kings defeated the San Antonio Spurs, 127 - 112, at Golden 1 Center on Monday evening. The Houston Rockets took down the Sacramento Kings, 127 - 101, at Golden 1 Center on Wednesday evening. The Los Angeles Clippers defeated the host Sacramento Kings, 116 - 109, at Golden 1 Center on Friday evening. The Sacramento Kings defeated the New York Knicks, 118 - 108, at Golden 1 Center on Monday.
