The Sacramento Kings defeated the Dallas Mavericks, 116 - 100, at Golden 1 Center on Thursday evening. The Mavericks (28 - 44) saw their offensive woes continue on Thursday, as the team shot a dismal 39 percent en route to the double - digit loss. While Dallas hung tight in the first half, Sacramento (35 - 36) delivered a strong 63 second - half points to secure the victory. Buddy Hield set the tone with his game - high 29 points, which included seven of Sacramento's 13 made three - pointers. The loss drops Dallas to just 2 - 13 since the All-Star break, while Sacramento now sits 6 games back from the final spot in the Western Conference playoffs. Marvin Bagley III also impressed for the Kings, finishing with 22 points and 12 rebounds off the bench. The rookie star shot 8 - of - 16 and blocked four shots in the compelling win. Bagley and Hield were two of the five Sacramento players to score in double figures in Thursday's tilt. Dallas's own rookie star, Luka Doncic, did not fare nearly as well. The Rookie of the Year hopeful shot just 4 - of - 19 from the field and 3 - of - 5 from the free - throw line on Thursday. Doncic did, however, make an impact with his rebounding, as he grabbed 10 boards despite the poor offensive showing. Justin Jackson led the way for the Mavs with 19 points. The Mavericks will remain in California to take on the Golden State Warriors on Saturday. The Kings, meanwhile, will gear up for a tilt with the last - place Phoenix Suns.

The Sacramento Kings defeated the visiting Phoenix Suns, 112 - 103, at Golden 1 Center on Saturday evening. The Suns got out to a great start on the road as they outscored the Kings, 32 - 19, in the first quarter. The Kings chipped away through the second quarter but still trailed by six at halftime. The Kings came out strong in the second half and claimed the lead halfway through the third quarter, before pushing ahead to take a 79 - 75 lead into the final frame. The Suns make a quick run to take the lead early in the fourth, but the Kings responded with a 9 - 2 run, and managed to hold the lead the rest of the way. This marks the second straight win for the Kings, and the third straight loss for the Suns. Harrison Barnes and Buddy Hield led the Kings with 25 points each, while Nemanja Bjelica and Marvin Bagley III both came up big with double - doubles. De'Aaron Fox added 13 points, nine assists, four rebounds and a steal, as the Kings shot 42 percent from the field, including 17 - of - 38 from deep. Meanwhile, Devin Booker led the Suns with 32 points, 10 assists, two rebounds and two steals, in 39 minutes. Deandre Ayton followed up with 19 points, 11 rebounds, a steal and a block, while Troy Daniels added 16 points, three rebounds, an assists and a block, off the bench. The Suns shot 41 percent from the field, including 9 - of - 34 from long range. The Suns (17 - 57) will look to bounce back as they take on the Jazz in Utah on Monday. The Kings (36 - 36) take on the Lakers in L.A. on Sunday.

The visiting Houston Rockets blew out the Sacramento Kings, 130 - 105, at Golden 1 Center on Tuesday. Houston (50 - 28) wasted no time on Tuesday, jumping out to a double - digit lead in the first quarter. The Rockets' offense was characteristically dominant, knocking down 26 three - pointers while shooting 49 percent from the field. The Rockets led for the remainder of regulation, as Sacramento (38 - 40) was unable to cut the deficit by more than a few possessions at a time. The Kings finished the game shooting 43 percent while making only seven three - pointers. Reigning MVP James Harden headlined the win with 36 points for the Rockets. The big scoring night came on the heels of a 50 - point triple - double in Houston's last contest. Harden also dished out 10 assists on Tuesday. The win broke a tie for third place in the Western Conference and moved Houston ahead of the Portland Trail Blazers. The Kings, meanwhile, saw 20 points from shooting guard Buddy Hield. Hield's four three - pointers led the team. Off the bench, Marvin Bagley III contributed 19 points and eight rebounds. The loss keeps the Kings in ninth place, where they will likely finish the season after having been mathematically eliminated from playoff contention earlier this week. The Rockets will visit the Los Angeles Clippers on Wednesday. Sacramento, meanwhile, will gear up for a tilt with the Cavaliers on Thursday.

The Sacramento Kings defeated the Phoenix Suns, 117 - 104, on Thursday at Golden 1 Center. It was a wire - to - wire victory for the Kings (39 - 40) on Thursday, who jumped out to an early lead and maintained it for the entire game besides the 14 seconds in the second quarter when it was tied. The Cavaliers (19 - 60) did an adequate job of keeping it within striking distance for most of the contest, but Sacramento was ultimately able to pull away in the final five minutes. Buddy Hield had it going from downtown throughout the contest, going 5 - of - 11 from deep on his way to a game - high 23 points in 29 minutes, while Bogdan Bogdanovic came off the bench to hit four threes of his own on his way to 18 points in 28 reserve minutes. Point guard De'Aaron Fox did most of his work from inside the arc Thursday night and finished with a double - double of 16 points and 10 assists. It was a very fluid and efficient offensive game for the Kings as a whole, as they dished out 28 assists to just six turnovers on the night. The Cavaliers, on the other hand, struggled mightily to take care of the basketball, turning it over 20 times, which matched their assist total for the night. Jordan Clarkson came off the bench to lead the team in scoring with 22 points, while rookie Colin Sexton was close behind with 19 points of his own in 23 minutes. With Kevin Love (shoulder) and Tristan Thompson (rest) both sidelined for the contest, Larry Nance and Ante Zizic were both called upon to play heavier doses of minutes, and they both shined in expanded roles. Nance posted a double - double with 11 points and a game - high 16 rebounds, while Zizic managed to record 14 points and 10 rebounds himself.

The New Orleans Pelicans defeated the Sacramento Kings, 133 - 129, at Golden 1 Center on Sunday evening. New Orleans (33 - 48) ran a shallow eight - man rotation on Sunday, giving most of its usual starters the night off. The Pelicans' young core thrived in a featured role, though, with the team's starting five combining for 106 points. Sacramento (39 - 42) knocked down 16 three - pointers while putting up a valiant contest. However, the Pelicans' wildly efficient 52 percent shooting proved too difficult for the Kings to overcome. Ian Clark recorded a team - high 31 points in a game that featured a number of impressive performances. Elfrid Payton stuffed the stat sheet for New Orleans, recording 24 points, 14 assists, and three blocks in Sunday's win. Former third overall pick Jahlil Okafor added another double - double with 23 points and 14 rebounds. For Sacramento, Harrison Barnes scored a team - high 29 points. Barnes, who was acquired by the Kings at the trade deadline this season, shot an efficient 10 - of - 19 from the floor en route to the high scoring total. De'Aaron Fox matched Payton's double - double with one of his own, tallying 24 points, 11 assists, and three steals in 35 minutes on the floor. New Orleans will host the Golden State Warriors on Tuesday, while the Kings will close out their season with a trip to Portland on Wednesday.

The New York Knicks defeated the visiting Atlanta Hawks, 126 - 107, at Madison Square Garden on Wednesday. While the first quarter was competitive, New York was able to dominate this game thanks to a monster second quarter. In fact, the Knicks rode a 49 - 25 second quarter to victory, as the Hawks never got the game within a single - digit margin for the entirety of the second half. Bench production was the difference for New York, as they outscored Atlanta's bench, 56 - 39. Defense was also critical for the Knicks, as they recorded 12 steals and six blocks while winning the turnover differential, 24 - 15. The Hawks (0 - 1) were led by Taurean Prince, as he tallied 21 points, six rebounds and six assists. Trae Young accumulated 14 points, six rebounds and five assists. Kent Bazemore provided 14 points, six boards and two steals. Vince Carter was the only other Hawk in double figures, as he dropped 12 points. The Knicks (10) got a gem out of Tim Hardaway Jr., as he led the way with 31 points, six rebounds, five assists and two steals. Enes Kanter totaled 16 points, 11 rebounds and three assists. Trey Burke started at point guard and provided 15 points, three rebounds and four assists. Mario Hezonja, Allonzo Trier, Noah Vonleh and Kevin Knox all reached double figures in scoring off the bench. Both teams play road games on Friday for their next outings, with Atlanta facing the Memphis Grizzlies and New York facing off with the Brooklyn Nets.

The Boston Celtics defeated the New York Knicks, 103 - 101, at Madison Square Garden on Saturday evening. The Celtics (2 - 1) looked ready to put a tough loss to the division - rival Raptors behind them early in Saturday's contest, as they punished the Knicks (1 - 2) to the tune of a 31 - 18 advantage through the first 12 minutes. However, New York turned the tables right on their visitors in the second, almost flipping that margin to head into halftime with a very manageable 50 - 48 deficit. They managed to claw back from the seven - point deficit they entered the final period with, getting within 101 - 100 with 10 seconds left following a Trey Burke driving dunk. However, a pair of clutch Jayson Tatum free throws proved just enough to hold off the feisty hosts. Tatum led the way for the Celtics with 24 points, a total he supplemented with 14 rebounds and two steals. Kyrie Irving and Marcus Morris followed with matching 16 - point tallies. Irving added five assists, one rebound and two steals, while Morris supplied six boards and two assists. Aron Baynes contributed 10 points and five rebounds while drawing the start for Gordon Hayward (rest), but he exited the game after logging just 12 minutes due to a hamstring injury. Terry Rozier turned 10 points of his own in 23 minutes. Al Horford mustered eight points, hauled in 10 rebounds, dished out three assists, recorded one steal and posted one block. Tim Hardaway, Jr. paced the Knicks with 24 points and also pitched in three rebounds, three assists and one steal. Enes Kanter continued the strong start to his season with a 17 - point, 15 - rebound double - double that also included two assists and two steals. Allonzo Trier turned in 15 points in 25 minutes off the bench. Burke was just short of a double - double with 11 points, nine assists, three rebounds and two steals. The Celtics head back home and await a Monday night visit from the Miami Heat, while the Knicks face off with the Bucks in Milwaukee on that same evening.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the host New York Knicks, 128 - 100, at Madison Square Garden on Friday. The 28 - point final margin is unfair for the Knicks, as this game was close until the final 10 minutes. In fact, there were 10 ties and nine lead changes in total, as a 47 - 16 fourth quarter in advantage of the Warriors made this look like a blowout. Golden State ended up shooting 59 percent from the field and 49 percent from long range while holding New York to just 43 percent from the field and 33 percent from long range. The assist - to - turnover differential was a big part of that, with the Warriors recording nine more assists than the Knicks while committing five fewer turnovers. The Warriors (5 - 1) got a spectacular performance out of Kevin Durant, as he scored 25 of his 41 points in the fourth quarter. He also added nine rebounds and five assists to his line on 17 - of - 24 shooting. Stephen Curry tallied 29 points, four rebounds and two assists. Draymond Green accumulated 18 points, four rebounds, six assists and three steals. Klay Thompson amassed 12 points, four rebounds and three assists. The Knicks (1 - 5) were led by Tim Hardaway Jr., as he accrued 24 points, two rebounds and four assists. Frank Ntilikina scored a season - high 17 points, as he received his first start at point guard. Trey Burke led the bench with 15 points, two rebounds and two assists. Enes Kanter was also moved to the bench, as he provided eight points and 13 rebounds. On deck for Golden State is a road matchup versus the Boston Celtics on Sunday. As for New York, they're off until Monday when they play host to the Brooklyn Nets.

The New York Knicks defeated the Brooklyn Nets, 115 - 96, at Madison Square Garden on Monday night. The Knicks (2 - 5) and the Nets (2 - 5) now have the same record and it happened thanks to a strong performance from the Knicks, as they dominated the game right from tip - off and were constantly increasing their lead as the game progressed. Brooklyn and New York were tied at 26 following the first quarter, but that would be the only occasion where both sides would be matched. The Knicks won the three subsequent quarters (26 - 18, 33 - 23 and 30 - 29, respectively) and ended winning comfortably against their crosstown rivals. Tim Hardaway was the best player for the Knicks since he finished with 25 points, eight assists and five rebounds, while Frank Ntilikina contributed with 16 points, five rebounds and four assists. Mitchell Robinson had 11 points in only 15 minutes, and Damyean Dotson chipped in with 10 points. Three bench players topped the 10 - point mark as well: Enes Kanter (15 points and 15 rebounds), Mario Hezonja (11 points) and Allonzo Trier (12 points). D'Angelo Russell (13 points) and Joe Harris (11 points) were the only two Nets players that cracked the 10 - point mark while starting the game; others such as Caris LeVert (four points) and Jarrett Allen (seven points, six boards) were not up to the required standards. The two leading scorers for Brooklyn came off the bench, as Spencer Dinwiddie contributed with 17 points and Rondae Hollis-Jefferson added 16 points. Shabazz Napier had 12 points.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the host New York Knicks, 107 - 101, at Madison Square Garden on Wednesday evening. The majority of the first quarter was close, back - and - forth action, with multiple ties and lead changes, with the Pacers emerging with a 28 - 25 lead heading into the second. The Pacers maintained a slight edge through most of the second, however, the Knicks never let it get out of sight. New York closed the quarter strong, to claim a two - point lead heading into halftime. The third quarter was more of the same, as neither team could create any real separation. Nonetheless, the Knicks outscored the Pacers by two in the quarter, to take an 81 - 77 lead into the final frame. The Pacers kept fighting, while the Knicks held them off for most of the quarter. However, the Pacers turned it up a notch in crunch time, where they outscored the Knicks, 12 - 4, in the final minutes to walk away with their third road win of the season. Domantas Sabonis led the Pacers with 30 points, nine rebounds, three assists and two blocks, in 21 minutes off the bench. Victor Oladipo followed up with 24 points, six rebounds, two steals, one assist and one block, in 32 minutes. Thaddeus Young tallied 13 points, 10 rebounds, five steals, three blocks and one assist. The Pacers shot 54 percent from the field, including 6 - of - 20 from long range. Meanwhile, Tim Hardaway Jr. tallied 37 points on 10 - of - 19 shooting, to lead the Knicks. Noah Vonleh followed up with 14 points, 10 rebounds, four assists, three blocks and two steals, while Alonzo Trier chipped in 14 points, in 23 minutes off the bench. The Knicks shot 43 percent from the field, including 12 - of - 25 from deep. The Knicks (2 - 6) will look to bounce back as they take on the Mavericks in Dallas on Friday. The Pacers (5 - 3) take on the Bulls in Chicago on Friday.

The Chicago Bulls defeated the New York Knicks, 116 - 115, after two overtime periods at Madison Square Garden on Monday night. Two of the weakest teams in the Eastern Conference ended playing one of the most entertaining, intense games of the 2018 - 19 NBA season thus far, as the Bulls (3 - 8) and the Knicks (3 - 8) both entered this game under .500 and playing some sloppy basketball by most standards. But this game ended being extremely intense, to the point that 58 minutes of basketball were needed to find a winner.. and the differential was only one point. In the end, Zach LaVine's clutch free - throw with less than two seconds on the clock gave the Bulls a huge win on the road. LaVine was the game's top scorer with 41 points, although he also committed eight turnovers, while Jabari Parker had 15 points with eight rebounds and Wendell Carter Jr. delivered 11 points, 13 boards and two assists. Antonio Blakeney contributed with 17 points in 20 minutes coming off the bench, as he filled the "absence "of Justin Holiday, who only scored six points while going 2 - for - 10 from the field in 47 minutes. Allonzo Trier carried the Knicks with a strong 21 - point performance, but Enes Kanter stole the show for the Knicks since he came off the bench and posted a huge double - double of 23 points and 24 rebounds, while also adding seven assists. Emmanuel Mudiay had 16 points and Mario Hezonja added 15, both off the bench. Two starters, Frank Ntilikina and Mitchell Robinson, failed to score.

The Orlando Magic defeated the host New York Knicks, 115 - 89, at Madison Square Garden on Sunday. It's rare to see a home team dominated so thoroughly in the NBA but that's just what the Magic did here to the Knicks. In fact, Orlando took advantage of a 30 - 10 first quarter, as they held a double - digit lead for the final three quarters. In addition, the Knicks never got the game within a 20 - point margin in the second half. Orlando's defense was stifling, as they held New York to just 35 percent from the field and 18 percent from three - point range. The assist - to - turnover ratio was also huge, with the Magic recording 31 assists to nine turnovers while New York committed 19 turnovers to 13 assists. The 10 steals recorded by the Magic was a big part of that, as the Knicks recorded just two steals on their end. The Magic (6 - 7) were led by Nikola Vucevic, as he totaled 21 points and 14 boards on 10 - of - 17 from the field. Evan Fournier collected 12 points, two rebounds and four assists. Terrence Ross led the bench with 22 points, three assists and two blocks. Mo Bamba also played well off the bench, amassing 15 points and eight boards. The Knicks (4 - 10) had no starters reach double figures in scoring, as Tim Hardaway Jr. led them with seven points and six boards on 2 - of - 12 shooting. Kevin Knox led the team in scoring off the bench, as he tallied 17 points and three boards. Enes Kanter was their best player, as he provided 16 points and 15 rebounds off the bench as well. On deck for Orlando is a road matchup versus the Washington Wizards on Monday. As for New York, they travel to play the Oklahoma City Thunder on Wednesday for their next outing.

The Portland Trail Blazers defeated the New York Knicks 118 - 114 at Madison Square Garden on Tuesday. CJ McCollum and Damian Lillard were too much to handle for the Knicks at home as they fell for a sixth straight game. New York paced the game well and entered the half up two points, but their very small lineup that consisted of four guards late failed to secure a defensive rebound down two points. Evan Turner's timed a missed Lillard shot perfectly which gave him the easy two point put back shot, and Enes Kanter missed a skyhook in the waning seconds of the fourth quarter, which secured the win for the Blazers (11 - 5). McCollum finished with 31 points and four rebounds on 13 - of - 23 shooting, which included five made threes. Lillard added 29 points, eight assists and six rebounds, while Jusuf Nurkic pitched in 13 points, 10 rebounds and four dimes. The Knicks (4 - 13) were led by Tim Hardaway Jr, who has now scored 29 - plus points in his last three outings, and finished Tuesday with 32 points, to go with five rebounds and four assists on 10 - of - 21 shooting. Rookies Kevin Knox and Mitchell Robinson were quiet off the bench and combined for eight points. Robinson did add two blocks in his 18 minutes of action. Both teams play the second game of a back - to - back on Wednesday, as the Knicks visit the Boston Celtics and the Blazers visit the Milwaukee Bucks.

The New York Knicks defeated the visiting New Orleans Pelicans, 114 - 109, at Madison Square Garden on Friday evening. The Pelicans got out to a good start on the road, as they built a 34 - 28 advantage after one quarter. The Knicks kept up the fight and answered back in the second, by outscoring the Pelicans by five points in the quarter, so that they trailed by one, 60 - 59, at halftime. The Pelicans came out strong in the third and quickly pushed their lead to seven, but the Knicks stayed with it, so as to trail by just three points, heading into the final frame. The Pelicans held the advantage to start the fourth and even pushed their lead to 101 - 92, with six minutes left in the contest. However, the Knicks mounted a 16 - 2 run, to take a five - point advantage with 34 seconds left. The Knicks were able to hang on for their second straight win. Emmanuel Mudiay came up huge for New York with 27 points, seven rebounds, four steals and two assists, in 28 minutes of action. Alonzo Trier also had a big night, with 25 points, eight rebounds and four assists, in 34 minutes off the bench. Enes Kanter finished with 17 points, 12 rebounds, three blocks, two assists and one steal, while Noah Vonleh added 14 points, 11 rebounds, five assists, two steals and two blocks. Meanwhile, Anthony Davis led the Pelicans with 33 points, 12 rebounds and four assists, in 32 minutes. Jrue Holiday followed up with 22 points, eight assists, five rebounds and three steals, while Nikola Mirotic chipped in 19 points nine rebounds, two assists, a steal and a block. The Pelicans shot 40 percent from the field, including 7 - of - 28 from deep. The Pelicans (10 - 9) will look to bounce back as they take on the Wizards in Washington on Saturday. The Knicks (6 - 14) head to Memphis to take on the Grizzlies on Sunday.

The New York Knicks defeated the visiting Milwaukee Bucks in overtime, 136 - 134, at Madison Square Garden on Saturday. While Milwaukee led for the majority of this game, it took an extra session to determine a winner. In fact, New York finished regulation on a 14 - 5 run to send the game into overtime. There were three ties and three lead changes in the overtime alone, as neither club led by more than three points. The Knicks defense was critical late, as they forced the Bucks to miss their final five shots, with all of those to either tie or take the lead. Three-point shooting was also huge, with New York hitting 20 - of - 34 and Milwaukee connecting on just 18 - of - 42. The Knicks also connected on 53 percent from the field while holding Milwaukee to 49 percent shooting. The Bucks (16 - 6) got another gem out of Giannis Antetokounmpo, as he collected 33 points, 19 rebounds, seven assists, three steals and two blocks. Eric Bledsoe accrued 27 points. five rebounds, seven assists and two steals. Malcolm Brogdon finished with 22 points, six rebounds and four assists. Brook Lopez totaled 13 points and nine boards but missed two free throws in the final seconds that would have tied the game. The Knicks (7 - 17) got a career - best 26 points from Kevin Knox, as he did that damage off the bench. Emmanual Mudiay led the starters with 28 points, three rebounds and seven assists. Tin Hardaway Jr. amassed 21 points, four rebounds and eight assists. Damyean Dotson was also a huge spark off the bench, providing 21 points and five boards. On deck for New York is a home matchup versus the Washington Wizards on Monday. As for Milwaukee, they're off until Wednesday when they play host to the Detroit Pistons.

The Washington Wizards defeated the New York Knicks, 110 - 107, at Madison Square Garden on Monday evening. The two teams came into the contest dealing with their respective share of struggles, and it was the hometown Knicks (8 - 17) that seemed more prepared to wage battle in the first half. New York had forged a 61 - 52 lead by intermission, but they saw that quickly wiped away in a disastrous third quarter. The Wizards (10 - 14) outscored their hosts by a 34 - 19 margin during that period, allowing them to go into the final 12 minutes with a six - point edge. New York would eventually go on a 120 run to close the gap to 107 - 104 with 35 seconds remaining, but a 26 - foot John Wall three - point jumper with 12 seconds left helped seal the win for the visitors. Bradley Beal led the way for the Wizards with 27 points, a total he supplemented with eight rebounds, seven assists, two steals and one block. Kelly Oubre, Jr. provided 21 points, five rebounds, one assist, three blocks and one steal. Wall generated an 18 - point, 15 - assist double - double. Markieff Morris matched Wall's scoring total off the bench and added seven rebounds, one assist and one steal. Otto Porter, Jr. supplied 15 points, five rebounds, three steals and three blocks. Tim Hardaway, Jr. paced the Knicks with 20 points, a total he supplemented with two assists. Dewayne Dotson followed with a bench - leading 17 points and also contributed nine rebounds, one assist and one steal. Emmanuel Mudiay registered 16 points, five rebounds, four assists and one block. Enes Kanter posted a 13 - point, 16 - rebound double - double that also included two assists and one steal. Noah Vonleh tallied 11 points, eight boards, one assist and one block. The Wizards remain on the road and head south to face the Atlanta Hawks on Wednesday night, while the Knicks pay a visit to the Boston Celtics on Wednesday evening as well.

The Brooklyn Nets defeated the New York Knicks, 112 - 104, at Madison Square Garden on Saturday evening. The Nets (10 - 18) got the early jump on their inter - city rivals in the first quarter by taking a 30 - 23 lead, an edge that they'd expanded to 11 by the half. They ultimately entered the final 12 minutes with a 94 - 77 advantage that was more than enough to withstand the Knicks' (8 - 19) best all - around quarter of the game. Brooklyn put on a shooting display, draining 49 percent of their attempts, including 50 percent from three - point range. Spencer Dinwiddie led the Nets with 25 points off the bench and added six assists, three rebounds and one steal. Rodions Kurucs supplied 20 points, six boards, two assists, two steals and one block. Allen Crabbe registered 17 points, four rebounds, two assists and one steal. Jarrett Allen generated a 14 - point, 12 - rebound double - double that also included two blocks. Joe Harris poured in 11 points. Enes Kanter paced the Knicks with a 23 - point, 14 - rebound double - double that also included three assists and one steal. Allonzo Trier managed 15 points and two rebounds. Emmanuel Mudiay contributed 13 points, four assists and one rebound. Mario Hezonja and Damyean Dotson pitched in 12 points apiece. Tim Hardaway, Jr. could only muster seven points on 2 - for - 12 shooting. The Nets remain on the road and pay a visit to the Philadelphia 76ers on Wednesday night, while the Knicks remain home and take on the Charlotte Hornets on Sunday evening.

The Charlotte Hornets defeated the New York Knicks, 119 - 117, at Madison Square Garden on Sunday evening. Charlotte (13 - 13) brought its record back to .500 with the relatively painless win on Sunday. The Hornets jumped out to a quick lead in the second quarter and brought it to double - digits with a run to start the third. While the Knicks (8 - 20) chipped away at the lead throughout the fourth quarter, Kemba Walker and the Hornets continued their strong 48 percent shooting night to earn the win. The Hornets overcame a career night for Knicks rookie Kevin Knox, who scored 26 points to go with 15 rebounds. Knox's standout performance was accompanied by similarly strong play from Frank Ntilikina. Ntilikina had seen multiple DNPs in the last two weeks after his slow start to the season, but on Sunday, he looked ready to go. The sophomore point guard shot 7 - of - 11 from the field en route to 18 points. Still, Charlotte was able to earn the win with ease, thanks, as usual, to a strong night from Kemba Walker. Walker scored 25 points to go with six assists and four steals in the win. It was also a big night for Tony Parker. The former San Antonio Spur delivered a gut - punch to the Knicks off the bench, scoring 16 points in just 16 minutes of action. On Wednesday, Charlotte will host the Detroit Pistons while the Knicks will travel to Cleveland to face the Cavaliers.

The Phoenix Suns defeated the host New York Knicks, 128 - 110, at Madison Square Garden on Monday, While this game was competitive in the first half, Phoenix rode a monster third quarter to victory. In fact, the Suns outscored the Knicks in the third, 41 - 17, as that allowed them to hold a double - digit lead for the entirety of the fourth quarter. Pheonix's defense came up big, as they held New York to 40 percent from the field and 26 percent from three - point range. The Suns connected on 52 percent from the field and 33 percent from long range while out - assisting the Knicks, 27 - 15. The Suns (7 - 24) were led by Devin Booker, as he collected 38 points, seven rebounds, two assists and two steals. T.J. Warren scored 19 of his 26 points in the third quarter, as he added five rebounds, three steals and two blocks to his tally. DeAndre Ayton totaled 21 points and 13 rebounds. Jamal Crawford was huge off the bench, providing six points and a season - high 14 assists. The Knicks (9 - 23) got another career - high from Emmanuel Mudiay, as he tallied 32 points, six rebounds and six assists. Kevin Knox amassed 17 points and five boards. Enes Kanter finished with 13 points, 10 rebounds and four assists. Mario Hezonja led the bench with 14 points and five rebounds. Both teams return to action on Wednesday, with Phoenix traveling to face the Boston Celtics and New York playing the Philadelphia 76ers on the road as well.

The Atlanta Hawks defeated the New York Knicks, 114 - 107, at Madison Square Garden on Friday evening. The Hawks (8 - 23) had come in having notched just two road wins in 16 tries, so it was difficult to have a positive outlook on their chances of prevailing after falling behind by a 39 - 28 score through one quarter. To its credit, Atlanta progressively battled back over the subsequent three quarters, and they sealed the victory by outscoring the Knicks (9 - 25) by a 27 - 18 margin in the final 12 minutes. The Hawks' dominance on the boards greatly helped their cause, as they outrebounded New York by a 54 - 35 margin. Kent Bazemore led the way with 22 points, a total he supplemented with six rebounds, one assist and one steal. John Collins followed with a 17 - point, 16 - rebound double - double that also included four assists. Kyle Huerter poured in 16 points. Tre Young registered 15 points, 10 assists, three rebounds and one steal. DeAndre Bembry and Alex Len managed 12 points apiece, while Jeremy Lin contributed 11. Emmanuel Mudiay paced the Knicks with 32 points and also dished out four assists. Kevin Knox went for 24 points, six rebounds, one assist and one steal. Tim Hardaway, Jr. collected 15 points, five assists and four rebounds. Noah Vonleh generated a 11 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included two assists, one steal and one block. Enes Kanter had 10 points and five rebounds. The Hawks remain on the road and tangle with the Detroit Pistons on Sunday afternoon, while the Knicks remain home and face off with the Milwaukee Bucks on Christmas Day.

The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the New York Knicks, 109 - 95, at Madison Square Garden on Tuesday afternoon. The Bucks (23 - 10) encountered a feisty Knicks (9 - 26) squad ready to defend their home court on Christmas Day, as New York forged a quick 24 - 22 lead after 12 minutes. However, Milwaukee began to assert itself with a strong 26 - point second quarter, leading to a slim 48 - 46 halftime lead. The third quarter was the pivotal period, however, as the visitors pulled away for good by adding 14 points to their advantage. New York acquitted itself well on the boards with a 58 - 50 rebounding advantage, but the Bucks' 45 percent success rate from the floor was markedly better than their hosts' 36 percent figure. Giannis Antetokounmpo led the Bucks with a 30 - point, 14 - rebound double - double that also included three assists, four steals and two blocks. Brook Lopez followed with 20 points, four boards and two blocks. Malcolm Brogdon mustered 17 points, six rebounds, four assists and three steals. Thon Maker paced the bench with 12 points and added three rebounds and two blocks. Eric Bledsoe supplied 11 points, six rebounds, five assists and one steal. Khris Middleton managed just six points on 2 - for - 12 shooting. Kevin Knox paced the Knicks with 21 points, adding six rebounds and three assists. Noah Vonleh followed with a 14 - point, 15 - rebound double - double that also included two blocks. Tim Hardaway, Jr. matched Vonleh's scoring total and added 10 rebounds, three assists and one steal. Enes Kanter totaled 12 points, six rebounds, one assist and one steal. Emmanuel Mudiay registered 11 points, five assists, three rebounds and one steal. The Bucks and Knicks meet up again on Thursday night in Milwaukee for a rematch.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the host New York Knicks, 121 - 106, at Madison Square Garden on Friday. While this wasn't a wire - to - wire win for Indiana, they led for all but a couple minutes. The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the New York Knicks, 108 - 105, at Madison Square Garden on Sunday. Redick also added 22 points, and Jimmy Butler chipped in with 16 points and eight boards. T.J. McConnell had six points and four assists off the bench. Emmanuel Mudiay might have missed the game - tying three - point shot at the end of regulation, but still had a decent game with 19 points, four assists and four rebounds. Luke Kornet thrived off the bench and chipped in with 23 points, five assists and five rebounds.

The Oklahoma City Thunder defeated the New York Knicks, 127 - 109, at Madison Square Garden on Monday afternoon. The Thunder (28 - 18) and the Knicks (10 - 35) opened the MLK-Day-slate on the NBA this Monday, but this was a one - sided game as soon as the ball started rolling. Jerami Grant chipped in with 16 points and six boards, while Steven Adams added 10 points, seven boards and three dimes. Dennis Schroder had 17 points coming off the bench. Emmanuel Mudiay added 14 points, while Noah Vonleh contributed 10 points and five boards to the losing cause. Allonzo Trier had a strong effort off the bench thanks to 16 points, eight assists, and six rebounds. Enes Kanter had 11 points.

The Houston Rockets defeated the New York Knicks, 114 - 110, at Madison Square Garden on Wednesday. Wednesday night's outing in New York City ended up being a thriller highlighted by career performances for each team. The Rockets (27 - 20) held a six - point lead with a minute to go and appeared to be well on their way to ending things, but then a 70 run by the Knicks over the next 30 seconds put the home team up by one. Ultimately, an Eric Gordon three - pointer put the Rockets up three with just over nine seconds remaining, and that was followed by a James Harden steal and dunk that ended the game. That dunk gave Harden 61 points, which is tied for the most points scored by a visiting player in Madison Square Garden, and he also recorded 15 rebounds, four assists and five steals. Eric Gordon added 20 points on 8 - of - 15 shooting from the field, and the new Rocket, Kenneth Faried, scored 11 points to make him the third and final Houston player to reach double figures. As for the Knicks (10 - 36), they were lead by a career - best performance from rookie Allonzo Trier, who scored 31 points on 12 - of - 18 shooting in 33 minutes off the bench. He hit a go - ahead layup with just 20 seconds to go, but Gordon's three ended up ruining the point guard's chances at being the hero Wednesday night. Four other New York players scored in double figures, but none scored higher than Emmanuel Mudiay's 14 points in 28 minutes. Ultimately what killed the Knicks' chances was their inability to take care of the ball, as the team committed 18 turnovers to recording just 15 assists, so it was fitting that the game ended on a Houston steal.

The Memphis Grizzlies defeated the New York Knicks, 96 - 84, at Madison Square Garden on Sunday afternoon. The Detroit Pistons defeated the host New York Knicks 115 - 89, at Madison Square Garden on Wednesday evening. The Houston Rockets defeated the Los Angeles Lakers, 125 - 115, at Staples Center on Saturday evening. Whether there's such a thing as an early - season "must win "is debatable, but the Rockets (1 - 1) came into Saturday's contest with a certain sense of urgency. Brandon Ingram and Chris Paul with just over four minutes remaining in the fourth quarter after a melee ensued following a James Harden drive to the basket. Paul posted a 28 - point, 10 - assist double - double that also included seven rebounds and a steal. Clint Capela managed a 19 - point, 12 - rebound double - double. The visiting San Antonio Spurs defeated the Los Angeles Lakers, 143 - 142, at Staples Center in overtime on Monday evening. San Antonio (2 - 1) seemingly put the nail in the coffin with just under 90 seconds remaining in regulation, as a put - back basket from LaMarcus Aldridge gave the Spurs an eight - point lead. The Lakers (0 - 3), though, did what seemed impossible and launched an 80 run in the final 88 seconds of game time to force overtime. The run was capped by a deep, game - tying three - pointer from superstar forward LeBron James. Despite the momentum shift at the end of regulation, overtime saw plenty of back - and - forth. James had a chance to help LA seal at least a second overtime at the free - throw line, but missed both shots with 11 seconds remaining in OT. The Spurs ultimately gained the lead on a Patty Mills jumper in the final seconds of overtime. In addition to his clutch put - back, Aldridge scored a game - high 37 points in the tense win. He added 10 rebounds and five assists. His fellow All-Star, the newly - acquired DeMar DeRozan, scored 32 points and dished out a whopping 14 assists to lead the team. Rudy Gay contributed another 16 points. LA, meanwhile, was without starters Brandon Ingram and Rajon Rondo, who are currently serving suspensions for their involvement in an altercation in Saturday's game against Houston. In their absence, James picked up the slack, scoring 32 points, grabbing eight rebounds, and matching DeRozan's game high of 14 assists. Sophomore forward Kyle Kuzma added a whopping 37 points in the loss. The loss extended the Lakers' losing streak to three games. The new - look team is still in search of its first win of the 2018 - 19 season. On Wednesday, San Antonio will host the Indiana Pacers while the Lakers will travel to Phoenix to face the Suns.

The Los Angeles Lakers defeated the visiting Denver Nuggets, 121 - 114, at Staples Center on Thursday evening. With the game coming down to the wire, the Lakers (2 - 3) got hot at the right time. With under 80 seconds left, LA went on a quick 50 run to pull away. Sophomore point guard Lonzo Ball started things off with a clutch three - pointer to put the Lakers up five, which was followed by a steal and breakaway dunk from Kyle Kuzma to seal the win. Los Angeles was led by a triple - double from LeBron James, who scored 28 points to go with 11 assists and 11 rebounds. Kuzma added 22 points, two of which came on his game - clinching dunk. The Lakers also saw a breakout contribution from JaVale McGee, who scored 21 points and grabbed seven rebounds in 31 minutes of action. Denver shot just 6 - of - 23 from beyond the arc. On Saturday, the Lakers will travel to San Antonio to take on the Spurs. The Nuggets, meanwhile, have the weekend off before hosting Anthony Davis and the Pelicans on Monday.

The Los Angeles Lakers defeated the Dallas Mavericks, 114,113 in a close game at Staples Center on Wednesday. It looked as though it would be an easy win for Los Angeles (3 - 5), as the team held a double - digit lead through much of the second half. Dallas (2 - 6), though, mounted an epic comeback effort, cutting the lead to six with 92 seconds of game time remaining. The Mavericks continued to whittle away at the deficit, cutting the lead to just one point on a Harrison Barnes three - pointer with 24 seconds remaining. Dallas finally tied the game on a Luka Doncic floater with only seven seconds left. With only seven seconds left, Los Angeles had one possession to try to take the lead and avoid overtime. Superstar forward LeBron James took matters into his own hands and drew a foul, but missed the first of his two free - throws with just two seconds remaining. On his second try, though, James knocked down the decisive free - throw, giving LA the one - point edge and the win. James led the Lakers with 29 points in the win. He added six assists and five rebounds. Veteran center JaVale McGee was also a key contributor in the win. McGee finished with 16 points and 15 rebounds in 34 minutes of action. As a team, the Lakers' offense was outstanding. LA shot 51 percent from the field and 10 - of - 17 from three - point range. For the Mavericks, Wesley Matthews led the way with 21 points. Harrison Barnes added another 19 points in the loss. Rookie sensation Luka Doncic continued his strong start to the season, tallying 14 points to go with seven assists and five rebounds. Doncic entered Wednesday's matchup averaging 20 points and 4 assists per game. Next up for Dallas is a visit from the New York Knicks on Friday. The Lakers, meanwhile, will travel to Portland to take on the Trail Blazers on Saturday.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the Los Angeles Lakers, 121 - 107, at Staples Center on Sunday evening. Despite missing Kawhi Leonard (ankle), the Raptors jumped out to a quick 10 - 4 start, and carried on to outscore the Lakers by a whopping 25 points in the first quarter, as they took a 42 - 17 lead into the second. The Lakers kept fighting but could not make a dent in the colossal margin, as they still trailed by 21 heading into the final frame. The Raptors cruised to their third straight win and improved to 3 - 1 on the road, while this marked the end of a two - game win streak for the Lakers, and also their third home loss of the season. Serge Ibaka led the Raptors with 34 points, 10 rebounds, two assists and two steals, in 29 minutes of action. Kyle Lowry had an amazing night, with 21 points, 15 assists, six rebounds, two steals and one block, in 33 minutes. Meanwhile, Kyle Kuzma led the Lakers with 24 points, five rebounds and two assists, in 31 minutes. LeBron James tallied 18 points, six assists, two rebounds and one block, while Lonzo Ball chipped in 12 points, nine rebounds, four assists and two steals, in 23 minutes. The Lakers shot 46 percent from the field, including, 6 - of - 24 from long range. The Lakers (4 - 6) will look to bounce back, as they play host to the Timberwolves on Wednesday. The Raptors (9 - 1) head to Utah to take on the Jazz on Monday.

The Los Angeles Lakers defeated the Minnesota Timberwolves 114 - 110 at Staples Center on Wednesday. The Lakers and Timberwolves battled all four quarters, wrestling with lead changes throughout. The Lakers came out with a run and gun style offense that saw Lonzo Ball push the pace, along with JaVale McGee finding some easy dunks down low. Minnesota entered the half with a two point lead, but the Lakers kept within striking distance all second half before taking the lead behind LeBron James' leadership. Derrick Rose had the hot hand all night, but when it mattered most, Rose's three point shot to take the lead in the waning seconds bounced off the rim after a great look at the top of the arc. The Lakers (5 - 6) were given three possessions with just under a minute left in the fourth quarter after new addition Tyson Chandler swatted back two rebounds towards Lebron James after a missed three pointer from himself and Kyle Kuzma. Chandler, who joined the team this week, made a massive impact with his nine rebounds. The Timberwolves set a new franchise record with 20 three pointers, seven of which came from the 2011 MVP Derrick Rose. Rose has seen a resurgence in his game and scored 31 points 11 - of - 17 shooting. Down 111 - 104 late in the fourth quarter, Rose hit back - to - back threes to single handedly keep his team alive. All five Minnesota starters finished in double figures scoring and all five also logged at least 37 minutes. LeBron James fell one assist shy of triple - double after he finished with 24 points, 10 rebounds and nine assists. Both the Timberwolves and Lakers will face the Sacramento Kings next, as the Kings will host a back - to - back with both teams starting with the Wolves on Friday and the Lakers Saturday.

The Los Angeles Lakers defeated the visiting Atlanta Hawks, 107 - 106, in a last - second thriller at Staples Center on Sunday evening. LeBron James won his team the game after almost giving it up, scoring the go - ahead basket on a put - back dunk with 15 seconds remaining after going 0 - of - 2 at the free - throw line. Atlanta, meanwhile, had the opportunity to answer on the final possession, putting the ball in the hands of rookie point guard Trae Young. Young drove to the basket and put up a lay - up as time expired, but was blocked by veteran center Tyson Chandler to end the game. In addition to his game - winning dunk, James led the Lakers (7 - 6) with 26 points. He added seven rebounds and four assists in the winning effort. LA is now 30 since signing Chandler as a free agent last week. Atlanta (3 - 10) found itself on the losing side once again, despite a number of stellar performances. Young had a team - high 12 assists while also scoring 20 points. Taurean Prince led the team with 23 points on 9 - of - 13 shooting. Big man Alex Len also posted a double - double, finishing with 17 points and 11 rebounds. The Hawks will continue their West Coast road trip with a visit to Golden State on Tuesday. LA, meanwhile, will host the Portland Trail Blazers on Wednesday.

The Los Angeles Lakers defeated the visiting Portland Trail Blazers, 126 - 117, at Staples Center on Wednesday evening. The Los Angeles Lakers defeated the Utah Jazz, 90 - 83, at Staples Center on Friday evening. The Orlando Magic defeated the Los Angeles Lakers, 108 - 104, at Staples Center on Sunday afternoon. The Lakers (11 - 8) and the Magic (10 - 10) played a very intense game and while Orlando seemed ready to cruise their way in the final minutes, Los Angeles mounted a furious comeback in the final 12 minutes that saw them tie the game into the final 60 seconds of the contest. The Los Angeles Lakers defeated the Indiana Pacers, 104 - 96, at Staples Center on Thursday evening. The Los Angeles Lakers defeated the visiting Dallas Mavericks, 114 - 103, at Staples Center on Friday evening. The Mavericks got out to a great start on the road, with a 17 - 6 lead, just four minutes into the quarter. They kept up the momentum and build a, 32 - 22, lead by the end of the quarter. The Los Angeles Lakers defeated the Phoenix Suns, 120 - 96, at Staples Center on Sunday afternoon. Richaun Holmes led the way with 15 points off the bench, while Josh Jackson and Trevor Ariza each added 13 points. Rookie DeAndre Ayton had a strong double - double of 10 points with 10 rebounds. The Los Angeles Lakers took down the San Antonio Spurs, 121 - 113, at Staples Center on Wednesday evening. The Los Angeles Lakers escaped with a win over the visiting Miami Heat, 108 - 105, at Staples Center on Monday evening. Kyle Kuzma was the team's leading scorer, complementing James' strong offensive output with an additional 33 points. Wade earned a double - double in what was likely his last game at Staples Center. He finished with 15 points and 10 assists off the bench. His 6 - of - 19 shooting night, though, was emblematic of his team's shaky overall offensive night. The Heat hit just 44 percent of its shots from the field in the loss and committed 17 turnovers. The Heat will visit Utah on Wednesday, while the Lakers travel to Houston to clash with the Rockets on Thursday.

The Los Angeles Lakers defeated the visiting New Orleans Pelicans, 112 - 104, at Staples Center on Friday evening.
