The Lakers finally created some separation in the second, and emerged with a four - point lead at halftime. Both teams came out strong in the second half, but the Lakers were once again able to come out of the quarter with a slight advantage, as they pushed their lead to six, heading into the final frame. The fourth quarter did not feature much scoring, but was intense nonetheless, as the Pelicans cut the deficit to three at the halfway point in the quarter. However, the Lakers answered by using an 80 over the next two minutes, to push their lead to 11, with 5:26 to go. The Lakers were able to hold on from there to earn end a two - game slide. LeBron James led the Lakers with 22 points, 14 assists, 12 rebounds and two steals, in 38 minutes. Kyle Kuzma tallied 23 points, three rebounds, one assist and a steal, while Brandon Ingram finished with 18 points, seven rebounds, two assists and a steal. The Lakers shot 47 percent from the field, including 8 - of - 32 from long range. Meanwhile, Anthony Davis led the Pelicans with 30 points, 20 rebounds, five assists and one block, in 39 minutes. Jrue Holiday tallied 18 points, 10 assists, six rebounds and three blocks, while Julius Randle added 21 points, eight rebounds, two assists and one block. The Pelicans shot 43 percent from the field, including 8 - of - 27 from deep. The Pelicans (15 - 18) will look to bounce back as they take on the Kings in Sacramento on Sunday. The Lakers (19 - 13) play host to the Grizzlies on Sunday.

The Memphis Grizzlies defeated the host Los Angeles Lakers, 107 - 99, at Staples Center on Sunday evening. The Lakers started out well but the Grizzlies closed the first quarter on a 14 - 2 run, to take a 26 - 20 lead into the second. The Lakers battled back and the teams traded the lead a couple times in the quarter, before the Grizzlies emerged with a 50 - 46 lead at halftime. The Grizzlies stayed in front for most of the third quarter, until the Lakers made a push to take a three - point lead entering the fourth. The battle continued through the fourth until the Grizzlies used a 14 - 8 run in the final few minutes to secure the road win and end a five - game losing streak. Jaren Jackson Jr. led the Grizzlies with 27 points, nine rebounds and one assist, in 30 minutes. Mike Conley tallied 17 points, eight assists, two steals and one rebound, while Marc Gasol finished with 17 points, nine rebounds, eight assists and one block, in 31 minutes. The Grizzlies shot 47 percent from the field, including 14 - of - 26 from long range. Meanwhile, LeBron James led the Lakers with 22 points, 14 rebounds, seven assists, a steal and a block, in 35 minutes. Brandon Ingram followed up with 20 points, four rebounds and three assists, while Ivica Zubac tallied 19 points, four rebounds, four blocks and one assist. The Lakers shot 49 percent from the field, including 10 - of - 30 from long range. The Lakers (19 - 14) will look to bounce back as they take on the Warriors in Golden State on Christmas Day. The Grizzlies (17 - 16) play host to the Cavaliers on Wednesday.

The Los Angeles Clippers defeated the host Los Angeles Lakers, 118 - 107, at Staples Center on Friday evening. The Clippers got out to a strong start as they led 28 - 23 after on quarter. The Lakers turned the tables in the second, as they outscored the Clippers by eight in the quarter, to take a three - point lead by halftime. However, the Clippers came out strong in the second half and regained control through the third, where they outscored the Lakers by five, to take an 82 - 80 lead into the final frame. They kept the pressure on through the fourth and outscored the Lakers by nine in the quarter, to secure their second straight win. This marked the second straight loss for the Lakers as they carry on without LeBron James (groin). Lou Williams led the Clippers with 36 points, seven rebounds and three assists, in 30 minutes off the bench. Danilo Gallinari finished with 19 points, 10 rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block, while Tobias Harris tallied nine points, 10 rebounds, one assist and one steal. The Clippers shot 44 percent from the field, including 6 - of - 19 from long range. Meanwhile, Kyle Kuzma led the Lakers with 24 points, eight rebounds and five assists, in 41 minutes. Lonzo Ball tallied 19 points, six assists, five rebounds and one steal, while Brandon Ingram added 17 points and seven rebounds. The Lakers shot 41 percent from the field, including 11 - of - 30 from long range. The Lakers (20 - 16) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Kings on Sunday. The Clippers (21 - 14) play host to the Spurs on Saturday.

The Los Angeles Lakers took down the Sacramento Kings, 121 - 114, at Staples Center on Sunday evening. Sunday was the third straight game in which the Lakers (21 - 16) were without superstar forward LeBron James, who is recovering from a groin injury. LA had dropped its first two games without James, but strong play from its young stars helped the team earn a win on Sunday. Though the Kings (19 - 17) led for much of the fourth quarter, strong late - game play from LA's Brandon Ingram helped to turn the tides. With under four minutes remaining, Ingram personally went on a 70 run, knocking down a three - pointer that gave the Lakers the lead. After a few late misses from Sacramento's De'Aaron Fox, LA was able to clinch the win on a pair of free - throws from Kentavious Caldwell-Pope. Caldwell-Pope was LA's leading scorer, providing 26 points off the bench. Ingram added another 21 points in total and also dished out nine assists. Sophomore guard Josh Hart also delivered a gem, scoring 22 points and grabbing seven rebounds. Sacramento, meanwhile, saw another strong all - around night from De'Aaron Fox. Though Fox missed a pair of crucial late - game shots, he still shot 12 - of - 19 on the night and scored 26 points. Fox continued to excel as a facilitator, dishing out three assists. Buddy Hield and Bogdan Bogdanovic each scored another 21 points. Sacramento will host the Portland Trail Blazers on Tuesday, while LA will see the Oklahoma City Thunder on Wednesday.

The visiting Oklahoma City Thunder defeated the Los Angeles Lakers, 107 - 100, at Staples Center on Wednesday evening. Neither team had led by more than six with 5:13 remaining in the fourth quarter. That changed, though, as OKC (24 - 13) brought Paul George and Steven Adams back in to close out the game. George quickly ended an 0 - of - 10 stretch for the Thunder, knocking down two straight shots and finishing with nine in the fourth quarter. After a late play in which LA's Tyson Chandler was assessed a Flagrant 1 for striking Terrence Ferguson in the face on a blocked shot, George iced the game by knocking down a pair of free - throws on behalf of the injured Ferguson. LA (21 - 17), meanwhile, dealt with an in - game injury of its own, as star forward Kyle Kuzma exited the game with a lower back contusion. For the Thunder, George led the way with 37 points and three steals. Former MVP Russell Westbrook, meanwhile, continued his shooting struggles, going just 3 - of - 20 from the field. That did not stop the star point guard from having an impact, though, as he still notched a triple - double, including a team - high 16 rebounds. LA, meanwhile, took its third loss in four games without LeBron James. James continues to be sidelined after sustaining a groin injury during a game at Golden State in late December. Brandon Ingram took on a lead role in LA's absence with James on the bench, scoring 17 points and taking a team - high 21 shots. Ingram, however, shot just 8 - of - 21 and committed four turnovers in the loss. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope led the Lakers with 25 points. On Friday, the Thunder will continue on the road with a visit to Portland. LA, meanwhile, will host the New York Knicks at Staples Center.

The New York Knicks defeated the Los Angeles Lakers, 119 - 112, at Staples Center on Friday night. Both teams took turns dominating the other at different points, but it was the Knicks (10 - 29) who were productive at the most important juncture to ensure the win. New York outscored the Lakers (21 - 18) by a 33 - 20 margin in the fourth quarter to put the finishing touches on a rare road win. Prior to that, they'd also opened the game with a big 39 - 25 lead over the first 12 minutes. Los Angeles battled back to win the middle periods, 64 - 47, which left them with a 92 - 86 advantage heading into the final period before the visitors' late surge. Tim Hardaway, Jr. paced the Knicks with 22 points, adding six rebounds and two assists. Enes Kanter generated a 16 - point, 15 - rebound double - double that also included three assists and three blocks. Trey Burke matched Kanter's scoring total. Emmanuel Mudiay supplied 15 points, seven rebounds and six assists. Kevin Knox turned in 14 points, five boards, one assist and one steal. Dewayne Dotson registered 11 points, three assists, two rebounds and four steals. Mario Hezonja posted 10 points. Brandon Ingram led the Lakers with 21 points, nine rebounds, three assists and one steal. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope managed 19 points, six boards and three assists. JaVale McGee furnished 18 points, nine boards, one assist and one block. Lonzo Ball filled out the stat sheet with 17 points, six rebounds, two assists, two steals and one block. Ivica Zubac delivered 10 points, six rebounds, two assists and one block. The Knicks remain on the road and take on the Portland Trail Blazers on Sunday night, while the Lakers pay a visit to the Minnesota Timberwolves on Sunday afternoon.

The Los Angeles Lakers defeated the Detroit Pistons, 113 - 100, at Staples Center on Wednesday evening. It was LA's eighth straight game without LeBron James (groin), but the team fared well without its star on Wednesday. The Lakers (23 - 19) jumped out to a double - digit lead in the second quarter and never looked back. The team went on a quick 90 run near the end of the first half, fueled by five straight points from point guard Lonzo Ball. The Pistons (17 - 22), meanwhile, continued to struggle with efficiency, shooting just 44 percent overall and 31 from three - point range. The story of the night was LA's Kyle Kuzma, who tallied a career - high 41 points in just 29 minutes of play. Kuzma was remarkably efficient, shooting 16 - of - 24 from the field and knocking down five three - pointers. The second - year forward was one of six double - digit scorers for the Lakers. Lonzo Ball, meanwhile, led the team with 11 assists. Detroit, meanwhile, struggled to produce any offense in the blowout loss. All-Star big man Blake Griffin scored just 16 points on 6 - of - 14 shooting, while star center Andre Drummond added only six points. In total, Detroit's starting five scored only 58 points and accounted for eight of the team's nine turnovers. The Pistons will visit Sacramento on Thursday, while the Lakers will take on Utah on Friday.

The Cleveland Cavaliers defeated the Los Angeles Lakers, 101 - 95, at Staples Center on Sunday evening. As the Lakers (23 - 21) continued to forge ahead without LeBron James (groin) in the lineup, they found an unlikely obstacle in his former team. Cleveland (9 - 35) owns the league's worst record and had dropped 12 straight heading into Sunday's matchup. Sunday's tilt with the Lakers ended the Cavaliers' skid, though, as all five starters scored in double figures en route to the win. The Cavaliers held a multiple - possession lead for much of the second half and managed to stave off a late - game comeback effort from LA. For the Lakers, the loss dropped the team to just 3 - 6 without James. Forward Cedi Osman showed flashes of the talent he showcased early in the season, scoring a team - high 20 points to lead the Cavaliers. Big man Tristan Thompson, recently returned from injury, finished with 15 points and 14 rebounds. Nearly matching Thompson's effort on the boards was Alec Burks, who tallied 13 rebounds to go with 18 points in Sunday's bounce - back win. LA, meanwhile, saw 29 points from sophomore forward Kyle Kuzma. The Utah product continued to excel in LeBron's absence, improving upon his season average of 19 points per game. As a team, though, the Lakers were not as impressive. LA shot just 40 percent and hit only seven threes in a loss that put the team in a tie with Utah for eighth in the Western Conference. LA will host another of the Eastern Conference's struggling teams when the Chicago Bulls come to town on Tuesday. Cleveland, meanwhile, will continue its West Coast trip with a visit to Portland on Wednesday.

The Los Angeles Lakers took down the visiting Chicago Bulls, 107 - 100, at Staples Center on Tuesday. The Lakers (24 - 21) continue to press on without LeBron James (groin) in the lineup. The team had dropped six of its previous nine games, but on Tuesday, they earned a comfortable win over Chicago (10 - 34). Despite recent struggles, sophomore point guard Lonzo Ball led the team with 19 points and also grabbed eight rebounds. Chicago, meanwhile, saw its offensive struggles continue, shooting just 40 percent from the field and 28 percent from three - point range. The Bulls entered Tuesday's matchup ranked last in the league in scoring at 101 points per game. In addition to Ball's strong showing, the Lakers enjoyed stellar play from forwards Brandon Ingram and Kyle Kuzma. Ingram scored 16 points and dished seven assists, while Kuzma added an additional 16 points to go with 11 rebounds. Chicago, meanwhile, saw six different players score in double digits. Unfortunately for the Bulls, no player contributed more than 18 points in the loss. Forward Jabari Parker, whose play had seen him benched in recent games, led the way with 18 points in just 16 minutes on the court in the loss. On Thursday, the Bulls will visit Denver while the Lakers will travel to Oklahoma City.

The Golden State Warriors took down the Los Angeles Lakers, 130 - 111, at Staples Center on Monday evening. The Warriors' (33 - 14) win evened the season series after the Lakers (25 - 23) trounced them on their home court on Christmas Day. Of course, that game saw the Lakers take a significant blow, as superstar LeBron James went down with a groin injury. James has been out of the Lakers' lineup ever since, and did not suit up for Monday's tilt. The Warriors, on the other hand, added one more All-Star to their already loaded lineup, as big man DeMarcus Cousins made his second appearance since returning from his Achilles tear. In characteristic fashion, the Warriors blew Monday's game wide open in the third quarter, where they outscored LA 45 - 25. Golden State already held a 10 - point halftime advantage, thanks in large part to a white - hot 21 - point first - half from Klay Thompson. The Warriors did not take their foot off the gas, however, as they racked up another 65 second - half points. Thompson in particular remained on fire, knocking down his first 10 three - point attempts in a row. He exited the game with 44 points on 17 - of - 20 shooting. On top of Thompson's impressive night, the Warriors saw 20 points from Kevin Durant, who shot 8 - of - 13 from the field. Steph Curry, meanwhile, had an off shooting night, going just 3 - of - 12 from the floor. He did, however, tally 12 assists. The Lakers, meanwhile, were without LeBron James, Rajon Rondo, or Lonzo Ball, each of whom was sidelined by an injury. In their absence, the team struggled, with only two starters scoring in double digits. Kyle Kuzma tallied 16 points, while Ivica Zubac led the team with 18 off the bench. On Thursday, the Warriors will visit the Wizards in DC, while the Lakers will host the Minnesota Timberwolves.

The Minnesota Timberwolves defeated the Los Angeles Lakers, 120 - 105, at Staples Center on Thursday. It was a slow start for the visiting Timberwolves (24 - 24) on Thursday, as they went into the locker room at half time trailing a Lakers (25 - 24) team that was without both LeBron James (groin) and Lonzo Ball (ankle). However, after taking a narrow league into the final period, Minnesota poured it on the home team over the final 12 minutes, winning the fourth quarter, 36 - 23, and leaving no doubt. Karl-Anthony Towns led the way for Minnesota with yet another double - double of 27 points and 12 rebounds in 31 minutes, while Andrew Wiggins was close behind with 23 points of his own on top of eight rebounds in 37 minutes. Additionally, with Jeff Teague (foot) out of the lineup, Jared Bayless saw 30 minutes at point guard off the bench and put together an impressive performance, as he finished with 16 points and eight rebounds in 30 minutes as a reserve. As for the Lakers, the loss was their third in a row as they continue to slid out of the playoff picture without James. All five starters scored in double figures, with Brandon Ingram's 20 points on 8 - of - 14 shooting leading the way, but the team as a whole couldn't buy a shot from behind the arc (shooting 29 percent) or take care of the basketball (19 turnovers). Kyle Kuzma, who was been a reliable offensive option as of late, really struggled to get anything going on that end of the floor, as he shot 0 - of - 4 from three and 4 - of - 12 overall en route to scoring just 10 points in 28 minutes. With this win, Minnesota took a 2 - 1 lead in the season series between these two teams.

The Los Angeles Lakers blew out the Phoenix Suns, 116 - 102, at Staples Center on Sunday evening. The win snapped a three - game losing streak for the Lakers (26 - 24) while extending Phoenix's (11 - 41) to eight games. After what had been a neck - and - neck game on Monday, Los Angeles pulled ahead late in the third quarter and never looked back. Phoenix committed costly turnovers on consecutive possessions to end the third quarter, allowing LA to maintain its momentum and a double - digit lead heading into the fourth quarter. The Lakers were led by a career night from Ivica Zubac, who had 24 points, 16 rebounds, and four blocks. The young center made the most of his extra touches with LeBron James, Kyle Kuzma, and Lonzo Ball all sidelined by injuries. Veteran point guard Rajon Rondo, who recently returned from his own injury, dished out 11 assists. Phoenix also had a large slate of injuries, with T.J. Warren, DeAndre Ayton, and De'Anthony Melton all missing Monday's tilt. Devin Booker led the team with 21 points, while Kelly Oubre, Jr. added another 17. On Tuesday, the Suns will visit San Antonio while LA will host the Philadelphia 76ers.

The Philadelphia 76ers blew out the Los Angeles Lakers, 121 - 105, at Staples Center on Tuesday evening. It was smooth sailing for Philadelphia (33 - 18), as the team led wire - to - wire. The Sixers led by 19 by the end of the first quarter, thanks to 11 points in the period from Ben Simmons. While LA (26 - 25) closed the gap to as little as eight points, the Sixers were able to hold a relatively comfortable lead for the duration of play. Philly did have a scary moment, though, when star big man Joel Embiid took a spill attempting to convert an alley - oop finish in the early fourth quarter. Embiid appeared to aggravate his back and exited for the locker room, though he returned to the bench to see the end of the game. He had 28 points and 11 rebounds before exiting. Simmons finished the game with 19 points, eight rebounds, and six assists for the Sixers, while Jimmy Butler scored another 20 points. The duo also combined for eight steals, contributing to the whopping 15 steals recorded by Philly as a team. The Lakers, again without LeBron James (groin), saw a career - high 36 points from Brandon Ingram. Ingram shot a wildly efficient 16 - of - 20 from the field and dished out five assists. Unfortunately for LA, Ingram was the only Lakers starter to record more than 12 points. JaVale McGee led the second unit with 17 off the bench. The 76ers will continue their road trip with a visit to the Warriors at Oracle Arena on Thursday. The Lakers, meanwhile, are due for a crosstown game against the Clippers on Thursday.

The Los Angeles Lakers came back from a 19 - point deficit to defeat the Houston Rockets, 111 - 106, at Staples Center on Thursday evening. The Rockets (33 - 25) seemed like a lock to start the second half of the season off with a win after they took a 19 - point third quarter lead. LeBron James and the Lakers (29 - 29), however, rallied to come back and even their record at .500. The Lakers were able to turn the tide in the final minutes after a few big shots from James. Perhaps equally important, though, was the foul trouble experienced by Houston. Reigning MVP James Harden committed three offensive fouls in the fourth quarter to foul out, while fellow All-Star Chris Paul fouled out in the final minute of action as well. LA capitalized on its opportunities at the free - throw line, shooting 27 - of - 33. LeBron led Los Angeles with 29 points. He added 11 rebounds to secure the double - double. Forward Brandon Ingram added another 27 points and 13 rebounds, while Kyle Kuzma put up 18 more to help put the team over the top. For the Rockets, Harden led the way with 30 points, preserving his historic streak of 32 straight games with at least 30 points. Chris Paul, meanwhile, flirted with a triple - double, totaling 23 points, 10 rebounds, and nine assists. In his return from a finger injury, big man Clint Capela notched 12 points and 11 rebounds. On Saturday, the Lakers will travel to New Orleans while the Rockets will visit Golden State.

The Los Angeles Lakers defeated the New Orleans Pelicans, 125 - 119, at Staples Center on Wednesday. The Lakers (30 - 31) fought hard late in the game to avoid dropping three in a row, including another against New Orleans (27 - 36). After the Pelicans cut the deficit to only one point in the final minute, Brandon Ingram put the Lakers back up three by knocking down a contested floater. From there, it was the LeBron James show, as the four - time MVP sealed the win with a turnaround three - pointer to give the Lakers a six - point advantage with just over 30 seconds remaining. The win comes as revenge after the Pelicans trounced the Lakers this past Saturday. James led the Lakers with 33 points and 10 assists. Veteran Rajon Rondo notched another double - double, scoring 11 points while dishing out a team - high 16 assists. Ingram also impressed with his play, scoring 23 points to continue his hot stretch since the All-Star break. New Orleans' Julius Randle, a former Laker, led all scorers with 35 points. Jrue Holiday finished the night with 19 points and 10 assists, while Elfrid Payton pitched in another 10 rebounds and nine assists. Anthony Davis, still on a minutes restriction following his highly - publicized trade request, had 22 points and eight rebounds in 21 minutes on the floor. Los Angeles will host the Milwaukee Bucks on Friday, while the Pelicans will visit Denver on Saturday.

The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the host Los Angeles Lakers, 131 - 120, at Staples Center on Friday night. The contest got out to a competitive start, with the Bucks taking a one - point lead after on quarter. The Lakers picked it up in the second where they outscored the visitors by seven, to take a 65 - 59 lead into halftime. The Lakers kept up the momentum to start the third, as they built a 12 - point lead by the halfway mark in the quarter. However, the Bucks rallied back to trail by just one, heading into the fourth. The score stayed tight though the fourth, with a couple of lead changes before sitting tied at 118, with 2:25 to go. Back-to-back threes from Malcolm Brogdon and Eric Bledsoe put the game out of reach, as the Bucks held on to earn clinch a playoff spot with their seventh straight win. Eric Bledsoe led the Bucks with 31 points on 12 - of - 24 shooting, nine rebounds, five assists and one block, in 30 minutes. Malcolm Brogdon followed up with 21 points, four assists and two rebounds, while Giannis Antetokounmpo added 16 points, 15 rebounds, six assists and three blocks. The Bucks shot 52 percent from the field, including 14 - of - 40 from long range. Meanwhile, LeBron James led the Lakers with 31 points, 10 assists, seven rebounds and one steal, in 38 minutes. Brandon Ingram finished with 31 points, eight rebounds, two assists and a block, while Rajon Rondo added 20 points, nine assists, eight rebounds and two steals. The Lakers shot 48 percent from the field, including 13 - of - 40 from deep. The Lakers (30 - 32) will look to bounce back as they take on the Suns on Saturday. The Bucks (48 - 14) will be right back in action, as they take on the Jazz in Utah no Saturday.

The Los Angeles Clippers took down their rival Los Angeles Lakers, 113 - 105, at Staples Center on Monday evening. The Lakers (30 - 34) entered Monday's contest in desperate need of a win. The LeBron James-led team had dropped its previous two contests and was five games out of the playoff picture heading into Monday's crosstown clash. While the Lakers seemed ready to play initially, putting up 34 points in the first quarter, the team's energy quickly began to wane. The Clippers (37 - 29) were able to regain the lead by halftime before building up a comfortable cushion in the second half. LAC started the fourth quarter with a quick 80 run to push the lead to 12, and over four minutes of scoreless basketball from the Lakers allowed the Clips to maintain their advantage. The outcome lifts the Clippers to seventh in the Western Conference while moving the Lakers to 6 games out from eighth place and the coveted final playoff spot. Early on, the Clippers saw a massive spark from Patrick Beverley. The veteran embraced the mismatch with his coverage of LeBron James and finished the first half with five steals. Danilo Gallinari, meanwhile, helped to fuel the Clippers' offensive outburst in the second half. He finished with a team - high 23 points on 9 - of - 15 shooting. The Lakers, meanwhile, saw a triple - double from veteran Rajon Rondo. Rondo, who has added a three - point shot recently, knocked down four triples on the night. James also delivered a gem, scoring 27 points to go with eight rebounds and six assists. Next on the agenda for the Lakers is a tilt with the Denver Nuggets at Staples Center on Wednesday. The Clippers, meanwhile, will host the Oklahoma City Thunder on Friday.

The Denver Nuggets blew out the Los Angeles Lakers, 115 - 99, at Staples Center on Wednesday evening. Things got off to a hot start for the Nuggets (43 - 21), who built a double - digit lead in the first quarter and led for the entirety of regulation. Denver was able to exploit two of the Lakers' (30 - 35) biggest weaknesses, holding LA to seven three - pointers and taking an 18 - 5 advantage on the offensive glass. The Lakers nearly clawed back in the early fourth quarter, when a layup from Alex Caruso was able to trim the deficit to only two points. However, Denver's Gary Harris scored on four of the next five possessions to help take the Nuggets' lead back to double figures. Harris shot 8 - of - 11 to finish with 19 points in the win. The Nuggets' leading scorer was veteran wing Will Barton, who tallied 23 points. Nikola Jokic also delivered a gem, finishing with 12 points, 17 rebounds, and eight assists. The win snapped a three - game losing streak for the Nuggets, who are now just one game out of first place in the Western Conference. LA, meanwhile, was led by 31 points and seven assists from LeBron James. James made history on Wednesday as he passed Michael Jordan for fourth on the all - time scoring list. However, the milestone was overshadowed by another loss for the Lakers, who have now dropped four in a row. LA currently sits 6 games out of the playoff picture with only 17 games remaining before the postseason. The Nuggets will visit Golden State on Friday to make a push for the top spot in the West. Los Angeles, meanwhile, will play host to the Boston Celtics on Saturday.

The Boston Celtics defeated the host Los Angeles Lakers, 120 - 107, at Staples Center on Saturday. Boston came into this game as a sizable favorite, as they added to Los Angeles' struggles here. The Celtics did most of their damage in the middle quarters, outscoring the Lakers, 68 - 52, in the second and third quarters. That allowed Boston to lead by at least five points for the entirety of the second half. Three-point shooting was key, with Boston hitting 14 - of - 38 while holding Los Angeles to 5 - of - 27. The Celtics (41 - 26) were led by Kyrie Irving, as he accumulated 30 points, seven rebounds, five assists, two steals and two blocks. Marcus Morris generated 16 points, seven rebounds and four assists. Marcus Smart amassed 16 points, two rebounds, five assists and two steals while Gordon Hayward led the bench with 15 points, two rebounds and two assists. The Lakers (30 - 36) got a triple - double from LeBron James, as he tallied 30 points, 10 rebounds and 12 assists. Moritz Wagner set career - highs with 22 points, six rebounds and three assists. Rajon Rondo accrued four points, six rebounds and nine assists. Johnathan Williams led the bench with 18 points and 10 boards. Boston returns to action on Monday, when they travel to face the Los Angeles Clippers. As for Los Angeles is a road matchup versus the Chicago Bulls on Tuesday

The Brooklyn Nets defeated the host Los Angeles Lakers, 111 - 106, at Staples Center on Friday evening. The contest got out to a competitive start, with the lead changing hands a few times, before the Lakers managed to take a three - point lead into the second. The Lakers held the lead for most of the quarter, but the Nets rallied back to take a one - point lead by halftime. The Nets came out strong in the third and pushed their lead to nine by the halfway point, but the Lakers tightened it up to make it a five - point game heading into the fourth. The Lakers did not give up and took the lead early in the fourth. The teams traded the lead through the quarter, until the Nets pulled ahead for one last time, as they held the advantage for the final four minutes, to earn their second straight win. With the loss, the Lakers are officially eliminated from playoff contention. Joe Harris was the high - point man for Brooklyn, with 26 points on 8 - of - 15 shooting, in 31 minutes. D'Angelo Russell finished with 21 points, 13 assists, three steals and two rebounds, while Jarrett Allen added 13 points, 11 rebounds and one block. The Nets shot 40 percent from the field, including 16 - of - 42 from deep. Meanwhile, JaVale McGee led the Lakers with 33 points, 20 rebounds, six blocks and one steal, in 34 minutes. LeBron James followed up with 25 points, 14 assists, nine rebounds, one steal and one block, while Kyle Kuzma tallied 18 points, five rebounds and one block. The Lakers (31 - 41) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Kings on Sunday. The Nets (38 - 36) take on the Trail Blazers in Portland on Monday.

The Los Angeles Lakers took down the Sacramento Kings, 111 - 106, at Staples Center on Sunday evening. LeBron James recorded his 81st career triple - double to help the Lakers (32 - 41) earn a narrow win over Sacramento (36 - 37). The Kings jumped out to a quick lead in the second quarter, but the Lakers responded with a 39 - point third quarter after the halftime break. Sacramento was able to make it a close game after Bogdan Bogdanovic knocked down a three - pointer to cut the deficit to just two with under 20 second remaining. However, James knocked down a pair of free - throws to make it a two - possession game, giving the Lakers the cushion they needed to close out the win. James finished with 29 points, 11 rebounds, and 11 assists. Kyle Kuzma delivered another 29 points while knocking down five three - pointers. The win comes on the heels of a 1 - 9 stretch for the Lakers, who currently occupy 11th place in the Western Conference. For the Kings, Marvin Bagley III scored 25 points and grabbed 11 rebounds off the bench. Five of Bagley's boards came on the offensive end in what proved to be a nice night for the rookie. Bogdanovic contributed another 17, but the Kings shot a dismal 38 percent from the floor as a team in the loss. Both teams will suit up again on Tuesday, with the Kings visiting Dallas and the Lakers hosting the Washington Wizards.

The Los Angeles Lakers blew out the Washington Wizards, 124 - 106, at Staples Center on Tuesday evening. The Lakers (33 - 41) earned a second straight win for the first time since the All-Star Break on Tuesday. The team distanced itself from its recent struggles with a strong offensive night, shooting 54 percent from the floor in the win. LA led from the first quarter onwards, capitalizing on a weak shooting night by the Wizards (30 - 45). Washington could not get anything to fall on Tuesday, shooting 43 percent from the field and 6 - of - 32 from beyond the arc. LeBron James scored 23 points for the Lakers while dishing out a team - high 14 assists. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope led the scoring charge for LA, pouring in 29 points in the blowout win. JaVale McGee also continued his career - best tear, scoring 20 points while grabbing 15 rebounds and blocking four shots. For the Wizards, Bradley Beal scored a game - high 32 points. The rest of Washington's starting five combined for just 27 points, though, as the team struggled to find reliable offense. Off the bench, Jabari Parker contributed 18 points. Both teams will face the second half of a back - to - back on Wednesday, with the Lakers visiting Utah and the Wizards traveling to Phoenix.

The Los Angeles Lakers defeated the visiting Charlotte Hornets, 129 - 115, at Staples Center on Friday evening. The contest got out to a high - scoring start, as the Hornets led for most of the first quarter, and took a 35 - 33 lead into the second. The Lakers kept up the pace in the second, while the visitors slowed down, as the Lakers outscored the Hornets by 12 in the quarter, to take a 10 - point lead into halftime. Both squads came out firing again in the third, as they matched each other for 32 points each in the quarter, with the Lakers taking a 101 - 91 lead into the final frame. The Lakers pushed their lead to 15 mid way through the quarter and easily held on for the home win. The loss marks the end of a four - game winning streak for the Hornets. The Lakers had three players top 20 points, led by LeBron James, who tallied 27 points, nine assists and three rebounds, in 31 minutes. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope followed up with 25 points, four rebounds, four assists and a steal, while Kyle Kuzma added 20 points, three rebounds and an assist. Rajon Rondo put on a show, as he dished 17 assists, with only one turnover, and nabbed five steals. Kemba Walker led the Hornets with 24 points, six assists, two rebounds and a steal, in 37 minutes. Dwayne Bacon followed up with 21 points, three rebounds, two assists and a steal, while Miles Bridges added 17 points, five assists, three rebounds and a steal, in 33 minutes. The Hornets (35 - 40) will look to bounce back as they take on the Warriors in Golden State on Sunday. The Lakers (34 - 42) take on the Pelicans in New Orleans on Sunday.

The Golden State Warriors blew out the Los Angeles Lakers, 108 - 90, at Staples Center on Thursday evening. The Warriors (54 - 24) wasted no time on Thursday, building a 27 - point lead by the end of the first quarter. The team poured in 18 three - pointers on the night to help preserve a comfortable lead throughout. The Lakers (35 - 44) closed the gap a bit in the fourth quarter, but it was far too little and too late for LA to stage a comeback. DeMarcus Cousins led the way for the Warriors with 21 points and 10 rebounds. Two-time MVP Steph Curry had a rare off night, shooting just 1 - of - 9 for seven points. It did not seem to matter, though, as Golden State still saw five players score in double digits en route to the blowout win. Quinn Cook added 18 points off the bench. The Lakers were led by Jonathan Williams' 17 points and 13 rebounds off the bench. The team was operating on limited capacity, as LeBron James (rest) and most of the Lakers' young core were not active on Thursday. Rookie big man Mo Wagner was the top - scoring Lakers starter with 13 points. Both teams will suit up again on Friday, with the Lakers facing the Clippers and the Warriors hosting the Cleveland Cavaliers.

The Los Angeles Lakers took down the Utah Jazz, 113 - 109, at staples Center on Sunday evening. It was the second straight win for the Lakers (37 - 44) against a playoff team, as LA managed to upset the Jazz (49 - 31) despite its slough of injuries. Operating without four members of their opening day starting five, the Lakers shot over 51 percent against a typically ironclad Utah defense. LA was tenacious on the glass, grabbing 16 offensive rebounds and outrebounding Utah 49 - 35 overall. Recent G-League callup Jemerrio Jones stood out after earning a start on Sunday. Jones grabbed 16 rebounds and dished out five assists while playing a whopping 38 minutes. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope logged a game - high 42 minutes and scored a team - high 32 points in the win. LA also saw 22 points from veteran center JaVale McGee. Utah was led by 21 points and 10 rebounds from Rudy Gobert. Donovan Mitchell scored another 19 points for the Jazz. The loss comes at an inopportune time for the Jazz, who are fighting for playoff seeding in a crowded Western Conference. With the loss, they now sit two games behind the fourth - place Portland Trail Blazers. Utah will host the Denver Nuggets on Tuesday, while the Lakers will clash with Portland.

The Portland Trail Blazers defeated the Los Angeles Lakers, 104 - 101, at Staples Center on Tuesday. Drama surrounding the Lakers' organization overshadowed the team's final game of the season on Tuesday, as Lakers (37 - 45) president Magic Johnson unexpectedly stepped down from his role this evening. Johnson held a press conference that lingered past the start time of the team's game to address his decision to move forward. On the court, though, the Lakers put up a tough fight against Portland (52 - 29), but the playoff - bound Blazers ultimately got the last laugh. Maurice Harkless came up in the clutch for Portland, scoring the team's last 10 points, including a game - winning three - pointer with just one second remaining. Harkless led the Trail Blazers with 26 points. He was also active on the defensive end, blocking four shots. Enes Kanter contributed a double - double for Portland in the win, finishing with 22 points and 16 rebounds. With the win, Portland sits at fourth in the Western Conference. However, a win on Wednesday coupled with a loss by Denver could move Portland into third place. The Lakers, meanwhile, saw 32 points from Kentavious Caldwell-Pope. It was the second straight game in which Caldwell-Pope tallied 32 points. Jemerrio Jones grabbed 15 rebounds, and all five Lakers starters scored in double figures in the narrow loss. Portland will visit Sacramento for its final game of the season on Wednesday.

The Orlando Magic defeated the visiting Miami Heat, 104 - 101, at Amway Center on Wednesday. In the opener for both of these Florida teams, it wasn't decided until the final seconds. There were numerous mistakes at the end of this game though, as there were three missed free - throws and two combined turnovers between the two teams in the final 30 seconds. Orlando was able to escape though, despite the fact that Miami ended the game on an 8 - 3 run. It was competitive throughout, as there were seven ties and 13 lead changes in total. The assist - to - turnover ratio was critical for the Magic, as they recorded four more assists than the Heat while committing four fewer turnovers. The Heat (0 - 1) were led by Goran Dragic, as he tallied 26 points, four rebounds and four assists. Josh Richardson accrued 21 points, five rebounds and three assists. Hassan Whiteside amassed 12 points, 18 boards and two blocks. Dwyane Wade was a nice spark off the bench, providing nine points, 11 rebounds and two assists. The Magic (10) got a gem out of Aaron Gordon, as he collected 26 points, 16 rebounds and two assists. Evan Fournier finished with 13 points, two rebounds and five assists. Nikola Vucevic accumulated 12 points, eight rebounds and four assists. Mo Bamba led the bench with 13 points, seven boards and two blocks. Miami has to play a dreaded second half of a back - to - back on Thursday, as they travel to play the Washington Wizards. As for Orlando, they host the Charlotte Hornets on Friday for their next outing.

The Charlotte Hornets defeated the host Orlando Magic, 120 - 88, at Amway Center on Friday. A 22 - 10 first quarter in advantage of Charlotte really set the tone in this game, as they held their lead for the final three quarters while winning each individual quarter. In fact, the Hornets held a double - digit lead for the entirety of the second half. Defense was the difference for Charlotte, holding Orlando to just 38 percent from the field and 19 percent from three - point range. Free-throw shooting was a huge factor as well, with Charlotte connecting on 17 - of - 20 and Orlando hitting just 10 - of - 14 from the charity stripe. The Hornets also dominated from long range, hitting 17 - of - 38 while the Magic connected on just 6 - of - 31 from three - point range. The Hornets (1 - 1) were led by Kemba Walker, as he tallied 26 points, two rebounds and five assists. Nicolas Batum accumulated 15 points, six rebounds, five assists and two steals. Miles Bridges led the bench with 15 points, eight rebounds and two assists. Michael Kidd-Gilchrist also played well off the bench, providing 12 points, nine rebounds, five assists and two blocks. The Magic (1 - 1) had no player score more than 14 points, as Nikola Vucevic led their starters with 12 points, eight rebounds, four assists and four blocks. Evan Fournier totaled 12 points and two boards while Aaron Gordon collected five points, 10 rebounds, two assists, two steals and two blocks. Terrence Ross led the team in scoring off the bench, dropping 14 points. Both teams play road games on Saturday for their next outings, with Orlando facing the Philadelphia 76ers and Charlotte playing the Miami Heat.

The Portland Trail Blazers defeated the host Orlando Magic, 128 - 114, at Amway Center on Thursday. This was an impressive performance from Portland, as they pulled out a wire - to - wire win. They did most of their damage in the first and fourth quarters, outscoring Orlando, 70 - 52. Both offenses were unstoppable, with Portland connecting on 55 percent of their shots while Orlando hit 50 percent from the field. The key for the Trail Blazers was the play of their backcourt, as they got a combined 63 points from their two starting guards while the Magic got just 26 points from their two backcourt players. The Trail Blazers (3 - 1) got a season - high 41 points out of Damian Lillard, as he also provided seven rebounds and six assists. C.J. McCollum accrued 22 points, two rebounds and two assists. Jusuf Nurkic finished with 18 points, 10 boards and two blocks. Zach Collins was huge off the bench, totaling 17 points, six rebounds, two assists and two steals. The Magic (2 - 3) were led by Nikola Vucevic, as he tallied 24 points, 11 rebounds, three assists and two steals. Evan Fournier accumulated 17 points, three rebounds and six assists. Aaron Gordon finished with 17 points, four rebounds and two assists. Terrence Ross was a nice spark off the bench, providing 21 points, four rebounds and two assists. Both teams play road games on Saturday for their next outing, with Portland playing the Miami Heat and Orlando traveling to play the Milwaukee Bucks.

The Sacramento Kings defeated the Orlando Magic, 107 - 99, at Amway Center on Tuesday evening. The Kings (4 - 3) came into the contest relishing in their newfound reputation as one of the fastest - paced and most offensively proficient teams in the NBA. However, they were also on the second game of a back - to - back swing through the Sunshine State after a big win in Miami on Monday, so it remained to be seen how they'd respond. The Magic (2 - 5) appeared to catch the visitors a bit flat early, jumping out to a 31 - 26 first - quarter lead. However, Sacramento turned it on from that point, flashing the impressive offense that's defined the early portion of their season by outscoring their hosts, 59 - 41, over the second and third periods. That left them in the driver's seat heading into the final 12 minutes, which eventually resulted in their second straight road victory. The Kings enjoyed a particularly expansive advantage in the shooting front, as they drained 49 percent of their attempts while limiting the Magic to a 40 percent success rate. Buddy Hield led the way for Sacramento with a 25 - point, 11 - rebound double - double that also included three assists and one block. Nemanja Bjelica supplied 21 points, eight rebounds, one assist, two steals and one block. Willie Cauley-Stein generated a 14 - point, 11 - rebound double - double of his own, while De'Aaron Fox matched the big man's scoring total and added five assists, two rebounds and two steals. Troy Williams (12 points, five rebounds, one assist, two blocks) and Marvin Bagley III (10 points, nine rebounds, two rebounds, one steal, one block) were very productive off the bench. Aaron Gordon paced the Magic with 18 points, and he added 10 rebounds, three assists, two steals and two blocks. Terrence Ross came off the bench to pour in 17 points. Nikola Vucevic contributed 15 points and a game - high 15 rebounds. He also dished out five assists. Jonathon Simmons supplied 12 points, five assists and three rebounds. Jonathan Isaac and Evan Fournier pitched in nine points apiece. The Kings remain on the road and take on the Atlanta Hawks on Thursday night, while the Magic remain home and tangle with the Los Angeles Clippers on Friday evening.

The Los Angeles Clippers defeated the host Orlando Magic, 120 - 95, at Amway Center on Friday. It's rare to see a home team dominated so thoroughly in the NBA but that was, unfortunately, the case for the Magic here. The Clippers really made their mark in the second quarter, outscoring Orlando, 35 - 22. The Magic never got the game within an eight - point margin from there, as the Clippers led by at least 13 points for the entirety of the fourth quarter. Three-point shooting was the difference in the game, with Los Angeles connecting on 13 - of - 26 from long range while holding Orlando to just 4 - of - 17. Rebounding was also huge, with the Clippers outrebounding the Magic, 50 - 40. Bench production was also critical, with Los Angeles winning that battle, 65 - 35. The Clippers (5 - 4) got a vintage performance from Lou Williams off the bench, as he provided 26 points, three rebounds and three assists. Tobias Harris led the starters with 21 points, seven rebounds and two assists. Boban Marjanovic got a rare start and accrued 10 points, 11 rebounds and two assists. Montrezl Harrell also played well off the bench, totaling 10 points, 12 boards and three blocks. The Magic (2 - 6) were led by Nikola Vucevic, as he tallied 22 points, 11 rebounds, three assists and three blocks. Evan Fournier finished with 19 points, three rebounds, four assists and three steals. D.J. Augustin was the only other Orlando player in double figures, as he collected 13 points, five rebounds and three assists. On deck for Orlando is a road matchup versus the San Antonio Spurs on Sunday. As for Los Angeles, they're off until Monday when they play host to the Minnesota Timberwolves.

The Orlando Magic defeated the visiting Cleveland Cavaliers, 102 - 100, at Amway Center on Monday. It's rare to see a game with just seven ties and five lead changes come down to the last shot but that was the case here. Evan Fournier played the hero, as he hit a game - winning jumper at the buzzer to break a tied game. Orlando rode a big fourth quarter to victory, outscoring Cleveland, 32 - 21, in the final quarter. The Magic won despite being dominated in shooting, as Orlando shot just 45 percent from the field and 32 percent from three - point range while Cleveland hit 51 percent from the field and 44 percent from long range. Transition offense was the only notable advantage for Orlando, as they won the fastbreak scoring, 21 - 11. The Cavaliers (1 - 9) were led by George Hill, as he tallied 22 points, four rebounds, six assists and four steals. Tristan Thompson amassed 19 points, 16 rebounds and four assists. Cedi Osman totaled 11 points and 10 boards. J.R. Smith and Jordan Clarkson scored 14 points apiece to lead the bench. The Magic (4 - 6) were led by Aaron Gordon, as he accrued 23 points, nine rebounds and three assists. Evan Fournier collected 15 points, five assists and three steals to go along with his game - winner. Nikola Vucevic accumulated 14 points, 10 rebounds and two blocks. Terrence Ross led the bench with 15 points and two boards. Both teams return to action on Wednesday, with Orlando welcoming the Detroit Pistons to Amway Center and Cleveland hosting the Oklahoma City Thunder.

The Detroit Pistons defeated the host Orlando Magic, 103 - 96, at Amway Center on Wednesday. This was truly a battle of four quarters, as each individual quarter was decided by at least five points. Detroit did their damage in the second and fourth quarters, outscoring Orlando, 57 - 36. The swings are evident by the fact that there were eight ties and nine lead changes in total. Rebounding was the difference for the Pistons, as they outrebounded the Magic, 50 - 40. The 13 steals recorded by Detroit marked a season - high, as they forced 20 turnovers from the Magic. Free-throw shooting was also critical, as Orlando hit just 7 - of - 8 from the charity stripe while Detroit connected on 18 - of - 20. The Pistons (5 - 5) got another monster double - double out of Andre Drummond, as he tallied 23 points, 19 rebounds, two assists and three steals on 10 - of - 16 shooting. Blake Griffin finished with 20 points, five rebounds and three assists. Reggie Jackson totaled 15 points and four assists. Stanley Johnson led the bench with 13 points, six rebounds and three assists. The Magic (4 - 7) were led by Evan Fournier, as he collected 27 points, four rebounds, three assists and three steals on 12 - of - 19 shooting. D.J. Augustin accumulated 16 points, four rebounds and seven assists. Aaron Gordon amassed 15 points, 10 rebounds and six assists. Terrence Ross led the bench with 15 points and four boards. Both teams return to action on Friday, with Orlando playing host to the struggling Washington Wizards and Detroit traveling to face the Atlanta Hawks.

The Orlando Magic defeated the visiting Washington Wizards, 117 - 108, at Amway Center on Friday. While Washington led for the majority of the first quarter, Orlando never relinquished the lead from there. In fact, the Magic led by 15 points at the half, as they held a double - digit lead for the majority of this game. Orlando's offense was on point, as they connected on 51 percent from the field, 42 percent from three - point range and 84 percent from the free - throw line. Rim protection was also key, with the Magic doubling up the Wizards in blocks, 6 - 3. The Wizards (2 - 9) were led by Bradley Beal, as he tallied 27 points, four rebounds, six assists and two steals. John Wall accrued 19 points, seven rebounds, 12 assists and two steals. Dwight Howard amassed 12 points and six boards. Kelly Oubre Jr. led the bench with 19 points, four rebounds and two steals. The Magic (5 - 7) got a double - double out of Nikola Vucevic, as he collected 21 points, 14 rebounds, three assists and two blocks. Aaron Gordon totaled 20 points, seven rebounds and four assists. Evan Fournier finished with 15 points, four rebounds, six assists and two steals. Mo Bamba, Terrence Ross and Jerian Grant all reached double figures in scoring off of the bench. On deck for Washington is a road matchup versus the Miami Heat on Saturday. As for Orlando, they travel to The Big Apple to play the New York Knicks on Sunday.

The Orlando Magic defeated the Philadelphia 76ers, 111 - 106, at Amway Center on Wednesday night. The 76ers (9 - 7) featured Jimmy Butler for the first time since acquiring him from the Minnesota Timberwolves, but that wasn't enough to secure the win on the road as the Magic (7 - 8) used a huge comeback to secure the win following their Monday loss against the Washington Wizards. But in reality, this game shifted leads time and time against. Philadelphia jumped to a 30 - 27 lead in the first quarter, but Orlando came back and finished the first half up by one (53 - 52). Philly recovered control of the game with a 35 - 23 third quarter, but the Magic flipped the script in the fourth quarter and with a 35 - 19 lead in the final 12 minutes (including a 210 scoring run) and secured a huge win against one of the top contenders in the Eastern Conference. Nikola Vucevic led the way for the Magic with an impressive performance of 30 points, eight rebounds, four assists and two blocks. Aaron Gordon had 17 points, six rebounds and six assists, while Wesley Iwundu contributed 11 points and two steals. Two bench players made a big impact, as Jonathon Simmons had 12 points and Terrence Ross added 15, including a decisive three - pointer with less than 10 seconds on the clock. J.J. Redick was the top scorer for the 76ers with 22 points, but he also added six assists and four rebounds. Joel Embiid had a triple - double since he contributed with 19 points, 13 rebounds and 10 assists. Wilson Chandler had 14 points, and debutant Jimmy Butler chipped in with 14 points in 33 minutes. Ben Simmons only had nine points, six assists and three rebounds.

The Orlando Magic defeated the visiting Los Angeles Lakers, 130 - 117, at Amway Center on Saturday. While Los Angeles held the lead for the first 15 minutes of this game, Orlando dominated from there. In fact, the Magic outscored the Lakers, 75 - 50 in the second and third quarters. In addition, Orlando held a double - digit lead for the final 20 minutes of this game. The Magic ended up shooting 54 percent from the field while holding the Lakers to 48 percent shooting. Ball movement was also critical, with Orlando out - assisting Los Angeles, 28 - 22. The Lakers (8 - 7) were led by LeBron James, as he tallied 22 points, four rebounds and seven assists. Brandon Ingram totaled 17 points, six rebounds and seven assists. Lonzo Ball failed to score but provided five rebounds, four assists and two steals. Lance Stephenson led the bench with 19 points, six rebounds and three assists. The Magic (8 - 8) got a monster double - double out of Nikola Vucevic, as he accrued 36 points, 13 rebounds and two steals on 15 - of - 23 from the field. D.J. Augustin amassed 22 points and seven assists. Evan Fournier finished with 15 points, five rebounds and four assists. Jonathan Simmons was a huge spark off the bench, providing 12 points, five rebounds and six assists. Both teams return to action on Sunday, with Orlando playing host to the New York Knicks and Los Angeles traveling to Florida the Miami Heat on the road.

The Orlando Magic defeated the New York Knicks, 131 - 117, at Amway Center on Sunday evening. The Magic (9 - 8) have shown a penchant for some prolific tallies on the scoreboard this season, and Sunday shaped up as a possible scenario for another big offensive night. That much was confirmed from the opening tip, as Orlando racked up 44 first - quarter points and held a 67 - 66 halftime lead on the Knicks (4 - 13). They tightened up their defense in the second half, limiting New York to under 30 points in each of the final two periods while compiling another 64 to secure the victory. As their final point total implies, the home squad enjoyed a sharp shooting night, draining 57 percent of their attempts. The bench played a pivotal role for the Knicks, but it was Tim Hardaway, Jr. who led the way with 32 points. He added two rebounds, two assists and three steals. Trey Burke followed with 31 points in 29 minutes on the second unit. Enes Kanter provided a 21 - point, 19 - rebound double - double while playing 38 minutes off the bench. Emmanuel Mudiay was the only other double - digit scorer with 12 points. Aaron Gordon paced the Magic with 31 points, a total he supplemented with two assists, one rebound and one steal. Nikola Vucevic had a near triple - double with 28 points, 10 rebounds and nine assists. Evan Fournier totaled 19 points, six assists, four rebounds, one steal and one block. Jonathan Isaac delivered 16 points, four boards, three assists, two steals and one block. D.J. Augustin generated 12 points, seven assists and three rebounds. Terrance Ross poured in 10 points off the bench. The Knicks return home to take on the Portland Trail Blazers on Tuesday night, while the Magic remains home and tangles with the Toronto Raptors on Tuesday evening as well.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the Orlando Magic, 93 - 91, at Amway Center on Tuesday. The Raptors (14 - 4) and the Magic (9 - 9) played a tight encounter on Tuesday, as this game was decided on a last - second bucket by Danny Green with only 0 seconds remaining after several back - and - forth buckets down the stretch. Toronto jumped ahead in the game with a 29 - 17 lead after the first quarter, but Orlando flipped the script in the subsequent two quarters: 20 - 18 in the second, and 38 - 26 in the third one. As such, the Magic entered the final 12 minutes of action with a two - point lead. But Toronto once again showed their ability to close games down, and ended winning after a 20 - 16 fourth quarter, and Green's jumper following an assist from Kyle Lowry. It was a thrilling end for a tight encounter that was decided down to the wire. Four Toronto players scored in double digits, and all nine players that saw action scored at least four points. Kawhi Leonard led the way with 18 points and six rebounds, while Pascal Siakam contributed with 15 points and nine boards. Green not only scored the game - winning shot, but he ended with 13 points. Serge Ibaka chipped in with 14 points, nine rebounds and four assists. Evan Fournier was the highest - scorer in the game since he finished with 27 points, four assists, and three rebounds. Aaron Gordon scored 16 points with nine rebounds and three blocks, and Nikola Vucevic posted a strong double - double of 14 points, 17 boards and four assists. No other player scored in double digits, but Jonathan Isaac (nine points, five boards) and Mo Bamba (seven points, five rebounds) contributed off the bench.

The Denver Nuggets defeated the host Orlando Magic, 124 - 118, at Amway Center on Wednesday evening. The Nuggets got out to a good start on the road, as they built a 22 - 10 lead early on, however the home team battled back to cut the deficit to just three points by the end of the quarter. The Magic continued their push early in the second, where they tied it up at 33. The second quarter was tight the whole way, as the Magic outscored the Nuggets, 26 - 25, in the quarter. The teams played to a standstill through the third, as they poured in 32 points each. The Magic trailed by two to start the fourth, but fought hard, swapping the lead back - and - forth with the Nuggets. The Magic trailed by three with just a few seconds left in regulation, when Terrence Ross hit a clutch three to send the game to overtime. Unfortunately for the home team, the Nuggets took control in overtime, where they outscored the Magic, 12 - 6, to earn their seventh straight win. Jamal Murray led the Nuggets with 31 points, eight assists, four rebounds and one steal, in 46 minutes. Paul Millsap came up big with 18 points, eight rebound and two assists, while Nikola Jokic tallied 12 points, 13 assists, eight point and one steal. The Nuggets shot 54 percent from the field, including 11 - of - 19 from long range. Meanwhile, Nikola Vucevic led the Magic with 24 points, 15 rebounds and four assists, in 37 minutes. Evan Fournier tallied 26 points, eight rebounds, four assists and one block, while Aaron Gordon tallied 19 points, six rebounds, five assists, one steal and one block. The Magic shot 47 percent from the field, including 20 - of - 49 from long range. The Magic (12 - 13) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Pacers on Friday. The Nuggets (17 - 7) take on the Hornets in Charlotte on Friday.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the Orlando Magic, 112 - 90, at Amway Center on Friday evening. The Pacers (15 - 10) jumped out to a 57 - 45 halftime lead, and that proved to be enough cushion to for a comfortable win. Indiana prevailed in every quarter and won both the shooting and turnover battles over the Magic (11 - 13) by healthy margins. They drained a solid 47 percent of their attempts while limiting Orlando to a 40 percent figure, including 24 percent from three - point range. They also took the ball from their hosts on 14 occasions while only committing nine turnovers themselves. The Pacers' bench saw some extended run due to the sizable second - half advantage and contributed 49 points. Bojan Bogdanovic led the Pacers with 26 points and added three rebounds, two assists and one steal. Cory Joseph followed with a bench - leading 15 points. Thaddeus Young supplied 14 points, seven rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block. Kyle O'Quinn generated a 12 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included two assists, two steals and two blocks over 27 minutes off the bench. Tyreke Evans poured in 11 points, while Myles Turner registered 10 points, six rebounds and one block. Nikola Vucevic paced the Magic with a 22 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included two assists. Aaron Gordon posted a 20 - point, 14 - rebound double - double and added four assists, one steal and one block. Terrence Ross mustered 11 points to lead the second unit. Evan Fournier finished with nine points. The Pacers head back home and face the Sacramento Kings on Saturday evening, while the Magic pay a visit to the Dallas Mavericks on Monday night.

The Orlando Magic defeated the Chicago Bulls, 97 - 91, in Mexico City, at Mexico City Arena on Thursday evening. The Bulls took the lead early on, but the Magic were able to keep it close, as they trailed 26 - 24 at the end of the quarter. The Magic picked up the momentum in the second, and built a 10 - point lead by the halfway mark of the quarter. They held no to take a 51 - 46 lead at the half. The Bulls came out tough in the third, but the Magic did not back down, and maintained a 77 - 71 lead to start the final frame. The Bulls started off the quarter strong again, this time taking the lead, as they pulled ahead 81 - 77 with 7:23 left in the contest. The Magic grinded it out down the stretch, as they held a one - point lead for almost two minutes down the stretch, allowing them to come up clutch on the offensive end, thanks to a couple of timely buckets by Nikola Vucevic. Vucevic led the Magic with 26 points, 10 rebounds, two assists, two steals and one block, in 32 minutes. D.J. Augustin followed up with 15 points, seven rebounds and two assists, while Evan Fournier and Jonathan Isaac added 10 points each. The Magic shot 42 percent from the field, including 11 - of - 33 from long range. Meanwhile, Zach LaVine led the Bulls with 23 points, five assists, three rebounds and two steals, in 40 minutes. Justin Holiday followed up with 18 points, five rebounds, three steals and two assists, while Bobby Portis chipped in 15 points, seven rebounds, one assist and one steal, in 21 minutes off the bench. The Bulls (6 - 23) will look to bounce back as they take on the Spurs in San Antonio on Saturday. The Magic (13 - 15) play host to the Jazz on Saturday.

The Orlando Magic defeated the Utah Jazz, 96 - 89, in Mexico City on Saturday afternoon. The Magic (14 - 15) and Jazz (14 - 16) engaged in a tightly contested first half, with Utah holding a slim two - point halftime advantage. They managed to add another two points to their lead in the third quarter, but Orlando won the shootout that unfolded over the final 12 minutes. The Magic managed to outscore the Jazz by a 41 - 30 margin in the fourth period, with their 47 percent shooting helping them overcome 22 turnovers. Donovan Mitchell spearheaded the Jazz with 24 points. Derrick Favors mustered 21 points, eight rebounds and two assists. Ricky Rubio generated 15 points, four rebounds, four assists and two steals. Rudy Gobert totaled only six points but hauled in 13 rebounds and dished out two assists, recorded two steals and managed two blocks. Evan Fournier paced the Magic with 24 points, supplementing them with seven rebounds and one steal. Terrence Ross produced a bench - leading 19 points. Nikola Vucevic turned in 15 points, 19 rebounds, five assists and two blocks. D.J. Augustin supplied 11 points, five assists and two rebounds. Aaron Gordon managed a modest eight points and added three assists, two rebounds and one steal. The Jazz next pay a visit to the Houston Rockets on Monday night, while the Magic head back home to take on the San Antonio Spurs on Wednesday evening.

The San Ajntonio Spurs defeated the Orlando Magic, 129 - 90, at Amway Center on Wednesday evening. The Spurs (17 - 15) came into the contest running hot, having claimed wins in five of their prior six times on the court. San Antonio's chances of extending that streak exponentially grew when it was revealed that star big man Nikola Vucevic would miss the game for the Magic (14 - 16) due to personal reasons. San Antonio set the tone by forging a 66 - 44 halftime lead that essentially sealed the win for them in just two quarters. However, they put the final nail in the coffin in the third quarter by compiling 38 points, a prolific amount they accomplished with excellent shooting up and down the roster. The Spurs finished with a 64 percent success rate from the floor, including 63 percent from three - point range. They were just as effective on the other end by limiting Orlando to a meager 38 percent figure. LaMarcus Aldridge paced the Spurs with 20 points, a total he supplemented with four assists, three rebounds and two steals. Marco Belinelli poured in 18 points to lead the bench. DeMar DeRozan and Bryn Forbes contributed matching 17 - point tallies. DeRozan added seven rebounds, six assists and one steal, while Forbes posted four boards. Rudy Gay supplied 14 points, six rebounds, three assists and one block. D.J. Augustin led the Magic with 17 points and added two assists and one steal. Aaron Gordon contributed 12 points, nine rebounds and seven assists. Evan Fournier matched Gordon's scoring total and also collected two rebounds, one assist and one steal. Jonathan Isaac delivered 10 points, five rebounds and one assist. Mo Bamba drew the start for Vucevic and contributed seven points, eight rebounds, two assists, two steals and two blocks. The Spurs head back home and take on the Minnesota Timberwolves on Friday night, while the Magic pay a visit to the Chicago Bulls on Friday evening as well.

The Miami Heat defeated the host Orlando Magic, 115 - 91, at Amway Center on Sunday evening. The Heat got out to a great start on the road by outscoring the Magic by 11 in the first quarter. The Magic tightened up in the second and cut the deficit to nine by halftime. However, the visitors showed no mercy, as they came storming out in the third to outscore the Magic by 10 in the quarter and take a 19 - point lead into the final frame. The Magic had no answer as their state rivals cruised to the 24 - point win. This marks the fifth straight win for the Heat, and the third loss in a row for the Magic. The Heat had six players score in double digits, led by Tyler Johnson, who finished with 25 points, 20 of which he scored in the third quarter alone. Justise Winslow added 22 points, six rebounds, five assists and four steals, while Josh Richardson tallied 15 points, 10 rebounds, four assists and two steals. The Heat shot 51 percent from the field, including 16 - of - 31 from long range. Meanwhile, Evan Fournier led the Magic with 17 points, six rebounds, four assists and a steal, in 26 minutes. The Washington Wizards defeated the Orlando Magic, 95 - 91, at Amway Center on Friday night. The Orlando Magic defeated the visiting Brooklyn Nets, 102 - 89, at Amway Center on Saturday. The Orlando Magic defeated the Minnesota Timberwolves, 122 - 112, at Amway Center on Thursday evening. Augustin contributed 14 points, five boards and five dimes. Isaiah Briscoe delivered 10 points, three assists and two rebounds. The Orlando Magic defeated the Golden State Warriors, 103 - 96, at Amway Center on Thursday evening. The Orlando Magic defeated the New York Knicks, 114 - 100, at Amway Center on Wednesday. The Magic (39 - 40) are on the verge of the playoff bubble and they had their backs against the wall entering this game against a Knicks (15 - 63) team that keeps both eyes on the Draft Lottery and just want the season to end. The first quarter ended with a 26 - 26 score, but the Magic would pull away in the second quarter and they'd never look back thanks to a 32 - 19 score. Even though the Knicks kept things close the rest of the way (29 - 27 win in the third and 26 - 29 loss in the fourth), they just couldn't bounce back and ended losing deservedly. Meanwhile, Orlando kept themselves alive for one more day on the playoff race. And that's all they could ask for at this stage. As it has been the trend during the entire season, Nikola Vucevic once again was Orlando's best player since he finished with 29 points, 13 rebounds and three assists. Evan Fournier chipped in with 19 points, while Aaron Gordon filled the stat sheet with 19 points, seven rebounds and six assists. Terrence Ross delivered a strong performance off the bench since he scored 23 points while adding four rebounds and five assists in only 24 minutes. Only four Knicks scored in double digits although all of them were part of the starting lineup. Mario Hezonja led the way with 29 points, nine rebounds and five assists, while Kevin Knox chipped in with 21 points and four boards. Mitchell Robinson contributed 12 points, nine rebounds, three steals and two blocks. Emmanuel Mudiay had 13 points with 10 assists.

The Orlando Magic defeated the visiting Atlanta Hawks, 149 - 113, at Amway Center on Friday evening. The Magic got out to a great start at home, with a 42 - 18 lead after one quarter. They kept their foot on the gas in the second, while the Hawks managed to scored 30 points in the quarter, the Magic outscored them by nine, to take a 33 - point into the halftime. John Collins added 20 points, six rebounds, one assist and one steal, while DeAndre' Bembry tallied 14 points, 10 rebounds, four assists and three rebounds. The Hawks shot 44 percent from the field, including 10 - of - 39 from long range. The Hawks (29 - 51) will look to bounce back as they take on the Bucks in Milwaukee on Sunday. The Magic (40 - 40) take on the Celtics on Sunday.

The Dallas Mavericks defeated the Minnesota Timberwolves, 140 - 136, at American Airlines Center on Saturday evening. The tone for what would turn out to be a scoreboard - busting affair was set in the first quarter, with the two clubs combining for 83 points during the period. The Mavericks (1 - 1) tightened up enough on defense during the second period to erase an eight - point deficit and send the contest into intermission deadlocked at 69 - 69. Both teams essentially matched each other basket for basket in the third, and the Timberwolves (1 - 2) entered the final quarter with a slim two - point lead. However, Dallas saved their best for last, putting up a game - high 43 points in the fourth quarter. Dennis Smith, Jr. scored the final three points on free throws after Minnesota had gotten to within a point after a pair of Karl-Anthony Towns buckets from the charity stripe with 4 seconds left. Towns led the way for Minnesota with 31 points and added five rebounds, two assists, one steal and one block. Derrick Rose followed with a bench - leading 28 points, a total he supplemented with five rebounds, five assists, two steals and one block. Jeff Teague just missed out on a double - double with 22 points, nine assists, two rebounds and one steal. Andrew Wiggins poured in 19 points and also supplied three rebounds, two assists and one steal. Taj Gibson's contributions included nine points and six boards, while first - round pick Josh Okogie pitched in six points, five boards, two assists and one steal while filling in for Jimmy Butler (rest). Dallas' first - rounder Luka Doncic made significantly more noise, leading the Mavericks with 26 points. He also posted six rebounds, three assists, two steals and one block. DeAndre Jordan posted a 22 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included one assist, five blocks and two steals. Dennis Smith, Jr., Wesley Matthews and Dwight Powell turned in a trio of 19 - point tallies, the latter doing so off the bench. J.J. Barea was productive off the second unit as well, pitching in a 12 - point, 11 - assist double - double that also included a rebound and two steals. The Timberwolves head back home for a Monday night showdown with the Indiana Pacers, while the Mavericks remain home and face the Chicago Bulls on that same evening.

The Dallas Mavericks defeated the Chicago Bulls, 115 - 109, at American Airlines Center on Monday evening. The visiting Bulls (0 - 3) impressively jumped out to a 61 - 59 halftime lead, with some red - hot shooting from Zach LaVine helping lead the way. However, Dallas countered with a 41 - 34 edge on the boards and by committing four fewer turnovers. LaVine tallied a game - high 34 points, which he supplemented with three rebounds, two assists, two steals and one block. Jabari Parker followed with a bench - leading 20 points and added three rebounds, an assist and a steal. Justin Holiday poured in 16 points, while Bobby Portis contributed 12 points, eight rebounds and two blocks in another start at power forward. Kris Dunn went for nine points, seven assists and four rebounds in his season debut. Wesley Matthews' 20 points paced the Mavericks. He added four assists, two rebounds and two steals. Luka Doncic provided 19 points, six assists, three rebounds and one steal. DeAndre Jordan posted an 18 - point, 16 - rebound double - double that also included one block. The forward trio of Dorian Finney-Smith, Dwight Powell and Maxi Kleber all generated 12 - point contributions. Finney-Smith and Kleber also brought down four rebounds each, while Powell had four boards and four assists. The Bulls head back home to face the Charlotte Hornets on Wednesday evening, while the Mavericks hit the road and take on the Atlanta Hawks on Wednesday night as well.

The visiting Utah Jazz defeated the Dallas Mavericks, 113 - 104, at American Airlines Center on Sunday. Utah withstood a tough comeback effort from the Mavericks, re - establishing a strong lead in the third quarter after having given away an 11 - point advantage in the second. The Jazz went on an 18 - 6 run in the late third and early fourth quarters, rebuilding a lead after the Mavericks tied it at 73 - 73. Dallas cut the lead to as little as six in the fourth, but Utah was able to hold firm until the final buzzer. Rudy Gobert led the Jazz (4 - 3) with 23 points and 16 rebounds in the win. Six of Gobert's rebounds came on the offensive end, and he shot 9 - of - 13 from the field. The reigning Defensive Player of the Year also tallied two steals and three blocks on the defensive end. Sophomore guard Donovan Mitchell also made a big contribution, scoring 20 points on 10 - of - 19 shooting. Dallas (2 - 4) saw a similarly impressive night from its own All-Star center, DeAndre Jordan. Jordan flirted with a triple - double, as he scored 12 points, grabbed 19 rebounds, and dished out nine assists in the loss. Dennis Smith, Jr. led the team with 27 points and hit 3 - of - 4 three - point attempts on the night. As a whole, though, the Mavericks could not find their rhythm offensively. The team shot just 42 percent on the night. The Mavericks will travel to San Antonio to take on the Spurs on Monday, while the Jazz have three days of rest before taking on the Timberwolves in Minnesota on Wednesday.

The New York Knicks defeated the Dallas Mavericks, 118 - 106, at American Airlines Center on Friday evening. The Knicks (3 - 6) impressively came out of the gates strong, taking a 33 - 27 first - quarter lead. However, the Mavericks (2 - 7) were able to climb all the way back and carry a slim three - point lead into halftime. Dewayne Dotson and Mario Hezonja each provided 11 points, with the former also supplying eight rebounds. Dennis Smith, Jr. led the Mavericks with 23 points and also posted two rebounds. Dorian Finney-Smith followed with a bench - leading 19 points and seven rebounds. He added two assists and two steals. Luka Doncic managed 18 points, nine rebounds, six assists and one steal. Harrison Barnes turned in 14 points, two assists and one rebound. The Knicks remain on the road and pay a visit to the Washington Wizards on Sunday evening, while the Mavericks remain home and also tangle with the Wizards in their next game, which unfolds Tuesday night.

The Dallas Mavericks defeated the visiting Washington Wizards, 119 - 100, at American Airlines Center on Tuesday, In a battle between two struggling teams, Dallas prevailed with a dominating win. In fact, they led for all but one minute, as they held a double - digit lead for over half of this fixture. The Mavericks ended the game strong, finishing on a 20 - 7 run. The Wizards (2 - 8) were led by John Wall, as he tallied 24 points, four rebounds, 10 assists and three steals. Bradley Beal finished with 19 points, six rebounds, four assists and two blocks. Otto Porter Jr. accrued 19 points, six rebounds, four assists, two steals and two blocks. Dwight Howard amassed eight points and 11 boards. The Mavericks (3 - 7) were led by Luka Doncic, as he accumulated 23 points, six rebounds and three assists. Wesley Matthews totaled 22 points and two boards. The Dallas Mavericks defeated the Oklahoma City Thunder, 111 - 96, at American Airlines Center on Saturday evening. The Mavericks (4 - 8) haven't exactly enjoyed a smooth start to their season, but the little success they have had, they've found on their home floor. Dallas had secured all three of their wins at American Airlines Center, and Saturday, they were facing a short - handed Thunder (7 - 5) squad once again playing without Russell Westbrook (ankle).
