Dallas shined on both ends of the floor, shooting 56 percent from the floor (including 48 percent from three - point range) while limiting the Thunder to a 39 percent success rate. Paul George and Steven Adams co - led the Thunder with matching 20 - point, 13 - rebound double doubles. Dennis Schroder drew another start for Westbrook and posted 19 points, six rebounds, three assists and two steals. Jerami Grant provided 13 points, two rebounds, two assists, two steals and one block. Luka Doncic paced the Mavericks with 22 points and added eight assists, six rebounds and one steal. J.J. Barea followed with 21 points, five assists, three rebounds and one steal in 22 minutes off the bench. Harrison Barnes and Dorian Finney-Smith posted matching 11 - point tallies, while Dennis Smith, Jr. turned in 10 points, five assists, three rebounds, two steals and one block. The Thunder heads back home and takes on the Phoenix Suns on Monday night, while the Mavericks hit the road and tangle with the Chicago Bulls on Monday evening as well.

The Dallas Mavericks defeated the visiting Utah Jazz, 118 - 68, at American Airlines Center on Wednesday evening. The Jazz got out to a good start on the road, with a 15 - 10 lead halfway into the first quarter. However, the Mavericks rallied back to take a 30 - 24 lead into the second. The Jazz came back to start the second and tied the game at 34, just a couple minutes into the quarter, but the Mavericks turned it up a notch, once again, to build a 58 - 46 by halftime. The Mavs did not look back from there as they held the Jazz to just 22 points for the entire third and fourth quarter, while they poured in 60 points, to pull off the wild, 50 - point victory. Harrison Barnes led the Mavericks with 19 points on 6 - of - 11 shooting, four rebounds and two assists, in 26 minutes. Luka Doncic had a solid night, with 13 points, six rebounds, two assists, two steals and one block, in 25 minutes. DeAndre Jordan finished with four points, 10 rebounds, four assists and one steal, in 22 minutes. The Mavericks shot 58 percent from the field, including 12 - of - 28 from long range. Meanwhile, Ricky Rubio was the high - point man for the Jazz, with 11 points, along with four steals, three rebounds and three assists, in 24 minutes. Donovan Mitchell tallied 10 points, three rebounds and three assists, while Rudy Gobert added 10 points, 10 rebounds, three steals and two assists, in 25 minutes. They shot 31 percent from the field, including a poor 6 - of - 35 from long range. The Jazz (7 - 7) will look to bounce back as they take on the 76ers in Philadelphia on Friday. The Mavericks (6 - 8) play host to the Warriors on Saturday.

The Dallas Mavericks defeated the visiting Golden State Warriors, 112 - 109, at American Airlines Center on Saturday evening. The Mavericks got out to a solid start at home, with an early 12 - 6 lead, which they were able to evolve into a 26 - 22 lead after one quarter. The Warriors made a push to start the second and took the lead within the first four minutes. However, the Mavericks hung around and trailed by just two, 59 - 57, at halftime. The Warriors pulled ahead by six early in the third, but the Mavericks quickly closed the gap to just two again. Nonetheless, the Warriors kept pressing and took an 86 - 82 lead into the final frame. The Mavericks simply would not back down, as they stayed within reach through the fourth quarter, before they overtook the Warriors thanks to solid defense and some clutch play in the final minutes. This marks the fourth straight win for the Mavericks, and the fourth loss in the last six games for Golden State. Luka Doncic led the way for Dallas, with 24 points, nine rebounds and four assists, including a couple super clutch plays down the stretch. Harrison Barns had a solid outing, with 23 points, eight rebounds and one assist, in 36 minutes, while DeAndre Jordan tallied 13 points, 10 rebounds, one steal and one block. The Mavericks shot 46 percent from the field, including 10 - of - 34 from long range. Meanwhile, the Warriors were without Stephen Curry (groin) and Draymond Green (toe). Kevin Durant led the way with 32 points, four rebounds, three assists and one block, in 36 minutes. Klay Thompson followed up with 22 points, four assists, three rebounds and two steals. The Warriors shot 45 percent from the field, including 9 - of - 33 from deep. The Warriors (12 - 5) will look to bounce back as they take on the Spurs in San Antonio on Sunday. The Mavericks (7 - 8) take on the Grizzlies in Memphis on Monday.

The Dallas Mavericks defeated the Brooklyn Nets, 119 - 113, at American Airlines Center on Wednesday evening. After a tightly contested first quarter, the Mavericks (8 - 9) built some cushion by outscoring the Nets (8 - 11) by a 27 - 18 margin during the second period. However, Brooklyn battled back in the third, and they entered the final 12 minutes with a 85 - 81 deficit. After multiple ties, Brooklyn was down just two points as late as the 4:3 mark of the fourth quarter before Dallas finished the game with a 16 - 12 run that was enough to hold off the visitors. Allen Crabbe returned to the starting lineup for the Nets and led the way with 27 points, a total he supplemented with three rebounds, one assist, two steals and one block. Spencer Dinwiddie came off the bench to supply 19 points, seven assists, two rebounds and one steal. D'Angelo Russell and Ed Davis each pitched in 17 points. Joe Harris and Jarrett Allen had quiet games with eight and six points, respectively. Harrison Barnes paced the Mavericks with 28 points and added five rebounds and a steal. Luka Doncic produced 21 points, nine rebounds, four assists and two steals. Devin Harris and J.J. Barea each delivered 18 points off the bench. DeAndre Jordan generated a 12 - point, 14 - rebound double - double that also included three assists and two steals. Maxi Kleber totaled 11 points. The Dallas Mavericks defeated the Boston Celtics, 113 - 104, at American Airlines Center on Saturday evening. The Mavericks (9 - 9) came into the contest having notched seven of their eight victories on the season on their home floor, and with two full days of rest since their most recent contest. In contrast, the Celtics (10 - 10) had lost in six of their 11 road tilts prior to Saturday, and were playing their fourth game in six nights. All of those trends surfaced as the game wore on, with Dallas holding an 87 - 82 lead by the end of three quarters. They then remained similarly ahead during the final 12 minutes, adding another four points to their advantage for the nine - point victory. Jayson Tatum paced the Celtics with 21 points, a total he supplemented with four rebounds, three assists, two steals and one block. The Celtics remain on the road and tangle with the New Orleans Pelicans on Monday night, while the Mavericks make the short trip to take on the in - state rival Houston Rockets on Wednesday evening.

The Dallas Mavericks took down the visiting Los Angeles Clippers, 114 - 110, on Sunday evening at American Airlines Center. The Clippers (15 - 7) trailed from the second quarter until the final minute, and were forced to fight an uphill battle in the fourth quarter. A late run helped push LA to tie the game at 107 - 107. From there, however, Dallas (11 - 10) controlled the game. After a tip - in put Dallas up two, DeAndre Jordan helped the Mavericks secure the win by stealing the ball from Lou Williams and hitting a clutch free - throw. Dennis Smith, Jr. finished the game by blocking a shot from Tobias Harris with under 10 seconds remaining, at which point Smith hit a pair of free - throws to seal the victory. Jordan finished the game with 16 points and a season - high 22 rebounds. He added three assists, a steal, and a block. Harrison Barnes led all scorers in the game with 30 points, which came on 11 - of - 28 shooting. Veteran point guard J.J. Barea scored another 24 points. For LA, Montrezl Harrell led the team with 23 points. The big man's breakout season continued, as he shot 11 - of - 15 and grabbed 10 rebounds in the loss. Lou Williams added 21 points and eight assists. One of the biggest problems for LA proved to be rebounding. While the Clippers grabbed only eight offensive boards, the Mavericks secured 17. The Clippers will visit New Orleans on Monday evening. Dallas, on the other hand, will remain at home and host the Portland Trail Blazers on Tuesday.

The Dallas Mavericks defeated the Portland Trail Blazers, 111 - 102, at American Airlines Center on Tuesday evening. The Mavericks (12 - 10) came into the contest with an impressive track record on their home floor, having notched nine wins in 11 tries. McCollum poured in 18 points and also provided four assists, three rebounds and two steals. Barea and Devin Harris pitched in matching nine - point tallies. The Trail Blazers head back home to tangle with the Phoenix Suns on Thursday night, while the Mavericks pay a visit to the New Orleans Pelicans on Wednesday night.

The Dallas Mavericks defeated the visiting Houston Rockets, 107 - 104, at American Airlines Center on Saturday. When Houston led 100 - 92 with four minutes remaining, it looked like the game was in hand but Dallas had other ideas. In fact, the Mavericks finished the game on a 15 - 4 run, as Luka Doncic scored 11 - straight points in that span to capture the win. Wesley Matthews matched those 21 points, adding three rebounds and three assists to his tally. On deck for Dallas is a home matchup versus the Orlando Magic on Monday. As for Houston, they play host to the Portland Trail Blazers on Tuesday for their next fixture.

The Dallas Mavericks defeated the visiting Orlando Magic, 101 - 76, at American Airlines Center on Monday. Dallas won this game in wire - to - wire fashion, as it wasn't close in the second half. In fact, the Mavericks won all four individual quarters, as they led by at least 15 points for the entirety of the fourth quarter. Dallas' defense was the difference, as they held Orlando to 36 percent from the field and 29 percent from three - point range. Getting to the free - throw line was huge as well, with the Mavericks connecting on 21 - of - 25 while the Magic hit just 4 - of - 5. The Dallas Mavericks defeated the visiting Atlanta Hawks, 114 - 107, at American Airlines Center on Wednesday evening. The Mavs got out to a good start, with an early 12 - 5 lead, and held the advantage through the first quarter. The Hawks cut the deficit to just one, but the Mavs answered to take a 28 - 26 lead into the second. The Hawks took the lead early in the second with a quick 6 - 2 run. The teams stayed within one possession of each other through the rest of the quarter, with the Hawks taking a 52 - 51 lead into halftime. John Collins added 20 points, 17 rebounds, one assists and one block, while Kent Bazemore finished with 22 points, five rebounds, two steals and one assist. The Hawks (6 - 21) head to Boston to take on the Celtics on Friday. The Mavericks (15 - 11) take on the Suns in Phoenix on Thursday.

The Sacramento Kings defeated the host Dallas Mavericks, 120 - 113, at American Airlines Center on Sunday evening. The Dallas Mavericks defeated the visiting New Orleans Pelicans, 122 - 119, at American Airlines Center on Wednesday evening. Barea added 18 points, seven assists, five rebounds and one steal. The Mavs shot 48 percent from the field, including 12 - of - 35 from long range. Meanwhile, Anthony Davis led the Pelicans with 32 points, 18 rebounds, two assists, one steal and one block, in 34 minutes. Jrue Holiday followed up with 25 points, six assists, five rebounds, one steal and one block, while Julius Randle chipped in 23 points, four rebounds, three assists and one steal. The Pelicans (15 - 20) will look to avoid a sixth straight loss as they play host to the Mavs on Friday. The Mavericks (16 - 17) next contest will be Friday in New Orleans.

The Dallas Mavericks defeated the visiting Oklahoma City Thunder, 105 - 103, at American Airlines Center on Sunday. In a battle between Western Conference rivals, this game wasn't decided until the final seconds. Dallas made the run that mattered most though, as they finished the game on a 10 - 2 spurt to turn a six - point deficit into a two - point victory. There were 11 ties and 18 lead changes though, as neither club led by more than 11 points. Three-point shooting was the difference, with Dallas connecting on 14 - of - 39 and Oklahoma City hitting just 9 - of - 38. The Timberwolves got out to a good start on the road, as they took a 32 - 27 lead after one quarter. The Mavs picked it up in the second and tied it up at 36, three minutes into the quarter. After a few lead changes, the Mavs and Timberwolves ended up tied at 58 by halftime. The third quarter started out close, but the Timberwolves took over toward the end of the quarter, to build a 10 - point lead entering the fourth. The Mavs did not back down and got out to a good start in the fourth. They kept fighting and managed to tie it at 99, with four minutes left. The last minutes was filled with ties and lead changes, but the Timberwolves were able to stick it out to finish on top, and end a two - game losing streak. Karl-Anthony Towns led the Timberwolves, with 28 points, 13 rebounds, three assists and three blocks, in 36 minutes. Andrew Wiggins followed up with 19 points, seven assists, three rebounds and two steals, while Tyus Jones added 15 points, six assists and a rebound. The Timberwolves shot 49 percent from the field, including 10 - of - 27 from deep. Meanwhile, Luka Doncic led the Mavs with 27 points, 12 rebounds, six assists and a block, in 31 minutes. Dwight Powell followed up with 25 points, eight rebounds, two assists, two steals and a block, while Trey Burke chipped in 12 points, four assists and two rebounds. The Mavs shot 46 percent from the field, including 7 - of - 39 from long range. The Mavericks (31 - 47) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Grizzlies on Friday. The Timberwolves (35 - 43) play host to the Heat on Friday.

The Memphis Grizzlies defeated the host Dallas Mavericks, 122 - 112, at American Airlines Arena on Friday evening. The contest got out to a competitive start, as the Mavericks led for most of the quarter, before the Grizzlies pulled ahead in the final minutes to take a 31 - 30 lead into the second. The Grizzlies picked it up in the second, as they outscored the Mavs by 11 in the quarter, to take a 12 - point lead by halftime. The Grizzlies pushed their lead to 20 mid way through the third, and took a 15 - point lead into the final frame. The Macs kept fighting in the fourth, but could not get within striking distance, as the Grizzlies held strong. Delon Wright led the Grizzlies with 26 points, 14 assists, 10 rebounds and two steals, in 39 minutes. Justin Holiday followed up with 20 points, two assists, two steals, a block and a rebound, while Tyler Dorsey added 17 points, nine rebounds and one assist. The Grizzlies shot 48 percent from the field, including 16 - of - 41 from deep. Meanwhile, Courtney Lee led the Mavs with 21 points, seven assists, four rebounds and three steals, in 30 minutes. Justin Jackson added 19 points, six rebounds, three assists and a steal, while Dirk Nowitzki chipped in 12 points, seven rebounds and one assist. The Mavs shot 43 percent from the field, including 17 - of - 47 from long range. The Mavericks (31 - 48) and Grizzlies (32 - 47) will go at each other again, as they face off in Memphis on Sunday.

The Dallas Mavericks defeated the visiting Phoenix Suns, 120 - 109, at American Airlines Center on Wednesday. While this wasn't a wire - to - wire win for the Mavericks, they dominated the final three quarters. In fact, a 33 - 18 first quarter really set the tone, as Phoenix could never get the game within four from there. Rebounding was a clear difference, with Dallas outrebounding Phoenix, 64 - 38. Ball movement was also key, with the Mavericks out - assiting the Suns, 28 - 21. The Suns (19 - 63) were led by Jamal Crawford, as he provided 51 points, five rebounds and five assists off the bench. He became the oldest player in NBA history to score at least 50 points. Josh Jackson led the starters with 17 points and eight rebounds. Dragan Bender totaled 12 points, 11 rebounds and six assists. The Mavericks (33 - 48) were led by Dirk Nowitzki, as he tallied 30 points, eight rebounds and three assists on 31 shots. Luka Doncic picked up another triple - double, collecting 21 points, 16 rebounds, 11 assists and three steals. Dwight Powell amassed 11 points and 11 boards while Dorian Finney-Smith led the bench with 15 points and 10 boards. This marked the season finale for the Suns, who finished with the second - worst record in the league. The Mavericks will have to play again on Wednesday when they travel to face the San Antomio Spurs.

The Brooklyn Nets defeated the visiting New York Knicks, 107 - 105, at Barclay's Center on Friday. Nine ties and 13 lead changes show just how close this game was, as this crosstown rivalry wasn't decided until the final shot. Caris LeVert played the hero, as he hit the game - winning lay - up with one second left to break a tied game. Rebounding was the difference in the game for Brooklyn, as they won that battle, 55 - 36. Ball movement was also critical, with the Nets handing out 22 assists and New York recording just 14 dimes. Brooklyn was lucky to win looking at the turnover differential though, as they recorded 22 turnovers while the Knicks turned the ball over only three times. The Nets ended up hitting 49 percent of their shots while the Knicks connected on just 41 percent from the field. The Knicks (1 - 1) were led by Enes Kanter, as he amassed 29 points and 10 boards on 12 - of - 19 shooting. Tim Hardaway Jr. matched those 29 points, adding two rebounds and three steals to his line. No other starter reached double figures in scoring. as Kevin Knox led the bench with 17 points and six boards. The Nets (1 - 1) got a fantastic performance out of Caris LeVert, as he collected 28 points, six rebounds and five assists on 8 - of - 13 shooting. D'Angelo Russell totaled 15 points, five rebounds and six assists. Jarrett Allen generated 15 points, 11 rebounds and four blocks. Spencer Dinwiddie was their best bench player, providing 10 points, three rebounds and six assists. Both teams play again on Saturday, with Brooklyn facing the Indiana Pacers on the road and New York playing host to the Boston Celtics.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the Brooklyn Nets, 120 - 114, at Barclays Center on Sunday evening. The Warriors (6 - 1) looked in absolute control of the game in this contest, the second of their three - game road trip, although things ended being far tighter than expected since the Nets (2 - 4) mounted a charge in the fourth quarter and came quite close to force an overtime. Golden State jumped to a 32 - 29 lead in the first quarter, and were pretty consistent the rest of the way since they also won the subsequent two quarters, 31 - 20 and 30 - 28, so they entered the final 12 minutes of action up by 16 points (93 - 77). However, Brooklyn woke up in the fourth and improved drastically, but it wasn't enough. The Nets won the final quarter 37 - 27, but Golden State held on and secured a tough win on the road. Stephen Curry was the top scorer for the Warriors with 35 points, seven rebounds and three assists, while Kevin Durant contributed with 34 points, eight rebounds and six assists. Klay Thompson chipped in with 18 points, and Draymond Green did an excellent job of filling out the stat sheet since he posted a line of eight points, four rebounds, 13 assists and five steals. Alfonzo McKinnie added with nine points and five boards. D'Angelo Russell was the best player for the Nets since he finished with 25 points, six rebounds and six assists, while Caris LeVert chipped in with 23 points and seven assists. Jarrett Allen had 11 points, three rebounds and four assists. Two players thrived off the bench, as Allen Crabbe finished with 14 points, and Spencer Dinwiddie added 12 of his own.

The Brooklyn Nets defeated the visiting Detroit Pistons in overtime, 120 - 119, at Barclay's Center on Wednesday. While Detroit led for the majority of the second half, this game wasn't decided until the final seconds. In fact, the Nets missed four three - pointers in the final minute of regulation, with all of those attempts to either tie or take the lead. They eventually hit one with 20 seconds left to send the game into overtime, as Detroit scored just five points in the final three minutes of regulation. Spencer Dinwiddie was the one who nailed that three, as he also hit the game - winning three - pointer with 7 seconds left in overtime. Ball movement really decided the game for Brooklyn, as they out - assisted Detroit, 26 - 16. In addition, the Nets really dominated down low, outscoring the Pistons in the paint, 62 - 38. The Pistons (4 - 3) were led by Blake Griffin, as he collected 25 points, nine rebounds, four assists and two steals. Andre Drummond totaled 24 points, 23 rebounds and two blocks. Reggie Jackson finished with 21 points, four rebounds and two assists. Stanley Johnson accrued six points, 12 rebounds and two assists. The Nets (3 - 5) got a spectacular bench performance from Spencer Dinwiddie, as he led the team with 25 points, four rebounds and four assists. Ed Davis also played well off the bench, amassing 10 points and 10 boards. Joe Harris led the starters with 23 points and five boards. Caris LeVert accumulated 19 points, six rebounds and six assists. On deck for Brooklyn is a home matchup versus the Houston Rockets on Friday. As for Detroit, they travel to play the Philadelphia 76ers on Saturday for their next outing.

The Houston Rockets defeated the host Brooklyn Nets, 119 - 111, at Barclay's Center on Friday. Despite the fact that Brooklyn led by 14 points at times in the second quarter, Houston was able to prevail thanks to a big second half. In fact, tje Rockets rode a 35 - 25 third quarter to victory, as they held the lead for the final 20 minutes of action. Getting to the free - throw line was the difference for Houston, as they hit 22 - of - 32 from the charity stripe while Brooklyn connected on just 12 - od - 20. Rim protection was also critical, with the Rockets recording 10 blocks and the Nets picking up just four. The Rockets (2 - 5) got a vintage performance out of Chris Paul, as he tallied 32 points, seven rebounds, 11 assists, two steals and two blocks. Clint Capela amassed 22 points, 13 rebounds, five assists and two blocks on 8 - of - 11 shooting. Eric Gordon finished with 21 points and three assists. Carmelo Anthony was huge off the bench, providing 26 points and four boards on 9 - of - 12 from the field. The Nets (3 - 6) got a career - high 29 points out of Caris LeVert, as he added four rebounds, two assists and three steals to his line on 10 - of - 17 shooting. Joe Harris went 7 - of - 9 from the field to total 18 points, two rebounds and four assists. D'Angelo Russell collected 12 points, three rebounds and three assists. Houston will play the second half of a back - to - back set on Saturday, as they travel to face the Chicago Bulls. As for Brooklyn, they play host to the Philadelphia 76ers on Sunday for their next fixture.

The Brooklyn Nets defeated the visiting Philadelphia 76ers, 122 - 97, at Barclay's Center on Sunday. Philly came into this game winless on the road this season and Brooklyn continued that ugly trend here. Despite the fact that the Sixers led after the opening quarter, the Nets outscored them by 28 points across the final three quarters. Prior to that, there were 11 ties and 17 lead changes in the first half, as Brooklyn led by at least 14 points for the entirety of the fourth quarter. The assist - to - turnover differential was a glaring difference, with Brooklyn recording 27 assists to nine turnovers while Philly committed 27 turnovers to just 16 assists. The Sixers (6 - 5) were led by Ben Simmons, as he tallied 20 points, 12 rebounds, three assists and four steals. Joel Embiid took just eight shots but finished with 16 points, 15 rebounds and four assists. Dario Saric amassed 14 points and three boards. J.J. Redick led the bench with 15 points and two assists. The Nets (4 - 6) highest scorers both had 21 points, as D'Angelo Russell led the starters with 21 points, two rebounds and six assists. Rondae Hollis-Jefferson led the bench with 21 points, six rebounds and three assists. Caris LeVert collected 20 points, five rebounds, two assists and four steals. Jarrett Allen accrued 15 points, 10 rebounds and two blocks. Spencer Dinwiddie also played well off the bench, providing 12 points and eight assists. On deck for Brooklyn is a road matchup versus the Phoenix Suns on Tuesday. As for Philadelphia, they travel to play the Indiana Pacers on Wednesday for their next outing.

The Miami Heat defeated the Brooklyn Nets, 120 - 107, at Barclays Center on Wednesday evening. The Heat (6 - 8) came into the contest reeling and looking to address some uncharacteristic defensive deficiencies that had seen them give up 110 points or more in four of the prior five games. Miami got off to an excellent start in that regard, limiting the Nets (6 - 9) to 21 points while collecting 37 of their own. The lead remained 61 - 49 at the half, and the visitors were able to expand it to a full 18 points entering the final 12 minutes. That allowed them to withstand Brooklyn's best quarter, as they tallied 35 points in the fourth. Miami leveraged six double - digit scoring efforts and 54 percent shooting to secure victory. Tyler Johnson paced the Heat off the bench with 24 points and supplemented them with five rebounds, one assist and two blocks. Goran Dragic supplied 21 points, four assists and three rebounds. Hassan Whiteside posted a 14 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included two steals and two blocks. Bam Adebayo had 12 points in just 10 minutes, while Rodney McGruder matched his scoring total while posting four rebounds and three assists. Justise Winslow mustered six points but also hauled in 11 rebounds and dished out three assists. Spencer Dinwiddie led the Nets with 18 points and also managed five assists, three rebounds and one steal. Rondae Hollis-Jefferson contributed 14 points and nine rebounds, while Shabazz Napier tallied 13 points, meaning bench players served as Brooklyn's top trio of scorers. D'Angelo Russell shot just 6 - for - 18 on his way to 12 points. Joe Harris pitched in 11 points, five rebounds and three assists, while Jared Dudley generated 10 points, five rebounds, one steal and one block. The Heat remain on the road and next visit the Indiana Pacers on Friday night, while the Nets visit the Washington Wizards that same evening.

The Los Angeles Clippers defeated the host Brooklyn Nets, 127 - 119, at Barclays Center on Saturday evening. The Nets got out to a good start at home, as they kicked things off with an 11 - 4 lead. The Clippers pushed back, but the Nets held on to take a, 37 - 32, lead into the second quarter. The Nets stepped it up with a 14 - 4 run to start the quarter, and once again held off the Clippers, who continued to chip away. The Nets led 67 - 60 at halftime. Both teams came out strong in the third and matched each other bucket for bucket, until the score was settled at 97 - 90, with the Nets' advantage heading into the final frame. The tides turned in the fourth quarter, as the Clippers hit a quick 70 run to tie it up. The game was tied at 110, with 4:36 to go, when the Clippers mounted a 9 - 2 run, to take a seven - point advantage with 2:13 remaining. The Clippers held on to earn their fourth straight win. Danilo Gallinari led the Clippers with 28 points on 9 - of - 14 shooting, in 32 minutes. Tobias Harris followed up with 27 points, eight rebounds and three assists, while Montrezl Harrell added 16 points, 10 rebounds, one assist and a block, in 27 minutes off the bench. The Clippers shot 51 percent from the field, including 11 - of - 23 from long range. Meanwhile, Jarrett Allen led the Nets with 24 points, 11 rebounds, two assists and a block, in 28 minutes. D'Angelo Russell followed up with 23 points, 10 assists, three rebounds, two steals and a block, while Joe Harris tallied 19 points, four rebounds, an assist and a steal. The Nets shot 46 percent from the field, including 13 - of - 28 from long range. The Nets (7 - 10) will look to bounce back as they take on the Heat in Miami on Tuesday. The Clippers (10 - 5) head to Atlanta to take on the Hawks on Monday.

The Minnesota Timberwolves defeated the host Brooklyn Nets, 112 - 102, at Barclay's Center on Friday. While there were four ties and five lead changes in the first half, Minnesota dominated from there. In fact, they led by at least four points for the final 20 minutes of action. They did most of their damage in the second and third quarters, outscoring Brooklyn, 67 - 46. The Timberwolves defense was critical, as they held the Nets to 42 percent from the field and 31 percent from three - point range. In addition, Minnesota recorded 15 steals and won the turnover differential, 18 - 7. The Timberwolves also won the points in the paint battle, 52 - 36, and outscored the Nets, 16 - 5, in fastbreak points. The Timberwolves (8 - 11) best player came off the bench, as Derrick Rose provided 25 points, two rebounds and three assists on 11 - of - 17 from the field. Karl-Anthony Towns led the starters with 21 points and nine boards. Taj Gibson amassed 16 points, 11 rebounds and three assists while Jeff Teague tallied 15 points, two rebounds and nine assists. The Nets (8 - 12) were led by Joe Harris, as he collected 18 points, six rebounds and four assists. , Jarrett Allen totaled 12 points and four boards. Spencer Dinwiddie led the bench with 18 points, three rebounds and eight assists. DeMarre Carroll also played well off the bench, generating 13 points, seven rebounds and two assists. On deck for Minnesota is a home matchup versus the Chicago Bulls on Saturday. As for Brooklyn, they play host to the Philadelphia 76ers on Sunday for their next outing.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the host Brooklyn Nets, 127 - 125, at Barclay's Center on Sunday. While Brooklyn held the lead for over 45 minutes of this game, Philly recaptured the lead when it mattered most. In fact, the Sixers finished the game on a 22 - 7 run, as they capped off their win with Jimmy Butler dagger. Butler hit a step - back three - pointer with 0 seconds left to turn a one - point deficit into a two - point victory. The assist - to - turnover differential really carried the Sixers, as they out - assisted the Nets, 28 - 19 while committing seven fewer turnovers. Brooklyn dominated offensively though, as they connected on 57 percent from the field and 40 percent from three - point range. The nine steals recorded by Philly was huge, as Brooklyn recorded just two on their end. The Sixers (14 - 8) not only got a game - winner from Jimmy Butler, but he also provided 34 points, 12 rebounds, two assists and four steals. Joel Embiid finished with 32 points, 12 rebounds, four assists and two blocks. J.J. Redick amassed 15 points, four rebounds and two assists. Ben Simmons accrued 13 points, five rebounds, nine assists, three steals and two blocks. Landry Shamet led the bench with 16 points. The Nets (8 - 13) got a spectacular performance from D'Angelo Russell, as he tallied 38 points, eight rebounds and eight assists on 16 - of - 28 shooting. Jarrett Allen totaled 17 points and 10 boards. Rondae Hollis-Jefferson finished with 13 points and six boards. Spencer Dinwiddie led the bench with 31 points, three rebounds and five assists on 11 - of - 15 from the field. Both these teams return to action on Wednesday, with Brooklyn playing host to the Utah Jazz and Philly welcoming the New York Knicks to Wells Fargo Center.

The Utah Jazz defeated the Brooklyn Nets, 101 - 91, at Barclays Center on Wednesday night. The Jazz (10 - 12) came into the contest looking for any type of reprieve from a forgettable stretch where they'd dropped six of eight games. Despite their unsightly record, the Nets (8 - 14) had played several quality teams tough already this season, so it promised to be an uphill battle for Utah. Sure enough, the two clubs essentially matched each other basket for basket in the first half, and the visitors entered the halftime locker room with a slim 43 - 42 advantage. They saw that get erased and then some during the third period, which put the Jazz at a 78 - 70 deficit entering the final 12 minutes. However, they locked up the much - needed road victory with a dominant 31 - 13 advantage during the fourth quarter, capping off a strong defensive effort in which they limited Brooklyn to 35 percent shooting. Donovan Mitchell led the way for the Jazz with 29 points and supplemented the total with five rebounds, one assist and four steals. Rudy Gobert took advantage of one of the most appealing matchups for centers in the NBA by generating a 23 - point, 16 - rebound double - double that also included three assists, four blocks and one steal. Royce O'Neal moved back to the bench with Mitchell back in action and led the reserves with 13 points and four rebounds. Raul Neto poured in 11 points, while Derrick Favors mustered nine points and 10 rebounds. Ricky Rubio notably went 0 - for - 9 from the field on his way to a six - point tally. Spencer Dinwiddie paced the Nets with 18 points in 22 minutes off the bench, adding three rebounds and two blocks. Rondae Hollis-Jefferson, Jarrett Allen and D'Angelo Russell all contributed 14 - point efforts. Hollis-Jefferson and Allen made theirs double - doubles with 11 and 10 rebounds, respectively. Shabazz Napier pitched in 10 points in 16 minutes off the bench. The Jazz next pay a visit to the Charlotte Hornets on Friday night, while the Nets remain home to tangle with the Memphis Grizzlies on that same evening.

The Memphis Grizzlies defeated the Brooklyn Nets in double overtime, 131 - 125, at Barclays Center on Friday night. The Grizzlies (13 - 8) and Nets (8 - 15) engaged in an epic battle, one that didn't seem headed toward the eventual final score through three quarters. Memphis held a modest 85 - 80 lead heading into the final 12 minutes, but they needed a Jaren Jackson three - pointer with 16 seconds left in regulation to knot the game at 111 - 111 and send it into overtime. The first extra period ended in a 117 - 117 deadlock thanks to Mike Conley's 10 - foot driving floating jump shot with 10 seconds remaining. Memphis finally pulled away in the second overtime by scoring the last seven points over the final 2:32, six which came from Conley. Conley led the way for the Grizzlies with a career - high 37 points, a total he supplemented with 10 assists, five rebounds and one block. Jackson registered 36 points, eight rebounds and two assists. Marc Gasol contributed a 15 - point, 15 - rebound double - double. Garrett Temple tallied 13 points. JaMychal Green pitched in 11 points and four rebounds off the bench. D'Angelo Russell paced the Nets with 26 points and added eight assists, one rebound, three steals and one block. DeMarre Carroll led the bench with 21 points and also posted 12 rebounds, one assist and one steal in 39 minutes off the bench. Jarrett Allen generated a 15 - point, 12 - rebound double - double that also included five assists, one steal and one block.Spencer Dinwiddie and Rondae Hollis-Jefferson had matching 15 - point tallies as well. The Grizzlies remain on the road and pay a visit to the 76ers on Sunday evening, while the Nets travel to the Nation's Capital and face the Wizards on Saturday night.

The Cleveland Cavaliers defeated the host Brooklyn Nets, 99 - 97, at Barclays Center on Monday evening. The contest got out to a very competitive start with multiple lead changes. The Nets used a 9 - 1 run to create some separation mid way though the quarter, however, the Cavaliers battled back to take a one - point, 30 - 29, lead to start the second. The Cavs carried the momentum, as they stayed one step ahead through the entire quarter, and pushed their lead to 56 - 50 by halftime. The Cavs came out strong in the second half and pushed their lead to 10, within the first couple of minutes. Nonetheless, the Nets kept fighting and cut the deficit to four, 80 - 76, entering the fourth. The Cavs pulled ahead to start the quarter, and held a decent cushion until about the three - minute mark, when the Nets began creeping back. The Nets managed to tie it up at 97, with 18 seconds on the clock. However, the Cavs' newest addition, Alec Burks stepped up in the clutch and threw - down a game - winning dunk. Jordan Clarkson led the Cavaliers with 20 points, 11 rebounds, four assists and one steal, in 28 minutes off the bench. Tristan Thompson followed up with 19 points, 14 rebounds, two assists and two blocks, while Collin Sexton tallied 15 points on 7 - of - 16 shooting. Alec Burks added 13 points seven rebounds and one assists, in 28 minutes off the bench. Meanwhile, D'Angelo Russell led the Nets with 30 points, eight rebounds, six assists and two steals, in 32 minutes. Spencer Dinwiddie followed up with 18 points, four assists, three rebounds and one steal, while Shabazz Napier chipped in 10 points, four rebounds and two assists off the bench. The Nets (8 - 17) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Thunder on Wednesday. The Cavs (5 - 18) play host to the Warriors on Wednesday.

The Oklahoma City Thunder defeated the Brooklyn Nets, 114 - 112, at Barclays Center on Wednesday. Things were looking bleak for the visiting Thunder (16 - 7), as they fell behind in the first half and faced an 18 - point deficit heading into the final quarter. Then, Paul George decided it was time to take over. The All-Star forward scored 24 points in the fourth quarter, including the Thunder's final seven points and a game - winning three - pointer with 3 seconds left on the clock. In the end, George finished with a game - high 47 points (15 - 27 FG, 6 - 13 3Pt), 15 rebounds and four assists across 37 minutes. As a team, it was a poor shooting night in all facets of the game, as Oklahoma City shot 34 percent from three, 43 percent from the field overall and just 58 percent from the free throw line. Fortunately, George came through to save the day over the final eight minutes. The Thunder's next highest scorer was Russell Westbrook, who didn't score a single point in the fourth quarter but finished with 21 points, 15 rebounds and 17 assists in 40 minutes. As for the Nets (8 - 18), they were on cruise control for 36 minutes Wednesday and looked to be well on their way to putting an end to their seven - game losing streak. However, just 19 points in the fourth quarter and failing to score in the final two and half minutes was not enough to get the job done. As a team, Brooklyn shot a fairly impressive 15 - of - 36 (42 percent) from behind the arc, but shot just 43 percent from the field overall. Allen Crabbe led the way with a team - high 22 points on 7 - of - 13 shooting from behind the arc, while Joe Harris added 19 points of his own. Point guards D'Angelo Russell and Spencer Dinwiddie each dropped 17 points but combined for just six assists.

The Brooklyn Nets defeated the visiting Toronto Raptors in overtime, 106 - 105, at Barclay's Center on Friday. While Brooklyn led for the majority of the first half, it took an overtime session to determine a winner. The second half was extremely competitive, as there were 10 ties and 12 lead changes, with neither club leading by more than five points. Brooklyn played some stifling defense at the end of overtime, as they held Toronto scoreless for the final 100 seconds, forcing them to miss their final four shots. Rebounding was the difference for the Nets, as they outrebounded the Raptors, 60 - 41. Brooklyn also played well defensively throughout, holding Toronto to 39 percent from the field and 31 percent from three - point range. The Raptors (21 - 6) were led by Kawhi Leonard, as he collected 32 points, three rebounds, four assists and four steals. Jonas Valanciunas finished with 24 points and eight boards. Pascal Siakam finished with 16 points, five rebounds, two assists and two blocks. Kyle Lowry went just 1 - of - 8 from the field but still led the team with 11 assists. The Nets (9 - 18) got a gem from D'Angelo Russell, as he tallied 29 points, five rebounds and five assists. Spencer Dinwiddie was huge off the bench, providing 17 points, two rebounds and eight assists. Jarrett Allen amassed 12 points, 10 rebounds, two assists, two steals and two blocks while Rondae Hollis-Jefferson totaled 11 points, four rebounds and two assists. Ed Davis scored just one point but provided 15 rebounds off the bench to lead the team. On deck for Brooklyn is a road matchup versus the New York Knicks on Saturday. As for Toronto, they return to action on Sunday, when they host the Milwaukee Bucks.

The Brooklyn Nets defeated the visiting Washington Wizards, 125 - 118, at Barclay's Center on Friday. In a battle between two struggling teams, Brooklyn prevailed with a victory. The second quarter really set the tone, with Brooklyn outscoring Washington, 43 - 28. That allowed the Wizards to lead for the entirety of the second half. Free-throw shooting was the difference in the game, with the Nets connecting on 26 - of - 31 and the Wizards hitting just 9 - of - 16. Rebounding was also critical, with Washington outrebounding Brooklyn, 46 - 25. Both offenses were on point, with both clubs hitting over 50 percent of their shots. The Wizards (11 - 18) were led by Bradley Beal, as he tallied 31 points and nine assists. John Wall totaled 17 points and 13 assists. Markieff Morris led the bench with 15 points, three rebounds and two assists. Austin Rivers played his final game as a Wizard and provided 14 points, three rebounds and three assists. The Nets (12 - 18) just signed Spencer Dinwiddie to an extension yesterday and he rewarded his organization by leading the team with 27 points, four rebounds and six assists off the bench. Joe Harris led the starters with 19 points, two rebounds and six assists. Rondae Hollis-Jefferson accrued 15 points, nine rebounds and six assists. Both teams return to action on Sunday, with Brooklyn welcoming the Atlanta Hawks to The Big Apple and Washington playing host to the Los Angeles Lakers.

The Brooklyn Nets defeated the Atlanta Hawks, 144 - 127, at Barclays Center on Sunday afternoon. The Nets (13 - 18) entered this game on the heels of a four - game winning streak, and managed to extend that positive run against a Hawks (6 - 23) squad that looked overmatched from start to finish. Brooklyn jumped to a 19 - point lead after the first quarter (42 - 23) and they never looked back in this one. Atlanta tried to turn things around and reduced the deficit to six points after a 43 - 30 second quarter. It seemed as if Atlanta were set to continue their push in the second half, but the Nets won the next two quarters (39 - 30 and 33 - 31, respectively) and secured a comfortable win by a 17 - point margin. Now Brooklyn have won their last five in a row, while Atlanta have now lost seven of their past eight. D'Angelo Russell was the star of the game for the Nets since he finished with 32 points, seven assists, six rebounds and two steals in only 29 minutes of action. Rondae Hollis-Jefferson filled the stat sheet as well thanks to 18 points, four boards, three assists and two steals, while Jeff Harris added 16 points with six assists. Jarrett Allen and Rodions Kurucs had 11 points, while Jared Dudley (16 points), DeMarre Carroll (15 points) and Spencer Dinwiddie (15 points, five assists) all reached double - digit scoring off the bench. Jared Collins was the best player for the Hawks since he finished with 29 points and eight rebounds. Trae Young had a double - double with 13 points and 10 assists, while Dewayne Dedmon also had one thanks to his 24 points and 12 rebounds, as well as three assists and one block. Kent Bazemore delivered 20 points and seven assists.

The Brooklyn Nets defeated the Los Angeles Lakers, 115 - 110, at Barclays Center on Tuesday evening. The Nets (14 - 18) started the game off with in the same impressive form that had netted them a five - game winning streak coming in. Brooklyn jumped out to a 62 - 57 halftime lead over the Lakers (18 - 13), and they didn't let up after intermission. The home squad matched Los Angeles basket for basket in the second half, holding off the visitors after they got as close as 113 - 110 with 17 seconds remaining. The shooting was impressive for both clubs, but the Nets were just a bit better with a 48 percent success rate overall, including 41 percent from three - point range. LeBron James led the way for the Lakers with 36 points, supplementing them with 13 rebounds, eight assists, one block and one steal. Lonzo Ball turned in 23 points, six rebounds, three assists and two steals. Kyle Kuzma posted a 22 - point, 11 - rebound double - double that also included three assists and one steal. Josh Hart and Tyson Chandler both started but provided just six and five points, respectively. D'Angelo Russell paced the Nets against his former squad, totaling 22 points, 13 assists, four rebounds and one block. Joe Harris supplied 19 points, four rebounds, two assists and one steal. The Brooklyn Nets defeated the Phoenix Suns, 111 - 103, at Barclays Center on Sunday evening. The Brooklyn Nets defeated the Charlotte Hornets, 134 - 132, in double overtime at Barclays Center on Wednesday night. Walker paced the Hornets with 35 points and added six rebounds, five assists and two steals. Lamb posted 31 points, six boards, three assists and two steals. Rondae Hollis-Jefferson contributed a 16 - point, 15 - rebound double - double that also included six assists and three blocks. Rodions Kurucs pitched in a 13 - point, 12 - rebound double - double that also included three assists, three steals and one block. Carroll delivered 12 points overall. The Hornets and Nets face off and do it all over again in the second game of the home - and - home series in Charlotte on Friday night.

The Brooklyn Nets defeated the New Orleans Pelicans, 126 - 121, at Barclays Center on Wednesday. The Nets (18 - 21) and the Pelicans (17 - 22) entered this game with the exact same record and fans that wanted a back - and - forth, tight contest were not disappointed. Brooklyn jumped to a 10 - point lead after the first quarter (39 - 29), and they extended that lead during both the second (34 - 29) and third (32 - 29) quarters, so they entered into the final 12 minutes of action with a huge 18 - point lead. However, New Orleans woke up in the final 12 minutes, but they fell short. Their 34 - 21 had them at the brink of pulling an impressive comeback, but they fell short and the Nets ended winning the game in front of their fans. Surprisingly, seven of the nine Brooklyn players that saw action managed to score in double figures. The top scorer was D'Angelo Russell, who had 22 points with 13 assists, while Joe Harris added 21 points. DeMarre Carroll had 19 points off the bench, and Spencer Dinwiddie contributed 18 points and four assists despite not starting. Jarrett Allen and Rodions Kurucs each had 10 points. The Pelicans' starting lineup did the heavy lifting in this one, since the bench only managed to score five points (in total) while shooting 2 - 7 combined. Anthony Davis was their top scorer with 34 points, 26 rebounds and four assists, while Elfrid Payton chipped in with 25 points and seven assists. Jrue Holiday had 20 points, Julius Randle chipped in with 21, and E'Twaun Moore delivered 16 points.

The Brooklyn Nets defeated the Atlanta Hawks, 116 - 100, at Barclays Center on Wednesday night. The Hawks (12 - 29) managed to jump ahead in this game and led by an astonishing 15 - point margin (38 - 23) following the first quarter, but that would be everything they do as the Nets (21 - 22) bounced back and quickly gained control of the contest. Brooklyn trimmed the deficit to just six points by halftime thanks to a 28 - 19 second quarter, and they would never look back in the second half. They won the remaining two quarters comfortably (35 - 23 and 30 - 20, respectively) and ended cruising their way towards a 16 - point victory that extended their current run to four wins in their last five games. Seven Brooklyn players scored in double digits in this game, led by D'Angelo Russell who finished with 23 points, four assists and three rebounds. Joe Harris delivered 16 points, while Jarrett Allen and Rodions Kurucs each chipped in with 11. DeMarre Carroll contributed 17 points off the bench, while Spencer Dinwiddie (16 points, five assists, four rebounds) and Shabazz Napier (11 points) also had good games while coming off the second unit. The best player for the Hawks was John Collins, who ended with 30 points and 14 rebounds. Trae Young had 17 points with seven assists, but he went 6 - 15 from the field and only 2 - 9 from three - point range. Kevin Huerter added 14 points and 10 boards, and Jeremy Lin played very well off the bench: 16 points, five rebounds, three assists and three steals.

The Brooklyn Nets defeated the Boston Celtics, 109 - 102, at Barclays Center on Monday. The Nets (22 - 23) have been quite inconsistent over the current 2018 - 19 NBA season, but they managed to deliver an impressive performance while facing one of the top teams in the Eastern Conference such as the Celtics (25 - 18). Brooklyn quickly jumped ahead to a 27 - 25 lead in the first quarter, but Boston kept things close and the first half ended with a 46 - 45 edge for the hosts. Brooklyn would jump through a huge 44 - 21 after the third quarter, which gave them a 24 - point edge heading into the final 12 minutes and even though Boston would cut the deficit in the final quarter (36 - 19), the Nets ended winning the game by a rather comfortable seven - point advantage. Jarrett Allen had an impressive performance on both ends of the floor, as he chipped in with 19 points, 12 rebounds and four blocks. Rodions Kurucs had 19 points, while Joe Harris added 13 points, eight boards and three assists. DeMarre Carroll added 10 points off the bench. Only three Boston players ended scoring with more than 10 points, and second - year player Jayson Tatum led the way with an impressive 34 - point performance, but he also contributed five rebounds, three assists and three blocks. Jaylen Brown had 22 points, but he also chipped in with six rebounds and two steals. Brad Wanamaker had a solid outing off the bench, with 13 points, four assists and three boards.

The Brooklyn Nets defeated the visiting Sacramento Kings, 123 - 94, at Barclay's Center on Monday. While Sacramento held a small lead at the half, Brooklyn absolutely dominated the second half. Spencer Dinwiddie led the bench with 11 points, three rebounds and six assists while Ed Davis snatched down 16 boards off the bench as well. The Chicago Bulls defeated the host Brooklyn Nets, 125 - 106, at Barclay's Center on Friday. While Brooklyn came into this game as a sizable favorite, Chicago dominated. The Portland Trail Blazers defeated the host Brooklyn Nets, 113 - 99, at Barclay's Center on Thursday. In the first game back from the all - star break, Portland came out with a huge road win. The Brooklyn Nets defeated the visiting Boston Celtics, 110 - 96, at Barclay's Center on Saturday. Boston played this game without Kyrie Irving and Al Horford for resting purposes and it clearly hampered them in this ugly loss. While Brooklyn didn't dominate any statistic, they won almost all of them. In fact, the Nets won the rebounding, assisting, turnovers and field goal percentage disparities. Their biggest differential was the turnover battle, winning that 15 - 12. The Celtics (45 - 32) were led by Gordon Hayward, as he provided 19 points, six rebounds and three assists off the bench. Daniel Theis also played well off the bench, tallying 16 points, four rebounds, two assists and two blocks. Marcus Morris was the only starter in double figures, as he amassed 16 points and five boards. The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the Brooklyn Nets, 131 - 121, at Barclays Center on Monday night. Antetokounmpo furnished a 28 - point, 11 - rebound double - double that also included two assists, one steal and one block. George Hill paced the second unit with 22 points. The Bucks next pay a visit to the Philadelphia 76ers on Thursday night, while the Nets remain home and face the Toronto Raptors on Wednesday evening.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the Brooklyn Nets, 115 - 105, at Barclays Center on Wednesday night. Jarrett Allen and DeMarre Carroll generated matching 12 - point tallies while also bringing down nine and five rebounds, respectively. Rodions Kurucks managed 11 points, four rebounds, two assists and one block. The Brooklyn Nets defeated the visiting Miami Heat, 113 - 94, at Barclay's Center on Wednesday. This game secured the six - seed for the Brooklyn Nets, as they won in dominating fashion. Jarrett Allen scored just one point but led the team with 14 rebounds. Rondae Hollis-Jefferson provided 10 points, 12 rebounds, three assists and three steals off the bench. Shabazz Napier amassed 20 points, five rebounds and five assists off the bench as well. Brooklyn has earned themselves a playoff berth, landing the six - seed in the east. That means they'll travel to face the Philadelphia 76ers in the opening round, with those teams splitting their four - game season series.

The Denver Nuggets defeated the Phoenix Suns, 119 - 91, at Pepsi Center on Saturday evening. The Nuggets (20) established their dominance early, gaining a 30 - 16 first - quarter advantage. While the Suns (1 - 1) seemed to wake up on offense in the second period, they still entered halftime with a 16 - point deficit that they never came close to really overcoming. Warren was next with a bench - leading 16 points, a total he complemented with three rebounds, one assist and one block. Isaiah Canaan supplied 15 points, four boards, two assists and one steal. The Suns head to Golden State to tangle with the Warriors on Monday night, while the Nuggets remains home and faces the defending champions on Sunday evening.

The Denver Nuggets defeated the Golden State Warriors, 100 - 98, at Pepsi Center on Sunday night. Both teams came undefeated into this game but against all odds, it would be the Nuggets (30) who kept their streak alive thanks to a couple of magnificent plays down the stretch. The Warriors (2 - 1) never gave up and tried to send the game to overtime in the final seconds, but a key behind - the - back block from Juan Hernangomez sealed the win for a Denver team that kept the opposition under 100 points for the third straight game. Jamal Murray struggled, however, finishing with just three points while going 0 - for - 9 from the field. Stephen Curry paved the way for the Warriors with a 30 - point, six - assist performance, while Kevin Durant also had a decent game since he finished with 20 points, 11 rebounds and seven assists, but only shot 7 - of - 19 from the field. Klay Thompson added 15 points, and Kevon Looney chipped in with 10 points and six boards off the bench.

The Denver Nuggets defeated the Sacramento Kings, 126 - 112, at Pepsi Center on Tuesday evening. The Nuggets (40) had made quite the statement with a 100 - 98 victory over the world champion Golden State Warriors on Sunday night, but on paper, they had an even bigger defensive challenge on their hands Tuesday. The Kings (1 - 3) came into the contest scoring the second - highest points per game (126), with several of their key young pieces excelling early in the new season. Frank Mason III turned in a full line of 14 points, seven assists, five rebounds and one steal. Iman Shumpert drew a second straight start and contributed 12 points, three assists, two rebounds and two steals. Willie Cauley-Stein and Yogi Ferrell generated matching 11 - point tallies. Jamal Murray overcame his left tibial contusion to pace the Nuggets with 19 points, four assists, one rebound and one steal. Gary Harris poured in 18 points and added five assists, three rebounds and one steal. Paul Millsap registered 15 points, five rebounds, one steal and one block. Nikola Jokic pitched in a 14 - point, 12 - rebound double - double that also included six assists and one steal. Trey Lyles contributed 12 points, five rebounds, three assists and one block. Mason Plumlee, Monte Morris and Malik Beasley all posted 11 - point efforts off the bench with some extra playing time due to the big second - half lead. The Kings head back home to take on the Memphis Grizzlies on Wednesday evening, while the Nuggets head to Los Angeles for a showdown with the Lakers on Thursday night.

The Denver Nuggets defeated the visiting New Orleans Pelicans, 116 - 111, at Pepsi Center on Monday. Anthony Davis was sidelined on Monday due to an elbow injury, but that did not stop New Orleans (4 - 2) from putting up a strong fight in the loss. After Denver (5 - 1) led by as much as 18 in the third quarter, the Pelicans clawed back through the third and fourth, eventually cutting the lead to as little as three. Ultimately, though, Denver's strong offense got the best of the Pelicans. The Nuggets hit 11 three - pointers and dished out 28 assists in the win. 10 of those dimes were dished out by Nikola Jokic, who narrowly missed out on a triple - double on Monday. The star big man finished with 12 points, 10 assists, and nine rebounds, continuing his strong third - year campaign. The Nuggets' backcourt of Gary Harris and Jamal Murray scored 23 points each and combined to shoot 17 - of - 35 on the night. New Orleans, meanwhile, saw offseason acquisition Julius Randle step up in Davis's absence. Randle scored 24 points to lead all scorers, and also finished with eight rebounds and six assists. Starting power forward Nikola Mirotic added another 17 points, 10 rebounds, and three steals. The team will look to continue its strong offensive production when Davis returns from his injury. On Wednesday, the Nuggets will visit Chicago while the Pelicans will travel to Golden State.

The Denver Nuggets defeated the Utah Jazz, 103 - 88, at Pepsi Center on Saturday evening. The two division rivals came into the contest pretty evenly matched despite the two - win difference in their records. The first half bore that out, as the Nuggets (7 - 1) only held a slim 47 - 46 edge at intermission. However, the Jazz (4 - 5) managed to separate some in the third, erasing their deficit and building a five - point lead going into the final 12 minutes. Then everything went downhill for the visitors, as they saw star two - guard Donovan Mitchell have to be helped off the court due to an ankle injury and were outscored by a 35 - 15 margin to close out the game. Mitchell did manage to return after getting his ankle taped, but it was a case of too little too late. Jae Crowder led the Jazz off the bench with 21 points in 32 minutes. Mitchell paced the first unit with 16 points despite missing some time, and he added five rebounds, two assists and five steals. Derrick Favors and Rudy Gobert had matching 12 - point tallies, with the Stifle Tower also hauling in 12 boards. Ricky Rubio contributed 11 points, six assists, four rebounds and four steals. Gary Harris paced the Nuggets with 20 points while adding four rebounds and an assist. Jamal Murray supplied 19 points, five rebounds and four assists. Paul Millsap turned in 13 points, five rebounds, two assists and three steals. Nikola Jokic provided just seven points but dished out 16 assists, hauled in 10 rebounds and recorded one steal. Malik Beasley paced the second unit with 12 points. The Jazz next head north of the border to tangle with the Toronto Raptors on Monday evening, while the Nuggets remain home for a showdown with the Boston Celtics on Monday night as well.

The Denver Nuggets defeated the visiting Boston Celtics, 115 - 107, at Pepsi Center on Monday evening. The Celtics got out to a great start on the road, with a quick 10 - 2 run, before going on to build a 34 - 19 lead by the end of the quarter. The Nuggets answered in the second, as they kicked things off with a 90 run, just minutes into the quarter, to cut the deficit to six. The Celtics managed to push their lead back to 10, but the Nuggets did not back down, as they outscored the Celtics, 19 - 11, through the rest of the quarter, to trail by just two at halftime. Both teams came out strong in the third, as they went back - and - forth to keep the score within one or two possessions, however, the Nuggets took over in the final minutes, where they outscored the Celtics 11 - 4, to take a seven - point lead into the fourth. The Nuggets did not look back from there, as they managed to stay one step ahead throughout the fourth, to earn their fifth straight win, and move to 60 at home. Jamal Murray went off for a career - high 48 points on 19 - of - 30 shooting, in 38 minutes, to lead the Nuggets. Gary Harris and Trey Lyles chipped in 13 points each, while Nikola Jokic tallied eight points, 10 rebounds and eight assists. The Nuggets shot 46 percent from the field, including 13 - of - 34 from long range. Meanwhile, Kyrie Irving led the Celtics with 31 points on 13 - of - 17 shooting, five rebounds, five assists, three steals and one block, in 33 minutes. Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown tallied 15 points each, while Al Horford finished with 12 points, six assists, four rebounds and one steal, in 32 minutes. The Celtics shot 51 percent from the field, including 9 - of - 31 from deep. The Celtics (6 - 4) will look to avoid a third straight loss, as they take on the Suns in Phoenix on Thursday. The Nuggets (9 - 1) take on the Grizzlies in Memphis on Wednesday.

The Brooklyn Nets defeated the host Denver Nuggets, 112 - 110, at Pepsi Center on Friday evening. The Nets got out to a strong start on the road, as they outscored the Nuggets by 10 in the first, to take a 34 - 24 lead into the second quarter. The game tightened up in the second, but the Nuggets could not make much of a dent in the lead, as they trailed 55 - 47 at the half. The Nuggets came out strong in the third and managed to tie it up at 65, halfway though the quarter, however, the Nets picked it up again, and pulled ahead by six, heading into the fourth. The Nuggets tightened things up early in the quarter, and the two teams fought it out down the stretch, tied at 102, with three minutes left. The game went down to the wire, with a tie game and the Nets' ball with 22 seconds left. Caris LeVert came up as the hero, as he drained a jumper to seal the win with 0 seconds left. This marks the third straight win for the Nets and the second straight loss for the Nuggets. LeVert finished with 17 points, five assists, two rebounds, one steal and one block, in 31 minutes, while D'Angelo Russell led the Nets with 23 points, five assists, four rebounds and two steals, in 26 minutes. Jarrett Allen added 18 points, nine rebounds, two assists, five blocks and one steal, in 30 minutes. The Nets shot 41 percent from the field, including 12 - of - 33 from long range. Meanwhile, Nikola Jokic led the Nuggets with 37 points, 21 rebounds, three assists, two blocks and one steal, in 33 minutes. Jamal Murray tallied 16 points, five assists, two rebounds and one steal, while Paul Millsap chipped in 11 points and 11 rebounds. The Nuggets shot 46 percent from the field, including 5 - of - 18 from long range. The Nuggets (9 - 3) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Bucks on Sunday. The Nets (6 - 6) take on the Warriors in Golden State on Saturday.

The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the Denver Nuggets, 121 - 114, at Pepsi Center on Sunday evening. The game had the feel of a heavyweight fight, as it featured two of the elite squads from each conference. The Bucks (10 - 3) established that they'd be able to hang in the challenging environment of Pepsi Center from the opening tip, as they essentially matched the Nuggets (9 - 4) basket for basket during the first quarter. Milwaukee then forged ahead in the middle periods, outscoring Denver by a 66 - 53 margin that allowed them to create enough cushion to head into the fourth quarter with an 11 - point advantage. The visitors got it done with some sharp shooting, as they drained 57 percent of their attempts, including 50 percent of their tries from distance. Brook Lopez led the way for the Bucks with 28 points, a total he supplemented with four rebounds, one assist, two blocks and one steal. Giannis Antetokounmpo filled out the stat sheet with 22 points, nine rebounds, eight assists, two steals and one block. Khris Middleton supplied 21 points, five rebounds and two assists. Malcolm Brogdon totaled 20 points, six boards, five assists and two steals. Eric Bledsoe contributed 12 points, eight rebounds, three assists, three steals and one block. Malik Beasley poured in 10 points off the bench. The Bucks head back home to face the Memphis Grizzlies on Wednesday evening, while the Nuggets remain home for a conference showdown with the Houston Rockets on Tuesday night.

The Houston Rockets defeated the Denver Nuggets, 109 - 99, at Pepsi Center on Tuesday evening. The Rockets (6 - 7) have progressively been resembling the team everyone envisioned after a forgettable start. Houston proved to be up to the task, coming out of the gates hot and trailing by just one point at halftime. The third quarter was pivotal, as the visitors gained 10 points worth of separation on the Nuggets (9 - 5). Then, the Rockets managed to match Denver basket for basket during the final 12 minutes, leading to a surprising double - digit victory. Both teams shot particularly well, but Houston's 55 percent success rate slightly edged the home squad's 50 percent figure. Clint Capela led the way for the Rockets with 24 points, nine rebounds, two assists and one block. James Harden followed with a 22 - point, 11 - assist double - double that also included five rebounds, three steals and one block. Chris Paul supplied 21 points, five rebounds, four assists and two steals. James Ennis III had one of his better offensive performances, registering 16 points. P.J. Tucker contributed a full line of 12 points, six boards, two assists, one steal and one block. Monte Morris paced the Nuggets with 19 points over 31 minutes off the bench. He added six assists and two rebounds. Jamal Murray and Gary Harris generated 15 points apiece. Nikola Jokic posted a 14 - point, 12 - rebound double - double that also included seven assists and two steals. Paul Millsap tallied 13 points, one assist and two steals. The Rockets head back home for a Friday night showdown against the Golden State Warriors, while the Nuggets remain home to tangle with the Atlanta Hawks on Friday evening as well.

The Denver Nuggets defeated the visiting Atlanta Hawks, 138 - 93, at Pepsi Center on Thursday evening. The Nuggets went straight to work, as they kicked the game off with a 130 run, through the four minutes of the quarter. They went on to outscore the Hawks, 35 - 23, in the first quarter. Denver remained relentless, as the Nuggets outscored the Hawks by 20 in the third quarter, to put the game entirely out of reach, with a 36 - point deficit heading into the fourth. Seven players scored in double digits for the Nuggets, led by Juancho Hernangomez, who tallied 25 points, nine rebounds, one assists and one steal, in 31 minutes. The Nuggets shot 56 percent from the field, including 13 - of - 31 from deep. Meanwhile, Jeremy Lin led the Hawks with 16 points, five rebounds and five assists, in 25 minutes off the bench. Kent Bazemore added 14 points and two rebounds, while Omari Spellman finished with 10 points, 10 rebounds, three assists, three steals and a block. The Hawks shot just 35 percent from the field, including 9 - of - 42 from long range. The Hawks (3 - 12) will look to end the slide as they take on the Pacers in Indiana on Saturday. The Nuggets (10 - 5) take on the Pelicans in New Orleans on Saturday.

The Denver Nuggets defeated the Orlando Magic, 112 - 87, at Pepsi Center on Friday evening. Following a tightly contested first quarter, the Nuggets (12 - 7) pulled ahead in the second to forge a 54 - 41 halftime lead. Trey Lyles paced the Nuggets with 22 points off the bench. Jamal Murray registered 16 points, six assists, five rebounds, two steals and one block. The Magic remain on the road and visit the Los Angeles Lakers on Sunday afternoon, while the Nuggets visit the Oklahoma City Thunder on Saturday night.

The Denver Nuggets blew out the Los Angeles Lakers, 117 - 85, at Pepsi Center on Tuesday evening. It was a strong night for Denver (14 - 7) on the defensive end, who held LA (11 - 9) to just 40 percent shooting on the night. The Nuggets entered Tuesday's contest boasting the fourth - highest defensive rating in the league, and they showed why on Tuesday. Six Denver players scored in double digits in the win. Jamal Murray and Paul Millsap each scored 20 points to lead Denver in scoring. For the Lakers, Kyle Kuzma led the way with 21 points. It was a rare off night for LeBron James, who shot just 5 - of - 15 for 14 points to go with seven rebounds and two assists. The Lakers as a team struggled on the glass, grabbing just eight offensive rebounds while allowing 15 offensive rebounds for Denver. Los Angeles will host the Indiana Pacers on Thursday, while the Nuggets will visit Portland on Friday.

The Denver Nuggets defeated the Memphis Grizzlies, 105 - 99, at Pepsi Center on Monday. Injuries have continued to plague the Nuggets (18 - 9) this season, but they fought through the absence of two starters Monday to earn a key victory over the Grizzlies after dropping back - to - back games to the Hornets and Hawks. They were led by a stellar outing from Nikola Jokic, who contnues to show how he's one of the best all - around players in the NBA. Jokic posted a game - high 27 points on 9 - of - 14 shooting to go along with 12 rebounds and six assists in 38 minutes. The most important performance from a Nuggets players Monday night, however, was from reserve point guard Monte Morris. Morris came off the bench to score 20 points on 8 - of - 12 shooting on top of five rebounds and six assists in 28 minutes. As for the Grizzlies (15 - 11), they have now dropped two games in a row, and Monday's loss can be chalked up to a lack of production from the starting unit. Mike Conley shot just 5 - of - 14 from the field, but he was the only Memphis starter to reach double figures, scoring a team - high 19 points in 32 minutes. Marc Gasol was just 2 - of - 6 from the field and scored just seven points, while rookie sensation Justin Jackson Jr. played just 20 minutes and managed to post only seven points in the process. The Grizzlies' bench, however, did everything it could to keep the team in the game. Led by Shelvin Mack's 14 points, the five Memphis reserves scored 51 of the team's 99 points, outscoring the five starters.

The Denver Nuggets defeated the visiting Oklahoma City Thunder, 109 - 98, at Pepsi Center on Friday evening. The Nuggets got out to a solid start at home as they outscored the visitors, 39 - 32, through the first quarter. The game tightened up in the second, but the Nuggets were able to keep the edge, as they took a 60 - 52 lead into halftime. The Thunder came out strong in the third and made it a one - point game halfway through the quarter, but the Nuggets bounced back to reclaim a six - point lead by the end of the quarter. The Nuggets pushed their lead to 11 in the fourth, but the Thunder cut it back down to three with 3:20 remaining. However, the Nuggets closed the contest on a 10 - 2 run, to secure their second straight win, and hand the Thunder their second straight loss. Nikola Jokic had a monster night for the Nuggets, with 24 points, 15 rebounds, nine assists and three steals, in 35 minutes. Jamal Murray followed up with 19 points, nine assists and one rebound, while Juancho Hernangomez added 16 points, four rebounds, three assists and a steal, in 33 minutes. Russell Westbrook tallied 13 points, 14 rebounds, two assists, two blocks and one steal, while Steven Adams finished with 26 points, 14 rebounds, two assists, two blocks and one steal. The Thunder (17 - 10) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Clippers on Saturday. The Nuggets (19 - 9) play host to the Raptors on Sunday.

The Denver Nuggets took down the Toronto Raptors, 95 - 86, at Pepsi Center on Sunday evening.
