The big story is Victor Oladipo though, as he was carted off with what appeared to be a serious knee injury. Darren Collison totaled 17 points, four rebounds and eight assists while Myles Turner amassed 13 points, 10 rebounds and four blocks. Toronto returns to action on Friday, as they travel to face the Houston Rockets. Indiana's next game will be on Saturday, as they play the Memphis Grizzlies on the road.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the Indiana Pacers, 132 - 100, at Bankers Life Fieldhouse on Monday evening. The Pacers (32 - 17) came into Monday's contest with a stellar record at Bankers Life Fieldhouse and numbers that corroborated a standing as the stingiest home defense in the NBA. However, that reputation has been earned with the likes of Victor Oladipo (knee) in the lineup, and the star two - guard naturally wasn't available Monday. Moreover, valued backup Tyreke Evans, Oladipo's replacement moving forward in the wake of the latter's season - ending injury, was also out versus the Warriors (36 - 14) due to a back issue. Although the home squad managed to be more competitive in the second period, the game was already essentially decided. Among its multiple advantages on the stat sheet, two of the most significant in Golden State's favor came in shooting percentage (54 to 43) and rebounding (48 - 38). Stephen Curry paced the Warriors with 26 points, adding six rebounds, three assists and two steals. Demarcus Cousins supplied 22 points, six boards and four assists. Kevin Durant and Klay Thompson contributed matching 16 - point tallies, with Durant also notably dishing out seven assists. Kevon Looney generated 15 points, five rebounds, two assists, one steal and one block. Myles Turner led the Pacers with 16 points, adding six rebounds, one assist, two steals and two blocks. Bojan Bogdanovic posted 15 points, three rebounds and two assists. Darren Collison contributed 13 points and eight assists. Aaron Holiday poured in 12 points and also furnished four assists and two rebounds. Thaddeus Young finished with 11 points, seven boards and four assists. The Warriors head back home to face the Philadelphia 76ers on Thursday night, while the Pacers travel to face the Washington Wizards on Wednesday evening.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the Los Angeles Lakers, 136 - 94, at Bankers Life Fieldhouse on Tuesday evening. The Pacers (35 - 19) were looking to continue steadying the ship after losing Victor Oladipo (knee) for the season recently, and the Lakers (27 - 27) ended up being the unfortunate team that was in their way. Indiana essentially sealed the win with a 69 - point first half, but they were almost as prolific in the second while putting up another 67. Moreover, the Pacers saw seven players hit double digits in the scoring column. LeBron James led the way for the Lakers with 18 points, adding nine assists, seven rebounds and one steal. JaVale McGee furnished 16 points, four boards and one steal. Lance Stephenson poured in 13 points. Brandon Ingram and Kyle Kuzma generated matching 12 - point tallies, with Ingram notably hauling in six boards as well. Bojan Bogdanovic led the Pacers with 24 points, supplementing them with five assists, one rebound and one steal. Myles Turner supplied 22 points and four blocks. Aaron Holiday, Domantas Sabonis and Edmond Sumner provided matching 17 - point contributions. Cory Joseph registered 13 points, four rebounds and four assists. Thaddeus Young stuffed the stat sheet with 12 points, 11 rebounds, eight assists and two steals. The Lakers next visit the Boston Celtics on Thursday evening, while the Pacers remain home and take on the Los Angeles Clippers on Thursday night as well.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the Los Angeles Clippers, 116 - 92, at Bankers Life Fieldhouse on Thursday. The Pacers (36 - 19) and the Clippers (30 - 26) were expected to be involved in a tight contest, but Indiana didn't have problems to dominate the game entirely and cruise to a huge win over Los Angeles. The Pacers quickly jumped to a five - point lead in the first quarter (36 - 31), but they ran away with the game in the second quarter where they opened up the gap to 18 points following a 35 - 22 run. Adding insult to the injury, the Clippers won the third quarter 27 - 20 and the game was essentially over from there. The Clippers won the final quarter 19 - 18, but they couldn't mount any sort of a comeback and Indiana cruised their way to a solid win. Bojan Bogdanovic was the top scorer for the Pacers since he finished with 29 points and seven rebounds. Myles Turner added 17 points with four blocks, and Darren Collison contributed 14 points and five assists. Thaddeus Young filled the stat sheet nicely since he ended the contest with 14 points, five rebounds, five steals and four assists. Cory Joseph chipped in with 13 points, nine boards and six assists off the bench. Montrezl Harrell was the top scorer for the Clippers since he contributed 19 points and four assists, but he also committed six turnovers. Danilo Gallinari had 12 points and also added five rebounds. No other Clipper in the starting lineup topped the 10 - point mark, but two bench players did it since both Lou Williams and Johnathan Motley had 10 points each.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 105 - 90, at Bankers Life Fieldhouse on Saturday night. The Pacers (37 - 19) came into Saturday's game showing signs of progress following some early struggles after Victor Oladipo's season - ending knee injury, as they'd won four consecutive contests. Jordan Clarkson led the way for the Cavaliers with 18 points, adding six assists and two rebounds. Larry Nance, Jr. and Collin Sexton each posted 16 points, with Nance notably hauling in 10 rebounds. No other Cleveland player managed double - digit scoring, although Brandon Knight came closest with nine points off the bench in his team debut. Marquese Chriss drew the start at power forward but pitched in just seven points, three rebounds, two assists and one steal. Bojan Bogdanovic led the Pacers with 23 points and supplemented them with two assists and one rebound. Darren Collison delivered 18 points, nine assists, one rebound and one steal. Myles Turner compiled 14 points, eight rebounds and three blocks. Domantas Sabonis generated a 13 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included three assists and one steal. Cory Joseph provided 10 points, 10 assists, eight rebounds and one steal. The Cavaliers head back home to take on the New York Knicks on Monday night, while the Pacers remain home and take on the Charlotte Hornets on Monday evening as well.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the Charlotte Hornets, 99 - 90, at Bankers Life Fieldhouse on Monday evening. The Pacers (38 - 19) were already trending up coming into Monday's contest, and they opened the game seemingly intent on continuing their excellent stretch of play. Indiana built a 32 - 19 first - quarter lead, and although the visiting Hornets (27 - 29) played much more competitively in the second quarter, the hosts still held a 54 - 38 halftime advantage. Charlotte made a game of it in the third by shaving 10 points off their deficit, but the home squad immediately went on an 80 run to open the final period and build enough cushion for the victory. Kemba Walker led the Hornets with 34 points, adding nine rebounds, three assists and two steals. Jeremy Lamb followed with 21 points while also supplying seven rebounds and two assists. Cody Zeller had a near double - double with 18 points, nine rebounds, one assist and one block. Marvin Williams mustered just five points but hauled in 11 rebounds, dished out three assists and recorded two steals. Nicolas Batum had two points on 1 - for - 8 shooting. Myles Turner led the Pacers with 18 points, nine rebounds, one assist, three steals and three blocks. Bojan Bogdanovic furnished 14 points and two rebounds. Darren Collison supplied 13 points, eight assists and four rebounds. Tyreke Evans posted 12 points, two assists and one rebound. Thaddeus Young registered 11 points, eight rebounds and six assists. Wesley Matthews offered eight points, five rebounds and three assists in his Indiana debut. The Hornets next pay a visit to the Orlando Magic on Thursday night, while the Pacers remain home and take on the Milwaukee Bucks on Wednesday evening.

The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the host Indiana Pacers, 106 - 97, at Banker's Life Fieldhouse on Wednesday. In a battle between two of the best teams in the Eastern Conference, this game came down to the wire. In fact, there were nine lead changes in this game, as neither team led by more than 10 points in the second half. Milwaukee ended the game strong, as they went on an 110 run with 4:45 remaining to make it a nine - point margin with one minute remaining. The Bucks (43 - 14) got another monster game from Giannis Antetokounmpo, as he collected 33 points, 19 rebounds, 11 assists and two steals en route to a triple - double. The Pacers (38 - 20) were led by Bojan Bogdanovic, as he tallied 20 points, six rebounds and three assists. Darren Collison amassed 14 points, six rebounds and seven assists. Myles Turner accumulated 11 points, six rebounds, two assists and two blocks while Domantas Sabonis led the bench with 14 points, nine rebounds, three assists and two steals. On deck for Milwaukee is a home matchup after the break against the Boston Celtics on February 21. As for Indiana, they'll play host to the New Orleans Pelicans on the 22nd for their next fixture.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the visiting New Orleans Pelicans, 126 - 111, at Banker's Life Fieldhouse on Friday. While New Orleans led by 20 points in the second quarter, they allowed Indiana to win in comeback fashion. In fact, the Pacers outscored the Pelicans, 68 - 40, in the second half. Julius Randle accumulated 15 points, four rebounds and two assists while Jrue Holiday finished with 14 points, seven rebounds and four assists. Thaddeus Young totaled 16 points, seven rebounds and four steals while Darren Collison generated 10 points and 12 assists. Domantas Sabonis led the bench with 18 points, 13 rebounds and four assists. Both teams have to play again on Saturday, with New Orleans playing host to the Los Angeles Lakers and Indiana traveling to face the Washington Wizards.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the Minnesota Timberwolves, 122 - 115, at Banker's Life Fieldhouse on Thursday. The Timberwolves (29 - 33) entered this game against the Pacers (41 - 22) in a good run of form with four wins in their last six games, and it showed since they quickly got themselves on top by nine points after the first quarter (35 - 26). However, the Pacers would flip the script in the second quarter and they got in the driver seat by halftime thanks to a huge 38 - 25 period that gave them a 64 - 60 lead. Minnesota made things tighter since they won the third quarter 30 - 28, and as a result, this was a two - point game heading into the final 12 minutes of action. Indiana didn't let the game slip away, however, and a 30 - 25 score in the fourth quarter sealed the deal in their favor. Bojan Bogdanovic continues to be one of the best players for Indiana in recent weeks and he carried the ballclub in this one, finishing with 37 points to go along with seven rebounds and four assists. Thaddeus Young filled the stat sheet admirably and finished with 15 points, five assists, five rebounds and three steals, while Wesley Matthews added 12 points. T.J. Leaf looked impressive coming off the bench as he contributed 18 points in 22 minutes of action. Karl-Anthony Towns was the scorer in this game as he had 42 points to go along with 17 rebounds and four assists. Jeff Teague had 13 points, six rebounds and five assists, but also had five turnovers and committed five fouls. Andrew Wiggins chipped in with 11 points, but shot 4 - 14 from the field. Anthony Tolliver (13 points) and Taj Gibson (12 points, nine rebounds) had solid efforts off the bench, though.

The Orlando Magic defeated the host Indiana Pacers, 117 - 112, at Banker's Life Fieldhouse on Saturday. There were 10 ties and 12 lead changes in this tightly - contested game, as neither club led by more than 11 points. Orlando won in comeback fashion, as they outscored Indiana, 34 - 25, in the fourth quarter. Offensive rebounding was the difference for the Magic, as they won that battle, 11 - 3. Thaddeus Young finished with 13 points, six rebounds, five assists and two steals while Cory Joseph led the bench with 14 points, three rebounds and three assists. Both teams return to action on Tuesday, with Indiana playing host to the surprising Chicago Bulls and Orlando traveling to face the Philadelphia 76ers.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the Chicago Bulls, 105 - 96, at Bankers Life Fieldhouse on Tuesday. The Pacers (42 - 23) were undoubtedly the better team on paper against a struggling Bulls (18 - 47) and they did everything they could to showcase that difference right from tip - off. Indiana quickly jumped to a 27 - 17 lead in the first half, and they would never relinquish that advantage within the end of each quarter. Chicago made things difficult, though, as they won both the second (25 - 22) and the third (33 - 28) quarters in order to made it a two - point game entering the final 12 minutes of action. But Indiana stepped it up a notch when it mattered the most and they won the final quarter by a seven - point margin (28 - 21). Most of the heavy lifting on Indiana's offense was made by the starting lineup, as every single starter scored at least 10 points while the entire bench combined for just 25 points. Bojan Bogdanovic led the way with 27 points and six rebounds, while Darren Collison filled the stat sheet and contributed 22 points, four rebounds, two assists, and two steals. Thaddeus Young (11 points, 10 rebounds, six assists) and Myles Turner (10 points, 11 rebounds, seven blocks) filled their respective stat sheets admirably, and Wesley Matthews chipped in with 10 points as well. The Bulls were even worse; not only their bench combined for a mere 23 points, but they only had three players topping the 10 - point mark. Zach LaVine led the way with 27 points, while Robin Lopez had 20 points with nine rebounds and Lauri Markkanen chipped in with 14 points and 13 rebounds of his own. Kris Dunn might have scored just five points, but added seven boards, five assists and two steals.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the New York Knicks, 103 - 98, at Bankers Life Fieldhouse on Tuesday evening. The Pacers (43 - 25) got more than they likely bargained for from the Knicks (13 - 55), which jumped out to a 29 - 27 first - quarter lead despite playing in their third game in the last four nights. However, the home squad came out of intermission playing well on both ends of the court, outscoring New York by a 30 - 21 margin during the period and building enough cushion to withstand a late surge by the visitors in the fourth. Emmanuel Mudiay paced the Knicks with 21 points, adding four rebounds, four assists and two blocks. Dewayne Dotson furnished 18 points, six rebounds, three assists and one steal. Kevin Knox supplied 16 points, five boards and one assist. Deandre Jordan delivered a 12 - point, 16 - rebound double - double that also included five assists. Noah Vonleh registered eight points, seven boards, three assists and two steals. Dennis Smith, Jr. only mustered seven points, three rebounds, three assists and one steal across 25 minutes. Bojan Bogdanovic led the Pacers with 24 points, supplementing them with four rebounds and two assists. Darren Collison furnished 16 points, nine assists, five rebounds and three steals. Myles Turner collected 15 points, nine rebounds, four assists, two steals and two blocks. Wesley Matthews poured in 14 points, while Thaddeus Young and Domantas Sabonis turned in matching 10 - point contributions and hauled in six and seven rebounds, respectively. The Knicks remain on the road and next pay a visit to the San Antonio Spurs on Friday night, while the Pacers remain home and tangle with the Oklahoma City Thunder on Thursday evening.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the visiting Oklahoma City Thunder, 108 - 106, at Banker's Life Fieldhouse on Thursday. While there were only a handful of ties and lead changes in this game, it came down to the wire. In fact, Oklahoma City took a 12 - 11 lead halfway through the first quarter and didn't surrender that lead until late in the fourth quarter. Indiana actually overcame a 13 - point halftime deficit by riding a 58 - 43 second half to victory. Wesley Matthews played the hero, as he made a putback lay - up with less than two seconds remaining to break a tied game. Free-throw shooting was the difference, with the Pacers hitting 27 - of - 32 and the Thunder connecting on just 16 - of - 20. Indiana's bench came up big too, outscoring Oklahoma City's bench, 31 - 25. Assists, steals, blocks and turnovers were all decided within one in this tightly - contested game. The Thunder (42 - 27) were led by Paul George, as he tallied 36 points, six rebounds, five assists and two steals. The Atlanta Hawks defeated the New Orleans Pelicans, 130 - 120, at Smoothie King Center on Tuesday evening. The New Orleans Pelicans defeated the Sacramento Kings, 121 - 118, at Smoothie King Center on Thursday. The Charlotte Hornets defeated the New Orleans Pelicans, 115 - 109, at Smoothie King Center on Wednesday evening. The Golden State Warriors defeated the host New Orleans Pelicans, 112 - 103, at Smoothie King Center on Tuesday. The Detroit Pistons defeated the Brooklyn Nets, 103 - 100, at Little Caesars Arena on Wednesday. It wasn't a great start for the Pistons (10) on Wednesday, as they fell behind 13 - 4 early and were not able to take their first lead of the game until the 3:25 mark in the second quarter. From there, the team watched its lead grow to as much as 13 points in the third period, and while the Nets (0 - 1) made one final push, they were not able to complete the comeback on opening night. Wednesday's win was all about frontcourt production for Detroit, with Blake Griffin and Andre Drummond leading the way. Griffin finished with a team - high 26 points (8 - 17 FG), eight rebounds and six assists across 34 minutes, while Drummond posted a monster double - double of 24 points and 20 rebounds in 32 minutes. In the end, what killed the Nets was their poor performance from the outside, as the team shot a horrid 5 - of - 27 from three - point range Wednesday night.

The Detroit Pistons defeated the Philadelphia 76ers in overtime, 133 - 132, at Little Caesar's Arena on Tuesday. The Sixers (2 - 2) got a spectacular performance out of Joel Embiid, as he led the way with 33 points, 11 rebounds, seven assists and three blocks. J.J. Redick was huge off the bench, providing 30 points, six rebounds and six assists. Robert Covington finished with 16 points, eight rebounds and two assists. Ish Smith led the bench with 21 points and three assists on 9 - of - 12 shooting. On deck for Detroit is a home matchup versus the Cleveland Cavaliers on Thursday. The Detroit Pistons defeated the visiting Cleveland Cavaliers, 110 - 103, at Little Caesars Arena on Thursday evening. The first quarter started out slow, but both teams battled, tied at 15 with 4:26 to go, before the Pistons gained the edge to lead, 30 - 27, heading into the second. The Cavs shot 46 percent from the field, including 8 - of - 24 from long range. The Cavaliers (0 - 5) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Pacers on Saturday. The Pistons (40) play host to the Celtics on Saturday.

The Boston Celtics defeated the host Detroit Pistons, 109 - 87, at Little Caesars Arena on Saturday evening. The Celtics took control mid way through the first quarter, where they amassed an 11 - point lead, and held on to lead, 30 - 21, heading into the second. Jaylen Brown led Boston with 19 points on 6 - of - 13 shooting, while Marcus Morris followed up with 18 points and eight rebounds, in 24 minutes off the bench. The Celtics (4 - 2) also look ahead to the rematch on Tuesday.

The Miami Heat defeated the host Detroit Pistons, 120 - 115, in overtime at Little Ceasar's Arena on Monday. The Charlotte Hornets defeated the Detroit Pistons, 113 - 103, at Little Caesars Arena on Sunday afternoon. The Hornets (7 - 6) and the Pistons (6 - 6) played what it seemed to be a tight encounter in the early going, but Charlotte pulled away for good in the second half to secure a huge win that puts them over .500 and, even though the season is quite young, it looks as if the Hornets can definitively contend for a playoff berth this season. Detroit jumped ahead to a 27 - 24 lead in the first quarter, but Charlotte stormed back to take a 51 - 49 lead at the break. From then, it was all Hornets since they won the remaining two quarters (32 - 26 and 30 - 28, respectively) to win the game comfortably by a 10 - point margin. Charlotte's two point guards carried the team in this game, as both Kemba Walker and Tony Parker finished with 24 points each. The French came off the bench to add four assists and three boards, while Walker chipped in with eight assists and three boards of his own. Cody Zeller contributed with 14 points and six rebounds, and both Marvin Williams and Jeremy Lamb delivered 10 points. The latter, though, also added six rebounds, three assists and two blocks. Andre Drummond led the way for the Pistons and he filled the stat sheet admirably since he ended the game with 23 points, 22 rebounds, three assists, three steals and two blocks. Reggie Jackson contributed with 19 points and seven assists, while Langston Galloway added 10 points off the bench. Blake Griffin, however, only had 10 points while going 4 - of - 16 from the field, but added six rebounds and five assists.

The Detroit Pistons defeated the visiting Cleveland Cavaliers, 113 - 102, at Little Caesars Arena on Monday evening. The Cavs shot 44 percent from the field, including 8 - of - 21 from long range. The Cavaliers (2 - 13) look ahead to Wednesday, when they play host to the Lakers. The Detroit Pistons defeated the visiting Houston Rockets, 116 - 111, in overtime at Little Ceasar's Arena on Friday. Tucker scored 11 points apiece. The Pistons (9 - 7) were led by Blake Griffin, as he tallied 28 points, nine rebounds and four assists. The Detroit Pistons defeated the Phoenix Suns, 118 - 107, at Little Caesars Arena on Sunday afternoon. The Pistons (10 - 7) have now won two straight in the midst of a five - game homestand, and they did it while playing at a stellar level during the final 12 minutes of action against a Suns (4 - 15) team that simply couldn't hold on to their slim advantage. Phoenix jumped to a three - point lead after the first quarter (30 - 27), but the Pistons were in front at half time by a two - point margin (62 - 60). Andre Drummond led the way with 19 points, 16 rebounds and five steals, while Reggie Jackson also contributed 19 points while adding eight assists. Blake Griffin posted a double - double with 16 points and 11 assists, and Reggie Bullock added 13 points. Langston Galloway (15 points) and Stanley Johnson (14 points) impressed off the bench as well. Devin Booker carried Phoenix's offense with a stellar 37 - point performance that also included five assists and four rebounds, but he didn't have a lot of help from his teammates. DeAndre Ayton chipped with a strong double - double of 25 points and 13 rebounds, while Jamal Crawford did his part with 12 points and five assists coming off the bench. Trevor Ariza disappointed with only five points in 36 minutes of action.

The Detroit Pistons defeated the visiting New York Knicks, 115 - 108, at Little Ceasar's Arena on Tuesday. On deck for New York is a road matchup versus the Philadelphia 76ers on Wednesday. As for Detroit, they return to action on Friday when they play host to the Chicago Bulls.

The Detroit Pistons defeated the visiting Chicago Bulls, 107 - 88, at Little Ceasar's Arena on Friday. Detroit came into this matchup as a sizable favorite and a wire - to - wire win shows just why. Both teams return to action on Saturday, with Chicago traveling to play the Houston Rockets and Detroit playing host to the Golden State Warriors.

The Detroit Pistons defeated the visiting Golden State Warriors, 111 - 102, at Little Ceasar's Arena on Saturday. It's rare to see Golden State playing from behind all game but that was the case here. In fact, a 30 - 22 second quarter really set the tone for Detroit, as they held the lead for the entirety of the second half. Reggie Jackson totaled 17 points, two rebounds and five assists. Stanley Johnson was a huge spark off the bench, providing 19 points, seven rebounds and two assists. Both these teams return to action on Monday, with Golden State traveling to face the Atlanta Hawks and Detroit playing host to the Oklahoma City Thunder.

The Oklahoma City Thunder defeated the Detroit Pistons, 110 - 83, at Little Ceasar's Arena on Monday. Andre Drummond had 13 points and also added six rebounds. Reggie Jackson only had 10 points while shooting 4 - 10 from the field. Jon Leuer contributed 12 points in nine only minutes coming off the bench.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the host Detroit Pistons, 117 - 111, at Little Caesars Arena on Friday evening. Jimmy Butler led the way for the 76ers with 38 points, six rebounds, six assists, three steals and one block, in 38 minutes. Ben Simmons, J.J. Redick and Mike Muscala chipped in 18 points each to help the cause. The Sixers shot 49 percent from the field, including 9 - of - 32 from long range. Meanwhile, Blake Griffin led the Pistons with 31 points, 12 rebounds and six assists, in 37 minutes. The Pistons (13 - 10) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Pelicans on Sunday. The 76ers (18 - 9) play host to the Pistons on Monday.

The New Orleans Pelicans defeated the Detroit Pistons, 116 - 108, at Little Caesars Arena on Sunday afternoon. The Pelicans (14 - 14) came out of the gates hot, outscoring the Pistons (13 - 11) by a 28 - 20 margin in the first 12 minutes. The Detroit Pistons defeated the Orlando Magic, 115 - 98, at Little Caesars Arena on Thursday evening. Aaron Gordon led the way for the Magic with 20 points, adding four assists, three rebounds and one steal. D.J. Augustin offered 18 points, four rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block. Evan Fournier poured in 13 points and added three assists and one rebound. Nikola Vucevic generated a 12 - point, 12 - rebound double - double that also included four assists and one steal. Ish Smith paced the Detroit bench with 15 points while also dishing out six assists and hauling in four rebounds. Langston Galloway turned in 12 points, two assists and one steal. The Magic remains on the road and visits the Indiana Pacers on Saturday evening, while the Pistons remain home and tangle with the Portland Trail Blazers on Saturday night as well.

The Detroit Pistons defeated the Portland Trail Blazers, 99 - 90, at Little Caesars Arena on Saturday night. After a first quarter that was a defensive slugfest, the two teams matched each other bucket for bucket in the second but still headed into halftime with only 65 combined points. However, The Pistons (39 - 37) found their stroke in the third, erasing a slim three - point deficit and building a seven - point advantage going into the fourth quarter. Detroit then continued playing excellent defense and kept the Trail Blazers (48 - 28) at bay throughout the final period. Ultimately, Portland shot just 37 percent and committed 16 turnovers. Damian Lillard paced the Trail Blazers with 23 points, adding eight rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block. Enes Kanter produced a 20 - point, 15 - rebound double - double that also included two steals. Seth Curry led the bench with 11 points. Maurice Harkless contributed 10 points, 10 boards, two assists, three blocks and one steal. Jake Layman matched Harkless' scoring total and added three rebounds, two assists, one steal and one block. Reggie Jackson led the Pistons with 28 points and supplemented them with five rebounds, five assists and one block. Andre Drummond generated a 22 - point, 19 - rebound double - double that also included four assists, four steals and three blocks. Langston Galloway netted 12 points. The Trail Blazers continue on the road and visit the Minnesota Timberwolves on Monday night, while the Pistons pay a visit to the Indiana Pacers on Monday evening.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the Detroit Pistons, 108 - 89, at Little Caesars Arena on Wednesday. The Pacers (47 - 32) wanted to earn a second - consecutive win over the Pistons (39 - 39) and that's exactly what they accomplished, although they far more dominant in this one. Indiana quickly jumped ahead to a 18 - 15 lead in the first quarter, and they would never relinquish that advantage. In fact, the Pacers won every single quarter in this one so they managed to destroy Detroit completely. The Pacers won the remaining three quarters by 26 - 21, 34 - 26 and 30 - 27, respectively, on their to a comfortable 19 - point win away from home. Five Indiana players scored in double digits in this one, and the top scorer was Thaddeus Young who finished with 21 points, eight rebounds, four assists and two steals. Bojan Bogdanovic had 17 points, four rebounds and three assists, while Myles Turner chipped in with 17 points and five boards. Cory Joseph thrived with 12 assists as well as six points. Domantas Sabonis had 15 points and 13 rebounds coming off the bench, and Doug McDermott delivered 14 points despite not starting. The Pistons once again didn't have Blake Griffin but Andre Drummond was their most reliable scorer since he finished with 28 points, 19 rebounds, three assists, three steals and three blocks. Wayne Ellington delivered 24 points with four boards, while Reggie Jackson chipped in with 16 points, five boards and four assists. Luke Kennard had 10 points off the bench.

The Charlotte Hornets defeated the Detroit Pistons, 104 - 91, at Little Caesars Arena on Sunday afternoon. The Hornets (38 - 42) and Pistons (39 - 41) both came into the contest with a chance at the postseason, but Detroit's chances were considerably higher. However, it was Charlotte playing with much more urgency early, as they built a 60 - 42 lead by halftime. The Pistons ultimately shot just 37 percent, including 24 percent from three - point range. Kemba Walker paced the Hornets with 31 points, adding eight rebounds, seven assists and one steal. Frank Kaminsky followed with 24 points, five rebounds, two assists and one block. Jeremy Lamb totaled 17 points, six boards, three assists and two steals. Dwayne Bacon poured in 14 points, while Miles Bridges furnished 10 points, five rebounds, five assists, two blocks and one steal. Ish Smith led the Pistons with 20 points, supplementing them with four rebounds and four assists. Blake Griffin totaled 16 points, four rebounds and four assists. Andre Drummond generated a 15 - point, 23 - rebound double - double that also included one assist and three blocks. Wayne Ellington turned in 14 points, four rebounds, three assists and one steal. The Hornets next pay a visit to the Cleveland Cavaliers on Tuesday evening, while the Pistons remain home to tangle with the Memphis Grizzlies on Tuesday night as well.

The Detroit Pistons defeated the Memphis Grizzlies, 100 - 93, at Little Caesars Arena on Tuesday night. The Pistons (40 - 41) came into the contest with the utmost urgency, knowing they'd need to win their last two games to control their own destiny and hang on to the eighth and final playoff spot in the Eastern Conference. It was therefore rather surprising to see Detroit get off to a poor start, as they were behind by a 32 - 20 margin after one quarter and 57 - 38 at halftime. They finally seemed to awaken to the reality of their circumstances coming out of intermission by cutting four points in the Grizzlies' (32 - 49) advantage during the third quarter, but it was a monumental 21 - 4 run over the first 5:58 of the final period that finally gave them a lead for the first time since 11:44 mark of the first quarter. Although it held Detroit to just 40 percent shooting, Memphis hurt its cause by committing 21 turnovers. Delon Wright and Bruno Caboclo co - led the Grizzlies with 15 points, with Wright notably pulling down nine rebounds. Tyler Zeller totaled 13 points, six rebounds, three assists and two blocks. Tyler Dorsey generated 12 points, four rebounds and three assists. Ivan Rabb, Chandler Parsons and Jevon Carter had matching nine - point tallies off the bench. Ish Smith led the Pistons with 22 points, adding four assists and three rebounds. Andre Drummond posted a 20 - point, 17 - rebound double - double that also included one assist, five steals and three blocks. Luke Kennard contributed 15 points, two rebounds and one assist. Reggie Jackson supplied 12 points, five assists, one rebound and one steal. Blake Griffin, whose workload is being managed due to knee soreness, posted just five points, two rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block while logging 18 minutes. The Grizzlies wrap up the season by hosting the Golden State Warriors on Wednesday night, while the Pistons visit the New York Knicks on Wednesday evening in another must - win game.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 116 - 104, at Scotiabank Arena on Wednesday evening. Both teams kicked off new eras in the regular - season opener for each, with the Raptors (10) rolling out prized offseason acquisition Kawhi Leonard and the Cavaliers (0 - 1) taking the floor without LeBron James to open a season for the first time since 2013. At least for Wednesday, Toronto's outlook was much brighter. Leonard generated a 24 - point, 13 - rebound double - double while working in concert with star holdover Kyle Lowry, who posted a game - high 27. Toronto gained a degree of separation with a 32 - 22 second - quarter advantage, and they shot 48 percent overall (including 42 percent from three - point range). Kevin Love paced the Cavaliers with 21 points, adding eight rebounds and two assists. Cedi Osman followed with a 17 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included four assists and two steals. George Hill and fellow guard Jordan Clarkson generated matching 15 - point tallies, with the former adding seven assists and two rebounds, and the latter registering three rebounds as well. Rodney Hood poured in 12 points and supplemented them with two boards, one assist and one steal. Tristan Thompson mustered just three points but also brought in 13 rebounds and dished out one assist. Rookie first - round pick Collin Sexton posted nine points and three rebounds in 17 minutes off the bench. Lowry added eight assists, one rebound, one steal and one block to his aforementioned scoring tally. Leonard also dished out two assists to supplement his double - digit point and rebound totals. Fred VanVleet contributed a bench - leading 14 points, along with five assists and two rebounds. Pascal Siakam pitched in 13 points, two rebounds, two assists and one block. Danny Green turned in 11 points, five boards, two steals and two blocks in his Raptors regular - season debut. Jonas Valanciunas hauled in 12 rebounds over 20 minutes. The Cavaliers remain on the road and take on the Minnesota Timberwolves on Friday night, while the Raptors host the Celtics in an early - season Eastern Conference showdown that same evening.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the visiting Boston Celtics, 113 - 101, at Air Canada Center on Friday, In a battle between the Eastern Conference elite, this game wasn't decided until the final minutes. In fact, Toronto ended the game on a 12 - 2 run, as it took seven ties and 13 lead changes to determine a winner. That late run by the Raptors gave them the only double - digit lead by either team, as the final 12 - point margin ended up being the largest lead of this game. The shooting disparity was the only noticeable difference in the stat sheet, with Toronto connecting on 47 percent of their shots while holding Boston to just 40 percent shooting. Free-throw shooting was imperative as well, with the Raptors hitting 14 - of - 17 and the Celtics going just 7 - of - 10 from the charity stripe. The Celtics (1 - 1) were led by Kyrie Irving, as he tallied 21 points, four rebounds and six assists. Jayson Tatum totaled 16 points, nine rebounds and two assists. Al Horford approached a triple - double, accumulating 14 points, 10 rebounds and nine assists. Gordon Hayward amassed 14 points, seven rebounds and two assists. The Raptors (20) got a spectacular performance out of Kawhi Leonard, as he accrued 31 points, 10 rebounds and three assists. Serge Ibaka finished with 21 points, six rebounds and two assists on 10 - of - 14 shooting. Kyle Lowry generated 15 points, six rebounds and six assists. Fred VanVleet led the bench with 11 points, six rebounds and seven assists. Both teams play road games on Saturday for their next outing, with Toronto playing the Washington Wizards and Boston facing off with the New York Knicks.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the Charlotte Hornets, 127 - 106, at Scotiabank Arena on Monday night. The Raptors (40) didn't have many problems to stay undefeated and secure their fourth straight win of the season against a Hornets (2 - 2) team that was never able to match Toronto's pace and intensity. Toronto quickly raced to a nine - point lead after the first 12 minutes of action (31 - 22) and they didn't have problems to close things out quickly. The best sign of Toronto's dominance was the fact that they won every single quarter of the game while scoring at least 30 points in each one of them: 31 - 22, 31 - 25, 35 - 32 and 30 - 27. Kawhi Leonard was the top scorer for the Raptors since he finished with 22 points and also added four rebounds and three assists, but Kyle Lowry also stood out with a double - double of 16 points and 14 assists. Danny Green had 16 points and Serge Ibaka came close to a double - double of his own with 15 points and eight boards. Jonas Valanciunas came off the bench to put 17 points and 10 rebounds in only 19 minutes. Kemba Walker led the way for the Hornets with 26 points, five rebounds and five assists in 33 minutes, but it wasn't enough. Jeremy Lamb added 16 points, and Nicolas Batum chipped in with 13 of his own. Two bench players also reached the 10 - point plateau: Willy Hernangomez (11 points, five boards) and Malik Monk (10 points, three assists).

The Toronto Raptors defeated the Minnesota Timberwolves, 112 - 105, at Scotiabank Arena on Wednesday night. The Raptors (50) are showing early in the season why they should be considered as one of the top teams in the Eastern Conference and they had no problems to dismantle a combative Timberwolves (2 - 3) squad that fought this game until the very end. However, the Raptors were in control early on and they never let it go: they jumped to a 26 - 19 lead in the first quarter and increased their lead to nine points at the break following a 31 - 29 second quarter. Minnesota showed some fight in the third quarter (26 - 26) and they won the final 12 minutes of action (29 - 31), but it wasn't enough. The Canadian franchise closed things out when they needed to, and remained undefeated through their first five games of the season. Kawhi Leonard led the way for Toronto with 35 points, five rebounds, two assists, two steals and two blocks, while Kyle Lowry once again posted a double - double with 13 points and 10 assists, while also adding six rebounds and four steals. Serge Ibaka contributed with 15 points, while Jonas Valanciunas came close to post another double - double off the bench with 16 points and nine rebounds in 20 minutes. Norman Powell added 10 points. Jimmy Butler once again led the Timberwolves with 23 points but he also filled the stat sheet with six steals, five assists and four rebounds. Taj Gibson had 13 points with six rebounds, and Jeff Teague finished with 12 points and nine assists. Karl-Anthony Towns disappointed, though, since he only had 12 points and eight boards.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the Dallas Mavericks, 116 - 107, at Scotiabank Arena on Friday evening. The Raptors (60) had proven invincible at home coming into Friday's contest, and their level of play in the first quarter was a good example of why. Toronto jumped on the Mavericks (2 - 3) early, establishing a 39 - 26 lead. While Dallas managed to bring their deficit down to a slim three points entering the final period, the home squad stepped up, outscoring the visitors by a 24 - 18 margin. Both shooting and rebounding were keys to victory, as the Raptors enjoyed a 48 percent - 41 percent advantage from the field and a 50 - 44 edge on the boards. Luka Doncic paced the Mavericks with 22 points, which he complemented with five rebounds and four assists. Wesley Matthews supplied 21 points and dished out one assist. DeAndre Jordan generated an 18 - point, 15 - rebound double - double that also included five assists and one block. Harrison Barnes turned in 14 points, six rebounds, three assists and one block. Jalen Brunson, who started for Dennis Smith, Jr. (ankle), and Maxi Kleber both generated eight - point deficits. Kawhi Leonard paced the Raptors with 21 points, nine rebounds, five assists, three steals and one block. Kyle Lowry posted a 20 - point, 12 - assist double - double that also included four rebounds and a block. Jonas Valanciunas started and managed 17 points, eight rebounds, one assist and one steal. Danny Green poured in 15 points and added eight rebounds, one steal and one block. Serge Ibaka pitched in a bench - leading 11 points along with eight rebounds, an assist and two blocks. The Mavericks heads back home and take on the Utah Jazz on Sunday evening, while the Raptors pay a visit to the Milwaukee Bucks on Monday night.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the Philadelphia 76ers, 129 - 112, at Scotiabank Arena on Tuesday evening. The Raptors (7 - 1) entered this game undefeated at home and the Sixers (4 - 4) were winless on the road; both streaks held up following the conclusion of this game as Toronto moved up to 60 at Scotiabank Arena while Philadelphia is now 0 - 4 away from Wells Fargo Center. The Canadian franchise didn't have problems to secure the win here, as they took advantage of the fact that this was the second game of a back - to - back for the Sixers, and cruised their way to a huge win. Toronto jumped to a 35 - 26 lead in the first quarter, and they bolstered that advantage both in the second (32 - 27) and third (38 - 33) quarters. Philly won the final 12 minutes (26 - 24), but it wasn't enough and Toronto closed things out with ease. Kawhi Leonard was the best player for the Raptors since he finished with 31 points, seven rebounds, four assists and four steals, once again looking like a complete threat on both ends of the court. Kyle Lowry chipped in with a double - double of 20 points and 12 assists, while Pascal Siakam did the same thanks to 15 points and 15 boards. Jonas Valanciunas once again thrived off the bench since he finished with 23 points and four rebounds in only 17 minutes. Ben Simmons led the way for the Sixers with 11 points, 10 assists and eight rebounds, but he also committed 11 turnovers. Joel Embiid was the team's leading scorer with 31 points and 11 rebounds, while Robert Covington chipped in with 15 points, four rebounds and four steals. J.J. Redick (13 points) and Mike Muscala (12 points, five boards) both looked solid off the bench.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the visiting New York Knicks, 128 - 112, at Air Canada Center on Saturday. Toronto came into this game as a heavy favorite and a 16 - point victory shows just why. They did most of their damage in the middle quarters, outscoring New York, 75 - 57, in the second and third quarters. In addition, the Raptors led by at least 15 points for the entirety of the fourth quarter. The shooting disparity was a clear difference, with Toronto shooting 53 percent from the field and 40 percent from three - point range while holding New York to just 46 percent from the field and 27 percent from long range. Ball movement was also critical, with the Raptors out - assisting the Knicks, 24 - 18. While New York shot a better percentage at the free - throw line than Toronto, the Raptors ended up taking more attempts, 40 - 22. The Knicks (4 - 9) got another gem out of Tim Hardaway Jr., as he tallied 27 points, four rebounds and two assists on 11 - of - 17 from the field. Enes Kanter was huge off the bench, totaling 15 points and 15 boards. Mario Hezonja, Emmanuel Mudiay, and Kevin Knox all reached double figures off the bench as well. The Raptors (12 - 1) got a career - best 23 points, three rebounds and two assists from Pascal Siakam, as he did that on 6 - of - 7 shooting. Serge Ibaka amassed 12 points and eight boards/. Kawhi Leonard accrued 12 points, seven rebounds and three assists while Kyle Lowry finished with 10 points, two rebounds and eight assists. Jonas Valanciunas provided a 19 - point, 10 - rebound double - double to lead the bench. O.G. Anunoby and Delon Wright also reached double figures in scoring off the bench as well. On deck for New York is a home matchup versus the Orlando Magic on Sunday. As for Toronto, they're off until Monday when they welcome the New Orleans Pelicans to Canada.

The New Orleans Pelicans defeated the Toronto Raptors, 126 - 110, at Scotiabank Arena on Monday evening. The Pelicans (7 - 6) delivered one of their most impressive performances of the season while playing on the road against the Raptors (12 - 2), one of the best teams in The Association so far, and they gave the Canadian franchise their first home loss of the current campaign. New Orleans' dominance was reflected by the fact that they won all four quarters in this one (31 - 29, 35 - 32, 28 - 22 and 32 - 27, respectively), not giving Toronto a chance to fight back during most of the game. With the win, the Pelicans are now riding a three - game winning streak, while the Raptors saw their six - game winning run come to an end in the first night of a back - to - back. E'Twaun Moore was the leading scorer with 30 points (13 - 18 from the field), while Jrue Holiday looked impressive thanks to his 29 points and 14 assists. Anthony Davis had another monster performance with 25 points, 20 rebounds, six assists and two blocks, and Julius Randle had a double - double of 17 points and 12 boards to go along with four assists. Pascal Siakam led the way for Toronto with 22 points, three rebounds and three blocks in 28 minutes of action. Kawhi Leonard filled the stat sheet admirably and contributed with 20 points, six rebounds, two assists, one steal and one block. Serge Ibaka had 19 points with 14 boards, and O.G. Anunoby added 17 points off the bench. Kyle Lowry struggled and only managed to score four points (1 - 9 from the field) but added 11 assists.

The Detroit Pistons defeated the host Toronto Raptors, 106 - 104, at Air Canada Center on Wednesday. Despite the fact that Toronto led for over 40 minutes of this game, it wasn't decided until the final seconds. In fact, Toronto held a 19 - point lead halfway through the third quarter, as Detroit responded with a 40 - 19 run to re - take the lead with four minutes remaining. The Pistons never relinquished the lead from there, as Reggie Bullock hit a game - winning floater at the buzzer to break a tied game. There were five ties and 10 lead changes in total, albeit all of those coming in the first five minutes and final five minutes of the game. Toronto's shooting was their downfall, as they went just 4 - of - 20 from three - point range and 10 - of - 17 from the free - throw line. Detroit won the game through long - range shooting, hitting 10 - of - 33 from three - point range. The Pistons bench also played a huge factor, outscoring the Raptors bench, 40 - 28. The Pistons (7 - 6) were led by Blake Griffin, as he collected 30 points, 12 rebounds, three assists, three steals and two blocks. Andre Drummond totaled 11 points and 14 boards. Reggie Jackson finished with 13 points and six assists. Stanley Johnson and Langston Galloway each reached double figures in scoring, as they each went 5 - of - 8 from the field off of the bench. The Raptors (12 - 3) were led by Kawhi Leonard, as he tallied 26 points, nine rebounds, four assists and three steals. Pascal Siakam amassed 17 points, seven rebounds and two assists. Kyle Lowry accrued 14 points, seven rebounds and seven assists. Greg Monroe provided 17 points and nine boards to lead the bench. Detroit won't play again until Monday, when they play host to the Cleveland Cavaliers. As for Toronto, they travel to play the Boston Celtics on Friday for their next outing.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the Washington Wizards, 123 - 101, at Scotiabank Arena on Friday evening. The Raptors (16 - 4) started this game strong and it was clear right from the start that they weren't going to give the Wizards (6 - 12) much of a chance. In fact, Washington saw how Toronto jumped to a 12 - point lead after the first quarter (38 - 26), and the Wizards couldn't get closer the rest of the way even if they won the second quarter by a 36 - 32 score. However, Toronto won the remaining two quarters (31 - 25 and 22 - 14), and now they have won the 80 percent of their games thus far in the 2018 - 19 NBA season. Six Toronto players scored in double digits and Kawhi Leonard paced the offense with 27 points, 10 rebounds, two assists and two steals. Kyle Lowry came one assist short of a double - double since he finished with 15 points and nine assists. O.G. Anunoby scored 15 points off the bench, while Serge Ibaka chipped in with 12 points, nine rebounds, and four blocks. Fred VanVleet added 13 points, seven assists and four boards in only 23 minutes. Bradley Beal was the highest scorer for the Wizards thanks to a 20 - point performance. Otto Porter Jr. filled the stat sheet with 17 points, seven rebounds and four assists, Kelly Oubre Jr. had 13 points with six rebounds, and Markieff Morris finished with 16 points. John Wall shot poorly from the field, but ended with 11 points and 11 assists.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the visiting Miami Heat, 125 - 115, at Air Canada Center on Sunday evening. It was a wire - to - wire win for Toronto (17 - 4), as the Raptors shot 52 percent from the field in a commanding win. The Raptors ran away with the game in the third quarter, when they led by as much as 19. Despite an early fourth quarter run by Miami (7 - 12) that cut the lead to just eight, Toronto was able to maintain a comfortable advantage until the final buzzer. Kawhi Leonard led Toronto with 29 points, 10 rebounds, and two steals. Paskal Siakim added 21 points as well as two steals and two blocks. All-Star point guard Kyle Lowry finished with a double - double, scoring 12 points and dishing out 10 assists. As a team, Toronto finished shooting 52 percent from the field and 80 percent from the free - throw line, in addition to hitting 11 three - pointers. Miami, meanwhile, saw incredible play from its second unit after its starters fell flat. Hassan Whiteside played just 12 minutes after picking up four personal fouls. This left plenty of play time for sophomore center Bam Adebayo, who had 21 rebounds and 16 points off the bench. Veteran star Dwyane Wade turned back the clock with a lights - out 35 - point performance to lead the second unit. On Tuesday, Miami will host the Atlanta Hawks, while the Raptors will visit Memphis.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the visiting Golden State Warriors, 131 - 128, at Air Canada Center on Thursday. While Golden State only held the lead for a couple minutes of this game, it took an overtime session to determine a winner. In fact, Golden State ended regulation on a 15 - 5 run to send the game into an extra session. With that said, the Raptors never trailed in the overtime, as their only deficit in the game came in the first five minutes of the first quarter. Toronto's offense was on point, as they went 47 - of - 90 from the field and 15 - of - 38 from three - point range. They also dominated at the free - throw line, hitting 22 - of - 24 while Golden State connected on 17 - of - 20.
