The Warriors (15 - 8) got another gem from Kevin Durant, as he tallied 51 points, 11 rebounds and six assists. This was the first time in his career that he's scored at least 40 points in three - straight games. Klay Thompson was the only other starter in double figures, as he totaled 23 points, three rebounds and three assists. Jonas Jerebko led the bench with 20 points, nine rebounds and three assists. Kevon Looney also played well off the bench, amassing seven points and 10 boards. The Raptors (19 - 4) were led by Kawhi Leonard, as he collected 37 points, eight rebounds and three assists. Pascal Siakam dropped a career - high 26 points on 8 - of - 10 shooting. Serge Ibaka finished with 20 points and four boards. Kyle Lowry accumulated 10 points, eight rebounds, 12 assists and three steals. Both teams return to action on Saturday, with Golden State traveling to play the Detroit Pistons and Toronto facing the Cleveland Cavaliers on the road.

The Los Angeles Clippers took down the New Orleans Pelicans, 129 - 126, at Smoothie King Center on Monday evening. After falling by just four points on the road on Sunday, the Clippers (16 - 7) managed to come out on the winning end of a close game in New Orleans. Despite a career - best 37 points from Pelicans' big man Julius Randle, LA was able to hang on to a narrow lead throughout the late fourth quarter. Both teams absolutely dominated on the interior, with the Clippers shooting 59 percent from the floor and New Orleans (12 - 13) shooting an admirable 53 percent. New Orleans also drained 13 three - pointers despite the loss. For the Clippers, Tobias Harris led the way with 27 points. Harris has been the unequivocal leader of this year's Clippers squad, earning Western Conference Player of the Month honors for October and November. In addition to Harris's strong play, the team saw 20 points from breakout star Montrezl Harrell. Harrell has scored 20 or more points in six of his last eight games despite averaging just over 25 minutes per game over that stretch. New Orleans, meanwhile, saw a career night from Randle. His 37 points came on 15 - of - 24 shooting from the field, and he also pulled down seven rebounds. Jrue Holiday added a whopping 32 points and 14 assists, while Anthony Davis displayed his typical dominance, finishing with 23 points, 14 rebounds, six assists, three steals, and three blocks. Despite those strong performances, New Orleans could not match LA's incredible offensive output. New Orleans will host the Dallas Mavericks on Thursday, while the Clippers will visit Memphis.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the visiting Philadelphia 76ers, 113 - 102, at Air Canada Center on Wednesday. In a battle between the Eastern Conference elite, Toronto showed why they're top dogs. They did most of their damage in the second and fourth quarters, outscoring Philadelphia, 65 - 45. It was competitive throughout though, as there were eight ties and seven lead changes in total. The Raptors defense was key, as they recorded 12 steals while winning the turnover differential, 21 - 11. Toronto did a ton of their havoc down low, outscoring the Sixers in the paint, 62 - 42. The Sixers (17 - 9) were led by Jimmy Butler, as he totaled 38 points and 10 rebounds on 15 - of - 27 from the field. J.J. Redick amassed 25 points and four assists. Joel Embiid went just 5 - of - 17 from the field but still finished with 10 points, 12 rebounds, five assists and two blocks. Ben Simmons accrued eight points, 10 rebounds and 11 assists. The Raptors (21 - 5) got a gem from Kawhi Leonard, as he tallied 36 points, nine rebounds and five steals. Serge Ibaka finished with 18 points, eight rebounds and two assists. Jonas Valanciunas was a huge spark off the bench, providing 26 points, eight rebounds and two assists. No other player reached double figures in scoring. Both teams return to action on Friday, with Toronto traveling to face the Brooklyn Nets and Philadelphia playing the Detroit Pistons on the road as well.

The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the host Toronto Raptors, 104 - 99, at Scotiabank Arena on Sunday. In a battle between two of the Eastern Conference elite, this matchup wasn't decided until the final shot. In fact, it took eight ties and 14 lead changes to determine a winner, as neither club led by more than 11 points. The statistics were incredibly even, as these clubs tied in field goal percentage, rebounds and steals while coming within two of one another in assists and turnovers. Three-point shooting was the only noticeable difference for Milwaukee, as they connected on 15 - of - 39 while holding Toronto to 15 - of - 44. In addition, the Bucks won the points in the paint battle, 38 - 32, and the fastbreak scoring, 12 - 7. The Bucks (16 - 8) were led by Giannis Antetokounmpo, as he collected 19 points, 19 rebounds and six assists. Brook Lopez matched those 19 points, adding two assists and two steals to his tally. Malcolm Brogdon tallied 18 points, two rebounds and two assists. Khris Middleton finished with 10 points, nine rebounds and five assists. The Raptors (21 - 6) were led by Serge Ibaka, as he accrued 22 points, six rebounds, four assists, two steals and two blocks. Kawhi Leonard amassed 20 points, eight rebounds, four assists, two steals and two blocks. Pascal Siakam totaled 17 points, seven rebounds, two assists and three blocks. Fred VanVleet led the bench with 19 points, two rebounds and two assists. On deck for Milwaukee is a home matchup versus the Cleveland Cavaliers on Monday. As for Toronto, they return to action on Tuesday when they face the Los Angeles Clippers on the road.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the visiting Indiana Pacers, 99 - 96, at Scotiabank Arena on Wednesday. While Indiana held the lead for 45 minutes of this game, it wasn't decided until the final shot. In fact, the Pacers blew a 17 - point lead late in the third quarter, as Toronto responded with a 24 - 11 fourth quarter to complete their comeback win. Toronto's defense was critical in that quarter, holding Indiana to 5 - of - 18 from the field while forcing seven turnovers. The Raptors defense was critical all night though, as they recorded 15 steals and 10 blocks while winning the turnover differential, 20 - 9. Toronto also did a great job in the interior, outscoring Indiana in the paint, 56 - 44. They won this game despite shooting 41 percent from the field and 23 percent from three - point range. The Pacers (20 - 11) were led by Victor Oladipo, as he tallied 20 points, two rebounds and four assists. Bojan Bogdanovic accrued 18 points, five rebounds and two steals. Myles Turner finished with 10 points, 14 rebounds and five blocks. Domantas Sabonis led the bench with 12 points, 10 rebounds and two assists. The Raptors (24 - 9) were led by Kawhi Leonard, as he collected 28 points, 10 rebounds, six assists and four steals. Pascal Siakam accumulated 17 points, seven rebounds, four assists and three steals. Greg Monroe made a spot start and amassed 13 points and eight rebounds. Fred VanVleet went just 4 - of - 17 from the field in a spot start but provided 11 points, two steals and three blocks with some great defense late. Both teams return to action on Friday, with Indiana traveling to face the surging Brooklyn Nets and Toronto playing host to the struggling Cleveland Cavaliers.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 126 - 110, at Scotiabank Arena on Friday evening. The Raptors (25 - 9) are clearly a superior team to the Cavaliers (8 - 25) when both squads are at full health, but Toronto came into Friday's game without the trio of Kyle Lowry (thigh), Danny Green (knee) and Serge Ibaka (knee). As a result, the game was highly competitive through three - plus quarters, but the home squad closed out the last five minutes on a 20 - 9 run. As the elevated final score implies, both teams shot very well, but the Raptors were just a bit better with a 53 percent succcess rate from the field. The Cavaliers were paced by Jordan Clarkson, who compiled 20 points and added four rebounds, four assists and a block. Collin Sexton turned in 17 points, five rebounds, three assists and one steal. Larry Nance, Jr. produced a 16 - point, 12 - rebound double - double that also included two assists, two blocks and one steal. Cedi Osman pitched in 12 points. The Raptors were paced by Kawhi Leonard, who totaled 37 points, six rebounds, one assist and one steal. O.G. Anunoby managed 21 points, eight rebounds and one block. Pascal Siakam delivered a 15 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included three assists and two steals. Fred VanVleet supplied a full line of 14 points, eight assists, five rebounds, two steals and one block. Norman Powell paced the second unit with 11 points. The Cavaliers head back home to face the Chicago Bulls on Sunday evening, while the Raptors pay a visit to the Philadelphia 76ers on Saturday night.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the visiting Chicago Bulls, 95 - 89, at Scotiabank Arena on Sunday. While there were only eight ties and nine lead changes in this game, it was tight throughout. In fact, neither club ever attained a double - digit lead, despite the fact that Toronto held the lead for the final 20 minutes of action. Offensive rebounding was huge for Toronto, as they won that battle, 17 - 7. They also did a great job of protecting the rim, out - blocking the Bulls, 8 - 2. Turnovers were also critical, with the Raptors forcing 18 turnovers from the Bulls, allowing them to take 12 more shots than Chicago, which happened to be Toronto's turnover total. The Bulls (10 - 27) were led by Lauri Marrkanen, as he tallied 18 points, 10 rebounds and two steals. Wendell Carter Jr. had his first game without a foul, as he totaled 16 points and 11 boards. Kris Dunn finished with 14 points, three rebounds, eight assists and two blocks. Zach LaVine went just 3 - of - 17 from the field to amass 13 points, three rebounds and two assists before mercifully fouling out. The Raptors (27 - 11) were led by Kawhi Leonard, as he generated 27 points and nine rebounds. Pascal Siakam accumulated 20 points, 12 rebounds and four assists. Fred VanVleet got another start and finished with 10 points, five rebounds and seven assists. Serge Ibaka, Danny Green and Greg Monroe had two blocks apiece. On deck for Toronto is a home matchup versus the Utah Jazz on Tuesday. As for Chicago, they return to action on Wednesday when they play host to the Orlando Magic.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the Utah Jazz, 112 - 116, at Scotiabank Arena on Tuesday. The Raptors (28 - 11) and the Jazz (18 - 20) delivered a high - scoring game at the north of the border, but in the end Toronto ended winning the game since they did a better job of taking advantage of their momentum across all four quarters. In fact, the Raptors jumped ahead 26 - 24 in the first quarter, but Utah answered right back and a 29 - 25 second quarter gave them a two - point lead entering the break (53 - 51). But the Raptors would pull away for good in the third quarter, where they won by a 12 - point margin (44 - 32). Utah won the final quarter by four points (31 - 27), but it wouldn't be enough and Toronto, who entered this game with a 7 - 7 record in their past 14 contests, secured a huge win in front of their crowd. Toronto's offense relied on only three players in this game, but the bet paid off admirably. Kawhi Leonard paved the way with an impressive 45 - point, six - rebound performance, although Pascal Siakam didn't hide and finished the contest with 28 points and 10 rebounds. Norman Powell had a solid effort with 14 points coming off the bench, while Fred VanVleet filled the stat sheet admirably: eight points, five assists, and four rebounds. Utah's biggest scoring threat came off the bench since Jae Crowder finished with 30 points (9 - 15 from the field). Derrick Favors had a solid outing as well since he chipped in with 21 points, nine boards and two blocks. Donovan Mitchell added 19 points with four rebounds and three assists, and Ricky Rubio contributed 14 points with eight assists. Gobert had 16 points and nine rebounds.

The Toronto Raptors took down the Indiana Pacers, 121 - 105, at Scotiabank Arena on Sunday evening. It was a contest between two of the Eastern Conference's top teams, as a win would have put Indiana (26 - 13) in first place for the first time since 2014. Toronto (30 - 12), however, delivered a memorable offensive performance, earning a win and becoming the first team in the NBA to reach 30 wins on the season. Despite the absence of superstar Kawhi Leonard (rest), Toronto shot the lights out, knocking down 52 percent of its shots and hitting 17 three - pointers. Eight Raptors players scored in double figures in the comfortable win. Kyle Lowry dished out a team - high eight assists in his first game since returning from a back injury. Lowry also scored 12 points and grabbed three steals. Norman Powell led Toronto with 23 points, and every Raptors starter scored at least 12 in Sunday's important win. For Indiana, Bojan Bogdonavic led the way with 21 points. Domantas Sabonis scored 16 points to go with 12 rebounds and six assists, and Victor Oladipo added another 16. It was not enough, though, as the team hit just four three - pointers and shot only 45 percent as a team. On Tuesday, the Pacers will visit Cleveland while Toronto will host the Atlanta Hawks.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the Atlanta Hawks, 104 - 101, at Scotiabank Arena on Tuesday evening. The dominant Raptors (31 - 12) may have underestimated their opposition Tuesday, as the Hawks (12 - 28) were able to forge a 31 - 28 first - quarter lead. The game was mostly a back - and - forth - affair right down to the final buzzer, when Toronto was able to leverage a pair of buckets from O.G. Anunoby and a dunk by Serge Ibaka to come back from a 101 - 98 deficit with 2:15 remaining. Earlier in the final period, the home squad had blown an 86 - 81 lead. Ball security was an issue for both clubs, with Atlanta guilty of a whopping 26 turnovers and the Raptors contributing 18 of their own. John Collins led the way for the Hawks with a 21 - point, 14 - rebound double - double that also included two assists and one steal. Jeremy Lin posted 20 points, nine assists and four rebounds. Trae Young turned in 19 points, five rebounds, four assists and two steals. Dewayne Dedmon supplied 12 points and nine boards. DeAndre' Bembry registered 11 points, six rebounds, five assists and five steals. Kawhi Leonard paced the Raptors with 31 points and also compiled six assists, four rebounds, six steals and one block. Kyle Lowry tallied 16 points, six assists, two rebounds, four steals and one block. Anunoby finished with a bench - leading 14 points. Pascal Siakam contributed a 13 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included three assists, one steal and one block. Serge Ibaka matched Siakam's scoring tally and also brought down six rebounds while recording two steals and two blocks. The Hawks remain on the road and visit the Brooklyn Nets on Wednesday night, while the Raptors remain home to face the Nets on Friday evening.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the Brooklyn Nets, 122 - 105, at Scotiabank Arena on Friday night. The Raptors (32 - 12) may have underestimated the improving Nets (21 - 23) to open the game, as they surprisingly fell behind by a 35 - 28 margin in the first 12 minutes. That likely served as a wake - up call, however, as Toronto went on to forge a 64 - 53 lead by halftime. They'd add another 13 points to their advantage in the third quarter, essentially sealing their win despite Brooklyn compiling 30 points in the final period. One of the Raptors' biggest advantages on the stat sheet was in turnovers, as they forced 17 from the visitors. D'Angelo Russell was one of only two double - digit scorers for the Nets and led the way with 24 points, nine assists, six rebounds and one steal. Shabazz Napier followed with 15 points, adding five assists and two rebounds. Jarrett Allen mustered nine points but added 12 rebounds. Alan Williams and DeMarre Caroll had matching eight - point tallies off the bench while pulling down eight and four rebounds, respectively. Kawhi Leonard paced the Raptors with 20 points and supplemented them with 11 rebounds, four assists and one steal. Pascal Siakam managed 16 points, six rebounds, two assists and one steal. Serge Ibaka had a near double - double with 14 points, nine rebounds, one assist and one block. O.G. Anunoby and Norman Powell had 13 points each off the bench. Delon Wright filled out the stat sheet with 12 points, five rebounds, two assists and three steals. The Nets head back home to face the Boston Celtics on Monday night, while the Raptors travel to the Nation's Capital to face the Washington Wizards on Sunday afternoon.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the visiting Phoenix Suns, 111 - 109, at Scotiabank Arena on Thursday evening. The Raptors got out to a great start at home, with a 32 - 20 lead after one quarter. The Suns picked it up in the second and chipped away at the deficit, so that they trailed by eight at halftime. The Suns carried the momentum into the second half, as they outscored the Raptors by nine in the third quarter to take a 78 - 77 lead into the final frame. The score stayed close through the fourth, as the teams exchanged baskets. The score was tied at 109 with 13 seconds left, and the Raptors went to Pascal Siakam out of the timeout. Siakam managed to convert the game - winning bucket on an isolation drive to the basket. Siakam finished with 10 points, 12 rebounds, five assists, two blocks and a steal, in 33 minutes. Serge Ibaka led the Raptors with 22 points on 11 - of - 19 shooting, six rebounds, one assist and a block, while Kyle Lowry tallied 16 points, nine rebounds, eight assists and two steals. The Raptors shot 50 percent from the field, including 7 - of - 28 from long range. Meanwhile, Devin Booker led the Suns with 30 points on 10 - of - 21 shooting, eight assists and two rebounds, in 35 minutes. Kelly Oubre Jr. followed up with 18 points, nine rebounds, one assist and one steal, while Deandre Ayton tallied 15 points, 17 rebounds, two assists, two steals and two blocks. The Suns (11 - 35) will look to bounce back as they take on the Hornets in Charlotte on Saturday. The Raptors (34 - 13) play host to the Grizzlies on Saturday.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the visiting Memphis Grizzlies, 119 - 90, at Scotiabank Arena on Saturday evening. The Raptors got out to a good start at home, holding the advantage through most of the first quarter, before taking a 23 - 19 lead into the second. They maintained an edge through the second, although the Grizzlies kept it close, so as to trail 55 - 48 at halftime. However, the Raptors blew the game open in the third quarter, where they outscored the visitors 45 - 14, to take a 38 - point lead into the final frame. The Grizzlies put up a fight in the fourth, but nothing near enough to give the home team a scare, as the Raptors cruised to their second consecutive win. This marks the fifth straight loss for Memphis. Danny Green led the Raptors with 24 points on 8 - of - 13 shooting, including eight three - pointers, along with seven rebounds, three assists, two steals and one block, in just 22 minutes. Serge Ibaka followed up with 18 points, five rebounds and one block, while Pascal Siakam added 17 points, eight rebounds, two assists and one steal. The Raptors shot 48 percent from the field, including 17 - of - 36 from long range. Meanwhile, Jaren Jackson Jr. led the Grizzlies with 16 points, nine rebounds and one assist, in 28 minutes. Ivan Rabb tallied 13 points, 11 rebounds, one assist and one block, in 21 minutes off the bench, while Shelvin Mack added 14 points, five assists, three rebounds and one steal, in 26 minutes off the bench. The Grizzlies (19 - 27) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Pelicans on Monday. The Raptors (35 - 13) play host to the Kings on Tuesday.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the Sacramento Kings, 120 - 105, at Air Canada Centre on Tuesday. The Raptors (36 - 13) once again showed why they are one of the top teams in the NBA during the 2018 - 19 season, as they came from behind against a surprising Kings (24 - 24) that seemed eager to leave their recent ugly loss on the rear view. Sacramento quickly jumped ahead on the score and they were up by five (34 - 29) following the first quarter, something that seemed to surprise many fans in attendance. But the Raptors turned things around rather quickly and once they got in control of the game, they didn't slip it away. Toronto won the second quarter by nine points (31 - 22) so they went up by four (60 - 56) at the break, and later closed things out in the second half. The Raptors won the remaining two quarters, 28 - 22 and 32 - 27 respectively, as they ended cruising their way towards a relatively comfortable win. The Raptors had a balanced scoring output in this game since they had six players scoring in double figures, but none reaching the 20 - point threshold. The absence of Kawhi Leonard didn't impact the side and the guard duo of Fred VanVleet and Kyle Lowry led the way for Toronto since both had 19 points. Serge Ibaka had 15 points with 10 boards, and Pascal Siakam 18 points. CJ Miles chipped in with 15 points off the bench. The Kings had seven players scoring over 10 points and they owned the highest scorer of the contest since Marvin Bagley III finished with 22 points and 11 rebounds. Bogdan Bogdanovic filled the stat sheet nicely since he contributed 16 points, nine assists, eight rebounds, and three steals to the losing cause. Buddy Hield added 11 points as well.

The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the host Toronto Raptors, 105 - 92, at Air Canada Centre on Thursday. In a game to determine the top seed in the east, Milwaukee prevailed in dominating fashion. A 34 - 22 second quarter really set the tone, as Milwaukee led by at least five points for the entirety of the second half. This marked the Bucks third win in four meetings with the Raptors this season, as they guaranteed themselves the tie - breaker over them. Rebounding was key for Milwaukee, as they won that battle, 50 - 39. The Bucks ended up shooting 49 percent from the field and 37 percent from three - point range while holding the Raptors to under 40 percent from the field and 26 percent from long range. Milwaukee also out - assisted Toronto, 21 - 16 The Bucks (37 - 13) were led by Giannis Antetokounmpo, as he collected 19 points, nine rebounds, five assists, four steals and two blocks. Khris Middleton accrued 18 points, five rebounds, four assists and two steals. Eric Bledsoe amassed 14 points, eight rebounds, six assists and four steals while D.J. Wilson led the bench with 16 points, five rebounds and two steals. The Raptors (37 - 16) were led by Pascal Siakam, as he tallied 28 points, three rebounds and three assists. Kawhi Leonard amassed 16 points, eight rebounds, two assists and three steals. Serge Ibaka finished with 12 points, 10 rebounds, two assists, two steals and three blocks. Kyle Lowry, Norman Powell and Fred VanVleet scored 10 points apiece. On deck for Milwaukee is a road matchup versus the Washington Wizards on Saturday. As for Toronto, they play host to the Los Angeles Clippers on Sunday for their next fixture.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the visiting Los Angeles Clippers, 121 - 103, at Air Canada Centre on Sunday. While this wasn't a wire - to - wire win for Toronto, they dominated throughout. In fact, a 42 - 28 second quarter really set the foundation, as the Raptors held a double - digit lead for the entirety of the second half. Rebounding was critical for the Raptors, as they outrebounded the Clippers, 56 - 36. Toronto's defense was also huge, as they held Los Angeles to 43 percent from the field and 17 percent from three - point range. Ball movement was also imperative, with the Raptors out - assisting the Clippers, 21 - 15. The Clippers (29 - 25) were led by Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, as he tallied 19 points, five rebounds, three assists and two blocks. Tobias Harris totaled 13 points, four rebounds and two assists. Lou Williams led the bench with 18 points, two rebounds and three assists. Montrezl Harrell got a rare start and amassed 10 points, three rebounds and four blocks. The Raptors (38 - 16) were led by Kawhi Leonard, as he collected 18 points, five rebounds and two assists. Serge Ibaka accumulated 16 points and 12 rebounds. Pascal Siakam finished with 15 points and four boards while C.J. Miles led the bench with the same line. Delon Wright provided 14 points, three rebounds, three assists and two steals off the bench. Both teams return to action on Tuesday, with Toronto traveling to face the Philadelphia 76ers and Los Angeles playing the Charlotte Hornets on the road as well.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the visiting Brooklyn Nets, 127 - 125, at Scotiabank Arena on Monday evening. The Nets got out to a great start on the road, as they held a 29 - 21 lead after one quarter. The Raptors trailed through the entire second quarter, but managed to trim the deficit to just four points by halftime. Both teams came out strong in the third, and it remained a one - possession game for most of the quarter, until it was tied at 92 by the start of the final frame. The Raptors got out to a strong start in the fourth and pushed to a seven - point lead, however, the Nets battled back with some ridiculous three - point shooting, to pull ahead with a 125 - 122 lead. The Raptors looked to Danny Green for a game - tying three. They then locked down for the stop on defense, before Kawhi Leonard banked in the game - winning jumper. This marks the fifth straight win for the Raptors, and the second straight loss for Brooklyn. Kawhi Leonard led the Raptors with 30 points, eight assists, four rebounds and one steal, in 34 minutes. Serge Ibaka followed up with 18 points, 12 rebounds, two blocks, a steal and an assist, while Pascal Siakam added 17 points, four rebounds, four assists and two steals. The Raptors shot 54 percent from the field, including 9 - of - 31 from long range. Meanwhile, D'Angelo Russell led the Nets with 28 points, 14 assists, seven rebounds and one steal, in 33 minutes. Joe Harris followed up with 24 points, four assists and two rebounds, while Allen Crabbe chipped in 22 points, three rebounds, one assist and one steal off the bench. The Nets shot 52 percent from the field, including 20 - 41 from long range. The Nets (29 - 29) will look to bounce back as they take on the Cavs in Cleveland on Wednesday. The Raptors (42 - 16) play host to the Wizards on Wednesday.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the visiting Washington Wizards, 129 - 120, at Scotiabank Arena on Wednesday evening. The Raptors got out to a solid start at home, with a 30 - 26 lead after one quarter. However, the Wizards turned it up in the second and outscored the Raptors by 10 in the quarter, to take a 65 - 59 lead into halftime. The Raptors came out on another level in the third quarter, where they poured in 44 points, to build a 10 - point lead of their own, heading into the fourth. The Wizards kept battling in the fourth, and outscored Toronto by one point in the quarter, but the Raptors were able to hold on for their sixth straight win. Pascal Siakam led the Raptors with 44 points, 10 rebounds, three blocks and two assists, in 32 minutes. OG Anunoby followed up with 22 points, five rebounds and one steal, while Kyle Lowry tallied 14 points, 13 assists, four rebounds and three steals. The Raptors shot 47 percent from the field, including 16 - of - 38 from long range. Meanwhile, Bradley Beal led the Wizards with 28 points, 11 assists, three rebounds, a block and a steal, in 43 minutes. Jeff Green followed up with 23 points, seven rebounds, two assists and a steal, while Jabari Parker added 22 points, nine rebounds, four assists and a steal. The Wizards shot 44 percent from the field, including 14 - of - 40 from long range. The Wizards (24 - 34) will be back in action on February 22nd, when they take on the Hornets, in Charlotte. The Raptors (43 - 16) will also enjoy a break before they are back in action on February 22nd, when they play host to the Spurs.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the San Antonio Spurs, 120 - 117, at Scotiabank Arena on Friday evening. The Raptors (44 - 16) found the Spurs (33 - 27) to be highly worthy interconference foe right from opening tip, as San Antonio actually held a one - point halftime advantage. Toronto wasn't able to make any inroads in the third quarter, actually adding another pair of points to their deficit entering the final period. However, down one with 17 seconds remaining, Kawhi Leonard forced a turnover from DeMar DeRozan, who ironically was making his return since being traded for Leonard this offseason. A dunk and a pair of free throws later, and Leonard had notched the final four points to complete the comeback victory. DeRozan led the way for the Spurs with 23 points, adding eight assists, four rebounds, two steals and one block. Marco Belinelli poured in 21 points and also offered six boards and two assists. Davis Bertans turned in 16 points, three rebounds and one steal. Patty Mills furnished 15 points, four assists and three rebounds. Rudy Gay generated a 12 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included two assists, one steal and one block. Bryn Forbes netted nine points, four assists and one rebound. LaMarcus Aldridge had just six points on 2 - for - 8 shooting, although he added eight rebounds. Leonard paced the Raptors with 25 points, supplementing them with six rebounds, two assists, two steals and one block. Pascal Siakam was a close second with 22 points and also posted six assists, three rebounds and two steals. Kyle Lowry and Danny Green mustered 17 points apiece. Serge Ibaka had a 13 - point, 15 - rebound double - double that also included two assists and a block. Jeremy Lin led the bench with 11 points. The Spurs remain on the road and pay a visit to the New York Knicks on Sunday evening, while the Raptors remain home and take on the Orlando Magic on Sunday afternoon.

The Orlando Magic defeated the Toronto Raptors, 113 - 98, at Scotiabank Arena on Sunday afternoon. The Magic (28 - 33) figured they'd have a substantial challenge on their hands coming into a road matchup against one of the Eastern Conference's powerhouses in the Raptors (44 - 17). However, their task was made significantly less daunting when they found out Kawhi Leonard would sit out the contest for rest purposes. A seemingly buoyed Orlando squad jumped out to a 25 - 15 first - quarter lead and still held a three - point advantage at halftime. Toronto managed to finally secure a tie at the 7:5 mark of the third quarter, but the visitors picked up the pace at that point. The Magic would go on to outscore their hosts by a 50 - 35 margin the rest of the way, leading to the double - digit victory. Among their various statistical advantages, Orlando enjoyed a 52 - 42 edge on the boards. Terrence Ross led the way for the Magic against his former squad with 28 points, adding nine rebounds and one assist. Nikola Vucevic generated a 23 - point, 12 - rebound double - double that also included four assists, two steals and one block. Jonathan Isaac furnished 16 points, six rebounds and two blocks. D.J. Augustin supplied 12 points, eight assists, five rebounds and one steal. Evan Fournier totaled 11 points, three rebounds, one assist and one block. Kyle Lowry paced the Raptors with 19 points, 10 assists, four rebounds and four blocks. Marc Gasol tallied 16 points, five rebounds and five assists. Serge Ibaka delivered 14 points and five rebounds. Pascal Siakam mustered a 10 - point, 11 - rebound double - double that also included three assists and two blocks. Danny Green and Jodie Meeks generated matching 10 - point tallies, with Green notably adding six rebounds and four assists. The Magic remain on the road and pay a visit to the New York Knicks on Tuesday evening, while the Raptors remain home and tangle with the Boston Celtics on Tuesday night.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the Boston Celtics, 118 - 95, at Scotiabank Arena on Tuesday evening. The Raptors (45 - 17) have mostly dominated on their home court this season, but they figured to get a stiff challenge from the division - rival Celtics (37 - 24). Accordingly, Boston built a slim two - point lead through the first quarter, but Toronto ensured that would be the last highlight the visitors would enjoy. The hosts won the second quarter by a 36 - 13 margin, giving them a 21 - point halftime lead that they'd expand to 27 by the end of the third. Among the Raptors' numerous statistical triumphs was a 49 percent - 38 percent edge in shooting and a 14 - 8 advantage in turnovers committed. Marcus Morris paced the Celtics with 17 points, adding six rebounds and one assist. Jayson Tatum and Terry Rozier generated matching 11 - point tallies, with Tatum notably bringing in seven boards. Jaylen Brown was the only other player in double digits, posting 10 points, eight rebounds, four assists and four steals. Gordon Hayward tallied nine points, two rebounds, two assists and one block. Al Horford and Robert Williams contributed eight points apiece. Pascal Siakam led the Raptors with 25 points, supplementing them with eight rebounds, two assists, two steals and one block. Kawhi Leonard followed with 21 points and added six rebounds, four assists and one steal. Serge Ibaka generated 14 points and two rebounds. Norman Powell poured in 11 points. Kyle Lowry mustered just seven points, but he also dished out 11 assists, hauled in six rebounds and recorded one steal. The Celtics head back home to tangle with the Portland Trail Blazers on Wednesday night, while the Raptors remain home and take on the Trail Blazers as well on Saturday evening.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the visiting Portland Trail Blazers, 119 - 117, at Scotiabank Arena on Friday evening. The Raptors got out to a strong start at home, with a 31 - 24 lead through one quarter. The Trail Blazers pushed back early in the second and took the lead, however, the Raptors reclaimed control and took a 61 - 54 lead into halftime. The Raptors came out strong in the third quarter and managed to hold their lead the whole way through, to take a nine - point lead into the final frame. The Trail Blazers kept fighting and chipped away until they tied it up at 103 with three minutes left in the contest. The score went back and forth down the stretch, but the Raptors came up huge behind some clutch plays from Kyle Lowry and Kawhi Leonard. Leonard hit the winning bucket for Toronto with just a few seconds left on the clock, securing the Raptor's ninth win in their last 10 games. Leonard led the Raptors with 38 points, five assists, three rebounds and three steals, in 34 minutes. Kyle Lowry tallied 19 points, 10 assists, seven rebounds, two blocks and an assist, while Marc Gasol finished with 19 points, eight rebounds, six assists, two steals and a block. The Raptors shot 56 percent from the field, including 10 - of - 28 from long range. Meanwhile, C.J. McCollum led the Trail Blazers with 35 points, five assists, four rebounds and one steal, in 39 minutes. Damian Lillard followed up with 24 points, eight rebounds and six assists, while Jake Layman chipped in 13 points seven rebounds, two steals, a block and an assist. The Trail Blazers shot 49 percent from the field, including 14 - of - 33 from deep. The Trail Blazers (38 - 24) will look to bounce back as they take on the Hornets in Charlotte on Sunday. The Raptors (46 - 17) take on the Pistons in Detroit on Sunday.

The Houston Rockets defeated the host Toronto Raptors, 107 - 95, at Air Canada Centre on Tuesday. In a battle between two title contenders, there were some massive swings in this game. In fact, Houston got out to a 22 - point lead thanks to a 32 - 18 second quarter but Toronto rode a 34 - 14 third quarter to make it competitive. The Rockets then responded with a 38 - 24 fourth quarter to take control, as they led by at least seven points for the final 10 minutes. Even with those major swings, there were five ties and 12 lead changes in total. Three-point shooting was the difference in the game, with the Rockets connecting on 15 - of - 34 and the Raptors hitting just 9 - of - 31. Turnovers were also key, with Houston winning the turnover differential, 13 - 9, thanks to out - stealing Toronto, 10 - 1. That allowed them to win the points off turnover differential, 26 - 4 and the fastbreak scoring battle, 23 - 7. The Rockets (39 - 25) were led by James Harden, as he finished with 33 points, three rebounds and three steals. Chris Paul went just 1 - of - 10 from the field to accumulate five points, six rebounds, 10 assists and two steals. Clint Capela generated nine points and 15 boards. Gerald Green led the bench with 18 points. The Raptors (46 - 19) were led by Kawhi Leonard, as he totaled 26 points and six rebounds. Pascal Siakam accrued 17 points, 10 rebounds and three assists. Serge Ibaka started and totaled 10 points, 15 rebounds, two assists and five blocks. Kyle Lowry went just 4 - of - 16 from the field to accrue eight points, six rebounds and six assists. Both teams will be off until Friday, with Houston playing host to the Philadelphia 76ers and Toronto traveling to face the dysfunctional New Orleans Pelicans.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the Los Angeles Lakers, 111 - 98, on Thursday at Air Canada Centre. The Raptors (49 - 20) came into Thursday's contest without two key players, with Kyle Lowry (ankle) and Serge Ibaka (suspension) both sidelined, but that didn't have much of an impact when it came to beating up on the lowly Lakers. Mostly because they still had star player Kawhi Leonard, who scored a team - high 25 points to go along with eight rebounds, four assists and two steals in the wire - to - wire victory. Pascal Siakam struggled mightily from the floor, going just 3 - of - 16, but he still managed to finish with 16 points thanks to his ability to get to the free throw line. Lastly, Normal Powell came up with a huge performance off the bench, scoring 20 points and grabbing eight rebounds in 24 key minutes as a reserve. It wasn't the most efficient offensive performance for the Raptors, however, as they shot 40 percent from the field, but the 16 threes they hit helped overcome that and propel them to victory. As for the Lakers (31 - 37), they have now lost six of their last seven games, and injuries have left them with a real lack of quality depth. The Warriors then sent Houston's James Harden to the line in the final seconds, where he made a shot before missing the second free - throw and failing to secure the offensive board. The loss snapped a league - best nine - game winning streak for the Rockets. Klay Thompson was the game's leading scorer with 30 points. Thompson shot 12 - of - 23 from the field and also knocked down five three - pointers. DeMarcus Cousins also delivered a strong showing, finishing with 27 points, eight rebounds, and seven assists. Curry was the third Warriors to eclipse 20 points, finishing with 24 in the much - needed win. Harden was Houston's leading scorer with 29 points on the night. The MVP hopeful added 10 assists and three steals. Clint Capela also had a double - double, tallying 13 points and 13 rebounds. The two strong showings were not enough for the Rockets, though, as the team was sunk by its 29 percent three - point shooting. Houston will host the Phoenix Suns on Friday, while the Warriors will travel to Oklahoma City on Saturday.

The Houston Rockets defeated the Phoenix Suns, 108 - 102, at Toyota Center on Friday night. The Suns (16 - 54) have been playing much more competitively of late, and they continued that trend early in their difficult road matchup versus the short - handed Rockets (43 - 26). Phoenix surprisingly jumped out to a 31 - 26 first - quarter lead and still held a two - point advantage at halftime. After a third quarter where each squad matched the other bucket for bucket, Houston finally took control with just over five minutes left in the fourth quarter, finishing the game on a 13 - 6 run. The home squad played without Chris Paul, who sat out for rest. Devin Booker led the way for the Suns with 27 points, adding seven assists and five rebounds. Kelly Oubre, Jr. supplied 22 points, four rebounds, two assists, four steals and two blocks. Deandre Ayton turned in a 17 - point, 14 - rebound double - double. Josh Jackson furnished 13 points, four rebounds, one assist and one block. Richaun Holmes generated a 12 - point, 11 - rebound double - double off the bench. James Harden paced the Rockets with 38 points and complemented them with 10 assists, seven rebounds, five steals and three blocks. Eric Gordon poured in 19 points and also compiled four rebounds and three assists. Danuel House, Jr. supplied 18 points, three rebounds and one steal. Clint Capela managed a 14 - point, 11 - rebound double - double that also included one steal and one block. The Suns next pay a visit to the New Orleans Pelicans on Saturday night, while the Rockets remain home to tangle with the Minnesota Timberwolves on Sunday night.

The Houston Rockets defeated the Minnesota Timberwolves, 117 - 102, at Toyota Center on Sunday evening. A scorching - hot third quarter helped Houston (44 - 26) open up a double - digit lead. After a tight first half, the Rockets came out of halftime locked in, knocking down a franchise - record 10 three - pointers in the third quarter. That was good for 43 points in the period, leaving Minnesota (32 - 38) trailing by 15. Houston ended the night having knocked down 21 three - pointers on 50 attempts. Both members of the Rockets' All-Star backcourt recorded a double - double on Sunday. Chris Paul led Houston with 25 points while dishing out 10 assists. Paul also played a major role in Houston's lights - out shooting, going 6 - of - 7 from beyond the arc. James Harden added another 20 points and 10 assists. Houston center Clint Capela also delivered a gem, tallying 20 points and 13 rebounds. For Minnesota, All-Star big man Karl-Anthony Towns was the top scorer with 22 points. Towns rounded out his performance with 10 rebounds, six assists, and two blocks. Rookie guard Josh Okogie also made an impact on offense, tallying 21 points despite the double - digit loss. On Tuesday, the Rockets will visit Atlanta while Minnesota will host the Golden State Warriors.

The Houston Rockets defeated the visiting San Antonio Spurs, 111 - 105, at Toyota Center on Friday. This was a true tale of four quarters, as there were some massive swings in this game. In fact, Houston led 36 - 24 after the first quarter but San Antonio rode a 34 - 19 fourth quarter to take the lead. The Rockets then rode a 30 - 24 fourth quarter to victory, as there were five ties and six lead changes in total. Three-point shooting was the difference in the game, with the Rockets connecting on 14 - of - 37 and the Spurs hitting just 7 - of - 24. Houston won despite being out - assisted 27 - 12. The Spurs (42 - 31) were led by Bryn Forbes, as he amassed 20 points, five rebounds and two assists. Derrick White generated 18 points, eight rebounds and three assists. DeMar DeRozan accumulated 16 points, eight rebounds and eight assists. LaMarcus Aldridge finished with 10 points, four rebounds and four assists. The Rockets (46 - 27) got another unbelievable performance from James Harden, as he tallied 61 points, seven rebounds and three steals on 9 - of - 13 from three - point range and 14 - of - 17 from the free - throw line. Chris Paul finished with 18 points, three rebounds and five assists. Clint Capela totaled seven points, 16 rebounds and four assists. Both teams return to action on Sunday, with San Antonio traveling to face the Boston Celtics and Houston playing the New Orleans Pelicans on the road as well.

The Houston Rockets defeated the visiting Denver Nuggets, 112 - 85, at Toyota Center on Thursday. While Denver got out to a lead in the first quarter, Houston dominated from there. In fact, a 40 - 19 second quarter really put separation between the two teams, as Houston held a double - digit lead for the entirety of the second half while leading by at least 15 points for the whole of the fourth quarter. The Rockets went 40 - of - 87 from the field and 15 - of - 40 from three - point range while holding the Nuggets to 31 - of - 84 from the field and 4 - of - 24 from long range. Houston also outrebounded Denver, 46 - 38 The Nuggets (50 - 24) were led by Jamal Murray, as he amassed 20 points, four rebounds, three assists and two steals. Nikola Jokic finished with 16 points, eight rebounds, six assists and two steals. Gary Harris totaled 11 points, two rebounds and three assists while Monte' Morris led the bench with 16 points, three rebounds and four assists. The Rockets (48 - 28) were led by James Harden, as he tallied 38 points, six rebounds and six assists. Eric Gordon amassed 18 points and one rebound on 7 - of - 11 from the field. Clint Capela finished with 17 points and 15 rebounds while Chris Paul accrued nine points, four rebounds, nine assists and two steals. Denver will have to play again on Friday, as they travel to face the struggling Oklahoma City Thunder. As for Houston, they're off until Saturday when they play host to the Sacramento Kings.

The Houston Rockets defeated the visiting Sacramento Kings, 119 - 108, at Toyota Center on Saturday. There were seven ties and seven lead changes in this tightly contested game, with neither team leading by more than 11 points. Houston rode a big fourth quarter to victory, outscoring Sacramento, 28 - 15. Free-throw shooting was the difference for the Rockets, as they connected on 24 - of - 27 while the Kings hit just 9 - of - 15. Sacramento actually dominated the rebounding and three - point shooting, as they hit 52 percent from long range while winning the rebounding battle, 49 - 38. The Kings (37 - 39) were led by Buddy Hield, as he tallied 21 points, two rebounds and three assists. Marvin Bagley III finished with 20 points and 12 rebounds. De'Aaron Fox accumulated 18 points, seven rebounds and 10 assists while Bogdan Bogdanovic led the bench with 24 points, nine rebounds and eight assists. The Rockets (49 - 28) got a masterful performance from James Harden, as he collected 50 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists. Clint Capela amassed 24 points, 15 rebounds and two blocks. Chris Paul generated 22 points, two rebounds, five assists and four steals while Eric Gordon dropped 17 points. These teams actually have a rematch for their next game on Tuesday but that matchup will be played in Sacramento.

The Houston Rockets defeated the visiting New York Knicks, 120 - 96, at Toyota Center on Friday evening. The Rockets got out to a great start at home, with a 32 - 16 lead after one quarter. They kept it up in the second, where they outscored the visitors by 13, to push their lead to 29 by halftime. The Rockets expanded their lead by another 10 points through the third quarter. The Knicks managed to pour in 32 points in the fourth, but it was not nearly enough to make a dent in the deficit. This marks the fifth straight win for the Rockets. James Harden led the Rockets with 26 points, eight rebounds, eight assists, one steal and one block, in 29 minutes. Clint Capela added 12 points, 15 rebounds and one block, while Chris Paul finished with 11 points, 10 assists, four rebounds and one steal. The Rockets shot 43 percent from the field, including 22 - of - 59 from deep. Meanwhile, Mario Hezonja led the Knicks with 16 points, 16 rebounds, 11 assists and a steal, in 42 minutes. Kevin Knox added 13 points and five rebounds, while Henry Ellenson chipped in 16 points and seven rebounds off the bench. The Knicks shot 45 percent from the field, including 6 - of - 27 from long range. The Knicks (15 - 64) play host to the Wizards on Sunday. The Rockets (52 - 28) play host to the Suns on Sunday.

The Houston Rockets defeated the visiting Phoenix Suns, 149 - 113, at Toyota Center on Sunday. Houston was expected to win this game easily and this final scoreline vindicates that thought. This was actually a wire - to - wire win for the Rockets, as a 34 - 24 first quarter set the foundation while a 43 - 23 second quarter ended up being the dagger. In addition, Houston held a 40 - point lead going into the fourth quarter and led by 43 points at times in that final quarter. Houston won nearly every statistic, as they ended up winning the rebounding, assisting, steals, blocks and turnover differentials. Houston's offense was unstoppable, as they connected on 53 percent from the field and 47 percent from three - point range while recording 34 assists. The 27 three - pointers by the Rockets marked an NBA record. The Suns (19 - 62) were led by Jamal Crawford, as he tallied 27 points, four rebounds and six assists off the bench. Dragan Bender led the starters with 19 points and eight boards. Mikal Bridges matched those 19 points, adding six rebounds and two assists to his tally. Josh Jackson finished with 12 points, nine rebounds and six assists. The Rockets (53 - 28) were led by James Harden, as he collected 30 points, 13 rebounds, nine assists and two steals. Eric Gordon totaled 26 points and one board. Clint Capela finished with 22 points, 13 rebounds and four assists. Danuel House Jr. led the bench with 13 points and six rebounds. Both these teams only have one game remaining on Tuesday, with Houston traveling to face the Oklahoma City Thunder and Phoenix traveling to face the Dallas Mavericks.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the visiting Timberwolves, 112 - 108, at AT & T Center on Wednesday. It was certainly a new - look Spurs (10) squad Wednesday night, but it was still a positive result for Gregg Popovich and company. It was a back - and - forth affair for the entire 48 minutes, but ultimately, the newest Spur, DeMar DeRozan, came through with the go - ahead layup and a pair of free throws to seal the game away. DeRozan finished the contest with a game - high 28 points on 10 - of - 21 shooting to go along with four rebounds and four assists in 38 minutes, making for a very impressive San Antonio debut. Fellow All-Star LaMarcus Aldridge was a monster on the boards Wednesday night, and his activity on the glass proved to be a major factor. Aldridge posted 21 points on a poor 7 - of - 23 shooting from the field, but he hauled in 19 rebounds (eight offense), and the Spurs cashed in on 10 - second chance points on his rebounds alone. A big reason for the Timberwolves (0 - 1) giving up so many crucial rebounds was the fact that their best rebounder, All-Star Karl-Anthony Towns, only played 22 minutes due to foul trouble. The big man finished with just eight points (2 - 6 FG) and nine rebounds in that time. Fortunately, his supporting cast did enough to keep Minnesota in the game. Jeff Teague poured in a team - high 27 points on 8 - of - 12 shooting from the field, while Jimmy Butler and Andrew Wiggins scored 23 and 20 points, respectively. Ultimately, Towns' absence ended up being just too much for the team to overcome.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the host San Antonio Spurs, 116 - 96, at AT & T Center on Wednesday evening. The Spurs started out strong at home, but the Pacers closed the first quarter on a 11 - 5 run to take a, 28 - 22, lead into the second quarter. The Pacers kept it up in the second, as they pushed their lead to 15 midway though the quarter, and held on to take a, 34 - 28, lead into halftime. The Pacers had the Spurs figured out in this one, as they came out in the third quarter and continued to maintain control over the game. The Spurs could barely cut the lead to single digits before Indiana took a, 88 - 71, lead into the final frame. The Pacers were able to cruise to the 20 - point win, as they outscored the Spurs, 28 - 25, in the fourth quarter, to earn their first road win of the season. Victor Oladipo led the Pacers with 21 points, nine assists, five rebounds and two steals, in 33 minutes. Tyreke Evans followed up with 19 points on 7 - of - 14 shooting, in 22 minutes off the bench, while Cory Joseph added 12 points, six rebounds, four assists and one steal, in 24 minutes off the bench. The Pacers shot 53 percent from the field, including 17 - of - 32 from long range. Meanwhile, DeMar DeRozan was the high - point man for the Spurs, with 18 points on 8 - of - 18 shooting. LaMarcus Aldridge was solid with 15 points, 13 rebounds, two assists and one block, while Rudy Gay added 11 points, 10 rebounds, two assists and one steal. The Spurs shot 40 percent from the field, including 6 - of - 19 from deep. The Spurs (2 - 2) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Lakers on Saturday. The Pacers (3 - 2) take on the Cavs in Cleveland on Saturday.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the visiting Los Angeles Lakers, 110 - 106, at AT & T Center on Saturday evening. The Lakers got out to a quick start with an early 8 - 2 lead and went on to take a 36 - 29 lead into the second quarter. The Spurs picked up in the defense in the second but could not cut into the lead much, as they trailed 60 - 54 at halftime. They picked up where they left off in the third, as the Spurs tied it up at 71 halfway through the quarter, however the Lakers managed to stay on top and take an 88 - 87 lead into the final frame. The Spurs kept fighting and pulled ahead halfway through the fourth. Although the Lakers kept it close, the Spurs managed to stay one step ahead the rest of the way en route to their second home win of the season. This is the second time the Spurs have defeated the Lakers already this season. DeMar DeRozan led the way for the Spurs with 30 points, 12 rebounds, eight assists, two steals and one block, in 39 minutes. Bryn Forbes and Rudy Gay tallied 16 points each, while LaMarcus Aldridge tallied 15 points, five rebounds and three assists. The Spurs shot 48 percent from the field including just 3 - of - 16 from long range. Meanwhile, LeBron James led the Lakers with 35 points, 11 rebounds, four assists and two steals, in 34 minutes. Kyle Kuzma followed up with 15 points, four rebounds and one assist, while Lance Stephenson chipped in 14 points, nine rebounds and two assists, in 23 minutes off the bench. The Lakers shot 48 percent from the field, including 13 - of - 33 from deep. The Lakers (2 - 4) look ahead to Monday when they take on the Timberwolves in Minnesota. The Spurs (3 - 2) play host to the Mavericks on Monday.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the visiting Dallas Mavericks, 113 - 108, at AT & T Center on Monday evening. The Mavericks started out well, keeping it close and playing with the lead for most of the first quarter, however the Spurs managed to take a two - point edge into the second. The Spurs pushed their lead to nine mid way through the second quarter and then to 13 with about a minute left, before settling on a 53 - 45 lead at halftime. The Mavericks came out strong in the third and outscored the Spurs by six, to cut the deficit to just two points, entering the fourth quarter. Things got intense in the fourth, as the Mavericks would not go away. They took a one - point lead with 4:55 remaining, but the Spurs, led by DeMar DeRozan, went into clutch mode to keep grab the one - point lead with 39 seconds left. The Mavericks had a chance to win, as they were down by one, with Dennis Smith Jr. at the line for two shots. However, Smith Jr. only hit one, leaving the Spurs 2 seconds on the clock. DeRozan shook free for a clean look, but it went in and out. The game went to overtime, where DeRozan sealed it for San Antonio with six points in the final two minutes. DeRozan led the Spurs with an impressive, 34 points on 12 - of - 21 shooting, nine assists, six rebounds and three steals, in 42 minutes. LaMarcus Aldridge followed up with 20 points, while Rudy Gay added 15 points, 11 rebounds, six steals and four assists, in 40 minutes. The Spurs shot 46 percent from the field, including 9 - of - 20 from deep. Meanwhile, Luka Doncic had a big night with 31 points on 11 - of - 18 shooting, including 4 - of - 6 from downtown. Dennis Smith Jr. followed up with 22 points on 9 - of - 19 shooting. The Mavs shot 47 percent from the field, including 10 - of - 34 from long range. The Mavericks (2 - 5) go on to L.A. to challenge the Lakers on Wednesday. The Spurs (4 - 2) take on the Suns in Phoenix on Wednesday.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the New Orleans Pelicans, 109 - 95, at AT & T Center on Saturday evening. The Spurs (6 - 2) came into the day not knowing if they'd have to tangle with All-Star Anthony Davis (elbow) who was highly questionable due to the injury that had already cost him three of the previous four games. As it turned out, the big man was healthy enough to suit up, but it hardly seemed to matter during the first half. San Antonio built a seemingly commanding 58 - 39 halftime lead over the Pelicans (4 - 5), but the visitors would regroup at intermission. New Orleans bounced back to outscore their hosts by a 56 - 51 margin in the second half, but it ultimately wasn't close to enough. Both teams shot in excess of 46 percent, although Davis was still clearly not at 100 percent while scoring a modest 17 points over 40 minutes. Jrue Holiday led the way for the Pelicans with 29 points, a total he supplemented with eight assists and four rebounds. Nikola Mirotic generated a 22 - point, 16 - rebound double - double that also included one assist. Davis supplemented his aforementioned scoring total with eight rebounds, three assists, five blocks and two steals. E'Twaun Moore registered 11 points. DeMar DeRozan paced the Spurs with 26 points and added four assists and three rebounds. LaMarcus Aldridge followed with a 22 - point, 12 - rebound double - double that also included six assists. Former Pelican Dante Cunningham and Patty Mills contributed matching 15 - point tallies from the starting five and the bench, respectively. Marco Belinelli poured in 14 off the second unit. Bryn Forbes (seven points) and Rudy Gay (six points) had quiet nights as starters. The Pelicans next pay a visit to the Oklahoma City Thunder on Monday night, while the Spurs remain home and take on the Magic in a Sunday evening battle.

The Orlando Magic defeated the San Antonio Spurs, 117 - 110, at AT & T Center on Sunday evening. The Magic (3 - 6) came into the contest in the midst of a tailspin, as they'd lost six of their previous seven games. However, they seemed like a different team from the start, as they took a 36 - 26 first - quarter lead. Even though the Spurs (6 - 3) regrouped to an extent in the second period, Orlando still took a 17 - point lead into the final 12 minutes, which gave them more than enough cushion to withstand a run by the home squad in the fourth quarter and escape with the win. The Magic drained 50 percent of their shots and turned the ball over just eight times, both keys to victory. Aaron Gordon led the way with 26 points, which he supplemented with eight rebounds and one steal. D.J. Augustin supplied 18 points, seven assists and five rebounds. Terrance Ross managed 17 points, four assists and three rebounds. Evan Fournier turned in 16 points and dished out seven dimes. Nikola Vucevic provided 13 points, eight rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block. DeMar DeRozan paced the Spurs with 25 points and added seven rebounds, five assists and two steals. Patty Mills paced the bench with 16 points. Marco Belinelli followed with 15 points in 21 minutes. LaMarcus Aldridge collected 14 points, six rebounds and three assists. Bryn Forbes tallied 13 points, two assists and a rebound. The Magic head back home to take on the Cleveland Cavaliers on Monday night, while the Spurs pay a visit to the Miami Heat on Wednesday evening.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the visiting Houston Rockets, 96 - 89, at AT & T Center on Saturday evening. The game got out to an interesting start, as the Spurs led, 17 - 8, six and a half minutes in, but then did not score for the next five minutes, as the Rockets caught up and managed to close the quarter with a 21 - 20 advantage. The game stayed close through the second, but the Spurs managed to pull back ahead, taking a 52 - 50 lead into halftime. The Spurs kept the momentum in the third, as they pulled ahead by seven halfway through the quarter, but the Rockets rallied back again, to make it a one - point game, as they trailed, 72 - 71, heading into the final frame. The fourth quarter featured more back - and - forth action, as the Spurs led, 86 - 85, with just over three minutes left. The Spurs held on and closed the game, as they outscored the Rockets 10 - 4 in the final minutes, to earn the impressive home win. LaMarcus Aldridge led the Spurs with 27 points, 10 rebounds, one assist and one block, in 35 minutes. DeMar DeRozan tallied 13 points, 11 rebounds and three assists, while Derrick White tallied 14 points, eight assists, four rebounds and two steals, in 29 minutes. The Spurs shot 45 percent from the field, including 10 - of - 20 from long range. Meanwhile, James Harden led the way for the Rockets with 25 points, six rebounds, three assists, two steals and two blocks, in 38 minutes. Clint Capela tallied 12 points, 17 rebounds, two blocks and an assist, while Eric Gordon added 23 points, four rebounds, two assists and two steals, in 30 minutes off the bench. Carmelo Anthony (illness) did not suit up. The Rockets (4 - 7) will look to avoid a third straight loss as they play host to the Pacers on Sunday. The Spurs (7 - 4) take on the Kings in Sacramento on Monday.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the Golden State Warriors 104 - 92 at AT & T Center on Sunday. The Spurs returned home and picked up a needed win to end the three game losing streak they carried into the contest, although the win will be overshadowed by the beat up Warriors lineup that was run in light of Stephen Curry (groin) and Draymond Green (toe) being sidelined. The Warriors announced that Curry will be reevaluated in a week and have struggled to find an offensive rhythm without the two - time MVP in the lineup. On Sunday, the firepower from behind the arc was lacking, which in turn kept the Warriors just out of the lead every quarter. The Warriors (12 - 6) shot 5 - of - 26 from three, and needed 51 points on 51 shots combined from Kevin Durant and Klay Thompson. One half of the splash brothers did hit a big time three with 3:38 remaining in the fourth quarter to pull the game within one point, but the Spurs (8 - 7) came back with seven unanswered points on the backs of DeMar DeRozan and LaMarcus Aldridge to put the game away. DeRozan had 20 points, six rebounds and nine assists on 8 - of - 19 shooting, while Aldridge posted 24 points, 18 rebounds and two blocks. The Warriors mixed in Damian Jones and Quinn Cook for 23 minutes and 29 minutes, respectively, to try and answer the subtraction of Curry and Green. Cook contributed 16 points on 7 - of - 12 shooting, to go with eight rebounds and two assists. Next up, the Spurs go back on the road to take on the New Orleans Pelicans on Monday, while the Warriors host the Oklahoma City Thunder on Wednesday.

The Memphis Grizzlies defeated the San Antonio Spurs, 104 - 103, at AT & T Center on Wednesday. The Grizzlies (12 - 5) continue to be one of the biggest surprises of the NBA, as Wednesday's victory in San Antonio was their fifth straight, and they now boast the best record in the Western Conference. The win didn't come easy, however, as a DeMar DeRozan jumper that put the Spurs (8 - 9) up one with 1 seconds ago appeared to have sealed the deal for the home team. Memphis managed to catch a break shortly after, though, as Marc Gasol drew a foul with under a second left and knocked down two game - winning free throws. Gasol finished with 20 points and 10 rebounds in 35 minutes, but it was point guard Mike Conley who led the way for the Grizzlies, as he scored a game - high 30 points to go along with nine assists in 35 minutes of his own. Gasol and Conley were the only Memphis starters to reach double figures, while JaMychal Green and Omri Casspi put up 12 and 11 points respectively off the bench. As for the Spurs, they were once again led by DeMar DeRozan, who briefly thought he was the hero with hardly any time remaining on the game clock. DeRozan finished with a team - high 24 points on 10 - of - 20 shooting in addition to five assists and five rebounds in 37 minutes. Rudy Gay added 21 points of his own on 7 - of - 10 shooting. LaMarcus Aldridge struggled shooting from the field, going a brutal 6 - of - 20, but he still managed to finish with a double - double of 19 points and 11 rebounds in 41 minutes.

The Houston Rockets defeated the host San Antonio Spurs, 136 - 105, at AT & T Center on Friday evening. The Rockets jumped out to a great start on the road, as they matched the Spurs with a 9 - 9 score after the first few minutes, before they outscored the home team, 30 - 12, through the remainder of the quarter. The Rockets carried the momentum in to the second, where they pushed their lead to 25, halfway through the quarter. The Spurs had no answer, as they trailed 70 - 47, at halftime. The third quarter did not bring any better luck for San Antonio, as the Rockets pushed their lead to 30, and went on to outscore the Spurs, 40 - 27, in the quarter, to take a, 110 - 74, lead into the final frame. None of the Spurs' starters played in the fourth, as they dropped their second game in a row. Clint Capela led the Rockets with 27 points, 12 rebounds, four blocks, one assist and a steal, in 29 minutes. Eric Gordon followed up with 26 points, three rebounds and two assists, in 25 minutes off the bench. James Harden finished with 23 points, 10 assists, seven rebounds and one block, in 27 minutes. The Rockets shot 50 percent from the field, including 22 - of - 54 from long range. Meanwhile, LaMarcus Aldridge led the Spurs with 20 points, six rebounds and two blocks, in 30 minutes. DeMar DeRozan followed up with 18 points, five assists, two rebounds and two steals, in 26 minutes, while Derrick White chipped in 11 points, nine assists and five rebounds, in 33 minutes off the bench. The Spurs shot 46 percent from the field, including 10 - of - 28 from deep. The Spurs (10 - 12) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Trail Blazers on Sunday. The Rockets (10 - 11) play host to the Bulls on Saturday.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the Portland Trail Blazers 131 - 118 on Sunday at AT & T Center. The final score did not depict the back and forth nature of this battle as the Spurs were able to pull away early in the fourth quarter with big time scores from Rudy Gay, DeMar DeRozan and LaMarcus Aldridge. The game itself had over 10 ties and nearly 20 lead changes, with the all - star back court of Damian Lillard and CJ McCollum firing on all cylinders trying to match the Spurs all - stars in the process. Portland (13 - 10) entered the fourth quarter down 97 - 90, but McCollum drained a three pointer right out the gate to pull within four. Rudy Gay answered with his vintage mid - range jumper and that was the nature of the final period. Anytime the Blazers pulled within the reach, the Spurs (11 - 12) answered immediately and did damage in the paint, which led to easy free throws. DeRozan finished with 36 points, eight rebounds, six assists and two steals. Aldridge contributed 29 points and eight boards. Derrick White found a clutch rhythm off the bench and knocked down 4 - of - 7 from the field on his way to 10 points, while Patty Mills added 15 points in 25 minutes. Lillard led all scorers with 37 points, to go with 10 assists and a pair of steals. McCollum added 24 points and Al-Farouq Aminu pitched in 20 points and nine boards. Both teams play on Tuesday, as the Blazers visit the Dallas Mavericks, while the Spurs visit the Utah Jazz.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the visiting Los Angeles Lakers, 133 - 120, at AT & T Center on Friday evening. The Lakers got out to a good start on the road, with an early. 9 - 2, lead. The Spurs picked it up and brought the game to a tie at 22, before the Lakers pulled ahead to lead, 36 - 32, after one. The Lakers kept the edge while the Spurs matched them bucket - for - bucket, with 36 points each in the quarter, to bring the lead to, 72 - 68, for the Lakers at halftime. The Spurs came out strong in the third quarter, and cut the deficit to just two, with 5:23 left in the quarter. However, the Lakers closed the quarter with a 17 - 9 run, to take a, 99 - 89, lead into the fourth. Nonetheless, the Spurs were not about to back down, as they started the fourth on a 10 - 2 run, to cut the deficit to just two points. They kept pushing an tied it up at 112, halfway through the quarter. The Spurs then used a quick 70 run, and did not look back from there, as clutch play, after clutch play sealed the much - needed win. For the Lakers, it marked the end of a four - game winning streak. DeMar DeRozan led the Spurs with 36 points, nine assists, eight rebounds and two blocks, in 36 minutes. LaMarcus Aldridge, Patty Mills and Jakob Poeltl finished with 14 points each, while Davis Bertans, who came up huge in the clutch, finished with 13 points on 4 - of - 7 shooting from long range. Meanwhile, LeBron James led the Lakers with 35 points, 11 assists, eight rebounds and two steals, in 37 minutes. Kyle Kuzma followed up with 27 points, eight rebounds, two assists and two steals, while Lonzo Ball tallied 13 points, 11 assists, four rebounds and one steal. The Lakers (15 - 10) will look to bounce back as they take on the Grizzlies in Memphis on Saturday. The Spurs (12 - 14) play host to the Jazz on Sunday.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the visiting Utah Jazz, 110 - 97, at AT & T Center on Sunday evening. The Jazz got out to an early, 9 - 4, lead, but the Spurs battled back to take a, 23 - 18, lead by the end of the first quarter. The Spurs carried the momentum into the second, where they opening things up by pushing their lead to 12, within the first four minutes of the quarter. They went on to outscore the visitors, 31 - 18, in the quarter, to take a, 54 - 36, lead by halftime. However, the Jazz responded in the third, as they chipped away at the deficit, cutting it to 10, to trail, 82 - 72, entering the final frame. The Jazz kept fighting and cut the gap to just five points, early in the fourth. However, the Spurs fired back, and quickly pushed the lead back to 10. They kept their foot on the gas down the stretch and held on for their second straight win. This marked the end of a two - game winning streak for Utah. DeMar DeRozan led the Spurs with 26 points on 10 - of - 23 shooting, eight assists, six rebounds, two steals and one block, in 38 minutes. Rudy Gay also had a huge night, with 23 points, 15 rebounds, two assists, one steal and one block. LaMarcus Aldridge added 20 points, six rebounds, three blocks and one assist.
