The San Antonio Spurs took down the Milwaukee Bucks, 121 - 114, at AT & T Center on Sunday evening. San Antonio (38 - 29) picked up its fifth straight win in impressive fashion on Sunday, besting the league - leading Bucks (50 - 17). Milwaukee initially seemed poised to win in a blowout, hopping out to a 15 - point lead in the first quarter. However, the Spurs rallied back and had cut the deficit to only six points by halftime. In an unusual turn of events, San Antonio was given another chance to regroup in the third quarter after the game was temporarily delayed by a bat flying around the court. The Spurs were able to take the lead by the end of the third quarter, thanks largely to strong play from DeMar DeRozan. San Antonio sealed the win with a quick run at the beginning of the fourth in which it extended the lead to double digits. LaMarcus Aldridge was the leading scorer for the Spurs with 29 points. The veteran All-Star added 15 rebounds, two steals, and two blocks in the win. DeRozan, meanwhile, finished with 28 points and dished out a team - high six assists. Sunday's win moved the Spurs into a tie for sixth in the Western Conference. For Milwaukee, MVP hopeful Giannis Antetokounmpo tallied 27 points and 13 rebounds to lead the team. Eric Bledsoe scored another 21 points, while Brook Lopez chipped in an 11 - point, 10 - rebound double - double. With the loss, the Bucks have now dropped three straight games on the road. The Bucks will continue their road trip with a visit to New Orleans on Tuesday. The Spurs, meanwhile, will take a trip to Dallas to take on the Mavericks.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the New York Knicks, 109 - 83, at AT & T Center on Friday night. The Knicks (13 - 56) had been playing more competitively in recent games, but they knew they'd be short - handed Friday due to a lower back injury sidelined Dennis Smith, Jr. for the contest. New York looked offensively challenged without their recent trade acquisition, scoring only 41 points during the first half and falling behind by 15 points at intermission. The visitors managed to put together a 28 - point third period, but they fell apart in the final period by scoring just 14 points. Dewayne Dotson paced the Knicks with 21 points and added two rebounds, two assists and two steals. Kadeem Allen followed with 16 points and also supplied three rebounds, two assists and three steals. Emmanuel Mudiay collected 14 points, four rebounds and two assists. DeAndre Jordan generated an 11 - point, 13 - rebound double - double that also included nine assists. Kevin Knox delivered seven points, one assist and one block. LaMarcus Aldridge led the Spurs with 18 points and 11 rebounds. DeMar DeRozan finished with 13 points, seven assists, four rebounds and two steals. Bryn Forbes matched DeRozan's scoring total and added one rebound. Jakob Poeltl managed 12 points, nine rebounds, two assists, five blocks and two steals. Rudy Gay and Marco Belinelli turned in matching 12 - point tallies off the bench. The Knicks head back home to take on the Los Angeles Lakers on Sunday afternoon, while the Spurs remain home and take on the Portland Trail Blazers on Saturday night.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the visiting Portland Trail Blazers, 108 - 103, at AT & T Center on Saturday evening. The contest got out to a competitive start, with the Spurs holding a two - point lead after a back - and - forth first quarter. The Spurs picked it up to start the second, as they built a double - digit lead, however, the Trail Blazers rallied back to take a 50 - 48 lead by halftime. It stayed competitive, as the teams were never more than a couple possessions apart in the third, with the Trail Blazers taking a four - point lead into the fourth. The Spurs came out strong in the fourth and took control by the halfway point in the quarter. They held the lead down the stretch to secure their eighth straight win. DeMar DeRozan led the Spurs with 21 points, eight rebounds, three assists and one block, in 33 minutes. Rudy Gay added 13 points, seven rebounds and one block, while LaMarcus Aldridge tallied 12 points, eight rebounds, two assists, three blocks and a steal. The Spurs shot 47 percent from the field, including 8 - of - 17 from deep. Meanwhile, Damian Lillard led the Trail Blazers with 34 points, six rebounds, five assists and one steal, in 37 minutes. Jusuf Nurkic followed up with 24 points, 16 rebounds, four assists, two steals and a block, while Rodney Hood chipped in 13 points and three rebounds, off the bench. The Trail Blazers shot 42 percent from the field, including 7 - of - 28 from long range. The Trail Blazers (42 - 27) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Pacers on Monday. The Spurs (41 - 29) play host to the Warriors on Monday.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the Golden State Warriors, 111 - 105, at AT & T Center on Monday. The Spurs (42 - 29) continue to roll, as despite playing their third game in four nights, the team managed to post a wire - to - wire victory over the NBA's best team. DeMar DeRozan led the way with a terrific all - around performance, recording a game - high 26 points, nine rebounds and eight assists across 38 minutes. His 25th and 26th points were the most important, as they came on a heavily contested jumper over Klay Thompson with just over a minute left that put the Spurs up six, and up for good. LaMarcus Aldridge was close behind with a double - double of 23 points and 13 rebounds on 8 - of - 12 shooting, while Rudy Gay came off the bench to score 17 points. As for the Warriors (47 - 22), it was a night to forget for their star backcourt, with Steph Curry and Thompson going a combined 14 - of - 43 from the field Monday night. Curry still managed to finish with a team - high 25 points thanks to making six threes, and he added seven rebounds, eight assists and three steals. Meanwhile, Thompson still hit four threes and finished with 14 points in 38 minutes. Kevin Durant didn't hit a single shot from behind the arc, going 0 - of - 4, but he still went 9 - of - 18 from the field and finished with 24 points. As a team, the Warriors shot a respectable 47 percent from the floor, but their lack of aggression resulted in few trips to the free throw line, and that may have cost them the victory, as they were just 10 - of - 12 from the stripe while the Spurs were 19 - of - 22.

The Miami Heat defeated the San Antonio Spurs, 110 - 105, at AT & T Center on Wednesday. Miami (35 - 36) came out firing Wednesday night, opening up a 15 - point lead at the end of the first half and building that up to 18 in the opening moments of the second. The Spurs, however, wouldn't go down without a fight and got within three points with just over a minute remaining. Thanks to a pair of stops, including a Dwyane Wade steal off DeMar DeRozan, Miami was able to escape with its third straight victory. Six Heat players scored in double figures Wednesday night, including all four players who came off the bench. Goran Dragic led the way with 22 points in just 22 minutes as a reserve thanks to an efficient 8 - of - 13 shooting performance. Dion Waiters had one of his best games since returning from injury, adding 18 points in 33 minutes, while Josh Richardson was close behind with 15 points of his own. The Heat have their hot shooting from downtown to thank for carrying them to victory, as the team shot 16 - of - 35 from behind the arc. As for the Spurs (42 - 30), they also had an impressive night shooting the ball from three, going 14 - of - 34 from long range, but they simply dug themselves a hole that they could never completely get themselves out of. LaMarcus Aldridge, Marco Belinelli and Patty Mills each posted a team - high 17 points, while DeMar DeRozan was the next highest scorer with 16. Rudy Gay added 15 points in 32 minutes off the bench, While Davis Bertans made three three - pointers on his way to 10 points.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the visiting Cleveland Cavaliers, 116 - 110, at AT & T Center on Thursday evening. The Spurs (44 - 32) celebrated the career of Manu Ginobili on Thursday, as the team held a ceremony for the retirement of his jersey. San Antonio nearly had the night spoiled, though, as it escaped a late challenge by the Cavaliers (19 - 57), dealing Cleveland its fourth straight win. The Spurs benefited from a highly efficient offensive night, shooting 53 percent from the field in the win. Cleveland, however, countered with a tough challenge on the glass. The Cavaliers out - rebounded San Antonio 49 - 33 despite coming up short. In the end, Patty Mills was able to seal the win for San Antonio by sinking a three - pointer to make it a two - possession game with just 14 seconds remaining. The clinching shot gave Mills 11 points and five rebounds in 23 minutes off the bench. All-Star guard DeMar DeRozan was the team's leading scorer with 25 points on the night. The Spurs saw an additional 19 points from Bryn Forbes, who contributed three steals on the defensive end to round out his strong showing. With the win, San Antonio is now just one win shy of clinching a playoff berth for the 22nd straight season. Cleveland, meanwhile, was led by 24 points from Colin Sexton. The performance brings Sexton's average to 21 points per game since the All-Star Break. Star big man Kevin Love also excelled, tallying 18 points to go with eight rebounds. The Cavaliers will continue their road trip with a visit to the Los Angeles Clippers on Saturday. San Antonio, meanwhile, will host the Sacramento Kings on Sunday afternoon.

The Sacramento Kings defeated the host San Antonio Spurs, 113 - 106, at AT & T Center on Sunday. It took 25 lead changes to determine a winner in this game, as neither club ever led by more than 12 points. The key for Sacramento was a 90 run to start the fourth quarter, as that gave them a game - high 12 - point lead. Three-point shooting was huge, with the Kings hitting 11 - of - 25 and the Spurs connecting on just 8 - of - 27. Free-throw shooting was also decisive, with Sacramento connecting on 24 - of - 28 and the Spurs hitting just 10 - of - 14. Sacramento also won the defensive rebounding battle, 35 - 27 The Kings (38 - 39) were led by Buddy Hield, as he tallied 26 points, five rebounds and three assists. Willie Cauley-Stein accrued 17 points, six rebounds and two steals. Harrison Barnes finished with 15 points, four rebounds and two assists. De'Aaron Fox collected 12 points, four rebounds and five assists. Bogdan Bogdanovic led the bench with 15 points, three rebounds, five assists and two steals. The Spurs (44 - 33) were led by LaMarcus Aldridge, as he accumulated 27 points, 18 rebounds, three assists and two steals. Rudy Gay started and finished with 18 points, nine rebounds and three assists. DeMar DeRozan amassed 16 points, two rebounds, seven assists and three steals while Marco Belinelli led the bench with 14 points. Both teams return to action on Tuesday, with San Antonio playing host to the Atlanta Hawks and Sacramento welcoming the Houston Rockets to Golden 1 Center.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the Atlanta Hawks, 117 - 111, at AT & T Center on Tuesday night. The Spurs (45 - 33) came into the contest with a playoff spot locked up, but looking to sharpen their collective knife prior to the postseason. San Antonio knew they'd be in for a challenge against the spoiler - minded Hawks (28 - 50), which gave them all they could handle in the first half. The home squad held a slim two - point lead at intermission, but Atlanta impressively wiped that out in third and entered the final period with a four - point advantage. However, a 17 - 12 run by the Spurs over the first 7:25 of the fourth quarter gave them a lead that they wouldn't relinquish the rest of the way. Kent Bazemore led the way for the Hawks with 26 points, adding four rebounds, two assists and three steals. Alex Len contributed 21 points, five rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block. Trae Young produced 15 points, six assists, one rebound and one steal. Kyle Huerter poured in 13 points. DeMar DeRozan paced the Spurs with 29 points, complementing them with seven rebounds, seven assists and two steals. Derrick White supplied 23 points, four rebounds, three assists and two blocks. Bryn Forbes netted 19 points, while LaMarcus Aldridge contributed a 16 - point, 11 - rebound double - double that also included three blocks. Patty Mills led the bench with 14 points. The Hawks head back home to face the Philadelphia 76ers on Wednesday evening, while the Spurs pay a visit to the Denver Nuggets on Wednesday night as well.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the Dallas Mavericks, 105 - 94, on Wednesday at AT & T. For both these teams, it was the final game of the regular season, but most importantly, it was the final game for NBA legend Dirk Nowitzki. While he and the Mavericks came up well short of the Spurs on Wednesday night, Nowitzki did get plenty of shots up and managed to lead the team in scoring with 20 points on top of 10 rebounds. It was his only double - double of his final season. Nowitzki was only outdone by LaMarcus Aldridge, who put the finishing touches on a terrific, potentially All-NBA, 2018 - 19 season. Aldridge posted a game - high 34 points on 15 - of - 21 shooting from the floor to go along with 16 rebounds to lead the way for the Spurs in their 48th victory of the season. DeMar DeRozan added 19 points, five rebounds, four assists and three steals, while point guard Derrick White scored 14 points of his own. As a team, San Antonio shot a decent 47 percent from the field. It was a strong close to the season for the Spurs, who won three games in a row and are now locked into the No. 7 seed in the Western Conference standings, finishing one game behind the Thunder. They are expected to play the Nuggets in the first round.

The Phoenix Suns defeated the visiting Dallas Mavericks, 121 - 100, at American Airlines Arena on Wednesday. Wednesday was a big night for both franchises, as it not only marked the start of the 2018 - 19 season, but also the debut of each team's highly - touted top - three draft pick. Number one pick DeAndre Ayton and third overall pick Luka Doncic both made big first impressions in the first game of their respective careers. Ayton helped his team earn a blowout win with a double - double, scoring 18 points and pulling down 10 rebounds in his debut. Doncic meanwhile, posted a respectable 10 points, eight rebounds, and six assists in his first taste of regular season NBA action. Phoenix (10) had many more positives to speak of beyond Ayton's dominant debut. Star shooting guard Devin Booker scored a dominant 35 points to go with seven assists. Booker showed off his impressive scoring arsenal, notching his 33rd point with a step - back three - pointer on Dallas's Dennis Smith, Jr. As a team, Phoenix saw one of its strongest offensive performances in recent memory, tying its season - high in assists from 2017 - 18 with 35 dimes. Dallas (0 - 1), meanwhile, struggled a bit offensively, shooting only 43 percent as a team. In addition to Doncic's NBA debut, Wednesday was also the Mavericks debut for All-Star center DeAndre Jordan. Jordan recorded a double - double in his first game in a Dallas uniform, finishing with 12 points and 11 rebounds. Dallas will host the Minnesota Timberwolves on Friday, while the Suns will visit Denver.

The Los Angeles Lakers defeated the Phoenix Suns 131 - 113 at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Wednesday. The Lakers found their first win of the season against one of the leagues youngest teams in the Suns. LeBron James quickly put behind him the free throw woes that resulted in a brutal OT loss to the Spurs earlier in the week and bounced back to lead Los Angeles (1 - 3) to their first win. A close first quarter that saw the Lakers end with a two point lead was overshadowed by an explosive 44 points in the second quarter. Javale McGree was at the heart of the action in that period, as he finished dunks (unlike his failed dunk in the first quarter, quickly shared on social media) and got to the free throw line in the twenty point rout to end the half. Phoenix (1 - 3) played from behind for the majority of the game, however, they saw a strong outing from their No. 1 overall pick DeAndre Ayton. LeBron James finished with 19 points, 10 assists, seven rebounds and three steals, while Lance Stephenson led all scorers with 23 points on 10 - of - 14 shooting off the bench. All five Lakers starters finished in double figures, including Josh Hart, who started in place of Kentavious Caldwell-Pope. Ayton finished with 22 points and 11 rebounds on 11 - of - 14 shooting and Devin Booker added 23 points, seven rebounds and seven assists in the loss. The Lakers will play the second game of a back - to - back at home against the Nuggets on Thursday, while the Suns will head to Memphis to play the Grizzlies on Saturday.

The San Antonio Spurs defeated the Phoenix Suns 120 - 90 at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Wednesday. Phoenix had no answer for the selfless and efficient Spurs game plan where no San Antonio player needed to log more than 28 minutes of action. DeMar DeRozan continued his impressive start to the season by knocking down 10 - of - 12 from the field on his way to 25 points. San Antonio picked up their third straight win and also received an all around good performance from LaMarcus Aldridge, who finished with 24 points on an equally impressive 10 - of - 13 shooting. The Spurs (5 - 2) jumped out to a 28 - 15 first quarter lead and the Suns could not find a rhythm, especially with Devin Booker (hamstring) sidelined. T.J. Warren tried to fill in on the scoring gaps and contributed 21 points, while rookie Mikal Bridges registered 16 points in 27 minutes off the bench. DeAndre Ayton added 13 points and eight rebounds in the loss, and was in over his head against a savvy veteran team in the front court. The Suns (1 - 6) have now dropped six straight games since winning their opening night matchup against the Mavericks. Next up, the Suns will welcome the Toronto Raptors on Friday, while the Spurs host Anthony Davis and the Pelicans on Saturday.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the host Phoenix Suns, 107 - 98, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Friday evening. The Suns had their leading scorer, Devin Booker, back in the lineup, after he missed three games with an hamstring issue. The Suns came out strong in the first and managed to take a 26 - 23 lead by the end of the first quarter. They held a slight edge for most of the second quarter, while the Raptors stole a one - point lead for a few seconds, the Suns got back on top, 52 - 48, by halftime. The Raptors flipped the narrative in the third, as they quickly took over with a small advantage, before pulling away to take a 77 - 71 lead into the fourth. The Raptors pushed their lead to 17, mid way through the quarter, and held on to earn their second straight win. This marked the seventh straight loss for Phoenix. Kawhi Leonard led Toronto with 19 points, six rebounds, five assists, two steals and one block, in 29 minutes. Jonas Valanciunas finished with 16 points, seven rebounds, four blocks, one steal and one assist, while Kyle Lowry tallied 11 points, 12 assists, six rebounds and two steals. The Raptors shot 49 percent from the field, including 12 - of - 33 from long range. Meanwhile, Isaiah Canaan led the way for the Suns, with 19 points on 8 - of - 12 shooting. Deandre Ayton finished with 17 points, 18 rebounds, two assists and two blocks, while Devin Booker tallied 18 points, six assists, four rebounds, one steal and one block. The Suns shot 44 percent from the field, including 8 - of - 26 from long range. The Suns (1 - 7) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Grizzlies on Sunday. The Raptors (8 - 1) take on the Lakers in Los Angeles on Sunday.

The Phoenix Suns defeated the visiting Memphis Grizzlies, 102 - 100, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Sunday evening. The Grizzlies got out to a good start on the road, holding the edge for most of the first quarter, to take a 28 - 21 lead heading into the second quarter. They stayed on top and pushed their lead to 10, with three minutes left in the second, however, the Suns made a push to end the half, and cut the deficit to just four by halftime. The third quarter started out very close, until the Grizz managed to pull ahead by 10, with five minutes to go. Again, the Suns closed the quarter with a run and made it a four - point game, heading into the final frame. The Grizzlies stayed in control though, as they built yet another 10 - point lead, early in the fourth. The Suns kept chipping away, and had it at a two - point game with just under five minutes remaining. It was a close finish, but Devin Booker led Phoenix in clutch, to outscore the Grizzlies 9 - 5 in the final few minutes, to walk away with the home win, and also end an ugly seven - game losing streak. Devin Booker led the Suns with 25 points on 7 - of - 17 shooting, and seven assists, in 34 minutes. Trevor Ariza followed up with 16 points, nine rebounds, five assists and two steals, while Mikal Bridges chipped in 14 points, in 25 minutes off the bench. The Suns shot 52 percent from the field, including 14 - of - 33 from long range. Meanwhile, Shelvin Mack was the high - point man for Memphis, with 21 points on 7 - of - 10 shooting, in 27 minutes off the bench. Dillon Brooks tallied 17 points on 7 - of - 10 shooting, in 29 minutes off the bench, while Mike Conley and Marc Gasol both had quiet nights. The Grizzlies shot 47 percent from the field, including 7 - of - 24 from deep. The Grizzlies (5 - 3) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Warriors on Monday. The Suns (2 - 7) play host to the Nets on Tuesday.

The Brooklyn Nets defeated the Phoenix Suns, 102 - 84, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Tuesday. The Nets (5 - 6) managed to make light work of the Suns on the road, as they essentially led Tuesday's contest from start to finish. Caris LeVert put together another strong performance for Brooklyn, scoring a game - high 26 points on 10 - of - 16 shooting in 32 minutes. It was his third straight game with at least 20 points and his seventh such performance of the season. It wasn't the prettiest of performances from the Nets, as they shot just 45 percent from the field and 25 percent from behind the arc, but five players scoring in double figures was enough for them to get it done Tuesday night. As for the Suns (2 - 8), they just couldn't get out of their own way. As a team, Phoenix committed 20 turnovers Tuesday, with the starting backcourt of Isaiah Canaan and Devin Booker accounting for seven of those. Booker did finish with a team - high 20 points, but he shot just 6 - of - 21 from the field. The struggles shooting the ball went far beyond beyond Booker, however, as the Suns as a whole shot a miserable 35 percent from the field. In fact, they did better shooting from behind the arc, where they hit 36 percent of their shots. The Suns have now lost eight of nine games since they won their season opener, and things aren't exactly looking up for the young squad in Phoenix.

The Boston Celtics defeated the Phoenix Suns in overtime, 116 - 109, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Thursday evening. Matters looked grim for the Celtics (7 - 4) for the majority of the night, as they surprisingly fell behind, 32 - 13, after one quarter. Although they were able to cut into their sizable deficit during the middle periods while outscoring the Suns (2 - 9) by 52 - 48 margin, they still entered the final 12 minutes trailing by 15. However, a 17 - 4 run by Boston over a 3:23 period late in the fourth quarter left them within one point of Phoenix. Following a pair of clutch T.J. Warren free throws, the Celtics were able to get the ball into the hands of Marcus Morris, who burned one of his old franchises with a three - pointer with 1 seconds on the clock. The visitors then took control in overtime, snapping a 109 - 109 tie with a 70 run over the final 2:5 of the extra period. Kyrie Irving keyed the Celtics with 39 points, a total he supplemented with seven rebounds, six assists, three steals and one block. He also provided the assist on Morris' game - tying three. Jaylen Brown and Morris each provided 17 points overall. They also hauled in six and eight rebounds, respectively. Terry Rozier provided 10 points, six boards and one assist off the bench. Gordon Hayward (eight points), Al Horford (seven points) and Jayson Tatum (four points) all had underwhelming performances. Devin Booker enjoyed another productive night versus the Celtics, leading the Suns with 38 points and adding nine assists, three rebounds and three steals. Warren supplied 29 points, seven rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block. Deandre Ayton posted a 14 - point, 10 - rebound double - double. Trevor Ariza filled out the stat sheet with 11 points, nine rebounds, six assists and one block. The Celtics remain on their road trip and pay a visit to the Utah Jazz on Friday night, while the Suns hit the road as well and face the New Orleans Pelicans on Saturday evening.

The Phoenix Suns defeated the visiting San Antonio Spurs, 116 - 96, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Wednesday evening. It was a brilliant night for Phoenix (3 - 11), a team that has not shown much brilliance early in the season. The Suns jumped out to an early lead and maintained it, thanks in large part to a 57 percent shooting night from the field. The Suns also hit a season - best 15 three - pointers. Meanwhile, everything seemed to be going wrong for the Spurs' offense. In addition to shooting only 42 percent from the field, San Antonio committed 19 turnovers in the loss. T.J. Warren led the Suns with 27 points in the win. Rookie big man DeAndre Ayton added a 17 - point, 10 - rebound double - double. Devin Booker also impressed, dishing out a team - high 12 assists to go with 13 points. For the Spurs, All-Star guard DeMar DeRozan scored a team - high 24 points, including a perfect 10 - of - 10 night at the free - throw line. Fellow All-Star LaMarcus Aldridge, though, had a tough night. The veteran big man shot just 3 - of - 12 from the field en route to just six points. The game evened the season between the two teams at one game apiece. San Antonio had earned a 120 - 90 blowout in its last trip to Phoenix, on Halloween. The Spurs will travel to LA to take on the Clippers on Thursday night. Phoenix, meanwhile, has two days off before hosting the Oklahoma City Thunder on Saturday.

The Oklahoma City Thunder defeated the host Phoenix Suns, 110 - 100, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Saturday evening. Both teams started out strong, as the first quarter featured many lead changes and ties, however, the Thunder came out on top, with a 30 - 25 lead after one. Things quieted down in the second, as the Thunder and the Suns both had trouble scoring the ball. They matched each other for 17 points each in the quarter, resulting in a, 47 - 42, Thunder lead at the half. The Thunder pulled away in the third, as they pushed their lead to 12, just three and a half minutes into the quarter. They outscored the Suns, 32 - 23, in the quarter, to take a 79 - 65 lead into the final frame. The Suns put up a fight in the fourth, but ultimately could hardly make a dent in the deficit, as the Thunder cruised to their third straight win. Paul George led the Thunder with 32 points, 11 rebounds, three steals, three blocks and two assists, in 39 minutes. Steven Adams followed up with 26 points, 10 rebounds and one steal, while Dennis Schroder tallied 15 points, seven assists, five rebounds and four steals. The Thunder shot 45 percent from the field, including 7 - of - 24 from deep. Meanwhile, T.J. Warren led the Suns with 23 points, five rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block, in 40 minutes. Devin Booker had a solid night, with 18 points, 11 assists and four rebounds, while Deandre Ayton tallied 19 points, nine rebounds, an assist and a steal. The Suns shot 45 percent from the field, including 12 - of - 29 from long range. The Suns (3 - 12) will look to bounce back as they visit Philadelphia to take on the 76ers on Monday. The Thunder (10 - 5) head to Sacramento to face the Kings on Monday.

The Indiana Pacers defeated the Phoenix Suns at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Tuesday. The Pacers set the pace early and maintained a 10 point lead for the majority of the second quarter, quietly answering the Suns comeback attempts early on. The momentum swung in favor the Suns late in the third quarter and carried through the rest of the game which finished with over 11 ties and lead changes and resulted in a wild finish capped off by Bojan Bogdanović's three pointer. Prior to Bogdanovic's three, Devin Booker answered Myles Turner's shot from behind the arc to keep a tie game. Booker was unable to answer a second time with the game on the line and the rest was finished at the charity stripe for Indiana (13 - 8). The Suns (4 - 16) were led by T.J. Warren who finished with 25 points and seven rebounds, while Booker added 20 points on a rough 7 - of - 21 shooting. Booker pitched in eight assists to aid the poor shooting effort. The Pacers bench stood out while four starters finished in low double figures, as Damontis Sabonis Doug McDermott each poured in 21 points a piece. Sabonis added a big 16 rebounds in his all around dominant game in 23 minutes off the bench. Indiana was without Victor Oladipo who is still nursing a knee injury. The Suns will play the second game of a back - to - back tomorrow when they visit the Clippers, while the Pacers visit the Lakers on Thursday.

The Orlando Magic defeated the host Phoenix Suns, 99 - 85, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Friday evening. The Suns got out to a good start at home, as they emerged with a, 25 - 21, lead after a competitive first quarter. The Magic picked it up in the second quarter, as they pulled ahead after just a few minutes and went on to outscore the home team, 30 - 23, in the quarter, to take a, 51 - 48, lead by halftime. The Magic pushed their lead to seven early in the third quarter. The Suns hung around and managed to keep it close, in part thanks to a last - second jumper from Jamal Crawford to cut the deficit to just four points by end of the quarter. However, the Magic turned up the defense in the fourth, where they held the Suns to just 14 points, while they poured in 24 points, to earn the decisive, 14 - point victory. Nikola Vucevic led the Magic with 25 points, 15 rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block, in 31 minutes. Terrence Ross came up large with 21 points on 7 - of - 15 shooting, in 30 minutes off the bench, while Aaron Gordon added 18 points, six rebounds, three assists and one steal, in 34 minutes. The Magic shot 48 percent from the field, including 8 - of - 27 from long range. Meanwhile, Deandre Ayton led the Suns with 19 points, six rebounds and two assists, in 31 minutes. Jamal Crawford followed up with 18 points, four assists and two rebounds, in 30 minutes off the bench, while Devin Booker (toe) did not play. The Suns (4 - 18) will look to get back on track as they take on the Lakers in Los Angeles, on Sunday. The Magic (11 - 12) head to Miami to take on the Heat, on Tuesday.

The Sacramento Kings blew out the Phoenix Suns, 122 - 105, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Tuesday. Sacramento (12 - 11) blew the game wide open in the first quarter, jumping out to a 36 - 9 lead. The hot start made it a wire - to - wire win for the Kings, who shot 54 percent from the floor on the game. Phoenix (4 - 20) did manage to climb back somewhat, scoring 38 points in the fourth quarter. However, it was far too little too late, as the game still ended in a double - digit loss. The Kings hit 11 three - pointers in the win. Seven players scored in double digits for Sacramento, including Buddy Hield, who led the way with 20 points. De'Aaron Fox finished with 16 points and six assists, while Willie Cauley-Stein notched a team - high four steals. Rookie star Marvin Bagley III missed the contest with back soreness. Phoenix, meanwhile, saw a double - double from backup big man Richuan Holmes. Holmes recorded 10 points and 10 rebounds in just 23 minutes of action, but also fouled out in that time. DeAndre Ayton finished the game with 10 points and nine rebounds. Devin Booker did not play in Tuesday's game after sustaining a hamstring injury in Phoenix's previous contest. On Friday, the Kings will visit the Cavaliers in Cleveland. The Suns, meanwhile, will see Portland on Thursday.

The Miami Heat defeated the Phoenix Suns, 115 - 98, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Friday evening. The Heat (10 - 14) saw the Suns (4 - 22) likely give them more than they expected in a tight opening period, one that saw Phoenix edge them by a 36 - 34 margin. However, Miami began to exert its will in the second period, forging a 60 - 50 halftime advantage. The home squad would be unable to mount a truly formidable challenge in the second half, leading to a comfortable win for the visitors. Turnovers were a pivotal factor, with the Heat forcing 20 while only committing 12 of their own. Bam Adebayo filled in for Hassan Whiteside (personal) and paced the Heat with a 22 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included two assists, one steal and one block. Justise Winslow turned in 20 points, eight rebounds, six assists, one steal and one block. Rodney McGruder supplied 14 points and five boards. Kelly Olynyk managed 13 points, four rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block. Tyler Johnson headed back to the bench with Goran Dragic (knee) returning to action and posted 12 points, five boards and three assists. Dragic furnished 11 points, 10 assists, one rebound and three steals. Troy Daniels led the Suns with 18 points and complemented them with four rebounds. Deandre Ayton mustered a 16 - point, 11 - rebound double - double that also included two assists. De'Anthony Melton and Mikal Bridges managed matching 12 - point tallies. The Heat remain on the road and tangle with the Los Angeles Clippers on Saturday night. The Suns are off until Monday evening, when they also take on the Clippers.

The visiting Los Angeles Clippers defeated the Phoenix Suns, 123 - 119, in overtime at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Monday evening. It seemed as though Phoenix (4 - 23) had the game under control, holding a nine lead with just six minutes remaining. Los Angeles (17 - 9), though, fought hard to tie the game up in the final minutes. The win keeps LA in fourth place in the Western Conference. The team has enjoyed a successful start to its 2018 - 19 campaign, thanks in no small part to star forward Tobias Harris. Harris was as dominant as ever on Monday, leading all scorers with 33 points and grabbing eight rebounds. Danilo Gallinari added another 25 points and shot an impressive 11 - of - 12 at the free - throw line in the win. The loss makes nine straight for the last - place Suns, who are on pace for their worst season in franchise history. It was a hard - fought loss, though, as the team shot 50 percent from the field and had seven double - digit scorers. DeAndre Ayton led the team with 20 points, 12 rebounds, and three blocks in the narrow loss. The Clippers will return home to host the Raptors on Tuesday, while the Suns will visit San Antonio.

The Phoenix Suns defeated the Dallas Mavericks, 99 - 89, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Thursday evening. Phoenix (5 - 24) entered Thursday's nationally - televised game amidst turbulence on and off the court. The Suns had dropped 10 straight games and had declined to play Trevor Ariza in their most recent game as they attempt to find a trade destination for him. Rumors had also begun to swirl that team owner Robert Sarver was threatening to relocate the team to Seattle or Las Vegas, prompting outrage from many Suns fans. On Thursday, though, the team got good news, as Sarver publicly promised to keep the team in Phoenix and the Suns earned their first win in over three weeks. The Suns saw a strong shooting night from beyond the arc, knocking down 10 three - pointers. Dallas (15 - 13), meanwhile, shot a dismal 5 - of - 33 from beyond the arc in one of its coldest nights of the season. T.J. Warren led Phoenix with 30 points, shooting 11 - of - 17 from the field in the win. Trevor Ariza also saw the court again, where he scored 13 points and grabbed eight rebounds. Josh Jackson added 14 points but shot just 5 - of - 17 from the field in doing so. Dallas, meanwhile, scored only 89 points, as none of its players scored more than 15 in the loss. Rookie wing Luka Doncic scored 13 points to go with five rebounds and six assists. Veteran big man DeAndre Jordan also had a nice night, scoring 14 points and pulling down 16 rebounds despite the loss. Phoenix will host the Minnesota Timberwolves on Saturday, while Dallas will see the Sacramento Kings on Sunday.

The Phoenix Suns defeated the visiting Minnesota Timberwolves, 107 - 99, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Saturday. There were nine ties and 17 lead changes in total, as Phoenix rode a big second half to victory. In fact, the Suns outscored the Timberwolves, 51 - 41, in the second half. Warren amassed 21 points and five boards. Deandre Ayton totaled 18 points, 12 rebounds and two assists. Mikal Bridges started and finished with 13 points, five rebounds, two assists, two steals and three blocks. On deck for Phoenix is a road matchup versus the New York Knicks on Monday. Minnesota also returns on Monday, as they play host to the Sacramento Kings.

The Oklahoma City Thunder defeated the host Phoenix Suns, 118 - 102, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Friday evening. The Thunder (22 - 12) take on the Mavericks in Dallas on Sunday.

The Denver Nuggets defeated the host Phoenix Suns, 122 - 118, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Saturday evening. The Golden State Warriors defeated the host Phoenix Suns, 132 - 109, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Monday evening. The Warriors took the early advantage, with a 31 - 27 lead after one quarter. The Warriors (25 - 13) play host to the Rockets on Thursday.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the host Phoenix Suns, 132 - 127, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Wednesday evening. The Sixers got out to a great start on the road, as they poured in 44 points in the first quarter and took a 44 - 32 lead into the second. They kept it up in the second, where they outscored the Suns by 11, to take a 72 - 49 lead into halftime. The 76ers (25 - 14) play host to the Mavericks on Saturday.

The Los Angeles Clippers defeated the host Phoenix Suns, 121 - 111, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Friday. The final scoreline makes this game look much closer than it actually was, as Los Angeles were in control throughout. In fact, a 38 - 19 first quarter really set the tone, as they held a double - digit lead for the final 36 minutes of action. The Charlotte Hornets took down the Phoenix Suns, 119 - 113, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Sunday evening. Charlotte (19 - 20) overcame its struggles on the road to earn a win in Phoenix, thanks in large part to its success at the free - throw line. The Suns, meanwhile, saw a combined 45 points from the duo of T.J. Warren and Josh Jackson. Charlotte will continue its West Coast road trip with a game against the Clippers in LA on Tuesday. Phoenix, meanwhile, will host the Sacramento Kings.

The Phoenix Suns defeated the visiting Sacramento Kings, 115 - 111, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Tuesday. Sacramento led by 19 points headed into halftime thanks to a 40 - 18 second quarter but fell apart in the second half. On deck for Phoenix is a road matchup versus the Dallas Mavericks on Wednesday. As for Sacramento, they return to action on Thursday when they play host to the Detroit Pistons.

The Phoenix Suns defeated the visiting Denver Nuggets, 102 - 93, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Saturday evening. Despite missing Devin Booker, the Suns got out to a good start at home, with a 31 - 23 lead after one quarter. Kelly Oubre Jr. led the Suns with 26 points, 11 rebounds, three assists, two steals and one block, in 29 minutes off the bench. The Nuggets shot 39 percent from the field, including 10 - of - 31 from long range. The Nuggets (28 - 13) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Trail Blazers on Sunday. The Suns (11 - 33) take on the Pacers in Indiana on Tuesday.

The Minnesota Timberwolves cruised past the Phoenix Suns, 118 - 91, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Tuesday. The Wolves quickly changed that, though, as 10 points in the quarter from Karl-Anthony Towns helped spark a run that gave Minnesota a 15 - point lead by halftime. Phoenix, meanwhile, saw a promising showing from sophomore wing Josh Jackson. Jackson helped tie the game up with a pair of free - throws in the second, which gave him two of his team - high 27 points. He added 10 rebounds and three blocks. Both teams will take the court again on Thursday, with Phoenix playing host to the Portland Trail Blazers and the Timberwolves taking a trip to Los Angeles to face the Lakers.

The Portland Trail Blazers defeated the host Phoenix Suns, 120 - 106, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Thursday evening. The Trail Blazers pulled ahead through the second, where they outscored the Suns by five, to take a 56 - 52 lead by halftime. The Suns kept battling, but could not trim the deficit through the fourth, as the Trail Blazers cruised to their 30th win of the season. Damian Lillard led the Trail Blazers with 24 points, three rebounds, three assists, two steals and two blocks, in 29 minutes. C.J. McCollum added 20 points, three rebounds, two assists and one steal, while Jake Layman finished with 20 points, eight rebounds, three assists, two blocks and one steal. The Trail Blazers (30 - 20) play host to the Hawks on Saturday.

The Atlanta Hawks defeated the host Phoenix Suns, 118 - 112, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Saturday evening. The Houston Rockets defeated the Phoenix Suns, 118 - 110, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Monday. Close behind was Kelly Oubre coming off the bench to score 23 points on a very efficient 9 - of - 13 shooting performance. Other rookie DeAndre Ayton posted another double - double of 15 points and 11 rebounds, while Devin Booker added 19 points, seven rebounds and five assists.

The New Orleans Pelicans defeated the Phoenix Suns, 130 - 116, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Friday evening. The Phoenix Suns defeated the visiting Milwaukee Bucks, 114 - 105, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Monday. There were nine ties and seven lead changes alone in the second half, despite the fact that the Bucks led for over 40 minutes of this 48 - minute game. Rim protection was the difference for the Suns, as they recorded 10 blocks while the Bucks picked up just two. Pheonix's defense was big all - around, as they held Milwaukee to 37 percent from the field and 29 percent from three - point range while connecting on 45 percent of their shots. The Bucks (48 - 15) were led by Giannis Antetokounmpo, as he tallied 21 points, 13 rebounds, six assists and three steals. Malcolm Brogdon finished with 19 points and seven boards. Eric Bledsoe accrued 15 points, five rebounds and five assists while Ersan Ilyasova provided a double - double off the bench. The Suns (13 - 51) were led by Kelly Oubre Jr. as he accumulated 27 points, 13 rebounds and three blocks. Devin Booker amassed 22 points, five rebounds and seven assists. On deck for Phoenix is a home matchup versus the New York Knicks on Wednesday. As for Milwaukee, they play host to the Indiana Pacers on Thursday for their next fixture.

The Phoenix Suns defeated the New York Knicks, 107 - 96, on Wednesday at Talking Stick Resort Arena. The Knicks (13 - 52) managed to get off to a good start, leading by six points after the first 12 minutes, but from that point, it was all Suns (15 - 51), who won their third straight game. After two dominant quarters from Phoenix, the home team ended up taking an 18 - point lead into the final quarter. The Suns managed to pull away on the back of their young backcourt star, Devin Booker, who had a season - high 41 points on 14 - of - 23 shooting Wednesday night. He was one of five Phoenix players to score in double figures and led what was a terrific display from behind the arc for the team. Booker went 6 - of - 10 from downtown, and the team as a whole finished 12 - of - 29 (41 percent) from three. As for the Knicks, it was their fourth straight loss after they pulled off a stretch where they won three of four games, and it came at the ends of a miserable offensive performance against a not - so - stingy Suns defense. As a team, New York shot a serviceable 46 percent from the floor, but they were sloppy with the basketball, turning it over 21 times to just 17 assists. DeAndre Jordan led the way with a double - double of 17 points and 14 rebounds in just 25 minutes, while Noah Vonleh, Dennis Smith and Damyean Dotson each added 15 points. Allonzo Trier was the only other player to score in double figures with 12 points off the bench.

The Utah Jazz took down the Phoenix Suns, 114 - 97, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Wednesday. After allowing Phoenix (16 - 52) to cut the difference to a single possession, the Jazz (38 - 29) ran away with Wednesday's game in the fourth quarter. Sophomore sensation Donovan Mitchell had seven points in 90 seconds to help seal the win for Utah late in the game. The biggest advantage for the Jazz came on the glass, where Utah held a 53 - 35 advantage over Phoenix. Utah also had a nice night shooting the ball, knocking down 12 three - pointers while limiting Phoenix to just seven. The star tandem of Mitchell and Rudy Gobert helped get the job done for the Jazz on Wednesday. Mitchell finished with a team - high 26 points on 10 - of - 18 shooting, including 4 - of - 6 from three - point range. Gobert, meanwhile, logged a double - double with 18 points and a whopping 20 rebounds. As a team, Utah shot over 46 percent and saw five double - digit scoring performances. For Phoenix, star shooting guard Devin Booker led the way with 27 points. Rookie big man DeAndre Ayton struggled to deal with Gobert's defense, going just 1 - of - 9 for two points in the loss. As a team, Phoenix was not particularly active from three - point range, attempting just 19 shots from beyond the arc. Utah will face the second half of a back - to - back as it takes on the Timberwolves on Thursday. The Suns, meanwhile, will visit Houston on Friday.

The Chicago Bulls defeated the Phoenix Suns, 116 - 101, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Monday evening. A hot start set the tone early for Chicago (20 - 51), as the Bulls cruised to a clean victory after gaining a double - digit lead in the first quarter. 10 quick points from Kris Dunn contributed to a 34 - point first for Chicago, giving the team a 14 - point advantage by the end of the quarter. From there it was smooth sailing, as efficient play led the Bulls to shoot over 51 percent from the floor in the win. Phoenix (17 - 55) could not find an offensive groove, shooting just 7 - of - 26 from three - point range and a dismal 16 - of - 26 at the free - throw line. Robin Lopez led Chicago in what proved to be a big man duel on Monday. Lopez scored a team - high 24 points on 11 - of - 14 shooting in the win. The veteran's strong play was complemented by stellar performances from Chicago's young core. Zach LaVine and Lauri Markkanen notched 20 points apiece, with LaVine also dishing out seven assists. Dunn, meanwhile, finished with 14 points and two steals. Phoenix saw equally promising play from its young stars. Reigning first overall pick DeAndre Ayton was the game's leading scorer with 25 points. Ayton also tallied 12 rebounds, three steals, and three blocks. Devin Booker also delivered a gem, scoring 25 points while dishing out seven assists. Ultimately, though, Phoenix's uninspired offensive effort could not get the job done against Chicago's efficient performance. Chicago will return home to host the Washington Wizards on Wednesday. The Suns meanwhile, will next suit up on Thursday, when they're scheduled to take on the Detroit Pistons.

The Detroit Pistons defeated the Phoenix Suns, 118 - 98, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Thursday. It was a close contest through the first 24 minutes, with the Suns (17 - 56) taking a narrow two - point lead into halftime, but from that point on, it was all Pistons (37 - 34). More specifically, the fourth quarter was all Detroit, as the team wasted no time rattling off a 17 - 2 run over the course of four minutes to put the game away. It was a complete team effort from the Pistons, with seven different players scoring in double figures Thursday night. Wayne Ellington led the way with a team - high 23 points after the sharp - shooter went 6 - of - 10 from behind the arc. Blake Griffin put together yet another terrific all - around performance with 17 points, seven rebounds and eight assists in 31 minutes while Andre Drummond posted a monster double - double of 16 points and 19 rebounds. Luke Kennard matched Drummond's 16 points in 25 minutes off the bench. As for the Suns, it was their second straight loss and fourth in five games. They shot a decent percentage from the field Thursday, going 48 percent from the field, but they committed a staggering 19 turnovers. That, combined with giving up 19 offensive rebounds, led to Detroit getting 17 more shooting possessions. Devin Booker lead the way with a game - high 26 points, while DeAndre Ayton posted 20 points and eight rebounds. Mikal Bridges and Richaun Holmes were the only other Suns players to reach double figures, scoring 13 and 10 points, respectively.

The Washington Wizards edged out the Phoenix Suns, 124 - 121, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Wednesday. For the second straight game, Phoenix (17 - 59) could not get the win despite a 50 - point night from Devin Booker. Booker shot 19 - of - 29 from the field and 9 - of - 10 at the free - throw line, but his strong play could not get the job done. Washington (31 - 45) was able to draw 28 fouls and get to the free - throw line 43 times, generating plenty of offense despite its poor 67 percent shooting night at the stripe. Thomas Bryant scored the last six points for Washington in the win, including a game - winning and - one with just 3 seconds remaining. He finished with 18 points and 19 rebounds. Bradley Beal and Jabari Parker led the Wizards in scoring with 28 points each. Parker was particularly impressive, grabbing 15 rebounds off the bench. The Wizards were able to dominate the glass all night, grabbing 15 offensive rebounds in total. Despite the team's strong overall offensive play, ball movement still stagnated at points, as the team finished with just 18 total assists. Phoenix, meanwhile, saw little offense outside of Booker's heroics. DeAndre Ayton had 14 points to go with 10 rebounds and two blocks. However, Booker was the undisputed story of the night, joining James Harden as only the second player this season to have multiple 50 - point games. Unfortunately for the Suns, both performances have come in a losing effort. The Wizards will visit Utah on Friday, while Phoenix will host the Memphis Grizzlies on Saturday.

The Memphis Grizzlies defeated the host Phoenix Suns, 120 - 115, Talking Stick Resort Arena on Saturday evening. The Suns got out to a great start at home, with a 38 - 23 lead after one quarter. The Grizzlies picked it up in the second and managed to trim seven points off the deficit, to make it n eight - point game by halftime. The Grizzlies kept the pressure on in the third and pushed to make it a four - point game entering the fourth. The Suns could not keep up the Grizzlies' intensity down the stretch, as the Grizz closed with a 14 - 9 run to earn the impressive comeback win. This marks the sixth straight loss for Phoenix. Jonas Valanciunas led the Grizzlies with 34 points, 20 rebounds, five assists, two blocks and a steal, in 34 minutes. Mike Conley tallied 33 points, five assists, four rebounds and three steals, while justin Holiday chipped in 14 points two rebounds, two steals and a block. The Grizzlies shot 46 percent from the field, including 32 percent from long range. Meanwhile, Devin Booker led the Suns with 48 points, 11 assists and three rebounds, in 43 minutes. Deandre Ayton tallied 17 points, 13 rebounds, an assist and a block, while Mikal Bridges chipped in 10 points, four rebounds, two assists and a block. The Suns shot 53 percent from the field, including 42 percent from deep. The Suns (17 - 60) play host to the Cavs on Monday. The Grizzlies (31 - 45) take on the Clippers in L.A. on Sunday.

The Phoenix Suns defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 122 - 113, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Monday evening. A 14 - 4 run to start the fourth quarter helped Phoenix (18 - 60) snap its six - game losing streak. The Suns had established an early double - digit lead thanks to a 40 - point second quarter, but the late run helped seal the much - needed win for the last place squad. Cleveland (19 - 59) battled back to make it a single - digit game again, but Phoenix had plenty of breathing room as it made its way to the final buzzer. As a unit, Phoenix shot over 54 percent from the floor in the win. After a slough of big scoring nights, Devin Booker impressed once again, this time with his passing prowess. Booker recorded a 25 - point, 13 - assist double - double to lead his team to victory. Josh Jackson recorded a double - double as well, grabbing 10 rebounds while scoring 19 points. Jackson also amassed a career - high five blocks in Monday's win. Cleveland saw big nights from its own young guards. Rookie point guard Colin Sexton continued his dominant post All-Star play, scoring 21 points to lead the team. Off the bench, Jordan Clarkson poured in 20 points. The team also saw 12 rebounds and four assists from center Larry Nance Jr.. Cleveland will continue its road trip with a visit to Sacramento on Thursday. Phoenix, meanwhile, will see the Utah Jazz on Wednesday.

The Utah Jazz defeated the Phoenix Suns, 118 - 97, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Wednesday. Disaster struck early for the Suns (18 - 61), as just eight minutes into Wednesday's contest, Devin Booker came down awkwardly on his ankle and was forced to leave the contest. At that point, Phoenix managed to grab a lead and took a six - point advantage into the second quarter. From that point, however, the Suns had little - to - no chance without their star player, and the visiting Jazz (48 - 30) slowly started to pull away before piling it on the home team in the fourth quarter. Donovan Mitchell led the way scoring for the Jazz with a game - high 29 points in 35 minutes, but the most impressive performance of the evening may have come from swingman Joe Ingles. Ingles shot a scorching 6 - of - 8 from behind the arc and 10 - of - 13 overall from the field on his way to scoring 27 points to go along with five rebounds and eight assists across 35 minutes. Rudy Gobert added a double - double of 17 points and 13 rebounds to go along with five blocks, while Utah's bench also came up in a big way Wednesday, scoring 41 points as a four - player unit. As a team, the Jazz were electric from behind the arc, shooting 16 - of - 32 (50 percent) from long range. The Suns, without Booker, unsurprisingly could not find the same success after a strong start to Wednesday's game. Booker looked to be on track for another strong offensive performance, scoring eight points in the first eight minutes, but the offense stalled as soon as he was forced to leave the game. The team hit just five of its 21 three - point attempts and shot 46 percent from the field overall. Richaun Holmes ended up leading the team in scoring with just 16 points on 8 - of - 16 shooting, while Ellie Okobo was close behind with 15 points of his own. Phoenix has failed to score 100 points in four of its last 11 games, with three of those times coming against the Jazz.

The Phoenix Suns defeated the visiting New Orleans Pelicans in overtime, 133 - 126, at Talking Stick Resort Arena on Friday. While both these teams are well out of playoff contention, it took an overtime session to determine a winner in this tightly - contested game. Phoenix started the overtime on a 10 - 3 run and that was simply too much for the Pelicans to overcome. It took a big second half for the Suns to get into overtime, as they outscored the Pelicans, 52 - 41. There ended up being 10 ties and six lead changes in total. The key for Phoenix was their defense, as they recorded 12 steals and 11 blocks while winning the turnover differential, 15 - 7. The Pelicans (32 - 48) were led by Julius Randle, as he tallied 31 points, 14 rebounds and three assists. Ian Clark accrued 24 points, four rebounds, four assists and two steals. Elfrid Payton accrued 14 points, five rebounds, 12 assists and two steals. Christian Wood led the bench with 17 points and five boards. The Suns (19 - 61) were led by Josh Jackson, as he collected 35 points, nine rebounds, five assists and two steals. Ray Spalding provided career - highs across the board, generating 21 points, 13 rebounds, three steals and three blocks. Dragan Bender generated 11 points, 10 rebounds, six assists and seven blocks. Jamal Crawford led the bench with 28 points and seven assists. Both teams return to action on Sunday, with Phoenix traveling to face the surging Houston Rockets and New Orlena traveling to face the Sacramento Kings.

The Sacramento Kings defeated the Oklahoma City Thunder, 131 - 120, at Chesapeake Energy Arena on Sunday evening. With their surprisingly high - powered offensive performances over the first three games, the Kings (1 - 2) have seemingly caught the rest of the NBA off guard. The latest team to fall victim to their high - scoring prowess was the Thunder (0 - 3), which failed to notch their first win of the season despite the debut of Russell Westbrook (knee). The perennial All-Star unexpectedly logged 35 minutes despite not having had the benefit of a training camp or preseason and racked up 35 points, 12 rebounds and eight assists. However, Sacramento saw every member of their first unit post double - digit scoring totals and shot a blistering 55 percent overall, including 46 percent from three - point range. In contrast, the majority of OKC'S offense ran through Westbrook and Paul George, and as a team, they only mustered a 23 percent success rate from behind the arc. Iman Shumpert drew the start and led the Kings with 26 points, a total he supplemented with four assists, three rebounds, three steals and two blocks. De'Aaron Fox supplied 22 points, 10 assists, four rebounds, one steal and one block. Buddy Hield pitched in 17 points, five boards and two assists. Willie Cauley-Stein and Marvin Bagley III generated matching 13 - point tallies from the first unit and bench, respectively. Each also brought down seven rebounds. Nemanja Bjelica totaled 12 points, five rebounds, four assists, three steals and one block. George followed Westbrook with 29 points, six rebounds, two assists and three steals. Dennis Schroder still logged 32 minutes despite Westbrook's return and posted 14 points, eight assists, four rebounds and one steal. Hamidou Diallo registered 11 points, two assists, a rebound and two steals. Adams managed 10 points, 14 rebounds, three blocks and two steals. The Kings remain on the road and next tangle with the Denver Nuggets on Tuesday evening, while the Thunder try again for their first win against the Boston Celtics at home on Thursday evening.

The Boston Celtics defeated the Oklahoma City Thunder, 101 - 95, at Chesapeake Energy Arena on Thursday night. The Celtics (3 - 2) will surely feel happy following this win on the road, as they had to come from behind to defeat a Thunder (0 - 4) team that crumbled in the second half and wasted a huge lead in the final 24 minutes of action. The Thunder went up by 16 points (50 - 34) in the first half of action, but Boston turned things around and a huge 40 - 23 win in the third quarter gave them a one - point lead leading into the fourth quarter. The Thunder tried to come back, but Boston closed things out in the final seconds and the win put them one game over .500, while the Thunder remain winless after their first four games. Jayson Tatum was Boston's top scorer since he finished with 24 points and six rebounds, while Al Horford (19 points and nine rebounds) and Kyrie Irving (15 points, five rebounds and five assists) also logged double - figure points the Celtics. Marcus Morris had a double - double coming off the bench with 21 points and 10 boards, but Gordon Hayward disappointed since he only scored five points in 23 minutes of action. As expected, Paul George and Russell Westbrook led the way for the winless Thunder; the former Indiana Pacers star contributed with 22 points and eight rebounds, while the star point guard came close to a triple - double thanks to 13 points, 15 rebounds and eight assists, but also committed five turnovers and five fouls. Dennis Schroder had 10 points with six assists off the bench, while Steven Adams added 12 points with six rebounds.

The Oklahoma City Thunder defeated the Phoenix Suns, 117 - 110, at Chesapake Energy Arena on Sunday evening. The Thunder (1 - 4) approached the contest with Steven Adams as a late scratch and Russell Westbrook uncertain to play due to shoulder soreness. However, the perennial All-Star did end up taking the court, posting 23 points, nine rebounds, seven assists and four steals. Oklahoma City enjoyed a prolific first half on offense, racking up 62 points by halftime and 96 through three quarters. The Suns (1 - 5) made some noise in the fourth quarter, but it was after the game was essentially decided. The Thunder drained 51 percent of its shots and also goaded the visitors into 22 turnovers, both keys to victory. Elie Okobo and T.J. Warren co - led the Suns with matching 18 - point tallies off the bench. Okobo added eight assists and five rebounds over 31 minutes, while Warren also supplied eight boards and one block. Deandre Ayton generated a 16 - point, 11 - rebound double - double that also included three assists and one steal. Ryan Anderson provided 15 points and five rebounds. Josh Jackson drew a second straight start for Devin Booker (hamstring) and mustered eight points, one rebound, one steal and one block. Paul George matched Westbrook's scoring total and also registered five assists, four rebounds, three steals and two blocks. Nerlens Noel contributed a 20 - point - 15 rebound double - double in Adams' stead, complementing it with two assists, four steals and one block. Jerami Grant compiled 14 points, four rebounds, one assist and one steal. Patrick Patterson came off the bench to pour in 17 points, while Dennis Schroder produced 12 points, seven assists and four rebounds. The Suns head back home to face the San Antonio Spurs on Wednesday evening, while the Thunder remain home and tangle with the Los Angeles Clippers on Tuesday night.

The Oklahoma City Thunder defeated the Los Angeles Clippers 128 - 110 at Chesapeake Energy Arena on Tuesday. The Thunder came away with their second win of the season after surging in the second half behind a 39 point third quarter and 35 point fourth quarter. Before Russell Westbrook and Paul George found their rhythm (combined for 64 points) the Clippers played a defensively efficient first half and came away with a 13 point lead behind Tobias Harris and Danilo Gallinari. A bang - bang play highlighted the fourth quarter after the Thunder pulled away with a double digit lead as Patrick Beverley dove for a loose ball and collided with Westbrook's knee. Both players came away talking as both benches cleared to keep the altercation from escalating to anything too serious. Billy Donovan, Westbrook and Beverley were all given technical fouls for the mess. Galliari led all Clippers scorers with 27 points on 7 - of - 15 shooting and a perfect 10 - of - 10 from the free throw line. Montrezl Harrell, who entered the matchup as one of the most efficient bench players to start the season, finished with 10 points and four rebounds in 22 minutes. Lou Williams led the bench with 17 points. The three ball was the key for the Thunder's second half surge after they finished shooting 53 percent as a unit from behind the arc. Both teams take to the road on Thursday as the Thunder will face the Charlotte Hornets, while the Clippers will visit the Philadelphia 76ers.

The Oklahoma City Thunder defeated the New Orleans Pelicans, 122 - 116, at Chesapeake Energy Arena on Monday evening. The Thunder (5 - 4) came into the contest looking to build on the significant momentum they'd begun generating after an 0 - 4 start, but they knew they'd be facing a Pelicans (4 - 6) squad at full strength. Anthony Davis was announced as active for the game shortly before tip - off, although OKC didn't seem the least bit bothered on their way to building a 36 - 28 first - half lead. It would prove to be a game of alternating advantages, however, as New Orleans came back to forge a 63 - 62 halftime edge. The home squad did come out of intermission with the hot hand, and the 100 - 86 edge they carried into the final 12 minutes would hold up when the visitors closed out the game with a 30 - point fourth quarter. Turnovers were key, as the Pelicans gave the ball up on 20 occasions while only taking it away 12 times from the Thunder. OKC notably pulled out the victory despite losing Russell Westbrook to a sprained left ankle in the second half. Julius Randle led the Pelicans with 26 points off the bench, and he added eight rebounds, one assist, one steal and two blocks. Jrue Holiday followed with a 22 - point, 14 - assist double - double that also included four rebounds and one block. Davis provided 20 points, eight rebounds, one assist and one block. Nikola Mirotic generated a 16 - point, 16 - rebound double - double. Paul George paced the Thunder with 23 points, a total he supplemented with eight assists, six rebounds and four steals. Dennis Schroder followed with a bench - leading 22 points and also contributed three rebounds, two assists and one steal. Steven Adams went for 18 points, eight rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block. Westbrook delivered 17 points, nine assists, seven rebounds and one steal before exiting. Jerami Grant finished with 13 points, six rebounds, one assist, two steals and one block. The Pelicans head back home and face the Chicago Bulls on Wednesday night, while the Thunder pay a visit to the Cleveland Cavaliers on Wednesday evening as well.

The Oklahoma City Thunder defeated the visiting Houston Rockets, 98 - 80, at Chesapeake Energy Arena on Thursday. Houston's offense has been struggling all season long and this 80 - point nightmare is hopefully rock - bottom. It was a thorough domination from start to finish, as Oklahoma City led by 10 points after the first quarter and by 20 points headed into the fourth quarter. In fact, the Thunder held a double - digit lead for the entirety of the second half. They held the Rockets to just 38 percent from the field and 26 percent from three - point range while forcing 17 turnovers. Oklahoma City also dominated the boards, outrebounding Houston, 52 - 37. Getting to the charity stripe was also huge for the Thunder, as they connected on 17 - of - 24 of their free - throws while the Rockets hit just 7 - of - 10. The Rockets (4 - 6) were led by James Harden, as he tallied 29 points, eight rebounds, five assists and three steals. Clint Capela totaled 17 points, seven rebounds and three assists. Chris Paul accrued 10 points, two rebounds, five assists and six steals. Carmelo Anthony had a nightmare game off the bench, scoring two points on 1 - of - 11 from the field. The Thunder (7 - 4) were led by Paul George, as he collected 20 points, 11 rebounds, six assists and six steals. Steven Adams amassed 19 points, 10 rebounds and four assists. Dennis Schroder accumulated 14 points, six rebounds and five assists. Jerami Grant and Terrence Ferguson also reached double figures in scoring to cap off the starting five. Both teams return to action on Saturday, with Houston traveling to face the San Antonio Spurs and Oklahoma City playing the Dallas Mavericks on the road as well.

The Oklahoma City Thunder defeated the Phoenix Suns, 118 - 101, at Chesapeake Energy Arena on Monday. It continues to, for the most part, be no Russell Westbrook no problem for the Thunder (8 - 5), as Monday's victory was their eighth in the last nine games. Paul George led the way once again in Westbrook's absence, scoring a game - high 32 points on 11 - of - 19 shooting from the field to go along with eight rebounds and six assists in 36 minutes. Dennis Schroder also continues to perform admirably in place of the superstar point guard, as he recorded 20 points, five rebounds, nine assists and four steals in 36 minutes, but he shot a pretty poor 6 - of - 19 from the field. The Thunder utilized the three - point line to their advantage Monday and it ended up being the difference in the game, as the team shot a scorching 13 - of - 27 (48 percent) from behind the arc. The Suns (2 - 11), on the other hand, were miserable with their outside shooting, going just 7 - of - 26 (27 percent) from three, which made is impossible for them to keep pace with the Thunder's hot shooting. T.J Warren led the way for Phoenix, scoring a team - high 21 points on 10 - of - 14 shooting, while Devin Booker was close behind with 19 points of his own in 37 minutes. Booker's performance wasn't nearly as efficient however, with the shooting guard going 7 - of - 18 from the field. The game may have been a lot uglier for the Suns had the team's bench not came through with the production they did, as the five reserves accounted for 38 points Monday night.

The Oklahoma City Thunder defeated the visiting New York Knicks, 128 - 103, at Chesapeake Arena on Wednesday. The Thunder got out to a great start at home, as they put together a 15 - 9 lead, just under four minutes into the game. The Thunder continued on the same trajectory through the quarter to take a 37 - 22 lead into the second. The Knicks picked it up in the second, but could not cut into the deficit much, as the Thunder held on to lead 65 - 49 at halftime. The Thunder did not look back, as they pushed their lead to 19, halfway through the first quarter and went on to cruise to their second straight win. Paul George led the Thunder with 35 points on 13 - of - 22 shooting, seven rebounds, five assists, two steals and one block, in 28 minutes. Steven Adams followed up with 19 points, six rebounds, five assists, two steals and one block, while Dennis Schroder tallied 15 points, 12 assists, four rebounds, one steal and one block. The Thunder shot 54 percent from the field, including 16 - of - 33 from deep. Meanwhile, Tim Hardaway Jr. led the Knicks with 20 points on 6 - of - 12 shooting, three rebounds, one assist and one block, in 24 minutes. Kevin Knox added 15 points, five rebounds, one assist and one steal, while Enes Kanter tallied 19 points on 8 - of - 11 shooting, five rebounds and one assist, in 22 minutes off the bench. The Knicks shot 44 percent from the field, including 7 - of - 26 from long range. The Knicks (4 - 11) will look to bounce back as they take on the Pelicans in New Orleans on Friday. The Thunder (9 - 5) take on the Suns in Phoenix on Saturday.

The Oklahoma City Thunder defeated the visiting Charlotte Hornets, 109 - 104, at Chesapeake Energy Arena on Friday evening. Both teams got out to a fiery start, as they combined for 64 points in the first quarter, with the Thunder taking a 33 - 31 lead into the second. The scoring continued in the second quarter, while the Thunder were able to maintain the advantage, outscoring the Hornets 29 - 26 in the quarter, to take a 62 - 57 lead into halftime. The Thunder came out strong in the third, but the Hornets managed to stay within range, as they were outscored by four points in the quarter and trailed by nine, entering the fourth. The Hornets kept up the fight in the fourth and managed to cut the deficit to just one point, just past the halfway mark in the quarter. Nonetheless, the Thunder managed to keep the edge and held on to earn their second straight win. Russell Westbrook led the Thunder with 30 points, 12 rebounds, eight assists and two steals, in 34 minutes. Dennis Schroder followed up with 23 points, five rebounds and one assist, while Paul George tallied 19 points, seven rebounds, six assists, two steals and one block, in 37 minutes. The Thunder shot 44 percent from the field, including 11 - of - 33 from long range. Meanwhile, Kemba Walker led the Hornets with 25 points, eight assists, two rebounds, two steals and one block, in 38 minutes. Jeremy Lamb followed up with 18 points, five rebounds, two assists, two steals and one block, while Frank Kaminsky chipped in 12 points, eight rebounds, two blocks, one assist and one steal, in 18 minutes off the bench. The Hornets (9 - 9) will look to bounce back as they take on the Hawks in Atlanta on Sunday. The Thunder (12 - 6) play host to the Nuggets on Saturday.

The Denver Nuggets defeated the host Oklahoma City Thunder, 105 - 98, at Chesapeake Energy Arena on Saturday evening. The Nuggets got out to a great start on the road, as they outscored the Thunder, 33 - 23, in the first quarter. The Nuggets kept up the intensity in the second and outscored the Thunder 30 - 19 in the quarter, to take a convincing, 63 - 42, lead by halftime. The Thunder picked it up in the third, but could not make a significant dent in the deficit, as they trailed, 79 - 66, entering the fourth. The Thunder continued their push in the fourth, as they cut the deficit to just seven points early in the quarter. The Nuggets did not slip up and maintained their edge. Despite a continued effort from the home team, the Nuggets hung on for their third straight win. Jamal Murray led Denver with 22 points, eight rebounds and eight assists, in 39 minutes. Nikola Jokic followed up with 16 points, five rebounds, five assists and one block, while Juancho Hernangomez tallied 15 points, eight rebounds, two steals and one block. The Nuggets shot 41 percent from the field, including 10 - of - 30 from long range. Meanwhile, Paul George led the Thunder with 24 points, 11 rebounds, three assists, three blocks and two steals, in 39 minutes. Russell Westbrook followed up with 16 points, 12 assists, 10 rebounds and one steal, while Steven Adams tallied 12 points, 14 rebounds and one steal, in 37 minutes. The Thunder shot 36 percent from the field. The Thunder (12 - 7) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Cavs on Wednesday. The Nuggets (13 - 7) play host to the Lakers on Tuesday.

The Oklahoma City Thunder defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers 100 - 83 at Chesapeake Energy Arena on Wednesday. Russell Westbrook notched a big triple - double which marked his 107th of his career, good for third on the all - time list and tied in good company with Hall of Fame point guard Jason Kidd. Westbrook finished with 23 points, 19 rebounds and 15 assists on 10 - of - 17 shooting. The Thunder (13 - 7) did not get off to a strong start and trailed early in the game, however, the Cavs could not keep pace with Westbrook and Paul George and proved to be heavily overmatched. George finished with 21 points and four blocks. The bright spot for Cleveland (4 - 16) in an otherwise bleak season so far was Colin Sexton as the rookie point guard scored 21 points on 9 - of - 20 shooting, to go with 10 rebounds and three assists. Sexton was matched up with Westbrook, who picked him apart defensively, regardless, the young bull has improved over his last five games. Jordan Clarkson notched 25 points in 32 minutes of action off the bench and the Cavs only played eight in their matchup. Kevin Love (toe) is still nursing his injury. Both teams play on Friday, as the Cavs visit the Boston Celtics, while the Thunder host the Atlanta Hawks.

The Oklahoma City Thunder defeated the visiting Atlanta Hawks, 124 - 109, at Chesapeake Energy Arena on Friday. While the first quarter was competitive, Oklahoma City dominated from there. In fact, they rode a 38 - 20 second quarter to victory, as Atlanta never got the game within a 10 - point margin in the second half. The shooting disparity was the difference, with the Thunder connecting on 52 percent from the field, 44 percent from three - point range and 93 percent from the free - throw line. The Hawks hit just 45 percent from the field, 31 percent from long range and 60 percent from the charity stripe. Rim protection was also critical, with Oklahoma City out - blocking Atlanta, 7 - 3. The Hawks (5 - 18) were led by John Collins, as he totaled 19 points and 11 rebounds. Tauren Prince amassed 15 points, three rebounds, two assists and two steals. Trae Young went just 4 - of - 15 from the field to accrue nine points, four rebounds and eight assists. Alex Len was huge off the bench, providing 19 points and five boards. The Thunder (14 - 7) got a near triple - double from Russell Westbrook, as he collected 23 points, nine rebounds and 10 assists. Alex Abrines hit seven three - pointers to finish with 21 points. Paul George tallied 20 points, five rebounds, three assists and two steals. Steven Adams scored just six points but still provided 13 points, three assists and three steals. Dennis Schroder hurt his old team, as he led the bench with 18 points, three rebounds, eight assists and two blocks. Nerlens Noel also played well off the bench, generating 14 points, seven rebounds, three steals and two blocks. Both teams are off until Monday when Atlanta plays host to the Golden State Warriors and Oklahoma City welcomes the Detroit Pistons to Chesapeake Energy Arena.

The Oklahoma City Thunder defeated the Utah Jazz, 122 - 113, at Chesapeake Energy Arena on Monday. The final score certainly indicates that the game was a lot closer than it actually was, as the Thunder (17 - 8) were in full control from start to finish en route to their fifth win in the last six games. After jumping out to an early lead, Oklahoma City never looked back and took a 24 - point lead into the fourth quarter. While the visiting Jazz (13 - 15) had a big final period and tried to make a push, they never had a legit chance to win Monday's game. Paul George's impressive stretch continued, as the swingman scored a game - high 31 points on 8 - of - 10 shooting from the field in just 30 minutes. Russell Westbrook struggled mightily from the field, going just 4 - of - 18 and scoring 12 points, but 11 rebounds and 10 assists gave the point guard yet another triple - double. Dennis Schroder, however, made up for Westbrook's struggles in a big way, coming off the bench to score 23 points in 30 minutes. As for the Jazz, this was their second straight loss as the team's up - and - down season continues. They had six different players score in double figures, but Donovan Mitchell scored just 19 points to lead Utah in scoring. Rudy Gobert added a double - double of 13 points and 14 rebounds, but for the most part, Utah's starters were a no - show Monday night. As a team, the Jazz shot a solid 51 percent from the field, but they couldn't get anything going from behind the arc, going just 8 - of - 29 from long range.

The Oklahoma City Thunder defeated the visiting Los Angeles Clippers, 110 - 104, at Chesapeake Energy Arena on Saturday. Oklahoma City led for over 40 minutes of this game, as a 34 - 24 fourth quarter in favor of Los Angeles is the only thing that made this scoreline look respectable.
