The Timberwolves will take to the road to visit Detroit on Thursday. Meanwhile, the Thunder next suit up on Friday in Portland.

The Minnesota Timberwolves defeated the visiting Washington Wizards in overtime, 135 - 130, at Target Center on Saturday. While Washington led for the majority of this game, it took an overtime session to determine a winner. In fact, this game stayed within a five - point margin for the final 15 minutes of regulation but Minnesota pulled away thanks to a 14 - 9 overtime session. Offensive rebounding was huge for Minnesota, as they outrebounded Washington, 19 - 10. Turnovers were also critical, with Washington committing 18 turnovers while forcing just nine from Minnesota. That allowed the Timberwolves to outscore the Wizards in points off turnovers, 22 - 10. The Wizards (27 - 39) got a near triple - double from Bradley Beal, as he tallied 36 points, 10 rebounds and nine assists. Trevor Ariza accrued 27 points, three rebounds and four assists. Bobby Portis amassed 21 points and 12 boards while Tomas Satoransky finished with nine points, three rebounds and 11 assists. The Timberwolves (31 - 35) were led by Karl-Anthony Towns, as he collected 40 points, 16 rebounds, two assists and two steals before departing because of a knee injury. Dario Saric totaled 13 points, six rebounds and three assists. Derrick Rose was huge off the bench, providing 29 points, three rebounds and three assists. Taj Gibson recorded a 15 - point, 13 - rebound double - double off the bench as well. Minnesota will return to action on Sunday, as they play host to the struggling New York Knicks. As for Washington, they welcome the Sacramento Kings to the nation's capital on Monday for their next outing.

The Minnesota Timberwolves defeated the visiting New York Knicks, 103 - 92, at Target Center on Sunday evening. Despite missing Andrew Wiggins (thigh) and Karl-Anthony Towns (knee), the Timberwolves rallied together for an impressive win. The contest got out to a competitive start, as the Timberwolves took a 23 - 22 lead after the first quarter. The Knicks made a run to take a lead early in the second, but the Timberwolves went on to outscore them by nine in the quarter, to push their lead to 10 by halftime. They carried the momentum into the third, where they pushed their lead to 15 by the halfway mark. The Knicks kept fighting, but Minnesota managed to hold a 15 - point lead at the start of the fourth. The Timberwolves stayed in control through the fourth, not letting the Knicks even within 10 points, as they cruised to their second straight win. Taj Gibson led the Timberwolves with 25 points, eight rebounds, two steals, a block and an assist, in 30 minutes. Jeff Teague also came up large, with 20 points, 10 assists, three rebounds, two blocks and a steal, while Keita Bates-Diop tallied 18 points, six rebounds, two steals, two blocks and one assist. The Timberwolves shot 45 percent from the field, including 9 - of - 30 from deep. Meanwhile, Damyean Dotson led the Knicks with 26 points, six rebounds, six assists and two steals, in 40 minutes. Dennis Smith Jr. finished with 13 points, four assists and two rebounds, while Alonzo Trier chipped in 15 points, two rebounds and two assists. The Knicks shot 43 percent from the field, including 10 - of - 25 from long range. The Knicks (13 - 54) will look to bounce back as they take on the Pacers in Indiana on Tuesday. The Timberwolves (32 - 35) head to Denver to take on the Nuggets on Tuesday.

The Golden State Warriors took down the Minnesota Timberwolves, 117 - 107, at Target Center on Tuesday evening. In what proved to be a quintessential Golden State win, Steph Curry scored 22 third - quarter points to elevate the Warriors (48 - 22) to victory. Curry's offensive outburst helped contribute to a barrage of three - pointers hit by the Warriors. Golden State finished with 19 makes from beyond the arc in the win. Minnesota (32 - 39), meanwhile, stayed competitive thanks to its tenacity on the glass. That was primarily fueled by star big man Karl-Anthony Towns, who delivered 26 points and 21 rebounds on the night. Curry finished with a team - high 36 points, including eight three - pointers. He was joined by a strong night from Klay Thompson, who poured in 28 points on 11 - of - 21 shooting. The Warriors were without star center DeMarcus Cousins, who was sidelined by a mild ankle injury. All five starters scored in double figures for Minnesota, but that was not enough to get the job done. The Timberwolves shot just 40 percent from the field and 9 - of - 36 from three - point range. Andrew Wiggins turned in a strong performance, though, finishing with 20 points, eight rebounds, and six assists. On Thursday, Golden State will host the Indiana Pacers while Minnesota will visit the Charlotte Hornets.

The Los Angeles Clippers defeated the Minnesota Timberwolves, 122 - 111, at Target Center on Tuesday evening. The Clippers (45 - 30) deployed one of the best strategies for winning on the road - - they got out to a sizable lead early. Los Angeles forged a 42 - 23 lead through the first 12 minutes and held a 75 - 55 halftime advantage. The Timberwolves (33 - 41) did manage to put a nine - point dent in their deficit overall during the second half, but that wasn't nearly enough to overtake Los Angeles. As their final point tally implies, the visitors shot extremely well, draining 54 percent of their attempts, including 50 percent from three - point range. Danilo Gallinari paced the Clippers with a 25 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included four assists and one steal. Lou Williams followed with 20 points, seven assists and four rebounds. Montrezl Harrell delivered 18 points, five rebounds, four assists and two blocks. Garrett Temple supplied 15 points, four rebounds, three assists and two steals. Patrick Beverley and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander contributed 11 and 10 points, respectively. Karl-Anthony Towns led the Timberwolves with a 24 - point, 13 - rebound double - double that also included three assists and two steals. Andrew Wiggins poured in 22 points and added three rebounds, three assists and two steals. Dario Saric furnished 18 points, five rebounds, one assist and one steal. Tyus Jones managed 13 points, eight assists and two rebounds. Josh Okogie and Jerryd Bayless managed nine points apiece. The Clippers remain on the road and next visit the Milwaukee Bucks on Thursday evening, while the Timberwolves remain home to tangle with the Golden State Warriors on Friday night.

The Minnesota Timberwolves defeated the visiting Golden State Warriors in overtime 131 - 130, at Target Center on Friday. This game was full of swings, as it wasn't decided until the final shot. In fact, Stephen Curry hit a game - tying three with 0 seconds left in OT but they fouled Minnesota on the inbound in the following possession. That allowed Karl-Anthony Towns to nail the game - winning free - throw, who then missed the second free - throw intentionally to run out the clock. There were nine ties and 12 lead changes in total, as Minnesota never trailed in the OT. Rebounding was the clear - cut difference, with the Timberwolves outrebounding the Warriors, 59 - 45. Their bench also came up big, outscoring Golden State's bench, 52 - 25. The Warriors (51 - 24) were led by Stephen Curry, as he went 11 - of - 19 from long range to tally 37 points, three rebounds, five assists and two steals. Kevin Durant finished with 23 points, 12 rebounds, seven assists and two blocks. Klay Thompson amassed 20 points, two rebounds and five assists. DeMarcus Cousins accrued 16 points and nine boards. The Timberwolves (34 - 41) were led by Andrew Wiggins, as he accumulated 24 points, nine rebounds and three assists. Josh Okogie amassed 21 points, five rebounds and four steals. Karl-Anthony Towns accumulated 15 points, 13 rebounds and seven assists. Gorgui Dieng was huge off the bench, providing 14 points and 10 boards. Minnesota suits up again on Saturday, as they play host to the Philadelphia 76ers. As for Golden State, they return to action on Sunday against the Charlotte Hornets.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the host Minnesota Timberwolves, 118 - 109, at Target Center on Saturday evening. The Sixers got out to a great start on the road, as they took a 38 - 20 lead after one quarter. The 76ers stayed control through the second, but the Timberwolves managed to trim it to a 13 - point deficit by halftime. The Sixers stayed on top through third the Timberwolves trimmed it to an 11 - point game entering the fourth. They kept pushing and cut it to a three - point game, just three minutes into the quarter. However, the Sixers regained control and held on for their second straight win. Tobias Harris led the 76ers with 25 points, seven rebounds and four assists, in 39 minutes. Ben Simmons added 20 points, 11 rebounds, nine assists, two steals and a block, while Jimmy Butler finished with 12 points, 13 rebounds, five assists and two steals. The 76ers shot 47 percent from the field, including 15 - of - 31 from long range. Andrew Wiggins led the Timberwolves with 24 points, six rebounds, five assists and two blocks, in 36 minutes. Karl-Anthony Towns followed up with 21 points, seven rebounds, two assists and a block, while Gorgui Dieng chipped in 13 points and three rebounds. The Timberwolves shot 45 percent from the field, including 11 - of - 26 from deep. The Timberwolves (34 - 42) play host to the Trail Blazers on Monday. The 76ers (49 - 27) take on the Mavericks in Dallas on Monday.

The Portland Trail Blazers defeated the Minnesota Timberwolves, 132 - 122, at Target Center on Monday night. The Trail Blazers (49 - 28) got the early jump on the hometown Timberwolves (34 - 43), forging a 38 - 23 lead through one quarter. However, Minnesota would impressively bounce back in the middle periods, outscoring Portland by a 77 - 59 margin in the second and third quarters. Holding a slim three - point advantage to start the fourth, the T-Wolves saw the Blazers turn the tables and go on a 27 - 14 run over the first 7; 32 of the period to build up enough cushion for the victory. As the final score implies, offense carried the night, with Portland draining 55 percent of its attempts, including 50 percent from distance, and Minnesota posting a 49 percent success rate from the floor. Rodney Hood drew the start and led the way for the Trail Blazers with 21 points, adding four rebounds, one assist and two steals. Enes Kanter generated a 20 - point, 11 - rebound double - double that also included one assist and five blocks. Seth Curry poured in 19 points. Damian Lillard posted a 15 - point, 12 - assist double - double that also included five rebounds. Evan Turner generated a 13 - point, 11 - rebound, 10 - assist triple - double that also included one steal. Jake Layman totaled 11 points. Andrew Wiggins paced the Timberwolves with 21 points, complementing them with seven rebounds, four assists and one steal. Gorgui Dieng led the bench with 18 points and also posted four rebounds, two assists, one steal and one block. Karl-Anthony Towns finished with 17 points, 12 rebounds, four assists and two blocks. Tyus Jones contributed a 14 - point, 10 - assist double - double that also included three rebounds and three steals. Dario Saric collected 13 points, two rebounds and two assists. The Trail Blazers head back home to take on the Memphis Grizzlies on Wednesday night, while the Timberwolves pay a visit to the Dallas Mavericks on Wednesday evening as well.

The Minnesota Timberwolves defeated the Miami Heat, 111 - 109, at Target Center on Friday night The Timberwolves (36 - 43) knew they'd have the opportunity to play spoiler against the Heat (38 - 41), which were in desperate need of a win to have an opportunity to vault back into the eighth seed they'd recently relinquished. Miami appeared to have a solid chance of securing a crucial victory after taking a 69 - 61 halftime lead, but they apparently left their offense in the locker room coming out of intermission. Minnesota would hold the visitors to just 40 second - half points, and they clinched the win when Dwyane Wade missed a 25 - foot three - point jumper at the buzzer. Wade paced the Heat with 24 points, adding three rebounds, three assists and one steal. Dion Waiters turned in 22 points. Goran Dragic and James Johnson generated matching 15 - point tallies, with Dragic also dishing out nine assists, pulling down seven rebounds and recording four steals. Justise Winslow generated 13 points, seven rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block. Dario Saric and Gorgui Dieng led the Timberwolves with 19 points apiece. Andrew Wiggins poured in 18 points, two rebounds, one assist and one steal. Karl-Anthony Towns contributed a 13 - point, 12 - rebound double - double that also included four assists and one steal, although he also committed a game - high 11 turnovers. Tyus Jones filled out the stat sheet with 12 points, six rebounds, four assists and two steals. The Heat next visit the Toronto Raptors on Sunday afternoon, while the Timberwolves remain home to face the Oklahoma City Thunder on Sunday afternoon as well.

The Oklahoma City Thunder defeated the Minnesota Timberwolves, 132 - 126, at Target Center on Sunday afternoon. The Thunder (47 - 33) came into the game looking to build some positive momentum ahead of the postseason after a recent extended stretch of sub - par play. OKC got off to a strong start in that regard, racking up 38 first - quarter points. However, the Timberwolves (36 - 44) did a good job keeping pace and were only down by two at halftime. Minnesota continued coming on in the third, outscoring the visitors by a 37 - 33 margin in the third to carry a slim two - point advantage into the final period. The Thunder then found their stride again, opening the fourth quarter on a 14 - 2 run over the first 3:57 to regain a lead they wouldn't relinquish. Russell Westbrook and Paul George co - led the Thunder with 27 points, with Westbrook also dishing out 15 assists and pulling down 10 rebounds. George added seven rebounds, six dimes and three steals. Dennis Schroder followed with 21 points, two rebounds, one assist and one steal. Jerami Grant produced 15 points, five boards and two blocks. Markieff Morris poured in 14 points and added six boards. Terrance Ferguson netted 11 points, four rebounds and two assists. Karl-Anthony Towns paced the Timberwolves with 35 points, adding seven rebounds, two assists, two steals and one block. Andrew Wiggins furnished 24 points, five boards, four assists and two steals. Dario Saric managed 23 points, three rebounds, one assist and one block. Tyus Jones generated a 10 - point, 13 - assist double - double that also included five rebounds. Gorgui Dieng matched Jones' scoring total and posted four rebounds. The Thunder head back home to tangle with the Houston Rockets on Tuesday night, while the Timberwolves remain home to take on the Toronto Raptors on Tuesday evening as well.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the host Minnesota Timberwolves, 120 - 100, at Target Center on Tuesday. While there were seven lead changes in the first 15 minutes, Toronto dominated after that. In fact, the Raptors rode a 43 - 19 second quarter to victory, holding a double - digit lead for the entirety of the second half. Defensive rebounding was key for Toronto, as they won that battle, 47 - 30. The Raptors ended up shooting 52 percent from the field and 43 percent from three - point range while holding the Timberwolves to 42 percent from the field and 31 percent from long range. The Raptors (58 - 24) were led by Kawhi Leonard, as he tallied 20 points and six rebounds. Fred VanVleet got another start and amassed 16 points, two rebounds, four assists and three steals. Chris Boucher was huge off the bench, providing 15 points, 13 rebounds, two assists and two blocks. Pascal Siakam accrued 10 points, four rebounds and two assists. The Timberwolves (36 - 45) were led by Gorgui Dieng, as he tallied 16 points, seven rebounds and five assists. Andrew Wiggins finished with 16 points, threee rebounds, three assists and two blocks. Dario Saric totaled 15 points and nine boards while Tyus Jones generated 11 points and 10 assists. No other player reached double figures in scoring. While that marked the season finale for the Raptors, the Timberwolves have to play again on Wednesday when they travel to face the Denver Nuggets.

The Portland Trail Blazers defeated the Los Angeles Lakers, 128 - 119, at Moda Center on Thursday evening. All eyes were on LeBron James in Thursday's season opener, as the 33 - year - old superstar made his debut in a Lakers uniform against the Trail Blazers. Perhaps unsurprisingly, James did not disappoint, as he delivered 26 points and 12 rebounds to lead his team. However, the big performance was not enough to prevent Damian Lillard and the Trail Blazers from spoiling his first game as a Laker. Lillard's 28 points helped earn Portland a win in its first game of the season. The Trail Blazers (10) overcame struggles to move the ball, scoring 128 points on only 21 assists. Portland maximized its offensive output thanks to strong shooting, knocking down 13 three - pointers and going 27 - of - 29 at the free - throw line. The Blazers also found offense from an unlikely source, as bench guard Nik Stauskas scored 24 points in only 27 minutes in his first game of the season. The Lakers (0 - 1) struggled to match Portland's offensive output and tenacity on the glass. LA grabbed only eight offensive rebounds, as opposed to 14 for Portland. The Lakers did see strong facilitation from veteran point guard Rajon Rondo, who scored 13 points and dished out 11 assists. Lost in the mix was last year's second overall pick Lonzo Ball, who scored just seven points on 2 - of - 7 shooting in 19 minutes off the bench. Los Angeles has another tough test up next, as it will play host to the Houston Rockets on Friday night. The Trail Blazers, meanwhile, will host the San Antonio Spurs.

The Portland Trail Blazers defeated the San Antonio Spurs, 121 - 108, at Moda Center on Saturday evening. The hard - fought contest fittingly began with a 22 - 22 deadlock over the first 12 minutes. However, the Trail Blazers (20) outscored the Spurs (1 - 1) by a 75 - 60 margin over the second and third quarters to gain distance, and they then held serve over the final 12 minutes to post the double - digit victory. Shooting was a key to the win, with Portland draining an impressive 54 percent of their attempts and San Antonio managing a 42 percent success rate from the field. As customary, a significant portion of the Blazers offense flowed through their backcourt, as the star duo of Damian Lillard and C.J. McCollum combining for 53 points on identical 9 - for - 15 shooting efforts. DeMar DeRozan paced the Spurs with 28 points, a total he supplemented with nine assists, three rebounds and two steals. Bryn Forbes was a distant second with 17 points and added three assists and two rebounds. LaMarcus Aldridge and Rudy Gay contributed matching 12 - point tallies, with the veteran duo also hauling in eight and seven rebounds, respectively. Davis Bertans (11 points) and Paul Gasol (10 points) were productive off the bench. Lillard's 29 points led the Trail Blazers, and he also contributed nine assists and two rebounds. McCollum followed with 24 points and a pair of assists and rebounds apiece. Jusuf Nurkic offered 12 points, eight rebounds, two assists, one steal and one block. Al-Farouq Aminu went for 10 points, six rebounds, one assist and one block. Zach Collins led the bench with 11 points. The Spurs remain on their West Coast swing and next face the Lakers on Monday night, while the Trail Blazers remain home and tangle with the Washington Wizards on Monday evening as well.

The Washington Wizards defeated the host Portland Trail Blazers, 125 - 124, at Moda Center on Monday evening. The game started out close, and stayed that way until it was tied up at 62 at halftime. Both teams came out ice cold in the third quarter, where the Wizards outscored the Trail Blazers by one, to take a, 78 - 77, lead into the final frame. The close contest continued right down to the wire, where after a series of lead changes and ties, it stood tied at 108, with 19 seconds remaining. Things began to get crazy as the Blazers drained a three to go up 111 - 108, only to have the Wizards answer with a three of their own, sending the game to overtime, tied at 111. Insanity ensued in overtime, as the teams once again matched shot, for shot, until the Wizards hit a three to lead 125 - 121, with 11 seconds left. The Blazers still hit another three to make it a one - point game, and after two missed free throws by John Wall, had a chance for the win, but came up short. This marks the first win of the season for the Wizards and the first lost for the Trail Blazers. Markieff Morris led the Wizards with 28 points, nine rebounds, one steal, one assist and one block, in 25 minutes. Bradley Beal tallied 25 points, eight rebounds, six assists and one block, while John Wall finished with 16 points, 10 assists, four rebounds, one steal and one block. The Wizards shot 42 percent from the field, including 15 - of - 27 from deep. Meanwhile, Damian Lillard was the high - point man for the Trail Blazers with 29 points, along with eight rebounds, eight assists and one steal, in 41 minutes. Jusuf Nurkic had a big night with 22 points, 18 rebounds, two assists and two steals, while Al-Farouq Aminu finished with 16 points, 16 rebounds, one steal and one block. The Blazers shot 40 percent from the field, including 11 - of - 39 from long range. The Trail Blazers (2 - 1) will look to bounce back as they take on the Magic in Orlando on Thursday. The Wizards (1 - 2) take on the Warriors on Wednesday.

The Portland Trail Blazers defeated the New Orleans Pelicans, 132 - 119, at Moda Center on Thursday. A well - rested Trail Blazers team managed to take advantage of a tired and banged up Pelicans squad Thursday, as the visiting team was playing its fifth game in seven nights and was without superstar Anthony Davis (elbow). Portland did, however, let the undermanned Pelicans hang around for three quarters before New Orleans grew too tired to keep pace over the last 12 minutes. Damian Lillard led the way for the Blazers, scoring a team - high 26 points to go along with seven rebounds and six assists in 31 minutes, while big man Jusuf Nurkic provided 20 points and nine rebounds of his own in just 28 minutes. The surprise performance of the night came from Al-Farouq Aminu, who posted a double - double of 17 points and 10 rebounds in 33 minutes. The driving force behind Portland's victory Thursday night was their terrific shooting from long range, as they went 18 - of - 35 (51 percent) from behind the arc. As for the Pelicans, they needed someone to step up in the absence of Anthony Davis, and Julius Randle was happy to do so, pouring in a game - high 29 points on 9 - of - 16 shooting in just 26 minutes off the bench. Randle, however, did most of his damage in the first half before eventually running out of gas down the stretch. Nikola Mirotic struggled shooting from the field, going 1 - of - 6 from behind the arc and 6 - of - 20 overall, but he still finished with yet another double - double of 18 points and 13 rebounds. The Pelicans as a team struggled mightily shooting the basketball, as they shot a miserable 8 - of - 29 (28 percent) from three and were just unable to keep pace with the Blazers on Thursday.

The Los Angeles Lakers defeated the Portland Trail Blazers, 114 - 110, at Moda Center on Saturday night. The Trail Blazers (6 - 3) came into the contest on an impressive run, having rattled off four straight wins, with three of those having come on the road. Portland was a slight favorite on their home floor against the inconsistent Lakers (4 - 5), yet Los Angeles essentially matched them basket for basket in the first half. The Blazers came out of the halftime locker room holding on to a slim one - point lead, but the visitors would flip the game on its proverbial head in the third period by doubling up their hosts, 32 - 16. That allowed them to withstand a 25 - 15 run by Portland over the final 6:53. The Lakers primarily got it done with pinpoint accuracy from the field, shooting 52 percent while limiting the Blazers to a 42 percent success rate. LeBron James led the way for the Lakers with 28 points and added seven assists, five rebounds and two blocks. Rajon Rondo followed with 17 points, 10 rebounds, six assists and three steals. JaVale McGee supplied 12 points, nine rebounds, one assist, six blocks and one steal. Kyle Kuzma matched McGee's scoring total and also registered six boards and a block. Josh Hart posted 11 points. Damian Lillard and C.J. McCollum paced the Blazers with matching 30 - point efforts. Lillard added four rebounds, four assists and three steals, while McCollum hauled in five boards and dished out four assists. Jusuf Nurkic generated a 14 - point, 13 - rebound double - double that also included two assists, two blocks and one steal. Evan Turner managed 11 points, three rebounds and three assists. Zach Collins added 10 points off the second unit. The Lakers head home and take on the Toronto Raptors in a Sunday night showdown, while the Trail Blazers remain home to face the Minnesota Timberwolves on Sunday evening as well.

The Portland Trail Blazers defeated the visiting Minnesota Timberwolves, 111 - 81, at Moda Center on Sunday. This was as about lopsided as it gets in the NBA, as Portland won all four individual quarters. They did most of their damage in the middle quarters, outscoring Minnesota, 62 - 37. The Trail Blazers played their best defense of the season, holding the Timberwolves to 31 percent from the field and 23 percent from three - point range. Rebounding was also decisive, with Portland outrebounding Minnesota, 66 - 38. The Trail Blazers took advantage of a friendly whistle, connecting on 28 - of - 32 from the free - throw line. The Timberwolves (4 - 6) had to play this game without Jimmy Butler (rest) and his ordeal really seems to be hurting this team. Karl-Anthony Towns did all he could, as he led the T'Wolves with 23 points, five rebounds and three assists. Andrew Wiggins was the only other player in double figures, as he amassed 17 points and three steals. The Trail Blazers (7 - 3) got a double - double out of Jusuf Nurkic, as he tallied 19 points, 12 rebounds and two assists on 8 - of - 11 shooting. Damian Lillard accrued 18 points, five rebounds and five assists. C.J. McCollum totaled 16 points, three boards and two steals. Meyers Leonard led the bench with 15 points, 12 rebounds and two assists. Minnesota will have to play again on Monday, as they travel to face the Los Angeles Clippers. As for Portland, they play host to the Milwaukee Bucks on Tuesday for their next outing.

The Portland Trail Blazers defeated the visiting Milwaukee Bucks, 118 - 103, at Moda Center on Tuesday evening. The Trail Blazers got out to a good start and held the lead early on. The Bucks tied it up at 21 late in the first quarter, but Portland squeezed back in front, to take a 33 - 31 lead into the second. The Trail Blazers kept the momentum, as they pushed their lead to 11, halfway through the quarter, and hung on to a 57 - 51 advantage by halftime. The home team brought the same energy in the third, as the Trail Blazers pushed their lead back to double digits, outscoring the Bucks, 34 - 26, in the quarter, to take a 91 - 77 lead into the fourth. The Bucks only managed to cut the deficit to single digits a couple of times in the final quarter, as the Trail Blazers stayed comfortably ahead, en route to their second win in a row. C.J. McCollum was on fire for Portland, as he led the way with 40 points on 17 - of - 26 shooting, six assists, five rebounds and four steals, in 35 minutes. Evan Turner was good off the bench, with 16 points, 11 rebounds, four assists and one steal, in 31 minutes of action. Damian Lillard chipped in 13 points, six rebounds, three assists and one block. The Trail Blazers shot 53 percent from the field, including 17 - of - 43 from long range. Meanwhile, Giannis Antetokounmpo led the Bucks with 23 points, nine rebounds, and six assists, in 37 minutes. Khris Middleton and Brook Lopez added 22 points each, while Tony Snell chipped in eight points off the bench. The Bucks shot 44 percent from the field, including 16 - of - 42 from long range. The Bucks (8 - 2) will look to bounce back as they take on the Warriors in Golden State on Thursday. The Trail Blazers (8 - 3) play host to the Clippers on Thursday.

The Portland Trail Blazers defeated the Los Angeles Clippers, 116 - 105, at Moda Center on Thursday. The Trail Blazers (9 - 3) continue to play great basketball, as they have now won five of their last six games. As it typically does, Thursday's win started with the production from the team's backcourt. Damian Lillard led the way for the home team, scoring a game - high 25 points, but he struggled a bit from the field, shooting just 11 - of - 25. Additionally, in what may be the most surprising stat of the night, Lillard did not attempt a single free throw in in 35 minutes of play. C.J. McCollum wasn't too far behind Lillard, scoring 23 points and grabbing seven rebounds in 35 minutes of his own. Jusuf Nurkic had another efficient night, but he fell one rebound short of a double - double with 16 points and nine boards in just 23 minutes. As a team, while Portland did not shoot particularly well from the field (41 percent), the team made the most of its trips to the charity stripe, hitting 26 - of - 28 free throws Thursday night. As for the Clippers (6 - 5), their loss put an end to a two - game winning streak. The main difference for Los Angeles in the loss was their inability to close out defensive possessions, as they allowed the Trail Blazers to get 14 offensive rebounds and they took eight more shots as a result. Lou Williams and Danilo Gallinari led the way for the Clippers on Thursday as each dropped 20 points. It was a rough night shooting the ball for Tobias Harris, who has emerged as the team's No. 1 option on offense this season, but he still managed to finish with a double - double of 15 points and 11 rebounds in 37 minutes. Rookie Shai Gilgeous-Alexander continues to impress in his first NBA season, scoring 19 points in 35 minutes as the starting point guard.

The Portland Trail Blazers defeated the visiting Boston Celtics, 100 - 94, at Moda Center on Sunday evening. The Trail Blazers got out to a great start at home, with a quick 50 lead, which helped them maintain the advantage through the whole quarter, as they built a 10 - point lead, before settling on a, 26 - 21, lead heading into the second. The Blazers continued their press into the second, where they outscored the Celtics 28 - 16 in the quarter, to take a 54 - 37 lead into halftime. The Celtics woke up a bit in the third, as they cut the deficit to nine halfway through the quarter. However, the Trail Blazers did not lose focus and pushed the lead back to 13 by the end of the quarter. The Celtics were not done yet, as they flew out of the gates to start the fourth and cut the deficit to two points. Nonetheless, the Trail Blazers managed to keep the edge, even as the Celtics made it a one - point game with 2:55 to go, Portland answered with a three by Al-Farouq Aminu. Aminu hit one more three in the clutch to help seal the fourth straight win for the Trail Blazers. Damian Lillard led the Trail Blazers with 19 points, 12 assists and five rebounds, in 35 minutes. Jusuf Nurkic followed up with 18 points, 17 rebounds and three assists, in 27 minutes. C.J. McCollum chipped in 14 points, two rebounds, one assist and one block, in 34 minutes. The Blazers shot 45 percent from the field, including 14 - of - 36 from long range. Meanwhile, Jayson Tatum led the Celtics with 27 points, eight rebounds and two blocks, in 34 minutes. Kyrie Irving followed up with 21 points, six assists, five steals and two rebounds, in 32 minutes. The Celtics (7 - 6) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Bulls on Wednesday. The Trail Blazers (10 - 3) take on the Lakers in Los Angeles on Wednesday.

The Los Angeles Clippers defeated the host Portland Trail Blazers, 104 - 100, in a down - to - the - wire thriller at Moda Center on Sunday evening. It was a back - and - forth game between two of the Western Conference's top teams. Portland (12 - 8) got off to a hot start, thanks in large part to a strong outing from All-Star point guard Damian Lillard. Lillard had six points in the final 90 seconds of the first half, helping his team establish a strong lead. While the Blazers led by as much as 15 early in the third quarter, a second half surge from the Clippers (13 - 6) made the game more competitive. LA outscored Portland 38 - 16 in the third quarter, taking a nine - point lead heading into the fourth. The Blazers fought their way back, though, and with 30 seconds remaining on the clock, LA led by only two points. Portland allowed LA to burn through the shot clock on its final possession, which ended in a missed jumper from Lou Williams. Miami, meanwhile, will continue its West Coast road trip with a visit to Sacramento on Friday.

The Portland Trail Blazers took down the San Antonio Spurs, 127 - 118, at Moda Center on Thursday evening. The Trail Blazers (33 - 21) staved off a valiant comeback effort by San Antonio (32 - 25) late in the second half. Portland seemed to be cruising to an easy victory as it took a 21 - point lead in the third quarter. The Spurs, however, clawed back, thanks in large part to DeMar DeRozan's 14 third - quarter points. San Antonio cut the deficit to just three points early in the fourth quarter, but the Blazers recaptured their lead with a game - clinching 15 - 4 run. C.J. McCollum was the driving force behind Portland's strong offense. He led the team with 30 points and hit seven three - pointers in the victory. Damian Lillard, meanwhile, had 24 points and nine assists while also demonstrating unusual energy on the defensive end. Lillard finished with five steals. DeRozan led all scorers with 35 points. He dished out six assists on top of his scoring, and also tallied six rebounds. However, his strong play was not enough to lead his team to a win. The Spurs allowed Portland to shoot over 55 percent and forced only seven turnovers on the night. The Spurs will hope to turn things around as they visit Utah on Saturday. The Trail Blazers, meanwhile, will take to the road with a trip to Dallas on Sunday.

The Portland Trail Blazers defeated the Golden State Warriors, 129 - 107, on Thursday at Moda Center. It was a tight game through three quarters of Thursday's contest between two of the best teams in the Western Conference, with the visiting Warriors (41 - 16) holding a narrow one - point lead over the Trail Blazers (34 - 23) after the first 36 minutes. The final quarter, however, was a much different story, as the away team slowly started to unravel while Portland poured it on. Neither Kevin Durant nor Stephen Curry scored a single point for Golden State in the fourth quarter, while Damian Lillard and the Trail Blazers lit a torch on offense, outscoring the Warriors 35 - 12 over the final 12 minutes, which included a 19 - 4 run to end the game. Lillard finished with a team - high 29 points on 6 - of - 8 shooting from behind the arc while seven other Trail Blazer players managed to reach double figures as the team hit 16 threes on the night (shooting 43 percent). The biggest key for Portland, however, was that the team didn't beat itself, committing just four turnovers to its 24 assists on the night. Meanwhile, Durant and Curry, despite going scoreless in the fourth, still managed to each finish with a game - high 32 points. However, they failed to get any support from their teammates, with no one else scoring in double figures. Klay Thompson had a miserable night shooting the basketball, going 2 - of - 16 from the field and scoring just nine points to go along with eight assists. The Warriors committed just eight turnovers themselves, but shot a fairly poor, by their standards at least, 40 percent from the field.

The Oklahoma City Thunder took down the Portland Trail Blazers, 129 - 121, in an overtime thriller at Moda Center on Thursday. Portland (39 - 26) and OKC (40 - 25) entered the game tied for third in the Western Conference, making it a key game for both teams. Thursday's matchup lived up to its potential with a wild overtime finish. Regulation finished in memorable fashion, with Portland narrowly succeeding in forcing OT. Oklahoma City took the lead when, with only 13 seconds left, Terrance Ferguson scored on a put - back layup after a collision between Paul George and Jusuf Nurkic. Tensions began to flare after the referees declined to review the incident. With tempers still running high, Nurkic drew a foul with 4 seconds remaining in regulation, but immediately picked up a technical foul after another dust - up with George. The tech was his second of the game, leading to an ejection. With Nurkic unable to shoot his free - throws, the Thunder elected to have Portland's Skal Labissiere take the shots in his stead. Labissiere missed both shots, but Markieff Morris committed a loose ball foul that sent Al-Faroq Aminu to the line to tie the game and send it to overtime. Overtime, though, proved to be less exhilarating as the Thunder quickly began to run away with the game. Russell Westbrook scored eight of the team's overtime points, including three on free - throws. OKC was able to exploit Nurkic's absence and attack the rim with success in OT. Westbrook finished with a team - high 37 points. Fellow All-Star Paul George also had a big contribution, scoring 32 points while grabbing 14 rebounds. For Portland, star point guard Damian Lillard delivered a season - high 51 points. Lillard was wildly efficient, shooting 15 - of - 28 from the field and 18 - of - 20 at the free - throw line. However, it was not enough to pick up the win, as the Trail Blazers shot just 39 percent overall from the field en route to the late - season loss. The Thunder will visit Los Angeles to take on the Clippers on Friday, while Portland will play host to the Phoenix Suns on Saturday.

The Portland Trail Blazers defeated the visiting Phoenix Suns, 127 - 120, at Moda Center on Saturday evening. The contest got out to a competitive start, with the Suns leading for most of the first quarter, before the Trail Blazers took a one - point advantage heading into the second. The Trail Blazers went off in the second quarter, outscoring the visitors, 42 - 24, in the quarter, to take a 66 - 47 lead by halftime. The Trail Blazers kept their foot on the gas through the third, as they maintained a near 20 - point advantage for the entire quarter, and took a 102 - 77 lead into the final frame. However, the Suns were not done yet, as they made a massive rally through the fourth, outscoring the Blazers 43 - 25 in the quarter to give them a good scare. Despite the strong push from the Suns, the Trail Blazers managed to hold the advantage and end a two - game losing streak. This marks the end of a three - game winning streak for the Suns. C.J. McCollum led Portland with 26 points, four assists, three rebounds, one steal and one block, in 30 minutes. Seth Curry followed up with 22 points, two rebounds and one steal, in 21 minutes off the bench, while Damian Lillard added 18 points, nine assists and two rebounds. The Trail Blazers shot 50 percent from the field, including 13 - of - 29 from long range. Meanwhile, Devin Booker led the Suns with 23 points, five assists, two rebounds and two steals, in 30 minutes. Deandre Ayton followed up with 21 points, eight rebounds and one assist, while Kelly Oubre Jr. added 17 points, seven rebounds, two steals, a block and an assist. The Suns shot 42 percent from the field, including 9 - of - 27 from deep. The Suns (15 - 52) will be right back in action, as they look to bounce back in Golden State on Sunday, where they take on the Warriors. The Trail Blazers (40 - 26) take on the Clippers in L.A. on Tuesday.

The host Portland Trail Blazers took down the Indiana Pacers, 106 - 98, at Moda Center on Monday evening. After an early nine - point lead put Indiana (44 - 27) in the driver's seat, Portland (43 - 27) answered back with a big run to end the first half. The Trail Blazers finished the second quarter on a 90 run that included two three - pointers from Damian Lillard. Portland carried that same energy into the second half, opening up a 16 - point lead by the end of the third quarter. Despite Indiana's notoriously stringent defense, the Blazers found success shooting the ball offensively. Portland finished the game shooting 13 - of - 32 from beyond the arc. Lillard headlined the win with 30 points and a season - high 15 assists. His presence was also felt on the defensive end, where he tallied three steals. As a team, Portland saw six double - digit scoring performances, including two off the bench from Seth Curry and Rodney Hood. On the Pacers' side, big man Myles Turner delivered a memorable night. Turner led the team with 28 points while also grabbing a team - best 10 boards. Five of those rebounds came on the offensive end. Forward Doug McDermott impressed as well, delivering 14 points off the bench. The Pacers will travel to Los Angeles for the second half of a back - to - back on Tuesday. Portland, meanwhile, will host the Dallas Mavericks this Wednesday.

The Portland Trail Blazers took down the Dallas Mavericks, 126 - 118, at Moda Center on Wednesday. The Trail Blazers (44 - 27) set the tone early with a 130 run in the first quarter to take a double - digit lead. Dallas (28 - 43) rallied back in the second to take the lead after a series of buckets by rookie guard Luka Doncic. However, Portland was able to regain control by the end of the first half, entering the break with a 13 - point advantage. It was smooth sailing for the Trail Blazers from there, as the team shot 50 percent from the field and knocked down 16 three - pointers on the night. Damian Lillard led the way with 33 points and 12 assists for the Blazers. The big night comes on the heels of a season - high 15 - assist performance against Indiana earlier in the week. Portland also capitalized on strong bench play from Seth Curry, who poured in 20 points to head up the second unit. The win marked Portland's fifth in its last six games. Doncic was Dallas's leading scorer with 24 points. He shot an efficient 8 - of - 16 from the floor and 7 - of - 7 at the free - throw line. Justin Jackson also impressed for the Mavs, finishing with 21 points off the bench. Neither performance was enough, though, as the Mavericks were sunk by their middling 33 percent three - point shooting night. The Mavericks will visit Sacramento on Thursday, while Portland will remain at home to take on the Detroit Pistons on Saturday.

The Portland Trail Blazers defeated the Detroit Pistons, 117 - 112, at Moda Center on Saturday evening. The contest got out to a competitive start as the Pistons and Trail Blazers traded the lead through the first quarter, with the Blazers taking a 32 - 28 lead into the second. The Trail Blazers pushed their lead to 12 late in the second, before the Pistons made a run to cut it to a three - point game by halftime. The Blazers came out strong in the third, but the Pistons stayed with it and managed to take a lead late in the quarter, carry a three - point lead into the fourth. The Pistons kept the momentum and led 108 - 103, with 4:28 left in the game. However, the home team caught fire at the right time, outscoring the visitors by 10 the rest of the way, to secure their third straight win. Damian Lillard led the Trail Blazers with 28 points, nine assists and six rebounds, in 37 minutes. Al-Farouq Aminu followed up with 22 points, seven rebounds, one assist and one steal, while Jusuf Nurkic added 15 points, six rebounds, three assists and two blocks. The Trail Blazers shot 54 percent from the field, including 11 - of - 26 from long range. Meanwhile, Blake Griffin led the Pistons with 27 points, six assists, three rebounds and one steal, in 35 minutes. Reggie Jackson followed up with 24 points, two rebounds, an assist and a steal, while Andre Drummond added 19 points, 11 rebounds, an assist, a steal and a block. The Pistons shot 50 percent from the field, including 14 - of - 34 from long range. The Pistons (37 - 35) will look to bounce back as they take on the Warriors on Sunday. The Trail Blazers (45 - 27) play host to the Nets on Monday.

The Portland Trail Blazers took down the Brooklyn Nets, 148 - 144, in double overtime at Moda Center on Monday evening. Portland's (46 - 27) dramatic win was overshadowed by a gruesome injury to star big man Jusuf Nurkic in double overtime. Nurkic went down with a serious lower leg injury with just over two minutes remaining in the period. He was carted off by Portland's medical staff. Nurkic exited the game with a team - high 32 points, 16 rebounds, and four blocks. Despite the horrific injury, the Trail Blazers were able to pull out the tough win. Portland had the chance to go up with 4 seconds remaining in regulation after the Nets' (38 - 37) D'Angelo Russell committed a turnover that led to Seth Curry drawing a foul on the other end. However, Curry went just 1 - of - 2 on his pair of free - throws to force the first overtime. After a back - and - forth throughout the first OT, Portland saw five points from Rodney Hood to help pull ahead and earn the win. On top of Nurkic's strong performance, Damian Lillard had 31 points for the Trail Blazers. Curry added another 20 off the bench for Portland, while Enes Kanter notched a 12 - point, 10 - rebound double - double. For Brooklyn, Russell had a team - high 39 points to go with nine rebounds and eight assists. Caris LeVert had 16 points and seven assists off the bench, while Spencer Dinwiddie added another 22. Next on the agenda for the Trail Blazers is a trip to Chicago on Wednesday. Brooklyn, meanwhile, will visit Philadelphia on Thursday.

The Portland Trail Blazers took down the Memphis Grizzlies, 116 - 89, at Moda Center on Wednesday evening. Portland (50 - 28) delivered a dominant third quarter to secure its 50th win of the season. The Trail Blazers held Memphis (31 - 47) to only 10 points in the third, holding the team to under 35 percent shooting in the second half. Portland coupled its strong defensive play with a well - rounded offensive attack, shooting over 51 percent from the field and seeing five double - digit scoring performances. The win keeps Portland within half a game of third place in the Western Conference. Evan Turner delivered a triple - double off the bench for the Trail Blazers, scoring 13 points to go with 12 rebounds and 11 assists. Enes Kanter had team highs in both points and rebounds with 21 and 15, respectively. Finally, Damian Lillard continued his All-Star season with a double - double, scoring 20 points and dishing out 10 assists. Memphis was led by 16 points off the bench by veteran Chandler Parsons. Former first - round pick Bruno Caboclo added three blocks and 11 points off the bench, while Ivan Rabb finished with 13 points and 10 rebounds for a double - double. Both teams hit the road on Friday, with the Grizzlies visiting Dallas and the Trail Blazers heading to Denver.

The Portland Trail Blazers took down the visiting Denver Nuggets, 115 - 108, at Moda Center on Sunday evening. Portland (51 - 29) bounced back from Friday's loss in Denver (53 - 27) with a dramatic home win. The Trail Blazers closed the game on a 17 - 1 run after falling behind for the first time since the first quarter. Six of those points came from Damian Lillard, whose 30 - point night made him the game's leading scorer. The win keeps Portland at fourth in the Western Conference, while the Nuggets stay steady at second. Veteran forward Al-Faroq Aminu scored 23 points to help Portland seal the win. He also notched a double - double thanks to his 11 rebounds. Enes Kanter, who has been the starting center for the Blazers since Jusuf Nurkic went down with a fractured lower leg, tallied 11 points and 13 boards in the win. For Denver, superstar big man Nikola Jokic got the day off for rest. Six different players scored in double figures, but it was not enough to tip the scales in the Nuggets' favor. Gary Harris led the charge with 18 points, while Trey Lyles chipped in 15 points and nine rebounds. Denver had an unusually poor night at the free - throw line, shooting just 11 - of - 20 from the stripe. Both teams will take to the road on Tuesday, with the Nuggets visiting Utah and the Trail Blazers facing the Lakers in LA.

The Portland Trail Blazers took down the Sacramento Kings, 136 - 131, at Moda Center on Wednesday evening. It was the final game of the season for both teams, which explains some of the unorthodox roster decisions made by each coach. Sacramento (39 - 43) scored 87 points in the first half, but elected to rest all of its starters after the break. The team made use of all 12 men on the roster, as only one player saw 30 or more minutes of action. Portland (53 - 29), on the other hand, played it safe from the start, resting almost all of its typical rotation players. Only six players took the floor for Portland. Still, the team was able to secure a comeback win thanks to a lopsided fourth quarter. The Trail Blazers poured in 38 fourth quarter points while holding Sacramento to just 18. Anfernee Simons played all 48 minutes for the Blazers, leading to a career - high 37 points. Simons added nine assists. Sophomore big man Skal Labissiere also stood out, recording 29 points and 15 rebounds in 41 minutes of action. The team shot over 58 percent from the floor, including 14 - of - 24 from three - point range. Sacramento, meanwhile, saw 17 points and nine assists from De'Aaron Fox. All of Fox's production came in the first half, as he sat out the second. Marvin Bagley III logged a team - high 30 minutes and scored 20 points in the season finale. With the win, Portland secures the third seed in the Western Conference. The Trail Blazers will face the Oklahoma City Thunder in the Western Conference first - round playoffs.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the visiting Oklahoma City Thunder, 108 - 100, at Oracle Arena on Tuesday night. What would have been a marquee matchup lost some of its muster due to injuries, as former MVP and Oklahoma City star Russell Westbrook missed the game as he continues to rehab from a knee surgery. Still, there was plenty of excitement, as the Thunder were able to come back and take the lead from the defending champions late in the game. After trailing by 10 before halftime, OKC came back in the third quarter and led 69 - 66. The teams grappled for the lead, but the Warriors were able to seal the game with a dagger floater from Kevin Durant in the final 30 seconds of regulation. Golden State (10) earned the win on its home court after celebrating its third championship banner in the last four years. Two-time MVP Steph Curry led his team with 32 points, also dishing out nine assists and grabbing eight rebounds. Durant finished the game with 27 points and six assists. Klay Thompson had an uncharacteristically poor shooting night, going just 5 - of - 20 on his field goal attempts. Oklahoma City (0 - 1), meanwhile, saw a strong performance from recently re - signed All-Star Paul George. George led his team with 27 points, which came on 9 - of - 23 shooting. He added four steals on the defensive end. New Zealand-born center Steven Adams helped to anchor the team on both ends, finishing the game with 17 points, 11 rebounds, four assists, and two steals. Ultimately, though, the team could not find the offense necessary to pull out the win; they shot just 36 percent from the field. Both teams will play again on Friday, with the Warriors traveling to Utah and the Thunder paying a visit to the LA Clippers.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the Phoenix Suns, 123 - 103, at Oracle Arena on Monday. The Warriors (3 - 1), who were coming off their first loss of the season Sunday night in Denver, made light work of the visiting Suns (1 - 2) in what was an impressive bounce - back effort. Golden State led with from wire - to - wire, and the team was once again led by Steph Curry, who continues to be on fire from behind the arc to start the regular season. Curry finished with a game - high 29 points (8 - 11 FG, 6 - 13 3Pt) to go along with eight assists and four rebounds in 30 minutes. Kevin Durant was close behind with 22 points on 9 - of - 17 shooting in just 26 minutes, while Klay Thompson struggled shooting, going just 1 - of - 6 from three - point range, but he still managed to finish with 16 points. As for the Suns, even in defeat, they still managed to get some stellar performances from their young stars. Devin Booker led the way with a team - high 28 points (11 - 21 FG, 3 - 9 3Pt), six assists, five rebounds and two steals in 38 minutes, while T.J. Warren put together an incredibly efficient performance off the bench, scoring 27 points on 12 - of - 17 shooting in just 24 minutes as a reserve. Rookie DeAndre Ayton posted his second double - double of the season, recording 20 points (6 - 11 FG) and 14 rebounds in 31 minutes. In the end, Phoenix was just unable to keep pace with the high - scoring Warriors, and that was mainly because of the team's inability to hit from behind the arc, where they shot just 9 - of - 33 (27 percent) from Monday night.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the Washington Wizards 144 - 122 at Oracle Arena on Wednesday. It was the Stephen Curry show right out the gate for the Warriors after a significant night for the two time MVP. Curry passed Jamal Crawford for fifth all time on the three point field goals made list and did it by pouring in 21 points first quarter. Golden State's point guard went on to score 51 points in 32 minutes. Add Kevin Durant's 30 points on 13 - of - 18 shooting and the game became far too much for the Wizards to handle as the game became a blowout early in the second quarter. Washington (1 - 3) attempted to go three - for - three during the first quarter and posted a respectable 37 points, however, the Warriors 46 points in front of their home crowd proved daunting. Bradley Beal poured in 23 points on 10 - of - 15 shooting, but the rest of the starters were unable to match the high pace and efficiency that the Warriors (4 - 1) were playing at. Curry's finished with 51 points, three assists and four rebounds on 15 - of - 24 shooting and 11 - of - 15 from behind the arc. John Wall, Marcus Morris and Otto Porter Jr. also finished in double figures scoring to aid Beal. Golden State finished 58 percent from the floor, redefining lights out even for Oracle Arena's standard. Both teams play on Friday, as the Warriors visit Madison Square Garden to take on the New York Knicks, while the Wizards continue their west coast road trip and meet the Sacramento Kings.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the New Orleans Pelicans, 131 - 121, at Oracle Arena on Wednesday. The Warriors (8 - 1) managed to survive a track meet in the Bay Area on Wednesday, and they earned their sixth straight victory in the process. Steph Curry was, yet again, sensational, scoring a game - high 37 points on 7 - of - 11 shooting from behind the arc and 12 - of - 20 shooting overall. He also dished out a game - high nine assists, barely edging out teammates Kevin Durant and Draymond Green, who each recorded eight. Durant finished with 24 points, while Green posted a very impressive stat line of 16 points, 14 rebounds and eight assists in 34 minutes. As a team, the Warriors consistently found ways to get open looks from three, and it paid off, as they shot 16 - of - 32 (50 percent) from long range. As for the Pelicans (4 - 3), they put up a good fight, but were unable to close the gap over the course of the second half. Jrue Holiday was the driving force behind the team's offense Wednesday night, as he scored a team - high 28 points to go along with nine assists in 42 minutes. It was a rough night, however, for superstar Anthony Davis, who didn't appear to be 100 percent healthy after missing the previous game with an elbow injury. Davis had just 17 points on 6 - of - 16 shooting and 12 rebounds in 41 minutes. Nikola Mirotic and E'Twaun Moore did an adequate job picking up the slack, scoring 26 and 21 points respectively. Up next, the Warriors will remain home to play the Timberwolves on Friday, while the Pelicans will head to Portland on Thursday to take on the Trail Blazers.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the visiting Minnesota Timberwolves, 116 - 99, at Oracle Arena on Friday evening. The Warriors jumped out to a good start at home, as they built a 21 - 11 lead halfway through the first quarter, and held on to lead 36 - 32 heading into the second. They stayed in front to start the second quarter, but the'Wolves battled back to take a two - point lead halfway thought the quarter. Things stayed tight until halftime, but it was the Warriors who emerged with a 61 - 58 lead at the break. The Timberwolves were not done yet, as they reclaimed the lead four minutes into the third quarter and held on to take a 87 - 83 lead into the final frame. However, the Warriors turned it on in the fourth. Led by eight straight points from Klay Thompson, they went on to outscore the Timberwolves 33 - 12 in the quarter, to cruise to their seventh straight win. Kevin Durant led the Warriors with 33 points, 13 rebounds, three assists and one block, in 36 minutes. Stephen Curry followed up with 28 points, nine rebounds, seven assists and two blocks, while Klay Thompson added 22 points, on 9 - of - 17 shooting. The Warriors shot 49 percent from the field, including 13 - of - 34 from long range. Meanwhile, Andre Wiggins led the Timberwolves with 22 points on 9 - of - 23 shooting, in 36 minutes. Jimmy Butler followed up with 21 points, five assists and three rebounds, in 35 minutes, while Karl-Anthony Towns tallied 13 points, 11 rebounds, one assist, two steals and a block. The Timberwolves shot 38 percent from the field, including 13 - of - 45 from long range. The Timberwolves (4 - 5) will look to bounce back as they take on the Trail Blazers in Portland on Sunday. The Warriors (9 - 1) play host to the Grizzlies on Monday.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the visiting Memphis Grizzlies, 117 - 101, at Oracle Arena on Monday evening. The Grizzlies got out to a good start on the road, as they emerged with a 31 - 29 lead after a hard - fought first quarter. They stayed strong in the second, and held the lead for almost the entire quarter. However, the Warriors were hot on their tail and had it tied it up at 58, by halftime. The third quarter started out similarly, but by the halfway point, was a whole different game, as the Warriors mounted a 23 - 8 run, to take a 92 - 73 lead into the final frame. They quickly pushed their lead to 20, and beyond, as they cruised to their eighth straight win, and moved to 60 at home this season. Klay Thompson led the Warriors with 27 points on 11 - of - 21 shooting, three assists, two rebounds and one steal, in 32 minutes. Kevin Durant followed up with 22 points, six rebounds, six assists, and one steal, in 31 minutes, while Stephen Curry added 19 points, seven assists, five rebounds, one steal and one block. The Warriors shot 51 percent from the field, including 13 - of - 23 from long range. Meanwhile, Dillon Brooks led the Grizzlies with 18 points on 6 - of - 13 shooting, in 23 minutes off the bench. Shelvin Mack and Jaren Jackson Jr. chipped in 15 points each, while Marc Gasol added eight points, 10 rebounds, nine assists, in 28 minutes. The Grizzlies shot 46 percent from the field, including 9 - of - 27 from long range. The Grizzlies (5 - 4) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Nuggets on Wednesday. The Warriors (10 - 1) play host to the Bucks on Thursday.

The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the host Golden State Warriors, 134 - 111, at Oracle Arena on Thursday evening. The Bucks got out to a great start on the road, as they kept it close, before managing to pull ahead in the final minutes of the first quarter, and take a 32 - 29 lead into the second. The Bucks kept their foot on the gas through the second, as they did not allow the Warriors to catch up, constantly pulled another step ahead, as they outscored the home team, 32 - 22, in the quarter, to take a 64 - 51 lead into halftime. The Bucks iced the game in the third, where they took to a 20 - 5 run to pull ahead by 26 late in the third quarter. Stephen Curry was forced to leave the game in the third, as he suffered a strained groin. The Bucks went on to cruise to their third road win, while the Warriors saw their eight - game winning streak come to an end. Draymond Green (toe) did not suit up in the contest. Eric Bledsoe led the Bucks with 26 points, six assists, four rebounds and one steal, in 26 minutes. Giannis Antetokounmpo followed up with 24 points, nine rebounds, four assists, two steals and two blocks, in 26 minutes, while Malcolm Brogdon finished with 20 points, three rebounds, two steals and one assist. The Bucks shot 52 percent from the field, including 9 - of - 35 from long range. Meanwhile, Klay Thompson led the Warriors with 24 points, three rebounds, three assists, two blocks and one steal, in 33 minutes. Kevin Durant followed up with 17 points, nine assists, five rebounds and one block, while Damian Jones tallied 12 points, four rebounds, one assist and a block. The Warriors shot 48 percent from the field, including 10 - of - 28 from deep. The Warriors (10 - 2) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Nets on Saturday. The Bucks (9 - 2) take on the Clippers in Los Angeles on Saturday.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the Brooklyn Nets, 116 - 100, at Oracle Arena on Saturday evening. The Warriors (11 - 2) came into the contest missing both Stephen Curry (groin) and Draymond Green (toe), and they were facing a clearly improved team in the Nets (6 - 7). However, Golden State didn't spend any time mulling over who wasn't suiting up, as they built a 36 - 30 first - quarter lead that they'd expanded to 65 - 53 by intermission. Not satisfied with that advantage, the home squad expanded their lead by another eight points in the third period to essentially cruise to victory. Both teams shot well, but the Warriors were especially sharp. They drained 55 percent of their attempts, including 44 percent of their tries from distance. Joe Harris paced the Nets with 24 points, a total he supplemented with two assists, one rebound and one steal. Shabazz Napier and Spencer Dinwiddie generated matching 14 - point tallies off the bench. D'Angelo Russell provided 12 points, five assists, three rebounds and two steals. Two young pieces that had been key to Brooklyn's early success, Jarrett Allen and Caris LeVert, underwhelmed with six and four points, respectively. Kevin Durant led the Warriors with a 28 - point, 11 - assist double - double that also included five rebounds, three steals and one block. Quinn Cook drew the start for Curry and totaled 27 points, five assists, four rebounds and one steal. Klay Thompson poured in 24 points and added one rebound, one assist, two steals and one block. Damian Jones and Jonas Jerebko each pitched in eight points. The Nets continue on the road and pay a visit to the Minnesota Timberwolves on Monday night, while the Warriors make the short trip to Los Angeles and tangle with the Clippers on Monday evening as well.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the Atlanta Hawks, 110 - 103, at Oracle Arena on Tuesday night. Golden State (12 - 3) came into the game dealing with drama, as Draymond Green was suspended by the team for Tuesday's contest due to an argument with fellow All-Star Kevin Durant during Monday night's loss to the Clippers. Green's suspension came amidst reports that he cursed at Durant and argued with teammates over his handling of the final play in regulation. With Green absent, the Warriors were missing two of their key players, as Steph Curry (groin) was also sidelined for Tuesday night's contest. Nevertheless, Golden State managed to put it together to hand the Hawks (3 - 11) their fifth straight loss. Both teams shot under 40 percent in the first half, but the offense picked up on both sides in the third quarter. Strong shooting helped propel Golden State to victory, as the team knocked down 12 three - pointers on 44 percent shooting. Atlanta, meanwhile, stayed close behind for much of the game, thanks in part to a strong 22 - point effort from Taurean Prince. Durant led all scorers with 29 points, while Klay Thompson trailed him with 24. Quinn Cook, filling in for the injured Steph Curry, scored 18 points and dished out six assists. For the Hawks, meanwhile, Kent Bazemore added another 18 points. Both teams will take to the road on Thursday, with the Hawks visiting Denver and the Warriors traveling to Houston.

The Oklahoma City Thunder took down the Golden State Warriors, 123 - 95, at Oracle Arena on Wednesday evening. Basketball action ground to a halt in the fourth quarter, as OKC's Hamidou Diallo went down with a gruesome knee and leg injury. Diallo sustained the injury while battling for a rebound. The rookie shooting guard left the floor on a stretcher; it is unclear yet what the exact nature of his injury is. Diallo's injury came in the middle of a dominant fourth quarter for OKC (11 - 6). The Thunder outscored Golden State 36 - 16 in the final quarter, thanks in large part to a stifling defensive effort. OKC already boasted the fourth - best defensive rating in the NBA. On Wednesday, they improved upon it by holding the league - best Golden State (12 - 7) offense to 95. The Warriors were limited to 43 percent shooting from the field and just 24 percent shooting from beyond the arc. The loss brings Golden State's losing streak to four games, making this the first four - game losing streak for the franchise in over four years. Dennis Schroder led the way for OKC with 32 points in the win. Schroder shot 12 - of - 19, including five three - pointers, and committed only one turnover on the night. Former MVP Russell Westbrook notched a triple - double, finishing with 11 points, 12 rebounds, and 13 assists. Paul George added an additional 25 points. Steph Curry (groin) missed his fourth straight game in Wednesday's loss. In his absence, Kevin Durant and Klay Thompson scored 27 points apiece. Durant also had 14 rebounds and three blocked shots. On Friday, OKC will host the Charlotte Hornets while Golden State will see the Portland Trail Blazers.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the visiting Portland Trail Blazers, 125 - 97, at Oracle Arena on Friday evening. The Trail Blazers got out to a good start on the road, as they held the advantage for most of the first quarter, before taking a 27 - 24 lead into the second. However, the Warriors turned on the jets in the second, as they outscored the Blazers 35 - 17 in the quarter, to take a 59 - 44 lead into the half. The Warriors picked up where they left off in the third, as they pushed their lead to 21 midway through the quarter, and held on to take a 19 - point, 92 - 73, lead into the fourth. The Trail Blazers came out fighting in the fourth, but could not get the deficit below double digits, as the Warriors cruised to a much - needed win, ending a four - game slide. Kevin Durant led the Warriors with 32 points, eight rebounds, seven assists, three blocks and two steals, in 37 minutes. Klay Thompson followed up with 31 points, eight rebounds, two steals, one assist and one block, while Quinn Cook chipped in 19 points, five rebounds and two assists. The Warriors shot 56 percent from the field, including 17 - of - 32 from long range. Meanwhile, Damian Lillard led the Trail Blazers with 23 points, eight assists, two rebounds, two steals and one block, in 34 minutes. Jusuf Nurkic followed up with 22 points, eight rebounds, one assist and one steal, while C.J. McCollum tallied 19 points, five assists, one rebound and one steal. The Trail Blazers shot 41 percent from the field, including 9 - of - 24 from long range. The Trail Blazers (12 - 7) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Clippers on Sunday. The Warriors (13 - 7) will look to keep up the momentum as they play host to the Kings on Saturday.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the visiting Sacramento Kings, 117 - 116, at Oracle Arena on Saturday evening. The Kings got out to a great start on the road, as they outscored the Warriors, 29 - 28, in the first quarter. The Kings kept up their ferocity, as they outscored the Warriors, 35 - 32, in the second, to take a, 64 - 60, lead into half time. The Warriors turned the tables in the third, as they pulled ahead by five early in the quarter. They went on to outscore the Kings by six in the quarter, to take a, 95 - 93, lead into the fourth. The Kings did not back down, as they continued to trade the lead with the Warriors throughout the fourth, but Golden State was able to hang down the stretch. Kevin Durant led the way for the Warriors with 44 points, 13 rebounds, seven assists and two blocks, in 40 minutes. Klay Thompson followed up with 31 points on 12 - of - 26 shooting, and four rebounds, while Damian Jones added 13 points, six rebounds and one assist, in 21 minutes. The Warriors shot 51 percent from the field, including 10 - of - 32 from long range. Meanwhile, Buddy Hield led the Kings with 28 points, seven rebounds, three assists and one block, in 33 minutes. Marvin Bagley III had a big night, with 20 points, 17 rebounds and two assists, in 33 minutes off the bench. Iman Shumpert chipped in 14 points, four rebounds and one steal. The Kings shot 44 percent from the field, including 11 - of - 27 from deep. The Kings (10 - 9) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Jazz on Sunday. The Warriors (14 - 7) play host to the Magic on Monday.

The Golden State Warriors took down the visiting Orlando Magic, 116 - 110, at Oracle Arena on Monday evening. Led by a whopping 49 points from All-Star forward Kevin Durant, the Warriors (15 - 7) were able to pull out a narrow win late in the game. With the Magic (10 - 11) up three with 1:45 remaining, Klay Thompson buried a three - pointer to tie the game up. Golden State went on to stifle Orlando on the defensive end, while Durant sealed the win by knocking down a three - point shot to go up by four with 21 seconds remaining. The win puts Golden State in first place in the Western Conference standings. Durant added nine assists, two steals, and two blocks to his incredible scoring outburst. Klay Thompson scored an additional 29 points in the win. Durant and Thompson were the only two Warriors to score in double digits in the win, but that did not seem to make a difference. The team still managed to shoot 49 percent from the field and hit 13 three - pointers. The Magic saw a stellar shooting night of its own, going 14 - of - 28 from three - point territory. Nikola Vucevic led the team with 30 points, 12 rebounds, and six assists. Veteran wing Terrance Ross added another 28 points. Unfortunately for Orlando, neither performance was enough to help the team get its record over .500. The Magic will visit Portland on Wednesday, while the Warriors travel to Toronto to face the Raptors on Thursday.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the Minnesota Timberwolves, 116 - 108, at Oracle Arena on Monday evening. For the first time in weeks, the Warriors (19 - 9) were able to put all four of their returning All-Stars on the court together. Draymond Green (toe) had not played since November 15, but he rejoined a lineup that had only recently regained two - time MVP Steph Curry. With Green and Curry joining Kevin Durant and Klay Thompson, the Warriors looked unstoppable on the offensive end. Minnesota (13 - 14) never led, and the Warriors held a double - digit advantage for much of the game. Golden State finished with 19 three - pointers, seven of which came from Curry. Curry was the game's high scorer, pouring in 38 points to lead his team to victory. Green added a team - high 10 rebounds and seven assists, while Durant and Thompson combined to score 48 points. All in all, it was an outstanding night for the Warriors' high - powered offense. Minnesota fought hard to keep the game competitive, but the team's 7 - of - 25 shooting from beyond the arc made it difficult to keep up. Karl-Anthony Towns led the Wolves with 31 points and 11 rebounds, while Derrick Rose scored another 21 points. On Wednesday, the Timberwolves will visit Sacramento while Golden State will host the Toronto Raptors.

The visiting Toronto Raptors cruised past the Golden State Warriors, 113 - 93, at Oracle Arena on Wednesday evening. Toronto (23 - 7) and Golden State (19 - 10) each entered Wednesday's game at first place in its respective conference standings. The Raptors own the league's best record, but had run into some questions in recent weeks, particularly after going just 1 - 3 over a four game stretch to start the month of December. It is safe to say Toronto has put some of those doubts to rest, as the team has kicked off its six - game West Coast road trip with consecutive blowout wins against the Clippers and Warriors. On Wednesday, the Raptors jumped out to an early lead, thanks in no small part to the strong play of Kyle Lowry. Lowry recently had a four - game stretch in which he shot just 4 - of - 28 for 15 points in total, but the All-Star guard bounced back in a big way on Wednesday. After scoring 21 points in Los Angeles, Lowry led his team with 23 points and 12 assists to help take down the defending champion Warriors on their home court. Toronto built a 14 - point lead by halftime and doubled down with a strong third quarter, clinching the win early at Oracle. Kevin Durant scored 32 points to lead all scorers, but it was not enough to propel the Warriors to victory. Two-time MVP Steph Curry had one of his worst nights of the season, struggling to match Lowry on either side of the ball. Curry totaled just eight points on 2 - of - 11 shooting in 32 minutes of play. His 2 - of - 8 shooting from beyond the arc was a major factor in Golden State shooting just 6 - of - 26 from three - point range in total. Next on the agenda for Toronto is a trip to Portland on Friday evening. The Warriors, meanwhile, will stay in Northern California to take on the Sacramento Kings at Golden One Center on Friday.

The Golden State Warriors cruised past the Memphis Grizzlies, 110 - 93, at Oracle Arena on Monday evening. The Warriors (21 - 10) entered the game boasting the league's top - ranked offense, but faced a substantial test in the Grizzlies (16 - 14), who had held opponents to just 102 points per game. Despite Memphis's elite defense, Golden State was able to score with ease, pouring in 12 three - pointers as five different players scored in double digits. The Grizzlies, meanwhile, had major struggles offensively. The team's shooting woes began with its starting unit, which combined for just 53 points. Memphis has now scored 100 or more in just one of its last 10 games. Kevin Durant and Steph Curry combined for 43 points in the win, though they combined to shoot just 13 - of - 31 from the floor. Klay Thompson pitched in another 16 points, while bench big man Jonas Jerebko delivered 16 points in just 26 minutes of play. Andre Iguodala, returning from a hip injury, tallied 10 points in 16 minutes off the bench. Memphis, meanwhile, struggled as a team, shooting only 28 percent from three - point range en route to another tough offensive night. Omri Casspi led the team with 20 points off the bench, which came on 8 - of - 10 shooting. Aside from Casspi, though, offense was sparse, as the team made just 36 shots in the loss. On Wednesday, the Warriors will visit Utah while the Grizzlies will travel to Portland.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the visiting Dallas Mavericks, 120 - 116, at Oracle Arena on Saturday evening. The Mavs got out to a strong start on the road and managed to hang on to a three - point advantage after one quarter. They kept it tight through the second as they matched the Warriors with 30 points a piece in the quarter, to take a three - point lead at halftime. The Warriors turned the tables in the third, however, as they outscored the visitors by 10, to take a seven - point lead heading into the final frame. Despite a rally from the Mavericks in the final minutes, the Warriors were able to hang on for their 14th home win of the season, while the Mavs dropped their fifth game in a row. Kevin Durant led the Warriors with 29 points, 12 rebounds, eight assists and one block, in 36 minutes. Stephen Curry followed up with 22 points, five rebounds, five assists and two steals, in 39 minutes. Draymond Green finished with 14 points, 10 rebounds, five assists and two block, while Klay Thompson chipped in 14 points, five rebounds, four assists, two steals and a block. Meanwhile, Wesley Matthews led the Mavericks with 25 points, four assists, three rebounds and one steal, in 35 minutes. DeAndre Jordan tallied 12 points, 23 rebounds, five assists, two steals and one block, while Luka Doncic added 19 points, five assists, three rebounds, a steal and a block. The Mavs (15 - 16) will look to avoid a sixth straight loss as they take on the Trail Blazers in Portland on Sunday. The Warriors (22 - 11) play host to the Clippers on Sunday.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the visiting Los Angeles Clippers, 129 - 127, at Oracle Arena on Sunday. There were 20 ties and 13 lead changes in this game, as it wasn't decided until the final shot. In fact, Avery Bradley recorded a dunk with 10 seconds left to tie the game but Stephen Curry countered that by hitting one of his patented lay - ups with 0 seconds left to win the game. Los Angeles lost this game despite having the best three - point shooting game of the season, as they connected on 18 - of - 23 from long range. The key for the Warriors was free - throw shooting, as they hit 31 - of - 36 while the Clippers connected on 23 - of - 29. Defense was also critical, with Golden State picking up nine steals and eight blocks while Los Angeles had just one apiece. Offensive rebounding was also decisive, with the Warriors winning that battle, 15 - 5. The Clippers (19 - 14) were led by Tobias Harris, as he tallied 32 points, eight rebounds and two assists. Danilo Gallinari amassed 25 points, 11 rebounds and three assists. Lou Williams was huge off the bench, as he provided 25 points, two rebounds and nine assists. Montrezl Harrell also played well off the bench, amassing 13 points, three rebounds and two assists. The Warriors (23 - 11) were led by Stephen Curry, as he collected 42 points, six rebounds and two assists. Kevin Durant accumulated 35 points, 12 rebounds, five assists and three blocks. Draymond Green finished with 14 points, four rebounds, six assists and five steals. Kevon Looney led their bench with 10 points and seven boards. On deck for Golden State is a Christmas Day showdown against the Los Angeles Lakers on Tuesday. As for the Clippers, they return to action on Wednesday when they play host to the Sacramento Kings.

The Los Angeles Lakers took down the Golden State Warriors, 127 - 101, on Christmas Day at Oracle Arena. It was a marquee matchup between two of the Western Conference's top teams on Christmas.
