Ultimately, however, it was not the Warriors' (23 - 12) night, as the team shot just 41 percent en route to a blowout loss. Struggles compounded for Golden State, as each of the team's four active All-Stars performed poorly in the loss. The team saw a dismal final quarter, culminating in Draymond Green fouling out with only four points scored on the night. It was a big win for the Lakers, who now sit at fourth in the Western Conference standings. All did not go as hoped for Los Angeles (20 - 14), though, as superstar LeBron James exited the game in the third quarter with a left groin strain. James did not return to action, though his team saw plenty of success in his absence. LA, without LeBron on the court, outscored Golden State 36 - 19 in the fourth quarter. LA saw a true team effort as it took down the defending champions. Seven players scored in double digits for the Lakers, and the team tallied 27 total assists. Kyle Kuzma led the team in scoring with 19 points, while veteran point guard Rajon Rondo delivered 15 points and 10 assists in just 23 minutes of action. Golden State, meanwhile, was led by a season - best 23 points from Andre Iguodala. Iduodala's vintage performance was not enough to help his team, though, as the Warriors shot just 41 percent from the field and 25 percent from three - point range. It was a particularly poor showing for Klay Thompson and Draymond Green, who combined to shoot just 4 - of - 14 while committing six turnovers on the night. Next on the agenda for the Lakers is a visit to Sacramento on Thursday. Golden State, meanwhile, will gear up to host the Portland Trail Blazers later this week.

The Portland Trail Blazers defeated the Golden State Warriors, 110 - 109, in overtime at Oracle Arena on Thursday. Despite committing a costly turnover at the end of regulation, Damian Lillard was the hero for Portland (20 - 15) once again on Thursday. After Draymond Green knocked down a three - pointer to put Golden State (23 - 13) up late, Lillard gave the Blazers the win by knocking down a three - pointer with five seconds remaining in overtime. Lillard's clutch three came after Portland gained possession on an errant pass by Golden State's Stephen Curry. The game proved to be a messy one down the stretch, but both sides saw brilliant performances from their stars. For Portland, Lillard combined with C.J. McCollum to score 45 points and knock down six three - pointers. Big man Jusuf Nurkic contributed a team - high 27 points to go with 14 rebounds and four assists in the win. Golden State, meanwhile, saw Curry score a game - high 29 points. The two - time MVP also grabbed two steals and blocked two shots, but his season - high seven turnovers were too much for Golden State to swallow on Thursday. Kevin Durant, meanwhile, notched a triple - double with 26 points, 10 rebounds, and 10 assists. Draymond Green flirted with a triple - double of his own, scoring 15 points, grabbing 11 boards, and dishing out eight dimes. The two teams will rematch in Portland on Saturday night.

The Houston Rockets defeated the host Golden State Warriors, 135 - 134, at Oracle Arena on Thursday evening. The Warriors got out to a great start at home with a 34 - 22 lead after one quarter and expanded their lead to 70 - 53 by halftime. The Rockets turned it up in the third quarter and outscored the Warriors by 11, to cut the deficit to six at the start of the fourth. They kept the pressure on through the fourth and managed to tie the game in the final second of regulation thanks to pure heroics from James Harden. The Rockets scored the first points in OT, but the Warriors battled back and held a two - point lead with five seconds remaining. However, Harden had more magic left in his bag, as he drilled a seemingly impossible game - winning three - pointer over two Warriors defenders to steal the win on the road. Harden led the Rockets with 44 points, 15 assists, 10 rebounds, two blocks and one steal, in 44 minutes. Clint Capela followed up with 29 points, 21 rebounds, two steals, one assist and one block, while Austin Rivers added 18 points, four rebounds, four assists and one steal. The Rockets shot 46 percent from the field, including 21 - of - 54 from long range. Meanwhile, Stephen Curry led the Warriors with 35 points, six assists and three rebounds, in 40 minutes. Kevin Durant finished with 26 points, seven rebounds, three assists and one block, while Klay Thompson tallied 26 points, five rebounds, four assists, three steals and two blocks. The Warriors shot 38 percent from the field, including 14 - of - 37 from long range. The Warriors (25 - 14) will look to bounce back as they take on the Kings in Sacramento on Saturday. The Rockets (22 - 15) will look for their eighth straight win as they take on the Trail Blazers in Portland on Saturday.

The Golden State Warriors demolished the New York Knicks, 122 - 95, at Oracle Arena on Tuesday. It was smooth sailing for the Warriors (27 - 14), who took a double - digit lead late in the second quarter and never looked back. Fueled by their 52 percent shooting, the Warriors cruised to victory thanks to strong star play. Klay Thompson scored a game - high 43 points, including an individual 90 run thanks to three consecutive three - pointers. New York (10 - 31), meanwhile, was held to just 39 percent shooting by a stingy Warriors defense. Thompson hit seven three - pointers and shot 18 - of - 29 overall from the field. Kevin Durant added another 24 points for the Warriors, while Steph Curry delivered a 14 - point, 14 - assist double - double. Curry, though, had one of his worst shooting nights of the season, going just 5 - of - 19 from the floor. Draymond Green also recorded a double - double, tallying 11 rebounds and 10 assists. For New York, the starting five contributed only 43 points in the blowout loss. Mario Hezonja tallied a team - high 19 points off the bench, while veteran center Enes Kanter contributed 12 points and 16 rebounds. New York's second unit totaled 52 points in Tuesday's loss. Golden State will host Chicago on Friday, while the Knicks will host the Indiana Pacers.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the visiting Chicago Bulls, 146 - 109, at Oracle Arena on Friday evening. The Warriors got down to business right off the jump, as they poured in 43 points in the first quarter, while holding the Bulls to just 17 points. The Bulls picked it up in the second quarter and outscored the Warriors by five, but still trailed by 21 at halftime. The Warriors got back to domination mode in the third, where they outscored the visitors 40 - 21 in the quarter, to take a 116 - 76 lead into the final frame. They were able to cruise to their third straight win, and 17th home win of the season, while the Bulls took their sixth straight loss. Klay Thompson led the Warriors with 30 points on 10 - of - 18 shooting, two rebounds, two steals and one assist, in 25 minutes. Stephen Curry followed up with 28 points, eight assists and five rebounds, while Kevin Durant tallied 22 points, five assists, four rebounds, one steal and one block, in 28 minutes. The Warriors shot 58 percent from the field, including 18 - of - 39 from long range. Meanwhile, Zach LaVine led the Bulls with 29 points on 10 - of - 16 shooting and four rebounds, in 26 minutes. Bobby Portis followed up with 16 points on 4 - of - 7 shooting, four rebounds, two steals and one assist, in 16 minutes off the bench, while Antonio Blakeney tallied 12 points on 4 - of - 7 shooting off the bench. The Bulls (10 - 32) will look to bounce back as they take on the Jazz in Utah on Saturday. The Warriors (28 - 14) take on the Mavericks in Dallas on Sunday.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the New Orleans Pelicans, 147 - 140, at Oracle Arena on Wednesday. On the second game of a back - to - back, the Warriors (31 - 14) came out sluggish and seemed to be a bit hungover from their throttling of the Nuggets on Tuesday night. They fell behind early to the visiting, and surging, Pelicans (21 - 24), who opened up a lead as large as 16 points in the third quarter and appeared to be pulling away. Then, Steph Curry happened. The two - time MVP hit seven threes in the third period on his way to scoring 23 points and leading a furious comeback that had the Warriors miraculously up by one point heading into the final 12 minutes. From there, while the Pelicans kept fighting, it was business as usual for the defending champions, as Curry and company weren't going to let it slip away at that point. Curry finished with a game - high 41 points while shooting 9 - of - 17 from three, while Kevin Durant added 30 points and 15 assists. As a team, Golden State shot a ridiculous 24 - of - 49 (49 percent) from three in the winning effort. The Pelicans, on the other hand, were even more impressive with their arial assault, as they shot a scorching 19 - of - 37 (51 percent) from the field, but it wouldn't be enough. Anthony Davis led the way as usual with 30 points, 18 rebounds and seven assists in 41 minutes, while Nikola Mirotic was close behind with 29 points in 29 minutes off the bench. New Orleans' third frontcourt star, Julius Randle, shot just 6 - of - 8 from the field, but still managed to finish with 23 points in 22 minutes.

The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the Golden State Warriors, 113 - 104, at Oracle Arena on Thursday evening. The Warriors got out to a good start at home, with a 35 - 30 lead after one quarter. The Sixers rallied ahead early in the second and kept it close through the quarter, but the Warriors regained control and brought a 60 - 53 lead into halftime. The 76ers came out on fire in the third and outscored the Warriors 42 - 26 in the quarter, to take a 95 - 86 lead into the final frame. Things slowed down in the fourth, as the teams matched each other with 18 points, while the 76ers managed to hover around a double - digit lead, en route to their second straight win. This marks the end of an 11 - game winning streak for the Warriors. Joel Embiid led the 76ers with 26 points, 20 rebounds, five assists, and two steals, in 33 minutes. Ben Simmons tallied 26 points, eight rebounds, six assists, three steals and a block, while J.J. Redick added 15 points, three assists and two rebounds. The 76ers shot 46 percent from the field, including 13 - of - 36 from long range. Meanwhile, Stephen Curry led the Warriors with 41 points, six assists, four rebounds and one steal, in 38 minutes. Kevin Durant followed up with 25 points on 11 - of - 24 shooting, four rebounds, four assists and two steals, in 37 minutes, while Kevon Looney added 14 points, five rebounds, two steals and two blocks. The Warriors shot 47 percent from the field, including 11 - of - 38 from long range. The Warriors (36 - 15) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Lakers on Saturday. The 76ers (34 - 18) take on the Kings in Sacramento on Saturday.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the visiting Los Angeles Lakers, 115 - 101, at ORACLE Arena on Saturday. While Los Angeles was competitive throughout this game, Golden State ultimately prevailed thanks to a 27 - 15 fourth quarter. In fact, the Lakers actually led for the majority of the third quarter, as the Warriors finished the game on a 27 - 12 run. The free - throw shooting was the difference in the game, with Golden State hitting 18 - of - 19 and Los Angeles connecting on 10 - of - 17. Ball movement was also critical, with the Warriors recording 31 assists to 10 turnovers while the Lakers picked up 23 assists to 15 turnovers. The Lakers (26 - 26) played this game without LeBron James (rest), as Brandon Ingram led the way with 20 points, four rebounds and three assists. Rajon Rondo collected 12 points, eight rebounds and 11 assists. Kyle Kuzma amassed 13 points, four rebounds and two assists while Lance Stephenson led the bench with 10 points, six rebounds and four assists. The Warriors (37 - 15) were led by Klay Thompson, as he totaled 28 points, five rebounds and two assists. Kevin Durant accumulated 21 points, five rebounds and 11 assists. DeMarcus Cousins tallied 18 points, 10 rebounds, four assists and two blocks. Andre Iguodala led the bench with 17 points, three rebounds and four assists. On deck for Los Angeles is a road matchup versus the Indiana Pacers on Tuesday. As for Golden State, they're off until Wednesday when they play host to the San Antonio Spurs.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the San Antonio Spurs, 141 - 102, at Oracle Arena on Wednesday. The Warriors (38 - 15) allowed their visitors to hang around for about a quarter and a half Wednesday night, but thanks to a stretch across the second and third quarters where Golden State went 24 - of - 25 from the field, the home team buried the Spurs with little difficulty. 12 of the Warriors' 13 active players saw double - digit minutes Wednesday, with every single one of them scoring at least two points thanks to the blowout nature of the game. Klay Thompson was on fire for all 29 of his minutes, going 4 - of - 5 from three and 11 - of - 13 from the field overall en route to scoring a game - high 26 points, while Kevin Durant was close behind with 23 points in 29 minutes of his own to go along with eight rebounds, nine assists and three steals. Steph Curry finished with 19 points, five rebounds and seven assists in another 29 minutes. As a team, it was a clinic from the Warriors, shooting 47 percent from behind the arc and 58 percent from the field overall. As for the Spurs (32 - 24), they simply did not have enough talent to keep up with the NBA's best team Wednesday, as they were without both DeMar DeRozan and LaMarcus Aldridge for rest purposes. As a result, Patty Mills came through as the team's top scorer with just 16 points, while Rudy Gay added 15 points of his own. As a team, San Antonio shot decent from behind the arc, going 12 - of - 32 from three, but their overall field goal percentage was just 43 percent and not nearly efficient enough to top Golden State. This dropped the Spurs' record on the road this season to 10 - 17 as they continue to be a very different team away from home.

The Golden State Warriors took down the Miami Heat, 120 - 118, in a down - to - the - wire tilt at Oracle Arena on Sunday. Miami (25 - 29) caught Golden State (40 - 15) off guard, jumping out to a 26 - 7 lead in the first quarter thanks to a flurry of perimeter offense. The Heat saw three quick three - pointers from Josh Richardson, who had the hot hand all night as he scored 37 points. Hassan Whiteside also contributed early for Miami, scoring six points off of offensive rebounds in the first quarter. However, the defending champs fought back in characteristic fashion. The Warriors delivered a classic third - quarter thrashing, pouring in 36 points to erase Miami's lead. Golden State held onto the lead thanks to a number of crunch - time shots from Kevin Durant, who led all scorers with 39 points. The All-Star backcourt of Klay Thompson and Steph Curry also impressed in the win, pitching in 54 combined points for the Warriors. Draymond Green took on a playmaking role in the Golden State offense, dishing out a season - high 14 assists on the night. It was a quiet night on offense for DeMarcus Cousins, who scored just seven points while pulling down only three rebounds. Cousins was a disruptive force defensively, though, logging three blocks and two steals. The Heat saw 24 points from Dion Waiters, who shot 9 - of - 19 from the field. It was also a big night for Justise Winslow, who poured in 22 points to go with six rebounds and four assists. Next on the agenda for Miami is a trip to Denver, where they will play the second half of a back - to - back on Monday. Golden State, meanwhile, is set to host the Utah Jazz on Tuesday.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the Utah Jazz, 115 - 108, at Oracle Arena on Tuesday evening. Utah (32 - 25) seemed ready to test the Warriors' (41 - 15) dominance, holding a lead until late in the fourth quarter. The Jazz's top - five defense shined in the loss, limiting Golden State's high - powered offense to 81 points through three quarters. However, Utah was unable to hold onto the game late, as Golden State poured in 34 fourth - quarter points to earn the victory. Steph Curry, who finished with 24 points, helped to seal the win in the final five minutes, knocking down a pull - up three - pointer and an ensuing layup to put Golden State up 10. Kevin Durant was the game's high scorer with 28 points. Durant also tallied seven assists in the win. Klay Thompson scored another 22 points, while DeMarcus Cousins contributed 12 points, 10 rebounds, and five assists. The Warriors shot over 49 percent from the field and knocked down 13 three - pointers. The Jazz were led by 25 points from sophomore guard Donovan Mitchell, who shot a dismal 10 - of - 29 from the field. Outside of Mitchell, Utah was remarkably efficient. The Jazz finished shooting over 47 percent from the field. Rudy Gobert had a double - double, finishing with 13 points and 16 rebounds. The Jazz will have two days of rest before enjoying the All-Star break, while Golden State will travel to Portland to tangle with the Trail Blazers on Wednesday.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the Sacramento Kings, 125 - 123, at Oracle Arena on Thursday. Another game against Sacramento, another down - to - the - wire finish for the Warriors, who almost let Thursday's contest get away from them due to some costly missed free throws and a couple of prayer three - pointers from Buddy Hield in the final seconds. Nevertheless, Golden State managed to get one last stop when it desperately needed to and walked away with the regular season sweep over the Kings. As per usual, the Warriors did most of their damage Thursday night from behind the arc. Steph Curry led the way, making 10 three - pointers on his way to scoring a game - high 36 points in 36 minutes to go along with six rebounds and seven assists. As a team, shot 41 percent from behind the arc, making an incredible 19 three - point shots along the way. Kevin Durant made just one of those threes, but he still finished with 28 points, nine rebounds and four assists, while Klay Thompson added 18 points of his own. As for the Kings, it was a valiant effort for a team that has struggled mightily away from home, but they have now lost to the Warriors three times this season by a combined eight points. Rookie big man Marvin Bagley continues to improve, and he put together one of his best performances of his debut season Thursday, scoring a team - high 28 points and grabbing 14 rebounds in 34 minutes off the bench. In what ended up being a complete team effort, six other Sacramento players managed to score in double figures, but ultimately, the team just wasn't able to keep pace with the sharp - shooting Warriors.

The Houston Rockets defeated the host Golden State Warriors, 118 - 112, at ORACLE Arena on Saturday. While Golden State came into this game as a monster favorite, Houston led throughout. In fact, they led for over 45 minutes of this 48 - minute game, as they held a double - digit lead for nearly half the game thanks to a 35 - 20 first quarter. Free-throw shooting was the difference, with Houston connecting on 22 - of - 24 and Golden State hitting just 14 - of - 20. The 13 steals recorded by the Rockets were huge as well, as that allowed them to win the turnover differential, 17 - 13. The Rockets (34 - 25) had to play this game without James Harden (cervical strain), as Chris Paul led the way with 23 points, five rebounds, 17 assists and two steals. Eric Gordon totaled 25 points and four assists. Kenneth Faried started and finished with 20 points, 10 rebounds and two assists. P.J. Tucker collected 18 points, 10 rebounds, four steals and two blocks while Clint Capela amassed eight points and 15 boards. The Warriors (42 - 17) were led by Kevin Durant, as he accumulated 29 points, four rebounds and three assists. Stephen Curry generated 25 points, nine rebounds and seven assists. Klay Thompson provided 20 points, four rebounds, six assists and two steals while DeMarcus Cousins finished with 13 points, 14 rebounds, three steals and four blocks. Both teams return to action on Monday, with Golden State traveling to face the Charlotte Hornets and Houston playing host to the defensively - inept Atlanta Hawks.

The Boston Celtics blew out the Golden State Warriors, 128 - 95, at Oracle Arena on Tuesday evening. Boston (39 - 26) came out swinging, opening the game on an 110 run. The Celtics never took their foot off the gas, as strong contributions off the bench allowed them to expand their lead to 25 by halftime. For a team that had averaged just 46 points in first halves since the All-Star Break, the 73 point first half outburst was a welcome change of pace. Much of that could be attributed to Gordon Hayward, who shot 7 - of - 8 to score 19 points in 13 minutes of play during the first half. Golden State (44 - 20), meanwhile, was able to trim some of the lead in the third quarter, going on an 11 - 3 run to cut the Celtics' advantage down to 17. The Warriors were particularly successful in changing the pace of play, outscoring Boston 12 - 2 on the fast break in the third quarter. However, the Celtics closed the third on a 90 run to take a 29 - point lead, all but securing the turnaround win. Hayward led the Celtics with 30 points in total. The strong performance was a much - needed one for the former Jazz star, who was averaging just 5 points per game since the All-Star Break. As a team, Boston looked like a different squad than the one that dropped five of its previous six games. The Celtics shot over 50 percent from the floor and dished out 38 assists in total. Kyrie Irving helped lead the charge as a facilitator, recording 11 assists to go with 19 points. Golden State, meanwhile, falls to 3 - 4 since the All-Star Break. The team was once again without Klay Thompson (knee), and his absence showed in the team's lackluster offensive numbers. The Warriors shot just 39 percent from the field on the night, including a dismal 5 - of - 16 shooting performance from All-Star Kevin Durant. Star big man DeMarcus Cousins also struggled, picking up five fouls and a technical while scoring only 10 points. The Celtics will suit up again on Wednesday, when they visit the Kings in Sacramento. Golden State, meanwhile, will prepare to host the Denver Nuggets on Friday.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the visiting Denver Nuggets, 122 - 105, at Oracle Arena on Friday evening. The Warriors got out to a strong start at home, as they built a 10 - point lead through the first quarter. They kept the pressure on and pushed their lead to 17, leading 67 - 50 by halftime. The Nuggets picked it up in the third, as they cut the deficit to single digits by the halfway mark in the quarter. However, the Warriors rallied to push their lead back to 15, heading into the fourth. The Warriors maintained a comfortable cushion through the fourth, as they cruised to their 24th home win of the season. Klay Thompson led the Warriors with 39 points, four assists, three rebounds, two steals and one block, in 35 minutes. Kevin Durant followed up with 26 points, six assists, four rebounds and two blocks, while Stephen Curry added 17 points, seven assists and four rebounds. The Warriors shot 54 percent from the field, including 18 - of - 36 from long range. Meanwhile, Monte Morris and Malik Beasley led the Nuggets with 17 points each, while both coming off the bench. Nikola Jokic followed up with 16 points, six rebounds, four assists, four steals and one block, while Jamal Murray was quiet with 11 points and three assists. The Nuggets shot 38 percent from the field, including 12 - of - 33 from deep. The Nuggets (43 - 22) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Timberwolves on Tuesday. The Warriors (45 - 20) play host to the Suns on Sunday.

The Phoenix Suns upset the Golden State Warriors, 115 - 111, at Oracle Arena on Sunday evening. The Suns (16 - 52) saw 37 points from Devin Booker as they came away with a comeback win at Golden State (45 - 21). Phoenix's outlook seemed bleak early on, as the Suns fell behind by as much as 16 in the first quarter. The team was able to claw back in the second, though, behind eight points in the quarter from Kelly Oubre. The Suns scored 40 points in the second and continued their strong play into the second half. Golden State found itself trailing in the fourth quarter when it took a major blow, as All-Star forward Kevin Durant went down with a turned ankle. Durant went to the locker room and did not return to the game with what was described as an "ankle contusion. "Booker and the Suns were able to hang onto the lead and close out the win in the final minutes. In addition to his strong scoring output, Booker tallied 11 assists and eight rebounds. Oubre also had a strong scoring night, tallying 22 points in total. Rookie sensation DeAndre Ayton added to his strong first - year campaign, finishing with 18 points, nine rebounds, and four assists while taking down the defending champs. Golden State, meanwhile, was led by 28 points from All-Star guard Klay Thompson. Two-time MVP Steph Curry finished with 18 points, seven rebounds, and eight assists. Kevin Durant, prior to his injury, had recorded 25 points and two rebounds in 30 minutes of play. With the loss, Golden State is now just 4 - 6 in its last 10 games. The Warriors will have a chance to get back on track with a visit to Houston on Wednesday. Phoenix, meanwhile, will gear up for a clash with the Utah Jazz.

The Golden State Warriors demolished the Indiana Pacers, 112 - 89, at Oracle Arena on Thursday. After a slow start for both squads, Golden State (49 - 22) took control of the game by scoring 10 points in the final two minutes of the first half. The Warriors began to pile it on in the third quarter, going on a quick 110 run to bring their lead to 22. Indiana (44 - 29) struggled to string together offense, shooting just 38 percent from the field and 6 - of - 23 from three - point range. Thaddeus Young was the only Pacers starter to score in double digits in the tough loss. For Golden State, however, offense came easy. All five Warriors starters scored in double digits as the team shot 49 percent from the floor. DeMarcus Cousins led the way with 19 points and 11 rebounds, while two - time MVP Steph Curry chipped in another 15 points and seven assists. The Warriors knocked down 13 three - pointers on just over 36 percent from deep. Indiana's leading scorer was Tyreke Evans, who poured in 20 points off the bench. Young also offered a bright spot for the Pacers, shooting 7 - of - 13 for 18 points and seven rebounds. However, the remainder of Indiana's starting lineup combined for just 18 points, leading to a stagnant offensive night for the Pacers. Golden State will host the Dallas Mavericks on Saturday, while Indiana will return home to take on the Denver Nuggets on Sunday.

The Dallas Mavericks defeated host Golden State Warriors, 126 - 91, at ORACLE Arena on Saturday. It wouldn't have been surprising to see the Warriors win this game in blowout fashion but the Mavericks turned the tables on them here. In fact, a 37 - 22 first quarter really set the tone, as Dallas led by 28 points at the half and by 38 points heading into the fourth quarter. It was actually a wire - to - wire win for Dallas, leading by at least 35 points for the entirety of the fourth quarter. The Mavericks ended up shooting 53 percent from the field and 43 percent from three - point range while holding Golden State to 40 percent from the field and 13 percent (4 - of - 30) from long range. Dallas out - rebounded Golden State, 49 - 36, and out - assisted them, 33 - 22. The Mavericks (29 - 44) got another triple - double from Luka Doncic, as he led the way with 23 points, 11 rebounds, 10 assists and three steals. Dirk Nowitzki amassed 21 points, five rebounds and two blocks. Jalen Brunson accrued 11 points, four rebounds and five assists while Maxi Kleber led the bench with 16 points and nine boards. The Warriors (49 - 33) were led by Kevin Durant, as he tallied 25 points, five rebounds and four assists. DeMarcus Cousins amassed 19 points, six rebounds and three assists. Quinn Cook started for Stpehen Curry (rest) and provided seven points, six rebounds and seven assists. Kevon Looney was the only other player in double figures, as he led the bench with 12 points and three boards. Golden State has to play again on Sunday, as they play host to the Detroit Pistons. As for Dallas, they return to action on Tuesday against the Sacramento Kings.

The Golden State Warriors took down the Detroit Pistons, 121 - 114, at Oracle Arena on Sunday evening. Sunday's tilt was an important one for the Warriors (50 - 23), who entered the game in a tie with Denver for first in the Western Conference. Golden State had taken its worst loss of the season on Saturday, falling by a 35 - point margin to the Dallas Mavericks. Things went smoothly for the Warriors on Sunday, however, as the team led by double figures at halftime and by 20 by the end of the third quarter. Golden State was able to overcome the absence of DeMarcus Cousins (rest), instead starting recently - signed big man Andrew Bogut. Detroit (37 - 36) was able to fight back with a 37 - point fourth quarter, but it proved to be too little, too late. The Pistons were unable to come within seven points of Golden State in the second half. Steph Curry led the way for the Warriors with 26 points. Klay Thompson added another 24, knocking down four three - pointers. Kevin Durant logged a double - double, shooting 5 - of - 6 for 14 points and dishing out 11 assists. In total, the Warriors shot 62 percent from the field and a highly efficient 13 - of - 25 from three - point range. For Detroit, Blake Griffin scored 24 points and dished out eight assists. The Pistons relied heavily on their second unit, which combined for 62 points on the night. Luke Kennard led the bench unit with 20 points on 8 - of - 12 shooting. The Pistons' Western Conference road trip will continue with a visit to Denver on Tuesday. The Warriors, meanwhile, will next suit up in Memphis on Wednesday evening.

The Golden State Warriors blew out the visiting Charlotte Hornets, 137 - 90, at Oracle Arena on Sunday evening. Sunday's win was a no - doubter for the Warriors (52 - 24), who led by as much as 45 during the third quarter. Golden State closed the first half on a 13 - 3 run and never looked back, outscoring Charlotte (35 - 41) by double figures in the third quarter to seal the blowout win. The Warriors were aided by a flurry of three - pointers, 11 of which came from the All-Star tandem of Steph Curry and Klay Thompson. Overall, Golden State shot 60 percent from the field and knocked down 21 three - pointers. Curry and Thompson scored 25 points and 24 points, respectively. The Warriors also saw nine assists each from Kevin Durant and Draymond Green. None of Golden State's starters played more than 29 minutes, as Sunday's win was wrapped up in neat fashion relatively early in the game. The Hornets, meanwhile, shot only 36 percent in the tough loss. No Hornets starter scored more than nine points. All-Star guard Kemba Walker shot 4 - of - 14 from the field in only 25 minutes of play, as things quickly got out of hand for Charlotte. The Hornets will look for redemption as they continue their West Coast trip with a visit to Utah on Monday. Golden State, meanwhile, will host the Denver Nuggets on Tuesday.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the Denver Nuggets, 116 - 102, at Oracle Arena on Tuesday. Tuesday's tilt had big stakes, as the Nuggets (51 - 26) entered the contest just one game behind the Warriors (53 - 24) for first place in the West. Golden State made quick work of the competition, though, hopping out to an early double - digit lead and never looking back. Denver trailed by double - digits for the entirety of the second half, shooting only 38 percent from the floor en route to the blowout loss. With their win, the Warriors now have a two game lead for first in the West with just five games remaining. The Warriors were led by 28 points and 12 rebounds from All-Star center DeMarcus Cousins. Kevin Durant tacked on another 21 points as the Warriors shot a blistering 54 percent from the floor in the win. Draymond Green finished with nine rebounds and nine assists, and five Warriors in total scored in double figures. Jamal Murray scored 17 points for Denver, making him the lone Nuggets player to score more than 11 points. Superstar big man Nikola Jokic was limited to 4 - of - 10 shooting and six turnovers. The team as a whole hit only seven three - pointers and committed 15 turnovers. Denver will host San Antonio on Wednesday, while the Warriors take on the Lakers in LA on Thursday.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 120 - 114, at Oracle Arena on Friday night. The Warriors (55 - 24) gave DeMarcus Cousins the night off, but they were otherwise at full strength. The talent gap between them and the Cavaliers (19 - 61) was evident in the first half, when Golden State forged a 68 - 49 halftime lead. However, Cleveland didn't lay down despite their lack of postseason aspirations and sizable deficit, outscoring their hosts by a 65 - 52 margin in the third and fourth quarters but falling just short. Collin Sexton led the way for the Cavaliers with 27 points, adding four assists, one rebound and two steals. Cedi Osman managed 15 points, six rebounds, two assists and two steals. Larry Nance, Jr. generated a 13 - point, 14 - rebound double - double that also included three assists, three steals and one block. David Nwaba matched Nance's scoring tally off the bench and also pulled down seven boards. Tristan Thompson and Ante Zizic produced matching 12 - point, six - rebound efforts. Stephen Curry bounced back from a poor shooting night Thursday to pace the Warriors with 40 points. He complemented them with seven assists, six rebounds and one block. Draymond Green tallied 20 points, eight rebounds, five assists, one steal and one block. Kevin Durant managed 15 points, eight assists, five rebounds, one steal and one block. Quinn Cook led the bench with 14 points. Klay Thompson furnished 11 points, four rebounds, three assists and one block. The Cavaliers return home to face the San Antonio Spurs on Sunday afternoon, while the Warriors remain home to tangle with the Los Angeles Clippers on Sunday night.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the visiting Los Angeles Clippers, 131 - 104, at Oracle Arena on Sunday evening. The contest got out to a competitive start but the Warriors managed to keep a slight edge for almost the entire first quarter, and take a four - point lead into the second. The Clippers kept fighting and took the lead momentarily mid way through the second, however, the Warriors pulled back ahead, to take a 62 - 55 lead into halftime. The Warriors flipped the switch in the third quarter and ran away with the game, as they outscored the Clippers by 24 in the quarter, to take a 31 - point lead into the final frame. The Clippers kept fighting but only outscored the Warriors by four points in the final frame, which was not enough, as the Warriors closed out their fifth straight win. This marks the third loss in a row for the Clippers. Stephen Curry led the Warriors with 27 points, six rebounds, four assists, a steal and a block, in 29 minutes. Kevin Durant followed up with 16 points, seven assists, three rebounds, one steal and a block, while Draymond Green finished with 10 points, 10 rebounds, nine assists, five steals and three blocks. Lou Williams added 13 points, five rebounds, five assists, three steals and two blocks, while Shai Gilgeous-Alexander tallied 12 points, three assists, one rebounds and one steal. The Clippers shot 48 percent from the field, including 10 - of - 19 from deep. The Clippers (47 - 34) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Jazz on Wednesday. The Warriors (56 - 24) take on the Pelicans in New Orleans on Tuesday.

The Miami Heat defeated the Washington Wizards, 113 - 112, at Capital One Arena on Thursday. After the Heat (1 - 1) were unable to convert on a potential game - winning possession in their season - opener Wednesday night, they made sure to not make the same mistake two games in a row. With Miami down by one point, a Dwyane Wade fadeaway jumper over John Wall hit the back of the rim, but Kelly Olynyk made sure he was in the right place at the right time. The big man got the rebound and laid it in with ease with just .2 seconds remaining to put the visiting team up one. The Wizards (0 - 1) didn't get a shot off in their final possession, and the Heat earned their first victory of the 2018 - 19 season. Josh Richardson led the way for Miami, scoring a game - high 28 points to go along with five assists and four rebounds in 38 minutes. It was, however, still a complete team effort from the Heat on Thursday night, with seven players scoring at least nine points. The team managed to overcome a very rough shooting night, as Miami shot just 39 percent from the field. As for the Wizards, their All-Star backcourt did everything they could to will the team to victory on opening night, with John Wall posting a team - high 26 points and nine assists, while Bradley Beal added 20 points of his own. Jeff Green was also impressive in his Wizards debut, scoring 17 points in 33 minutes off the bench. Washington was without starting center Dwight Howard (back), but the team still somehow managed to block 15 shots.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the host Washington Wizards, 117 - 113, at Capital One Arena on Saturday evening. Despite missing Kawhi Leonard (rest) the Raptors earned an impressive win in Washington. The Wizards started out well, but the Raptors overtook them late in the quarter to hold a 24 - 22 advantage heading into the second. The second quarter stayed close until Toronto pulled away late to amass a 10 - point. However, the Wizards came right back with an 11 - 4 run, to cut the deficit to just three, heading into halftime. The Wizards continued their push into the third quarter, where they squeezed ahead and held a three - point lead with 5:27 to go in the quarter. The Raptors turned it around again as they closed the quarter on a 20 - 9 run, to take a 90 - 82 advantage into the final frame. The Raptors pushed their lead to 13, midway through the fourth, but the Wizards were not done yet, as they made it a two - point game with just 38 seconds left. However, a clutch shot by Fred VanVleet ensured the Raptors remain undefeated on the season, with their third straight win. Kyle Lowry led the Raptors with 28 points, 12 assists, three rebounds, one steal and one block, in 34 minutes. Jonas Valanciunas and Serge Ibaka chipped in 16 points each, as well as provided a combined16 rebounds. Fred VanVleet added 13 points, five assists and four rebounds, in 26 minutes off the bench. The Raptors shot 44 percent from the field, including 10 - of - 29 from long range. Meanwhile, Bradley Beal had a big night with 32 points, six assists, three rebounds, one steal and one block, while John Wall followed up with 25 points, six assists, four rebounds, four steals and one block. The Wizards (0 - 2) will look to bounce back as they take on the Trail Blazers in Portland on Monday. The Raptors (30) host the Hornets on Monday.

The Oklahoma City Thunder defeated the host Washington Wizards, 134 - 111, at Capital One Arena on Friday. These teams are heading in opposite directions and this 23 - point final spread shows exactly which way they're headed. While Washington led for the majority of the first quarter, a 44 - 20 second quarter in advantage of Oklahoma City was simply too much for the Wizards to overcome. In fact, the Thunder led by at least 19 points for the entirety of the second half. Oklahoma City's offense was unstoppable, as they connected on 57 percent from the field and 47 percent from three - point range. The 34 assists recorded by the Thunder was a huge part of that, as they also won the turnover differential, 18 - 13. The Thunder (4 - 4) were led by Russell Westbrook, as he collected 23 points, three rebounds, 12 assists and four steals on 10 - of - 16 shooting. Jerami Grant finished with 22 points, four rebounds and four assists on 9 - of - 11 from the field. Paul George accrued 17 points, four rebounds, seven assists and two steals. Dennis Schroder led the bench with 16 points, six rebounds and five assists. The Wizards (1 - 7) best player was Bradley Beal, as he amassed 27 points, two rebounds and four assists on 10 - of - 16 shooting. Dwight Howard scored 20 points on 7 - of - 8 from the field in his Washington debut. John Wall accumulated 19 points, two rebounds and nine assists. Kelly Oubre Jr. led the bench with 14 points, four boards and two blocks. On deck for Washington is a home matchup versus the New York Knicks on Sunday. As for Oklahoma City, they're off until Monday when they welcome the New Orleans Pelicans to OKC.

The Washington Wizards defeated the New York Knicks, 108 - 95, at Capital One Arena on Sunday evening. The Wizards (2 - 7) came into Sunday's contest in dire need of a win, as they'd dropped seven of their first eight games. They seemingly had a good opportunity to right their ship against the Knicks (3 - 7), but they needed to up their level of play significantly from what it had been until that point. Washington was able to get off to a strong start by taking a 24 - 17 lead in the first quarter, which allowed them to hold on during the middle periods when New York made a run to narrow their deficit to three points going into the final 12 minutes. Then, Washington was able to turn up their play a notch, outscoring the visitors by a 27 - 17 margin to seal the victory. Enes Kanter paced the Knicks with an 18 - point, 12 - rebound double - double. Trey Burke supplied 13 points, three assists and a steal. Dewayne Dotson tallied 11 points, six rebounds and two assists. Mitchell Robinson offered 10 points, six rebounds and one block. Mario Hezonja matched Robinson's scoring total and added eight boards, three assists and three steals. John Wall spearheaded the Wizards with 26 points, seven assists, two rebounds and five steals. Bradley Beal registered 22 points, eight rebounds, three assists and four blocks. Markieff Morris compiled 16 points, six rebounds, five assists, two blocks and one steal. Jeff Green followed with a bench - leading 14 points and also managed nine boards and two blocks. Dwight Howard started and generated a 10 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included one steal and one block. The Knicks head back home to take on the Chicago Bulls on Monday night, while the Wizards pay a visit to the Dallas Mavericks on Tuesday evening.

The Washington Wizards defeated the visiting Orlando Magic, 117 - 109, at Capital One Arena on Monday. This eight - point final margin is unfair to the Magic, as it was extremely competitive throughout. In fact, neither club led by more than 10 points, as there were 17 ties and 18 lead changes in total. A 14 - 4 run by Washington in the middle of the fourth quarter was critical, as that turned a tied ball game into Washington's biggest lead with four minutes remaining. In addition, the first three quarters all ended in stalemates, as a 34 - 26 fourth quarter ultimately won Washington the game. Defensive rebounding was huge for the Wizards, as they won that battle, 34 - 26. Getting to the free - throw line was also huge, with Washington connecting on 24 - of - 33 while Orlando hit just 8 - of - 11. The Wizards also won the points in the paint battle, 46 - 38 and won the fastbreak differential, 15 - 5. The Magic's (6 - 8) leading scorer came off the bench, as Terrence Ross provided 21 points, three rebounds and two assists. Evan Fournier led the starters with 20 points, two rebounds and five assists. Aaron Gordon collected 18 points, 10 rebounds, three assists, two steals an two blocks. Nikola Vucevic amassed 17 points, 11 rebounds and three assists. The Wizards (4 - 9) were led by John Wall, as he tallied 25 points, four rebounds and 10 assists. Bradley Beal totaled 21 points, eight rebounds, four assists and two steals. Dwight Howard finished with 17 points and eight boards while Markieff Morris generated 16 points and eight rebounds. Jeff Green led the bench with 18 points, six rebounds and two steals on 6 - of - 7 from the field. Both teams return to action on Wednesday, with Orlando playing host to the Philadelphia 76ers and Washington remaining home to face the Cleveland Cavaliers.

The Washington Wizards defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers, 119 - 95, at Capitol One Arena on Wednesday evening. The Wizards (5 - 9) came into the contest showing some signs of life after a dreadful start, as they'd notched consecutive wins against the Heat and Magic in their prior two games. However, Cavaliers (2 - 12) were feeling good in their own right, having surprised the Charlotte Hornets by a 113 - 89 margin Tuesday. The possibility for a letdown therefore existed, and the first quarter indicated that's exactly what was in the cards. Washington forged a 41 - 29 lead after 12 minutes that they'd expanded to 73 - 52 by halftime. That essentially allowed the home squad to tread water in the second half and still finish with a comfortable victory. Although the Wizards were guilty of 17 turnovers on the night, they forced 23 from the Cleveland while also holding them to a 19 percent success rate from three - point range. Rookie Collin Sexton paced the Cavaliers with 24 points and added three rebounds and two assists. David Nwaba followed with 11 points off the bench, which he partly supplemented with seven rebounds. Larry Nance, Jr. and Rodney Hood generated matching 10 - point tallies on the starting five. Nance also had six rebounds, five assists, four steals and two blocks, while Hood had a pair of rebounds and assists each. Andrew Harrison supplied 10 points on the second unit as well, while Tristan Thompson registered nine points, eight boards, two assists, two steals and one block. Bradley Beal led the Wizards with 20 points while also recording three rebounds, three assists and three steals. Otto Porter, Jr. provided 15 points, four rebounds, three assists and two steals. Austin Rivers poured in 12 points off the bench. Markieff Morris and Dwight Howard had 11 and 10 points, respectively, with Howard also grabbing seven boards. John Wall mustered eight points, nine assists, five rebounds, two steals and one block in just 21 minutes. The Cavaliers are off until next Monday, when they'll take on the Detroit Pistons in Motown. The Wizards remain home and await a visit from the Brooklyn Nets on Friday evening.

The Brooklyn Nets defeated the host Washington Wizards, 115 - 104, at Capital One Arena on Friday evening. The Wizards got out to a good start on the road, with an early 10 - 4 lead, an held on to take a 30 - 26 lead into the second. They managed to stay on top to begin the quarter, but the Nets picked up the pace and pulled ahead to take a 56 - 54 lead into halftime. The Nets picked up where they left off in the third quarter, as they pushed their way to a 10 - point lead, five minutes into the quarter, and went on to outscore Washington by 10 in the quarter, to take a 91 - 79 lead into the final frame. The Wizards had no answer, as the Nets held a 15 - point lead halfway through the quarter, and went on to end a three - game losing streak, while the Wizards saw their three - game winning streak come to an end. Spencer Dinwiddie led the Nets with 25 points, eight assists, four rebounds and three steals, in 31 minutes off the bench. D'Angelo Russell followed up with 23 points, six assists, three rebounds and two steals, in 29 minutes. Jarrett Allen had a big night, with 16 points, 12 rebounds, two blocks and a steal, in 31 minutes. The Nets shot 42 percent from the field, including 9 - of - 33 from long range. Meanwhile, Dwight Howard led the Wizards with 25 points, 17 rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block, in 27 minutes. Bradley Beal followed up with 20 points, six rebounds, two assists and a block, while Kelly Oubre Jr. chipped in 18 points, in 27 minutes off the bench. The Wizards shot 42 percent from the field, including 3 - of - 18 from deep. The Wizards (5 - 10) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Trail Blazers on Sunday. The Nets (7 - 9) play host to the Clippers on Saturday.

The Portland Trail Blazers defeated the Washington Wizards, 119 - 109, at Capital One Arena on Sunday evening. The win snapped a two - game losing streak for Portland (11 - 5), who had dropped back - to - back contests heading into Sunday's matchup. Washington (5 - 11), on the contrary, has now dropped two straight after what seemed like a revitalizing three - game win streak last week. It was tough to question Portland's dominance in Sunday's win, though, as the team quickly jumped out to a double - digit lead in the first quarter. The game was all but sealed by the stifling defense the Blazers exhibited in the second quarter. Washington was held to just 16 points on under 40 percent shooting from the field in the period. Damian Lillard bounced back from a rather pedestrian 16 - point outing on Friday to score a game - high 40 points in the win. Though he shot just 12 - of - 29 from the floor, Lillard made up for it with a 13 - of - 15 performance at the free - throw line. C.J. McCollum added another 25 points, while big man Jusuf Nurkic flirted with a triple - double, tallying 13 points, 14 rebounds, and eight assists on the night. For the Wizards, meanwhile, John Wall led the way with 24 points. Kelly Oubre, Jr. led the bench unit with 19 points in 29 minutes of action on the floor. The team, however, struggled to make the best use of its opportunities at the free - throw line, effectively playing itself out of the game at the stripe. Washington went just 10 - of - 21 from the free - throw line. Portland will continue its road trip with a visit to Madison Square Garden to take on the Knicks this Tuesday. Washington, meanwhile, will play host to the LA Clippers.

The Washington Wizards defeated the Los Angeles Clippers, 125 - 118, at Capital One Arena on Tuesday evening. The Wizards (6 - 11) came into the contest with controversy swirling around them, given recent rumors that no current player is untouchable in a trade and plenty of rumblings about infighting among some of the team's stars. Therefore, when the Clippers (11 - 6) opened up a 40 - 21 first - quarter lead, it wasn't likely to much of anyone's surprise and normally would have set the tone for a blowout win for the visitors. That wasn't to be Tuesday, however, as Washington clawed back by outscoring Los Angeles, 65 - 55, in the middle periods. That allowed them to enter the final 12 minutes with a 95 - 86 lead, one that they'd preserve by showing some impressive killer instinct while outpacing their visitors by a 39 - 23 fourth - quarter margin. Tobias Harris led the way for the Clippers with 29 points, a total he supplemented with nine rebounds and one assist. Montrezl Harrell managed 20 points, nine rebounds, two assists and one block. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Lou Williams each provided 17 points. Marcin Gortat posted nine points and seven rebounds against his old Wizards teammates. John Wall paced the Wizards with 30 points and added eight assists, four rebounds, two steals and two blocks. Bradley Beal generated 27 points, seven assists, three rebounds and one block. Jeff Green followed with a bench - leading 20 points and complemented them with seven boards, three assists, one steal and one block. Tomas Satoransky turned in 13 points, seven rebounds, three assists, three steals and one block. Markieff Morris poured in 12 points and added five rebounds and a pair of assists off the bench. The Clippers return home to take on the Grizzlies on Friday afternoon, while the Wizards remain home and tangle with the Toronto Raptors on Friday night.

The Washington Wizards defeated the visiting New Orleans Pelicans, 124 - 114, at Capital One Arena on Saturday. There were 14 ties and 20 lead changes in this tightly - contested battle, as it wasn't decided until the final quarter. Washington rode a big fourth quarter to victory, outscoring New Orleans, 34 - 23. The Wizards offense was unstoppable, as they went 51 - of - 90 from the field while recording 30 assists. Rim protection was also critical, as they tripled up the Pelicans in blocks, 9 - 3. Washington did most of their damage down low, outscoring New Orleans in the paint, 70 - 44. The Pelicans (10 - 10) had to play this game without Anthony Davis (quad), as that clearly hampered them in this defeat. Julius Randle played admirably in his absence, as he collected 29 points, 15 rebounds and seven assists on 10 - of - 16 shooting in a start. Jrue Holiday accrued 16 points, five rebounds and nine assists. Nikola Mirotic finished with 24 points and nine boards while E'Twaun Moore provided 19 points, five rebounds and six steals. The Wizards (7 - 12) were led by Otto Porter Jr., as he tallied 29 points, seven rebounds, four assists and two steals on 12 - of - 15 from the field. John Wall accumulated 22 points, seven rebounds and eight assists. Bradley Beal amassed 18 points, six rebounds, eight assists and three blocks. Austin Rivers and Markieff Morris combined for 33 points, 11 rebounds, four steals and three blocks to lead the bench. Both teams play home games on Monday for their next outing, with New Orleans welcoming the Boston Celtics and Washington playing host to the Houston Rockets.

The Washington Wizards defeated the Houston Rockets, 135 - 131, at Capital One Arena on Monday evening. This game between the Wizards (8 - 12) and the Rockets (9 - 10) was expected to be a high - scoring affair right from the start, and it didn't disappoint anyone since both teams combined for over 260 points while needing an overtime period to find a winner. The first quarter alone had 72 points (42 - 30 for Houston), but the Wizards won the second quarter by a 14 - point margin (37 - 23). Houston won the third quarter by six points (33 - 27), but the Wizards once again answered in the fourth (31 - 27), so both teams needed to play five more minutes to decide the winner. The Wizards took advantage of the opportunity and with a 10 - 6 OT period, they secured a huge win at home. John Wall led the way for the Wizards with a 36 - point, 11 - assist performance, while Bradley Beal had a very good performance as well since he finished with 32 points. Otto Porter Jr. chipped in with 14 points and six rebounds. Markieff Morris had an impressive performance off the bench with 22 points and 10 rebounds. Jeff Green contributed 13 points, four boards and three assists. James Harden was the undisputed star for the Rockets and had one of the best games (individually) during the current season, finishing with 54 points, 13 assists, eight rebounds and three steals, but he also committed 11 turnovers. Eric Gordon had a stellar outing as well since he had 36 points. Clint Capela had a strong double - double of 17 points and 14 boards. James Ennis III finished with 10 points.

The Washington Wizards defeated the Brooklyn Nets, 102 - 88, at Capital One Arena on Saturday night. The Wizards (9 - 14) came into Saturday's contest having just dropped a 123 - 98 decision to the Philadelphia 76ers on Friday night, while also dealing with ongoing trade rumors surrounding the team's biggest stars. However, they had a potentially vulnerable opponent in the Nets (8 - 16), which had endured a double - overtime defeat to the Memphis Grizzlies 24 hours earlier and then had to travel for Saturday's game. To its credit, Brooklyn hung close during the first half and entered intermission with a manageable 42 - 39 deficit. The home squad would pull away for good in the third, however, adding seven points to their lead and then capping it off with a 34 - point final period. Washington's defensive effort was superb all the way around and exemplified by the fact they limited the Nets to 37 percent shooting, including 24 percent from three - point range. Allen Crabbe led the way with the Nets with 14 points, a total he supplemented with two rebounds and two steals. Rondae Hollis-Jefferson provided 11 points, eight rebounds and one steal. DeMarre Carroll supplied 10 points and five rebounds off the bench. Spencer Dinwiddie and D'Angelo Russell registered eight points apiece and dished out eight and seven assists, respectively. John Wall paced the Wizards with 30 points and added nine assists, five rebounds and one steal. Bradley Beal tallied 22 points, three rebounds and one block. Markieff Morris came off the bench to pour in 20 points and also posted seven rebounds, two assists, three steals and two blocks. Otto Porter, Jr. returned to the lineup after a one - game absence for rest and compiled seven points, 11 rebounds, two assists and three steals. Tomas Satoransky drew a spot start and went for seven points, three assists and one rebound. The Nets head back home to face off with the Cleveland Cavaliers on Monday night. The Wizards hit the road and take on the New York Knicks on Monday evening as well.

The Boston Celtics defeated the Washington Wizards, 130 - 125, at Capital One Arena on Wednesday night. The Celtics (17 - 10) are one of the hottest teams in the league at the moment and they have pushed their winning streak up to seven with another solid display, although they had to work harder than expected in this one to get past a Wizards (11 - 17) squad that never gave up. Boston had to trail during the entire first half, however, as Washington won the first two quarters, 28 - 24 and 27 - 22, respectively. Boston surged out of nowhere with a 38 - 22 third quarter that saw them go up by seven points, but the Wizards rallied in the fourth and sent the game to OT. There, Boston was better when it mattered the most and a 17 - 12 edge in the extra five minutes of action allowed them to keep their winning run alive for, at least, one more game. Undoubtedly, Kyrie Irving was Boston's best player since he finished with 38 points and seven assists. Marcus Morris delivered a solid effort since he contributed 27 points, and Marcus Smart chipped in with 18 of his own while adding five rebounds, three assists and three steals. Jayson Tatum had a double - double of 12 points and 12 rebounds. Terry Rozier had 10 points off the bench. John Wall was the star for the Wizards since he finished the contest with 34 points, 13 assists and six rebounds, but also committed five turnovers. Bradley Beal added 22 points, seven rebounds and four assists for the losing cause, while Jeff Green also added 22 points but with 10 rebounds. Kelly Oubre Jr. thrived coming off the bench since he finished the game with 20 points while playing 38 minutes.

The Washington Wizards defeated the visiting Los Angeles Lakers, 128 - 110, at Capital One Arena on Sunday. While Los Angeles came into this game as the favorite, Washington looked like the much better team on this night. A 33 - 23 first quarter really set the tone, as the Wizards held the lead for the final 45 minutes of action. In fact, Washington led by at least 15 points for the entirety of the second half, as they led by 23 points heading into the fourth quarter. The Wizards offense was unstoppable, as they connected on 51 percent from the field and 42 percent from three - point range while recording 30 assists. Their defense was huge as well, as they won the rebounding battle, 51 - 43 while picking up 14 steals. The Lakers (18 - 12) were led by Kyle Kuzma, as he tallied 20 points, six rebounds and three assists. LeBron James finished with just 13 points, six rebounds and three assists. Lonzo Ball collected 10 points, five rebounds, four assists, three steals and two blocks. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope led the bench with 25 points, six rebounds and five assists. The Wizards (12 - 18) got a vintage performance from John Wall, as he accumulated 40 points, six rebounds, 14 assists, three steals and two blocks. Bradley Beal accrued 25 points, 12 rebounds and three assists. Jeff Green started and totaled 20 points and seven boards. Sam Dekker had a season - high 20 points, five rebounds, four assists and three steals to lead the bench. Both teams return to action on Tuesday, with Washington traveling to face the Atlanta Hawks and Los Angeles playing the Brooklyn Nets on the road as well.

The Washington Wizards defeated the Phoenix Suns, 149 - 146, in triple overtime at Capital One Arena on Saturday evening. The matchup between two teams with losing records turned out to be a classic, with a see - saw first four quarters giving way to three extra periods. The first overtime came about after Jeff Green sank a pair of free throws following a T.J. Warren shooting foul with 3 seconds remaining. Devin Booker missed a would - be game - winning 30 - point jumper with a second remaining. A Booker free throw with 7 seconds left in the first OT knotted the game at 122, and this time it was Bradley Beal missing the opportunity to finish the game with a misfire on a 17 - footer with 0 seconds remaining. A Thomas Bryant tip - in with 12 seconds left in the second OT was responsible for extending the game to a third, when Tomas Satoransky and Jeff Green sank a trio of free throws in the closing seconds to finally seal the win. Booker led the Suns with 33 points, and he added 14 assists, four rebounds, one steal and one block. Warren finished with 28 points, eight rebounds, four assists, two steals and two blocks. Deandre Ayton contributed a 26 - point, 17 - rebound double - double that also included one assist, one steal and one block. Kelly Oubre, Jr. was productive against his old team, delivering 20 points, five rebounds and one steal. Richaun Holmes pitched in 12 points, five rebounds, one steal and one block, while De'Anthony Melton and Jamal Crawford generated matching 10 - point tallies. The Suns remain on the road and play the Brooklyn Nets on Sunday evening, while the Wizards visit the Indiana Pacers on Sunday afternoon.

The Chicago Bulls defeated the host Washington Wizards, 101 - 92, at Capital One Arena on Friday evening. The Wizards got out to a good start as they led by two after one quarter. The Bulls picked it up in the second but still trailed by two at halftime. However, they picked it up in the third, where they outscored the home team by four, to take a two - point lead heading into the fourth. The Bulls kept the momentum through the final frame, where they outscored the Wizards by seven to seal their fifth road win of the season. Zach LaVine led the Bulls with 24 points, three assists and one rebound, in 28 minutes. Wendell Carter Jr. followed up with 17 points, 13 rebounds, three blocks, two assists and one steal, while Lauri Markkanen added 14 points, 14 rebounds and one block. The Bulls shot 47 percent from the field, including 8 - of - 22 from long range. Meanwhile, Bradley Beal led the Wizards with 34 points, seven rebounds, five assists and two steals, in 37 minutes. Jeff Green added 11 points, seven rebounds and four assists, while Thomas Bryant tallied 12 points, eight rebounds, two assists, three blocks and one steal. The Wizards shot 40 percent from the field, including 9 - of - 30 from long range. The Wizards (13 - 23) will look to bounce back as they play host to the Hornets on Saturday. The Bulls (10 - 26) take on the Raptors in Toronto on Sunday.

The Washington Wizards defeated the Charlotte Hornets, 130 - 126, at Capital One Arena on Saturday evening. The Wizards (14 - 23) were playing with heavy hearts to an extent Saturday, as they found out earlier in the day that star point guard John Wall will miss the rest of the season due to impending heel surgery. However, Washington came out with a commitment to forge ahead, as they outpaced a hot - shooting Hornets (17 - 18) squad in the first half to the tune of a 67 - 61 halftime advantage. However, this was a game that would come down to the wire, with Kemba Walker's final three points of a 47 - point outburst bringing Charlotte to within 127 - 126 with 2 seconds remaining. Trevor Ariza then turned around and logged the final three points of the night for Washington with a bucket and a free throw over the last two seconds. Walker added four rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block to his game - high point tally. Marvin Williams followed with 17 points, seven rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block. Jeremy Lamb mustered 13 points, five rebounds and one assist. Michael Kidd-Gilchrist and Devonte' Graham supplied matching 11 - point tallies and added six and four rebounds, respectively. Ariza paced the Wizards with 24 points, adding nine assists and seven rebounds. Thomas Bryant generated a 21 - point, 10 - rebound double - double that also included three assists and one block. Tomas Satoransky turned in 20 points, six assists and four rebounds. Sam Dekker and Chasson Randle offered matching 11 - point contributions. The Hornets head back home to face the Orlando Magic on Monday night, while the Wizards remain home and tangle with the Atlanta Hawks on Wednesday evening.

The Washington Wizards defeated the Atlanta Hawks, 114 - 98, at Capital One Arena on Wednesday evening. The Wizards (15 - 23) had notched 10 of their 14 victories on their home floor coming in, so it wasn't a surprise to see them jump out to a 64 - 53 halftime lead. The Hawks (11 - 26) seemed to wake up at intermission, however, compiling 31 points in the third quarter to slice seven points off their deficit. Atlanta clawed all the way back to knot the game at 94 with 6:44 remaining, before Washington would flash their killer instinct. The home squad would go on to finish the game on an 18 - 4 run to seal the victory, and they saw all five members of their starting five hit double digits in the scoring column. Alex Len paced the Hawks with 24 points in 23 minutes off the bench. He added 11 rebounds and three blocks. John Collins supplied 21 points, eight boards and three assists. Kyle Huerter turned in 12 points, five assists, one rebound and one block. DeAndre' Bembry registered 11 points and seven rebounds. Daniel Hamilton and Jeremy Lin generated eight points apiece, with Hamilton also hauling in seven rebounds. Tre Young mustered just five points but dished out nine assists and recorded one block. Bradley Beal led the Wizards with 24 points and also posted six assists, four rebounds and two steals. Jeff Green managed 22 points, six rebounds and six assists. Thomas Bryant managed a 16 - point, 15 - rebound double - double that also included one assist, two steals and two blocks. Tomas Satoransky delivered 14 points, 11 rebounds, seven assists and two steals. Trevor Ariza collected 12 points, five rebounds, four assists and one steal. Otto Porter, Jr. led the bench with nine points. The Hawks remain on the road and tangle with the Milwaukee Bucks on Friday night, while the Wizards pay a visit to the Miami Heat on Friday evening as well.

The Washington Wizards defeated the Philadelphia 76ers, 123 - 106, at Capital One Arena on Wednesday night. The Wizards (17 - 25) were coming off a significant loss to the 76ers (27 - 15) just 24 hours earlier, but they opened Wednesday's contest ready to extract some revenge. Washington had forged a 63 - 48 lead by halftime, and they made sure to keep their foot on the gas in the second half. The home squad shot a stellar 54 percent, including 48 percent from three - point range. The Wizards also played some impressive defense for a change, forcing 24 turnovers and limiting the Sixers to a 30 percent success rate from three - point range. Joel Embiid was a bright spot for the 76ers, posting a 35 - point, 14 - rebound double - double that also included two assists, three blocks and one steal. Jimmy Butler provided 23 points, nine rebounds, two assists and two steals. Furkan Korkmaz furnished 16 points, five rebounds, two assists and two steals. Ben Simmons supplied 15 points, 10 rebounds, eight assists and two steals. Bradley Beal paced the Wizards with 34 points, supplementing them with five assists, two rebounds, one steal and one block. Otto Porter, Jr. followed with 23 points, six rebounds and three steals. Trevor Ariza delivered 17 points, five boards, one assist and two steals. Sam Dekker registered 11 points, two boards, an assist and a steal. The 76ers now head back home to face the Atlanta Hawks on Friday night, while the Wizards remain home to tangle with the Milwaukee Bucks on Friday night.

The Washington Wizards defeated the visiting Milwaukee Bucks, 113 - 106, at Capital One Arena. While Milwaukee was the heavy favorite headed into this game, Washington was able to prevail. A 40 - 26 first quarter really set the tone, as the Wizards held the lead for the final three quarters. Three-point shooting was key for Washington, as they hit 18 - of - 33 while Milwaukee connected on 13 - of - 40. All of the other statistics were nearly even. The Bucks (29 - 12) had to play this game without Giannis Antetokounmpo, as this may go down as their worst loss of the season. Khris Middleton led the way in his absence, as he tallied 25 points, eight rebounds and three assists. Eric Bledsoe accrued 18 points, eight rebounds, nine assists and three steals. Malcolm Brogdon finished with 15 points, six rebounds and eight assists. The Wizards (18 - 25) were led by Bradley Beal, as he accumulated 32 points, five rebounds, seven assists and three steals. Trevor Ariza amassed 20 points, three rebounds, three assists and two steals. Tomas Satoransky recorded the first triple - double of his career, as he accumulated 18 points, 12 rebounds and 10 assists. Both teams return to action on Sunday, with Washington playing host to the Toronto Raptors and Milwaukee traveling to face the struggling Atlanta Hawks.

The Toronto Raptors defeated the Washington Wizards, 140 - 138, at Capital One Arena on Sunday afternoon. The Raptors (33 - 12) and the Wizards (18 - 26) undoubtedly played one of the best games of the 2018 - 19 NBA season thus far, as they needed 58 minutes of basketball to find a winner and the game ended with a slim two - point margin. Toronto were in control during most of the game, however, since they won two of the first three quarters (36 - 21, 25 - 29, 37 - 34 on their favor) to enter the fourth with a healthy 14 - point lead. But Washington woke up and sent the game to OT with a terrific performance in the final 12 minutes of action (40 - 26). One overtime wasn't enough, but in the end, Toronto survived this game and clawed back to earn the win on the road. Kawhi Leonard was the best player for the Raptors since he finished with 41 points and 11 rebounds across 45 minutes. Kyle Lowry and Pascal Siakam each had double - doubles, too - while the point guard contributed 12 points and 11 assists to the winning cause, Siakam chipped in with 24 points and 19 rebounds. Danny Green had 16 points with eight rebounds. Delon Wright added 17 points off the bench. Bradley Beal was the game's highest scorer since he finished with a triple - double of 43 points (17 - 36 shooting), 15 assists and 10 rebounds. Trevor Ariza came quite close of adding a triple - double of his own since he had 23 points, 10 assists and nine boards. Thomas Bryant had 18 points and 11 rebounds. Otto Porter Jr. contributed off the bench with 27 points and eight rebounds in 44 minutes.

The Washington Wizards defeated the New York Knicks, 101 - 100, at O2 Arena in London on Thursday. The Wizards (19 - 26) and the Knicks (10 - 34) played this game on a neutral arena and there is no doubt they gave fans an unbelieveable showdown that went down to the wire, as this game was decided with a lay - up in the final second of regulation. The Knicks got off to an impressive start, though, winning the first quarter by 10 points (30 - 20) and extending their lead in the upcoming two quarters (33 - 33 and 26 - 24, respectively) so they entered the final 12 minutes of action up by a considerable 12 - point margin. However, the Wizards came alive in the final quarter and not only they won that frame by 13 points (24 - 11) but they also did it in style: the Wizards won this game thanks to a Thomas Bryant lay - up with only 0 seconds left on the clock. Six Washington players ended the game scoring over 10 points and Bradley Beal was the team's top scorer with 26 points, nine rebounds, four assists and two steals. Tomas Satoransky had 14 points and five assists, while Trevor Ariza filled the stat sheet thanks to 12 points, seven rebounds and seven assists. Otto Porter Jr. had an impressive effort off the bench since he chipped in with 20 points and 11 boards. Emmanuel Mudiay led the way for the Knicks with 25 points and seven rebounds. Luke Kornet chipped in with 16 points and five steals, while Noah Vonleh contributed with a strong double - double of 13 points and 10 rebounds. Allonzo Trier and Damyean Dotson each had 13 points coming off the bench. Kevin Knox was a disappointment, however, as the rookie only had five points while shooting 2 - 11 from the field.

The Washington Wizards defeated the visiting Detroit Pistons, 101 - 87, at Capital One Arena on Monday. While this wasn't necessarily a wire - to - wire win for the Wizards, they led for all but a couple minutes in the first quarter. In fact, a 29 - 17 first quarter really set the tone for the rest of the game, as Washington held a double - digit lead for the final three quarters. The Wizards simply looked like a better team, as they had seven players reach double figures in scoring while the Pistons had just two. Washington did a ton of their damage down low, outscoring Detroit in the paint, 46 - 32. They also won the transition scoring battle, 25 - 10. The Pistons (20 - 26) were led by Blake Griffin, as he collected 29 points, nine rebounds and four assists. Reggie Bullock was the only other Detroit player in double figures, as he accrued 12 points, seven rebounds and four assists. Bruce Brown Jr. finished with four points, five rebounds and four assists. The Wizards (20 - 26) were led by Trevor Ariza, as he tallied 20 points, 12 rebounds and four assists. Bradley Beal accumulated 16 points, four assists and three blocks. Thomas Bryant amassed 11 points and 12 boards while Tomas Satoransky totaled 10 points, four rebounds and eight assists. Otto Porter Jr. led the bench with 19 points and four rebounds. Detroit will return to action on Wednesday when they play the New Orleans Pelicans on the road. As for Washington, they travel to face the Golden State Warriors for their next fixture on Thursday.

The Golden State Warriors defeated the host Washington Wizards, 126 - 118, at Capital One Arena on Thursday. While the first 10 minutes of this game was competitive, that was the only time Golden State felt in jeopardy. In fact, they won that quarter, 37 - 28 and held the lead for the final three quarters. Golden State's offense was unstoppable, as they shot 57 percent from the field while recording 34 assists. Rim protection was also huge, with the Warriors tripling up the Wizards in blocks, 6 - 2. Most of Golden State's damage was done in the paint, as they outscored Washington down low, 70 - 48. The Warriors (34 - 14) were led by Stephen Curry, as he tallied 38 points, four rebounds and three assists. Kevin Durant collected 21 points, two rebounds, five assists, two steals and three blocks. Draymond Green accumulated seven points, 15 rebounds and seven assists. DeMarcus Cousins totaled 17 points, six rebounds and three assists in 24 minutes. The Wizards (20 - 27) were led by Trevor Ariza, as he amassed 27 points, three rebounds, three assists and two steals. Tomas Satoransky accrued 20 points, three rebounds, 10 assists and three steals. Thomas Bryant generated 14 points, five rebounds and four assists while Bradley Beal finished with 22 points, 10 rebounds and three assists. On deck for Washington is a road matchup versus the Orlando Magic on Friday. As for Golden State, they return to action on Saturday when they travel to face the Boston Celtics.

The Washington Wizards defeated the Indiana Pacers, 107 - 89, at Capital One Arena on Wednesday evening. The Wizards (22 - 29) have had a largely disappointing season to say the least, but their home record has been a source of pride. Washington came into Wednesday's contest with a solid 15 - 9 mark at Capital One Arena, and their first half effort against the short - handed Pacers (32 - 18) was a testament to why. The hosts built an impressive 59 - 45 lead by halftime, and they won the second half by a slightly less commanding 48 - 44 margin as well. The Wizards were strong on both ends of the floor, draining 53 percent of their attempts while limiting Indiana to a 39 percent success rate. Thaddeus Young led the Pacers with 13 points, adding seven rebounds, five assists and one block. Bojan Bogdanovic supplied 12 points, two boards and two assists. T.J. Leaf and Doug McDermott generated matching 12 - point tallies off the bench. Aaron Holiday poured in 10 points and added three rebounds. Domantas Sabonis matched Holiday's scoring total and also posted eight rebounds, three assists and one steal. Myles Turner furnished nine points, six rebounds, three assists and one steal over 27 minutes. Bradley Beal paced the Wizards with 25 points, six rebounds, six assists and one steal. Jeff Green tallied 23 points, six assists, five rebounds and two blocks. Chasson Randle generated 13 points, Trevor Ariza and Jordan McCrae pitched in matching 12 - point efforts while hauling in three and two rebounds, respectively. The Pacers remain on the road and tangle with the Orlando Magic on Thursday night, while the Wizards remain home and take on the Milwaukee Bucks on Saturday evening.

The Milwaukee Bucks defeated the host Washington Wizards, 131 - 115, at Capital One Arena on Saturday. While Washingon grabbed the first lead in this game, that was the only time they were competitive. In fact, Milwaukee took a 38 - 26 lead after the first quarter, as a 35 - 24 second quarter put the game to bed. That allowed the Bucks to hold a double - digit lead for the entirety of the second half. Milwaukee ended up shooting 50 percent from the field and 44 percent from three - point range while holding Washington to 46 percent from the field and 30 percent from long range. The Bucks also went a perfect 24 - of - 24 from the free - throw line while winning the defensive rebounding battle, 40 - 33. The Bucks (38 - 13) were led by Giannis Antetokounmpo, as he totaled 37 points, 10 rebounds and two assists. Brook Lopez accumulated 21 points, six rebounds, two steals and two blocks. Khris Middleton collected 20 points, seven rebounds and six assists while Malcolm Brogdon amassed 15 points, nine rebounds and five assists. The Wizards (22 - 30) were led by Bradley Beal, as he generated 24 points, four rebounds and three assists. Otto Porter Jr. started and finished with 18 points, seven rebounds, two assists and four steals. Trevor Ariza tallied 12 points, six rebounds and four assists while Jeff Green led the bench with 20 points, three rebounds, two assists and two blocks. Both teams return to action on Monday, with Washington playing host to the Atlanta Hawks and Milwaukee traveling to face the surprising Brooklyn Nets.

The Atlanta Hawks defeated the host Washington Wizards, 137 - 129, at Capital One Arena on Monday. In a battle between two of the worst defenses in the league, both these offenses went off.
